# Cedar Design Web

> Vue 3 component library. Package: @cedar-design/ui-vue. Component prefix: C / c-.

Read the quick start and the relevant component page before generating code. Follow the documented props, events, slots, imports and styles. Do not substitute APIs from another component library.

Documentation language: en-US.

# Affix

The same scenarios, parameters and interactions as Cedar. Only component prefixes differ; themes and site shells remain independent.

## Basic examples

### Basic usage

Example source: src/affix/__demos__/basic.vue

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { ref } from 'vue'
const containerRef = ref<HTMLElement>()
</script>

<template>
  <p>Scroll inside the bordered area.</p>
  <div ref="containerRef" class="scroller">
    <div class="scroll-content">
      <c-affix :target="containerRef"><c-button status="primary">Basic usage</c-button></c-affix>
    </div>
  </div>
</template>

<style scoped>
.scroller {
  height: 200px;
  overflow: auto;
  border: 1px solid currentColor;
}
.scroll-content {
  min-height: 600px;
  padding: 16px;
}
</style>
```

## Layout and arrangement

### Affix direction, offset and container

<!-- demo-config-notes:start -->
#### Configuration reference for this comparison

| Configuration | Purpose | Related examples |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `target` | Scroller or selector; finds nearest scrolling ancestor when omitted, falling back to window | Affix direction, offset and container |
| `offset-top` | Distance from the scroll container top; accepts CSS lengths | Affix direction, offset and container |
| `offset-bottom` | Distance from the bottom; takes precedence over offset-top, including 0 | Affix direction, offset and container |
<!-- demo-config-notes:end -->


Scroll each bordered area separately to compare top/bottom affixing and offsets within an explicit scroll container.

Example source: src/affix/__demos__/offset-container-comparison.vue

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { useDemoLocale } from "../../__demos__/locale";
const demoCopy = useDemoLocale("affixOffsetContainerComparison");
import { ref, type ComponentPublicInstance } from "vue";
const asHTMLElement = (
  element: Element | ComponentPublicInstance | null,
): HTMLElement | undefined =>
  element instanceof HTMLElement ? element : undefined;
import { proxyRefs as demoProxyRefs } from "vue";

const scene1 = demoProxyRefs(
  (() => {
    const containerRef = ref<HTMLElement>();
    return { containerRef };
  })(),
);

const scene2 = demoProxyRefs(
  (() => {
    const containerRef = ref<HTMLElement>();
    return { containerRef };
  })(),
);

const scene3 = demoProxyRefs(
  (() => {
    const containerRef = ref<HTMLElement>();
    return { containerRef };
  })(),
);
</script>

<template>
  <div class="demo-comparison">
    <section
      class="demo-comparison-case demo-comparison-case--1"
      data-comparison-scene="top"
    >
      <h4>{{ demoCopy.top }}</h4>
      <p>Scroll inside the bordered area.</p>
      <div
        :ref="(element) => (scene1.containerRef = asHTMLElement(element))"
        class="scroller"
      >
        <div class="scroll-content">
          <c-affix :target="scene1.containerRef" :offset-top="80"
            ><c-button status="primary">Top offset</c-button></c-affix
          >
        </div>
      </div>
    </section>

    <section
      class="demo-comparison-case demo-comparison-case--2"
      data-comparison-scene="bottom"
    >
      <h4>{{ demoCopy.bottom }}</h4>
      <p>Scroll inside the bordered area.</p>
      <div
        :ref="(element) => (scene2.containerRef = asHTMLElement(element))"
        class="scroller"
      >
        <div class="scroll-content">
          <div style="height: 240px"></div>
          <c-affix :target="scene2.containerRef" :offset-bottom="20"
            ><c-button status="primary">Bottom offset</c-button></c-affix
          >
        </div>
      </div>
    </section>

      class="demo-comparison-case demo-comparison-case--3"

        class="scroller"
      >
        <div class="scroll-content">
          <div style="height: 40px"></div>
          <c-affix :target="scene3.containerRef" :offset-top="20"
            ><c-button status="primary">Scroll container</c-button></c-affix
          >
        </div>
      </div>
    </section>
  </div>
</template>
```

## Interaction and control

### Change event

<!-- demo-config-notes:start -->
#### Configuration reference for this comparison

| Configuration | Purpose | Related examples |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `target` | Scroller or selector; finds nearest scrolling ancestor when omitted, falling back to window | Change event, Disabled, CSS mode and manual update |
| `offset-top` | Distance from the scroll container top; accepts CSS lengths | Change event, Disabled, CSS mode and manual update |
| `disabled` | Disable affixing | Disabled, CSS mode and manual update |
| `css-mode` | Use native position: sticky, subject to ancestor overflow and container boundaries | Disabled, CSS mode and manual update |
| `z-index` | Stacking level | Disabled, CSS mode and manual update |
<!-- demo-config-notes:end -->


Example source: src/affix/__demos__/fix-change.vue

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { ref } from 'vue'
const containerRef = ref<HTMLElement>()
const fixed = ref(false)
</script>

<template>
  <p>Scroll inside the bordered area.</p>
  <div ref="containerRef" class="scroller">
    <div class="scroll-content">
      <div style="height: 40px"></div>
      <c-affix :target="containerRef" :offset-top="20" @change="fixed = $event"
        ><c-button status="primary">Change event</c-button></c-affix
      >
    </div>
  </div>
  <p role="status">Fixed: {{ fixed }}</p>
</template>

<style scoped>
.scroller {
  height: 200px;
  overflow: auto;
  border: 1px solid currentColor;
}
.scroll-content {
  min-height: 600px;
  padding: 16px;
}
</style>
```

### Disabled, CSS mode and manual update

Example source: src/affix/__demos__/controls.vue

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { nextTick, ref } from "vue";
const containerRef = ref<HTMLElement>();
const affixRef = ref<{ updatePosition: () => Promise<void> }>();
const disabled = ref(false);
const cssMode = ref(false);
const spacerHeight = ref(40);
const updates = ref(0);
async function updateLayout() {
  spacerHeight.value = spacerHeight.value === 40 ? 100 : 40;
  await nextTick();
  await affixRef.value?.updatePosition();
  updates.value++;
}
</script>

<template>
  <c-space wrap size="12px" style="margin-bottom: 12px">
    <c-checkbox v-model="disabled"> Disabled</c-checkbox>
    <c-checkbox v-model="cssMode"> CSS sticky</c-checkbox>
    <c-button @click="updateLayout">Change layout and update position</c-button>
  </c-space>
  <p aria-live="polite">Position updates: {{ updates }}</p>
  <div ref="containerRef" class="scroller">
    <div class="scroll-content">
      <div :style="{ height: `${spacerHeight}px` }"></div>
      <c-affix
        ref="affixRef"
        :target="containerRef"
        :disabled="disabled"
        :css-mode="cssMode"
        :offset-top="12"
        :z-index="2"
      >
        <c-button status="primary">Scroll to pin</c-button>
      </c-affix>
    </div>
  </div>
</template>

<style scoped>
.scroller {
  height: 200px;
  overflow: auto;
  border: 1px solid currentColor;
}
.scroll-content {
  min-height: 600px;
  padding: 16px;
}
</style>
```

## API

<!-- same-source-api:start -->
### Affix Props

| Prop | Description | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| offset-top | Distance from the scroll container top; accepts CSS lengths | `number / string` | `0` |
| offset-bottom | Distance from the bottom; takes precedence over offset-top, including 0 | `number / string` | `undefined` |
| target | Scroller or selector; finds nearest scrolling ancestor when omitted, falling back to window | `string / HTMLElement / Window` | `undefined` |
| target-container | Extra outer scroller to listen to; omitted means no extra listener, and it is not a clipping boundary | `string / HTMLElement / Window` | `undefined` |
| z-index | Stacking level | `number / string` | `10` |
| disabled | Disable affixing | `boolean` | `false` |
| css-mode | Use native position: sticky, subject to ancestor overflow and container boundaries | `boolean` | `false` |

### Affix Events

| Event | Arguments and timing |
| --- | --- |
| change | `(fixed: boolean, offset: number)`, emitted when the fixed state changes. While fixed, offset is the affix threshold; otherwise it is the distance to the corresponding container edge. Disabling affixing reports 0. |

### Affix Slots

| Slot | Description | Prop |
| --- | --- | --- |
| default | Content to affix | — |

### Affix Methods

| Method | Description | Arguments | Returns |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| updatePosition | Rebind scrollers and recalculate on the next animation frame | — | `Promise<void>` |

### Usage notes

Props, event arguments, slots and public methods match across platforms. CSS mode follows browser sticky rules; examples use independent scroll containers.
<!-- same-source-api:end -->

## Types

The component exports the following types

```ts
import type { AffixInstance } from '@cedar-design/ui-vue'
```

`change` only reports transitions in fixed state: repeated measurements while fixed do not repeat true, and disabling releases fixation with false and 0. Viewport units are reevaluated on measurement. CSS mode delegates valid lengths to native sticky; JS mode resolves numbers, numeric strings, px, rem, vw, vh, vmin and vmax. target controls listeners and JS measurement, while native sticky remains constrained by actual CSS ancestors. After deactivation, a pending `updatePosition()` cannot restore listeners from an older activation.


### Imports and event types

The subentry default component and the named components from the subentry and root are the same component. Props includes actual listener parameters. Events remain notifications and do not await returned Promises. Use only the documented instance methods.

```ts
import Affix, { Affix as NamedAffix } from '@cedar-design/ui-vue/affix'
import { Affix as RootAffix } from '@cedar-design/ui-vue'
import type { AffixProps, AffixInstance } from '@cedar-design/ui-vue'
import type { AffixProps as SubAffixProps } from '@cedar-design/ui-vue/affix'
const options: AffixProps = { onChange: (fixed: boolean, offset: number) => fixed && offset.toFixed() }
```


### Units and diagnostics

JS mode parses only finite numbers, decimal/scientific numeric strings, and px, rem, vw, vh, vmin or vmax, including negative offsets. Unsupported JS lengths such as em, %, calc() and var() warn in development and measure as zero instead of treating a numeric prefix as pixels. CSS mode delegates to native sticky, converting numeric strings to px and leaving other valid CSS expressions to the browser. NaN/Infinity/blank values receive Vue prop validation warnings. Invalid CSS offsets are removed and JS measurement falls back to zero. target changes listeners and JS measurement, not the actual native sticky scroll ancestor or clipping boundary.

## Appearance and states

### Appearance configuration comparison

Choose an axis to compare its available values with the same content and model. Other settings remain unchanged while comparing.

Example source: src/alert/__demos__/appearance-lab.vue

```vue
<script setup>
import { useDemoLocale } from "../../__demos__/locale";
const demoCopy = useDemoLocale("comparison");
import { reactive as __demoReactive } from "vue";

const __demoAppearance = __demoReactive({
  variant: "tonal",
  status: "default",
});

import { computed as demoComputed, ref as demoRef } from "vue";
const demoCompareFields = [
  { name: "variant", values: ["tonal", "outline", "standard"] },
  {
    name: "status",
    values: ["info", "success", "warning", "danger", "default"],
  },
];
const demoCompareAxis = demoRef("variant");
const demoComparedOptions = demoComputed(
  () =>
    demoCompareFields.find((field) => field.name === demoCompareAxis.value)
      ?.values ?? [],
);
</script>
<template>
  <c-space direction="column" :size="16">
    <c-form layout="vertical">
      <c-form-item layout="vertical" size="sm" label="variant">
        <c-radio-group
          v-model="__demoAppearance['variant']"
          aria-label="variant"
          :options="[
            { label: 'tonal', value: 'tonal' },
            { label: 'outline', value: 'outline' },
            { label: 'standard', value: 'standard' },
          ]"
          variant="button"
          size="sm"
        />
      </c-form-item>
      <c-form-item layout="vertical" size="sm" label="status">
        <c-radio-group
          v-model="__demoAppearance['status']"
          aria-label="status"
          :options="[
            { label: 'info', value: 'info' },
            { label: 'success', value: 'success' },
            { label: 'warning', value: 'warning' },
            { label: 'danger', value: 'danger' },
            { label: 'default', value: 'default' },
          ]"
          variant="button"
          size="sm"
        />
      </c-form-item>
    </c-form>
    <p class="demo-config-comparison-hint">{{ demoCopy.hint }}</p>
    <c-radio-group
      v-model="demoCompareAxis"
      :aria-label="demoCopy.configuration"
      :options="
        demoCompareFields.map((field) => ({
          label: field.name,
          value: field.name,
        }))
      "
    />
    <div class="demo-config-comparison">
      <section v-for="sample in demoComparedOptions" :key="String(sample)">
        <p>
          <code>{{ demoCompareAxis }}={{ sample }}</code>
        </p>
        <c-alert v-bind="{ ...__demoAppearance, [demoCompareAxis]: sample }"
          >This is an info alert.</c-alert
        >
      </section>
    </div>
  </c-space>
</template>

<style scoped>
.demo-config-comparison {
  display: grid;
  grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fit, minmax(min(100%, 220px), 1fr));
  gap: 20px;
  min-width: 0;
  max-width: 100%;
}
.demo-config-comparison > section {
  min-width: 0;
}
.demo-config-comparison p {
  margin: 0 0 8px;
}
</style>
```

## API

### Alert Props

| Prop | Description | Type | Default |
| --------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------- | ------------ |
| status | Alert status | `'info' \| 'success' \| 'warning' \| 'danger' \| 'default'` | `'info'` |
| variant | Visual variant | `'standard' \| 'tonal' \| 'outline'` | `'standard'` |
| color | Custom background color; overrides the background derived from type | `string` | - |
| title | Alert title | `string` | - |
| message | Content text; the default slot can also supply it | `string` | - |
| show-icon | Whether to show an icon | `boolean` | `true` |
| closable | Whether to show the close button | `boolean` | `false` |
| banner | Whether to display a top banner without borders or rounded corners | `boolean` | `false` |
| center | Whether to center the content | `boolean` | `false` |
| elevation | Elevation: `true`, `false`, or a level from `0-24` | `boolean \| number` | `false` |

### Alert Events

| Event | Description | Arguments |
| ----------- | ------------------ | ----------------------------- |
| close | Triggered when the Close button is clicked and can only be used when the Close button is displayed | `(event: MouseEvent) => void` |
| closed | Emitted after close transition | - |

### Alert Slots

| Slot | Description | Prop |
| ---------- | -------- | ---- |
| default | Content | - |
| icon | Icon | - |
| title | Title | - |
| action | Actions | - |
| close-icon | The close icon of alert | - |

```ts
import type {
```

## Usage notes

`type="default"` renders no built-in icon. Use `#icon` when an icon is needed.



The close button supports keyboard activation. close fires once; closed fires after the leave transition finishes.

### Close labels and elevation types

The close control uses the shared `common.close` locale key and updates reactively with its language scope. The `close-icon` slot replaces only the graphic. Customize `locale.common.close` through Cedar ConfigProvider, or the `'common.close'` message through Maple LocaleProvider.

`elevation` accepts only booleans or numbers. Use `:elevation="4"` for a numeric level; the string `elevation="4"` is outside the public type. Keyboard activation and clicks emit a MouseEvent; `closed` still fires after the leave transition.

## CSS Variables

See `style/token.less`; all variables use the `--c-alert-` prefix. Example override:

```css
:root {
  --c-alert-padding-vertical: 12px;
  --c-alert-padding-horizontal: 20px;
}
```

Colored titles, content, icons and outline borders use readable system content colors. standard and tonal share the same level-1 background; standard adds a subtle decorative border. Default titles use content-primary; body text and icons use content-secondary. The content variable also sets the root inherited color, used by close icons and actions without an explicit color. Maple dark mode inherits these colors while retaining its geometry overrides: 16px padding, 22px icons, 12px icon/close gaps and 1.5 body line height. color changes only the background; callers must also verify foreground contrast. The table lists :root defaults, not theme overrides.

### Scroll Lifecycle

Example source: src/anchor/__demos__/scroll-lifecycle.vue

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { ref } from "vue";
import Anchor, { AnchorLink } from "../index";

const active = ref(true);
const mounted = ref(true);
const container = ref<HTMLElement>();
const changes = ref(0);
</script>

<template>
  <div>
    <c-button html-type="button" @click="active = !active"
      >切换 KeepAlive</c-button
    >
    <c-button html-type="button" @click="mounted = !mounted"
      >卸载／挂载</c-button
    >
    <p>
      切换链接后立即停用或卸载；激活后再次点击，检查旧滚动不会恢复。change
      通知：{{ changes }}
    </p>
    <KeepAlive v-if="mounted">
      <Anchor
        v-if="active"
        :scroll-container="container"
        :change-hash="false"
        @change="changes++"
      >
        <AnchorLink href="#anchor-lifecycle-first" title="第一段" />
        <AnchorLink href="#anchor-lifecycle-second" title="第二段" />
      </Anchor>
    </KeepAlive>
    <div ref="container" style="height: 180px; overflow: auto">
      <section id="anchor-lifecycle-first" style="min-height: 240px">
        第一段内容
      </section>
      <section id="anchor-lifecycle-second" style="min-height: 240px">
        第二段内容
      </section>
    </div>
  </div>
</template>
```

## Reading direction

The axis and highlight sit at inline start; link indentation uses logical positioning. Vertical scrolling and anchor targets are unchanged.

## API

### Anchor Props

| Parameter | Description | Type | Default |
| ---------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------- | :-------: |
| boundary | Scrolling `boundary` value. After setting the value to a number, it will stop scrolling when the distance is `boundary` from the scrolling container. | `'start' \| 'end' \| 'center' \| 'nearest' \| number` | `'start'` |
| show-line | Whether to show the left axis | `boolean` | `true` |
| show-background | Whether to show the background | `boolean` | `true` |
| scroll-container | Scroll container | `string \| HTMLElement \| Window` | `-` |
| change-hash | Whether to change the hash. When set to `false`, clicking on the anchor will not change the hash of the page | `boolean` | `true` |

When scroll-container is an element, clicking an anchor scrolls each container between the target and that boundary, without scrolling ancestors outside it or the window. Targets outside the specified container are not scrolled. With Window or no container, the scroll chain extends to the window. Numeric boundary offsets apply at the outermost scroll target.

The line and background can be shown independently. Their positions are recalculated when visibility or link dimensions change.

Anchor tracks same-page hash links. Non-hash URLs keep native navigation and do not participate in automatic positioning. The root is a div; provide role="navigation" and aria-label as needed. The active link uses aria-current="location". Numeric boundary values must be finite and may be negative; invalid values warn in development and fall back to start.

### Anchor Events

| Event | Description | Arguments |
| ------ | ------------------ | ------------------------------------------------ |
| select | Emitted on link click; preHash is the active anchor before the click | hash: `string \| undefined`<br>preHash: `string` |
| change | Emitted when the active link changes | hash: `string` |

### AnchorLink Props

| Parameter | Description | Type | Default |
| ------ | ------------------ | -------- | :----: |
| title | Anchor link text | `string` | `-` |
| href | Anchor link URL | `string` | `-` |

<!-- Source: src/auto-complete/README.en-US.md; locale: en-US; page: /en/components/auto-complete/ -->

# AutoComplete

Text input with suggested completions. Suggestions accept arrays or an explicit options loader; the component manages request waiting and cancellation, while ordinary events remain notifications.

## Reading direction

The editor and suggestion popup inherit source dir, including in custom containers. Horizontal caret keys keep native editing behavior; vertical keys navigate candidates, Enter selects and Escape closes. Candidate updates preserve the native composition buffer until composition ends instead of repainting the previous model value.

## Search and visibility

Default matching searches labels and ignores case; search-fields can include values. Custom filter-option callbacks own their case policy; false bypasses local filtering for remote results. Candidate visibility is private and follows input/focus plus should-open. Public open/default-open and their events control the deferred field editor. Trigger presentation options cannot force candidate visibility.

## Basic examples

### Basic

Example source: src/auto-complete/__demos__/basic.vue

```vue
<template>
  <c-auto-complete
    v-model="value"
    :options="options"
    placeholder="输入或选择城市"
    clearable
    style="width: 100%; max-width: 320px"
  />
  <p>当前值：{{ value || '-' }}</p>
</template>

<script setup lang="ts">
import { ref } from 'vue'

const value = ref('')
const options = [
  'Beijing',
  { value: 310000, label: 'Shanghai' },
  { value: 'chengdu', label: 'Chengdu' },
  { value: 'wuhan', label: 'Wuhan', disabled: true },
]
</script>
```

### Interaction state comparison

Toggle disabled, read-only and error states, then interact with the same instance. Recovery controls remain outside the target; error appearance alone does not validate data.

<details>
<summary>Configuration details and limits</summary>

```vue
    <c-auto-complete v-model="value" edit-mode="click" :options="options" />
    <p>Committed value: {{ value || '—' }}</p>
  </div>
</template>
```

## Appearance and states

### Appearance configuration comparison

<!-- demo-config-notes:start -->

#### Configuration reference for this comparison

| Configuration | Purpose | Related examples |
| ----------- | -------------------------------------------- | ------------ |
| `options` | Suggestions, including groups; unique values become strings on selection | Appearance configuration comparison |
| `clearable` | Allow clearing a nonempty editable value | Appearance configuration comparison |

Example source: src/auto-complete/__demos__/appearance-lab.vue

```vue
<script setup>
import { useDemoLocale } from "../../__demos__/locale";
const demoCopy = useDemoLocale("comparison");
import { reactive as __demoReactive } from "vue";
import { ref } from "vue";
const value = ref("研发");
const options = [{ value: "研发" }, { value: "研发平台" }, { value: "设计" }];
const __demoAppearance = __demoReactive({ variant: "filled", size: "md" });

import { computed as demoComputed, ref as demoRef } from "vue";
const demoCompareFields = [
  { name: "variant", values: ["filled", "outline", "standard"] },
  { name: "size", values: ["xs", "sm", "md", "lg", "xl"] },
];
const demoCompareAxis = demoRef("variant");
const demoComparedOptions = demoComputed(
  () =>
    demoCompareFields.find((field) => field.name === demoCompareAxis.value)
      ?.values ?? [],
);
</script>
<template>
  <c-space direction="column" :size="16">
    <c-form layout="vertical">
      <c-form-item layout="vertical" size="sm" label="variant">
        <c-radio-group
          v-model="__demoAppearance['variant']"
          aria-label="variant"
          :options="[
            { label: 'filled', value: 'filled' },
            { label: 'outline', value: 'outline' },
            { label: 'standard', value: 'standard' },
          ]"
          variant="button"
          size="sm"
        />
      </c-form-item>
      <c-form-item layout="vertical" size="sm" label="size">
        <c-radio-group
          v-model="__demoAppearance['size']"
          aria-label="size"
          :options="[
            { label: 'xs', value: 'xs' },
            { label: 'sm', value: 'sm' },
            { label: 'md', value: 'md' },
            { label: 'lg', value: 'lg' },
            { label: 'xl', value: 'xl' },
          ]"
          variant="button"
          size="sm"
        />
      </c-form-item>
    </c-form>
    <p class="demo-config-comparison-hint">{{ demoCopy.hint }}</p>
    <c-radio-group
      v-model="demoCompareAxis"
      :aria-label="demoCopy.configuration"
      :options="
        demoCompareFields.map((field) => ({
          label: field.name,
          value: field.name,
        }))
      "
    />
    <div class="demo-config-comparison">
      <section v-for="sample in demoComparedOptions" :key="String(sample)">
        <p>
          <code>{{ demoCompareAxis }}={{ sample }}</code>
        </p>
        <c-auto-complete
          v-model="value"
          :options="options"
          clearable
          v-bind="{ ...__demoAppearance, [demoCompareAxis]: sample }"
        ></c-auto-complete>
      </section>
    </div>
  </c-space>
</template>
```

Example source: src/auto-complete/__demos__/remote.vue

```vue
<template>
  <c-auto-complete
    v-model="value"
    :options="options"
    :filter-option="false"
    placeholder="输入关键字获取远程建议"
    style="width: 100%; max-width: 320px"
    @search="handleSearch"
  />
</template>

<script setup lang="ts">
import { onBeforeUnmount, ref } from 'vue'

const value = ref('')
const options = ref<string[]>([])

let requestId = 0
onBeforeUnmount(() => requestId++)
const handleSearch = async (keyword: string) => {
  const current = ++requestId
  const result = await Promise.resolve(keyword ? Array.from({ length: 4 }, (_, index) => `${keyword}-${index + 1}`) : [])
  if (current === requestId) options.value = result
}
</script>
```

### Shared field loading

`loading` displays the shared field indicator. `loading-mode` is `default` (indicator) or `line` (an indeterminate bottom line); it defaults to `default`. Rendering belongs to FieldDecorator. Loading does not implicitly disable editing or change readonly. Set those states separately.

## Usage notes

### Editing and confirmation

Use `edit-mode` to configure editing; field > FormItem > Form precedence applies, defaulting to `direct`. Supported values: `direct / click / dblclick`. Non-direct modes open an editor through the field value. Choosing a suggestion commits immediately by default; custom text uses confirmation. With need-confirm, suggestions also remain drafts until confirmation. Cancel, reset or enabling readPretty discards an uncommitted draft.

Cedar uses edit-mode="click" / "dblclick" to open an editor popup near the field. Enter/F2 also opens it; cancel/Escape discards the draft, and confirmation commits it. readPretty is an independent reading setting, separate from readonly and disabled.

`before-commit(payload, done, context)` can guard saving the editor. FormItem validates the candidate first; invalid candidates keep the editor open. `open / default-open / update:open` control the editor. `#read="{ value, text }"` customizes read content. See the unified field presentation examples in Form.

`read-pretty` is an independent boolean alongside `readonly` and `disabled`. It inherits from field to FormItem to Form; explicit `false` overrides the parent. The default is `false`. Reading mode renders no editor.

The candidate list shares group, selected and disabled styling with Select, and AutoComplete variables follow their Select counterparts by default. In direct mode the list opens below the input and updates while scrolling; trigger-props can change placement or enable automatic flipping. The field presentation owns the deferred editor while the internal input owns suggestions; each platform retains its public edit-mode values.

### Search fields

`searchFields` / `search-fields` is a readonly `('label' | 'value')[]`, defaulting to `['label']`. Multiple fields use OR matching, case-insensitive by default. `['value', 'label']` searches codes and names; fieldNames maps semantic fields to business fields. An empty array matches no items for a nonempty query. Values are compared as strings; object traversal, object values and pinyin matching require a custom callback. A custom callback takes precedence and decides case handling itself. Remote results use the existing protocol for disabling local filtering. Cascader retains path semantics and checks the configured fields on each path node.

### Configuration

Clearing does not emit search or reopen candidates, including when focus returns from a keyboard-focused clear button to the input. The parent controls the value: each rejected clear or selection still emits a change proposal; an accepted candidate selection notifies Form once.

## API

### Empty values and reading placeholders

`empty-values` recognizes empty data; `empty-value` keeps existing clear output. `empty-text` defaults to `'-'` under `read-pretty`, with Field > FormItem > Form precedence and custom read slots first. With explicit `empty-values`, built-in required uses the policy; custom validators receive original data. See the [shared guide](llms/en-US/guide/empty-values.md).

| Prop | Type | Default and scope |
| ------------ | ------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------- |
| empty-values | readonly unknown[] | Field > FormItem > Form > component-family default; replaces the whole list |
| empty-text | string | Field > FormItem > Form > '-'; explicit '' is valid |

These props belong to field presentation; pure panels do not gain reading mode. Form and FormItem provide inherited settings. The existing empty-value type and clear fallback remain component-specific.

### AutoComplete Props

| Prop | Description | Type | Default |
| -------------------- | --------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------- |
| need-confirm | Applies only to overlay editing. Choosing a suggestion commits and closes by default; true keeps a draft until confirmation. Submission still runs form validation and before-commit; rejection keeps the editor open. AutoComplete typing does not auto-submit; a changed text draft provides a confirmation button, while choosing a suggestion completes selection immediately. | `boolean` | `false` |
| `model-value` | Controlled text | `string \| null` | `—` |
| `default-value` | Initial uncontrolled text | `string` | `''` |
| `options` | Suggestions, including groups; unique values become strings on selection | `(AutoCompleteOption \| SelectOptionGroup)[]` / `(query, { signal }) => Array / Promise` | `undefined` |
| `field-names` | Map value, label, disabled and other fields | `AutoCompleteFieldNames` | `—` |
| `should-open` | Opening policy; does not filter candidates | `(value: string) => boolean` | `value.length > 0` |
| `filter-option` | Filter by label; false for remote filtering | `AutoCompleteFilterOption` | Automatic: enabled for arrays, disabled for loader functions |
| `case-sensitive` | Case-sensitive built-in matching | `boolean` | `false` |
| `popup-container` | Popup container; same contract as Trigger | `PopupContainer` | `—` |
| `trigger-props` | Trigger configuration; cannot override owned opening and disabled state | `TriggerProps` | `—` |
| `virtual-list-props` | Enable and configure virtual scrolling | `VirtualListProps` | `—` |
| `size` | Five sizes; inherit Group / Form / global configuration when unset | `xs \| sm \| md \| lg \| xl` | `md` |
| `variant` | Input variant; inherits Group when unset | `filled \| outline \| standard` | `outline` |
| `disabled` | Disabled; inherited when unset, explicit false overrides | `boolean` | `undefined` |
| `readonly` | Readonly; focus/copy allowed, suggestions stay closed | `boolean` | `undefined` |
| `error` | Error state; inherits FormItem when unset | `boolean` | `undefined` |
| `clearable` | Allow clearing a nonempty editable value | `boolean` | `false` |
| `placeholder` | Placeholder or floating hint text | `string` | `—` |
| `hint` | Enable Input floating hint | `boolean` | `undefined` |
| `line` | Show border or underline | `boolean` | `true` |
| `text-color` | Instance text color | `string` | `—` |
| `focus-color` | Instance focus color | `string` | `—` |
| `blur-color` | Instance unfocused hint color | `string` | `—` |
| `enterkeyhint` | Virtual keyboard action hint | `InputHTMLAttributes['enterKeyHint']` | `—` |
| `aria-label` | Accessible input name | `string` | `—` |
| `max-length` | Finite nonnegative length or `{ length, errorOnly? }`; 0 is unlimited; invalid values diagnose and fall back to no limit | `number \| { length: number; errorOnly?: boolean }` | `0` |
| `show-word-limit` | Display word count | `boolean` | `false` |
| `word-length` | Custom length calculation | `(value: string) => number` | `—` |
| `word-slice` | Custom slicing | `(value: string, maxLength: number) => string` | `—` |
| `input-attrs` | Native input attributes; combobox state is owned by the component | `Record<string, unknown>` | `—` |
| edit-mode | Editing mode, inherited from FormItem and Form | `'direct' \| 'click' \| 'dblclick'` | `'direct'` |
| read-pretty | Independent read presentation; explicit false overrides the parent | `boolean` | `false` |
| empty-value | Clear output; explicit null is submitted unchanged | `string \| null \| (() => string \| null)` | `''` |
| empty-values | Empty-value recognition; field takes precedence over FormItem and Form | `readonly unknown[]` | `-` |
| empty-text | Read empty text; an explicit empty string is valid | `string` | `'-'` |
| before-commit | Guard before saving a deferred edit; return a boolean or Promise, or complete via done | `(payload: { value: unknown; previousValue: unknown }, done: (allow?: boolean) => void, context: { signal: AbortSignal; event?: Event }) => void \| boolean \| Promise<void \| boolean>` | `-` |
| open | Controlled editor visibility, separate from native input focus | `boolean` | `-` |
| default-open | Initial visibility of an uncontrolled editor | `boolean` | `false` |
| search-delay | Query debounce in milliseconds for an explicit options loader; search notifications are not delayed | number | 250 |
| search-fields | Built-in search fields, mapped through field-names | `readonly ('label' \| 'value')[]` | `['label']` |
| loading | Manual waiting feedback; does not implicitly disable text editing | boolean | false |
| loading-mode | Field waiting feedback style | default \| line | default |

### AutoComplete Events

| Event | Arguments |
| --- | --- |
| keydown | event: KeyboardEvent |
| update:modelValue | value: string \| null |
| input | value: string, event: Event |
| search | value: string, event: Event |
| change | value: string \| null, event: Event |
| select | value: string, option: AutoCompleteOptionInfo, event: Event |
| clear | event: Event |
| focus / blur | event: FocusEvent |
| dropdown-scroll / dropdown-reach-bottom | event: Event |
| load-error | error: unknown |
| update:open / open-change | open: boolean |

`keydown` notifies before the internal keyboard action; call `preventDefault()` to suppress it.
When suggestions are embedded in the editor, Escape closes the editor. When suggestions are a separate popup, Escape closes that popup first.

Typing: `input → update:modelValue → search`; selection: `update:modelValue → select → change`; clear: `clear → input → update:modelValue → change`. Selecting the same value emits only select. change is a commit on blur, Enter or selection. Input owns typing/focus/clear Form notifications; AutoComplete notifies Form once for suggestion commits. Selection applies maxLength; select.value is the committed string, while option.value retains the original suggestion. clear receives an event, not a string.

options is an explicit data loader accepting query and { signal }; it may return an array or a Promise. Failures emit load-error, and refresh retries the current query. Ordinary events such as search only notify and do not collect listener Promises. open events refer only to the deferred field editor.

### AutoComplete Slots

| Slot | Description and arguments |
| --- | --- |
| option | data: AutoCompleteOptionInfo |
| empty | Empty candidate content inside the field editor; no arguments. Cedar shows it with its native input; Maple shows it in the editor candidate area. |
| footer | Menu footer |
| prefix / suffix | Input prefix / suffix |
| clear-icon | clear(event?: Event): void |
| read | value: string \| null, text: string; preserves the raw empty model |

default does not replace the input. option customizes candidates, read customizes reading content, and empty customizes the field editor with no candidates. Ordinary direct input closes the menu when no candidates match.

### AutoComplete Methods

| Method | Arguments | Returns |
| --- | --- | --- |
| focus | - | void |
| blur | - | void |
| refresh | - | `Promise<void>` |

Arrow keys reopen the popup after Escape closes it: ArrowDown activates the first enabled candidate and ArrowUp the last, without committing the model; Enter selects. Composition, canceled keyboard events, readonly/disabled and should-open conditions are respected; Tab retains native focus navigation. Vue useId provides stable SSR identifiers. While candidates are open, aria-controls links the input to the list; the reference is removed on close. When virtualization unmounts the active item, its reference is temporarily removed and restored after remounting.

## Types

```ts
import type {
  AutoCompleteProps,
  AutoCompleteInstance,
  AutoCompleteOption,
  AutoCompleteOptionData,
  AutoCompleteOptionInfo,
  AutoCompleteFieldNames,
  AutoCompleteFilterOption,
} from "@cedar-design/ui-vue";
```

### Type imports

Root and component entries export `AutoCompleteEmits`、`AutoCompleteSlots`、`AutoCompleteExpose` alongside Props and Instance. Emits are event argument tuples derived from the runtime validators; Expose contains focus/blur.

`case-sensitive` only makes built-in local filtering `case-sensitive`: `ap` matches `Apple` when false, but not when true. It does not require choosing an option or validate the value. A custom `filterOption` takes priority; `filterOption=false` disables local filtering and makes `case-sensitive` irrelevant.

## Configuring the cleared value

`empty-value` defines the output of an existing clear action. Omission preserves the component fallback; supported types remain component-specific. It does not change empty-values recognition or Form reset defaults.

## Loading options through a function prop

Pass options(query, { signal }) directly; useAsyncData is unnecessary. options still accepts arrays, and an explicit array, including [], takes precedence. The component manages loading, stale-result isolation and cancellation. load-error reports failures, and the instance refresh() method retries. A business loader may accept only query and ignore the second argument.

AutoComplete text input always supports searching; filter-option only controls local matching and does not issue requests. Explicit options loaders disable secondary local filtering by default; arrays enable it. Business code usually does not need filter-option.

```vue
<c-auto-complete v-model="text" :options="loadSuggestions" />
```

`empty-value` accepts explicit `null` (or `() => null`). Clearing publishes `null` unchanged; omission preserves the existing default. The UI displays null as blank without converting ordinary empty-string input to null. In confirmation mode, clearing changes the draft and confirm commits it; without confirmation, clearing commits directly.

Public focus/blur methods are callable from initial mount. Focus opens an editable deferred editor and targets it after readiness; disabled, readonly, or reading fields do not open. Blur only blurs the current target without reopening. Stored methods never bind an old editor; closure, mode changes, deactivation, or unmount cancel queued calls.

Refresh can retry the component-owned asynchronous option source before the editor opens, using the existing AbortSignal, loading, and load-error protocol without opening the editor; static arrays do not create extra requests.

Follow-up acceptance testing (not yet completed): use real screen readers, such as VoiceOver and NVDA, with supported browsers to verify spoken input names, suggestion loading and navigation, selection, dismissal, and form errors.

## API

<!-- same-source-api:start -->
The default image `error` icon retains a nonempty `alt` as its accessible name; an empty `alt` denotes decoration. Provide appropriate semantics for a custom `error` slot. The default slot may switch dynamically between images and text; application code owns slotted image load events and styles.

When `trigger-icon` contains no interactive control, the avatar exposes button semantics and supports Enter and Space. Describe the action with `trigger-aria-label` or the root `aria-label`. If the slot supplies its own interactive control, that control handles keyboard input. The default click-triggered group summary can be opened by keyboard; Escape closes it and restores focus.

### Avatar Props

| Prop | Description | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| shape | Avatar shape | `circle / square` | `circle` |
| image-url | Image URL | `string` | `-` |
| alt | Image alternative text | `string` | `''` |
| size | Avatar width and height; numbers are px, strings are CSS lengths | `number / string` | `-` |
| auto-fix-font-size | Whether to shrink long text automatically | `boolean` | `true` |
| trigger-type | How the action icon is shown | `button / overlay` | `button` |
| trigger-aria-label | Accessible name of the interaction | `string` | `—` |
| trigger-icon-style | Custom style for the action icon | `CSSProperties` | `-` |
| object-fit | Image fitting mode | `fill / contain / cover / none / scale-down` | `cover` |
| color | Background color | `string` | `-` |
| bordered | Whether to show a border | `boolean` | `false` |
| border-color | Border color | `string` | `-` |
| loading | Placeholder image while loading | `string` | `-` |
| error | Fallback image URL when image loading fails | `string` | `-` |
| lazy | Whether to lazy-load the image | `boolean` | `false` |
| hoverable | Whether to scale on hover | `boolean` | `false` |

### Avatar Events

| Event | Description | Arguments |
| --- | --- | --- |
| click | Emitted when the avatar is clicked | `(event: MouseEvent) => void` |
| load | Emitted when the image loads | `() => void` |
| error | Emitted when image loading fails | `() => void` |

### Avatar Slots

| Slot | Description |
| --- | --- |
| default | Text, icon, or loading content for an image |
| error | Fallback content when image loading fails |
| trigger-icon | Action icon on the avatar |

### Avatar Methods

No custom public methods.
<!-- same-source-api:end -->

Group `shape` and `auto-fix-font-size` override item values, and a supplied group `size` takes priority. `max-count` is a nonnegative integer; zero or an invalid value means unlimited. Numeric `size` must be finite and nonnegative; invalid numbers use the default, while strings are CSS lengths. `offset` accepts finite negative numbers or CSS length strings; invalid numbers use the default spacing. The summary participates in group stacking order, which overrides z-index in `max-style`.

### AvatarGroup Props

| Prop | Description | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| shape | Child avatar shape | `circle / square` | `circle` |
| size | Child avatar width and height; numbers are px, strings are CSS lengths | `number / string` | `-` |
| auto-fix-font-size | Whether to shrink child avatar text automatically | `boolean` | `true` |
| max-count | Maximum visible avatars; `0` means unlimited | `number` | `0` |
| z-index-ascend | Use ascending stacking order | `boolean` | `false` |
| max-style | Custom summary avatar style | `CSSProperties` | `-` |
| max-popover-props | Summary Popover props | `PopoverProps` | `-` |
| offset | Overlap offset | `number / string` | `-` |
| vertical | Stack avatars vertically | `boolean` | `false` |

### AvatarGroup Slots

| Slot | Description |
| --- | --- |
| default | Avatar list |

### Reduced motion

Built-in CSS transitions follow `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`. Removing transitions does not change final visibility, selected/expanded state or event semantics. Applications control custom animations inside slots.

<!-- Source: src/back-top/README.en-US.md; locale: en-US; page: /en/components/back-top/ -->

# BackTop

Visibility RAF and JS duration/easing interpolation have separate ownership. Old listeners/canceled or consumed frames cannot replay after target replacement/deactivation/disposal. Recheck after custom easing before writing; RAF/cancel/time origin use the target owner window. Retained inactive/disposed commands are inert, activation does not resume old animation. Scoped14/full30 per copy pass using controlled queues/iframe, not native browser/OS proof. Default200ms/API remain; no CSS token added.

A native button that scrolls the page or an explicit container to the top.

## Basic examples

### Basic usage

Example source: src/back-top/__demos__/basic.vue

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { onMounted, ref } from 'vue'

const scroller = ref<HTMLElement>()
onMounted(() => {
  if (scroller.value) {
    scroller.value.scrollTop = 240
    scroller.value.dispatchEvent(new Event('scroll'))
  }
})
</script>

<template>
  <div class="back-top-demo">
    <p>在面板内滚动，超过 120px 时显示按钮。</p>
    <div class="back-top-demo__frame">
      <div ref="scroller" class="back-top-demo__scroll">
        <p v-for="row in 30" :key="row">A · 滚动内容 {{ row }}</p>
      </div>
      <c-back-top
        :target-container="() => scroller"
        :popup-container="false"
        :visible-height="120"
        :right="16"
        :bottom="16"
        aria-label="回到顶部"
      />
    </div>
  </div>
</template>

<style scoped>
.back-top-demo { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 12px; }
.back-top-demo > p { margin: 0; }
.back-top-demo__frame { position: relative; display: flex; gap: 12px; }
.back-top-demo__scroll { flex: 1; min-width: 0; height: 240px; overflow: auto; border: 1px solid #ddd; border-radius: 8px; }
.back-top-demo__scroll p { padding: 8px 12px; margin: 0; }
</style>
```

The examples use isolated local containers. Omit `target-container` to listen to the page, not the nearest scrollable ancestor. A selector that is invalid or missing hides the button; use a reactive getter for a container mounted asynchronously. `popup-container` controls where the button renders, not what scrolls.

## Lifecycle and edge cases

### Scheduling Lifecycle

<!-- demo-config-notes:start -->
#### Configuration reference for this comparison

| Configuration | Purpose | Related examples |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `target-container` | Scroll target; omitted means page | Scheduling Lifecycle |
| `popup-container` | Render target; false renders locally | Scheduling Lifecycle |
| `duration` | Animation duration in ms; 0 is immediate | Scheduling Lifecycle |
| `easing` | Built-in curve or normalized progress function | Scheduling Lifecycle |
<!-- demo-config-notes:end -->


Example source: src/back-top/__demos__/scheduler-lifecycle.vue

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { useDemoLocale as useInlineDemoLocale } from "../../__demos__/locale";
const inlineCopy = useInlineDemoLocale("backTopSchedulerLifecycleInline");

import { ref } from "vue";
import type { BackTopInstance } from "@cedar-design/ui-vue";
const first = ref<HTMLElement>();
const second = ref<HTMLElement>();
const active = ref(true);
const alternate = ref(false);
let retained: BackTopInstance | undefined;
const capture = (instance: BackTopInstance | null) => {
  if (instance) retained = instance;
};
const lower = () => {
  if (first.value) first.value.scrollTop = 300;
  if (second.value) second.value.scrollTop = 300;
};
</script>
<template>
  <div style="position: relative">
    <c-button @click="lower">{{ inlineCopy.scrollDown }}</c-button>
    <c-button @click="alternate = !alternate">{{
      inlineCopy.switchTarget
    }}</c-button>
    <c-button @click="active = !active">{{ inlineCopy.activate }}</c-button>
    <c-button @click="retained?.scrollToTop()">{{
      inlineCopy.retainedCommand
    }}</c-button>
    <p>
      Start an animation, switch or deactivate before completion. Old work must
      not resume.
    </p>
    <div ref="first" style="height: 100px; overflow: auto">
      <div style="height: 500px">Target A</div>
    </div>
    <div ref="second" style="height: 100px; overflow: auto">
      <div style="height: 500px">Target B</div>
    </div>
    <KeepAlive>
      <c-back-top
        v-if="active"
        :ref="capture"
        :target-container="() => (alternate ? second : first)"
        :popup-container="false"
        :duration="1000"
        easing="linear"
      />
    </KeepAlive>
  </div>
</template>
```

## Usage notes

### Easing and errors

duration must be finite, nonnegative milliseconds; zero scrolls immediately. Invalid durations produce Vue prop validation warnings in development and retain the immediate-completion runtime fallback. The easing presets are linear, quartOut and easeInOutCubic; invalid names warn and fall back to quartOut. A custom function receives progress from 0 to 1: finite results are clamped to 0–1, while nonfinite or nonnumeric results use the current linear progress. Promises are not awaited. Thrown errors propagate unchanged to the calling environment; that frame schedules no further animation, and scrollToTop can retry. No click success or extra error event is fabricated.

## API

### BackTop Props

| Prop | Description | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `target-container` | Scroll target; omitted means page | `string \| HTMLElement \| (() => HTMLElement \| null \| undefined)` | `—` |
| `popup-container` | Render target; false renders locally | `string \| HTMLElement \| false` | `body` |
| `visible-height` | Inclusive scroll threshold in px, numeric strings accepted | `number \| string` | `200` |
| `duration` | Animation duration in ms; 0 is immediate | `number` | `200` |
| `easing` | Built-in curve or normalized progress function | `'linear' \| 'quartOut' \| 'easeInOutCubic' \| ((progress: number) => number)` | `'quartOut'` |
| `right` | Right offset; number in px, string accepts CSS units | `number \| string` | `—` |
| `bottom` | Bottom offset; number in px, string accepts CSS units | `number \| string` | `—` |
| `elevation` | Shadow level; true uses level 2 | `boolean \| number` | `true` |
| `aria-label` | Accessible name | `string` | `'Back to top'` |

When `popup-container=false`, the button is positioned absolutely; give its containing block `position: relative`. Repeated clicks replace the previous animation; changing target, deactivation and unmount cancel queued work. Reduced-motion preference skips animation. Horizontal scroll position is preserved.

### BackTop Events / Slots / Methods

- `click(event: MouseEvent)`: emitted once per activation.
- Default slot: noninteractive text or icons. The root is already a native button; do not nest another Button or link.
- `scrollToTop()`: scrolls the current target without emitting an additional click.
- Keyboard: Tab focuses the visible button; Enter / Space activates it. Hidden buttons are not focusable.

## Types

```ts
import type { BackTopProps, BackTopInstance, BackTopTarget, BackTopEasing } from '@cedar-design/ui-vue'
```

### Imports and event types

The subentry default component and the named components from the subentry and root are the same component. Props includes actual listener parameters. Events remain notifications and do not await returned Promises. Use only the documented instance methods.

```ts
import BackTop, { BackTop as NamedBackTop } from '@cedar-design/ui-vue/back-top'
import { BackTop as RootBackTop } from '@cedar-design/ui-vue'
import type { BackTopProps, BackTopInstance } from '@cedar-design/ui-vue'
import type { BackTopProps as SubBackTopProps } from '@cedar-design/ui-vue/back-top'
const options: BackTopProps = { onClick: (event: MouseEvent) => event.preventDefault() }
```

## API

<!-- same-source-api:start -->

Numeric `content` supports finite nonnegative values. Zero appears only when `show-zero` is true; dot mode and the `content` slot follow the same rule. Strings are displayed verbatim, including `0`. Negative and non-finite numbers are hidden. `max=0` disables truncation and an invalid maximum falls back to 99. Offsets accept finite negative values; invalid offsets fall back to `0`. In floating mode positive offsets move inward from the anchored edge, while positive vertical offsets at side midpoints move downward. Inline mode ignores horizontal offset and applies vertical offset as a block margin selected by start/end. A provided default slot counts as a host even when empty. The `content` slot overrides the default badge but remains subject to `show` and numeric zero visibility.

### Badge Props

| Parameter | Description | Type | Default |
| --------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- | :---------: |
| description | Fallback description text | `string` | `-` |
| content | Badge content | `number \| string` | `-` |
| max | Maximum displayed numeric badge value. Numeric content above this value is shown as `${max}+`. | `number` | `99` |
| dot | Display a dot | `boolean` | `false` |
| offset-x | Horizontal offset; ignored in inline mode | `number` | `0` |
| offset-y | Vertical offset | `number` | `0` |
| color | Custom color; outline uses it for border and text | `string` | `-` |
| text-color | Content text color | `string` | `-` |
| mode | Layout mode | `'floating' \| 'inline'` | `floating` |
| position | Physical corner or left/right midpoint inside the host box, default top-right. Only used in floating mode; RTL does not mirror it | `'top-right' \| 'top-left' \| 'bottom-right' \| 'bottom-left' \| 'left' \| 'right'` | `top-right` |
| inline-position | Inline badge at the logical start or end of the host content, default end. Only used in inline mode | `'start' \| 'end'` | `end` |
| size | Size | `'xs' \| 'sm' \| 'md' \| 'lg' \| 'xl'` | `md` |
| status | Semantic status | `SemanticStatus`<br>`'default' \| 'primary' \| 'secondary' \| 'tertiary' \| 'info' \| 'success' \| 'warning' \| 'danger'` | `danger` |
| show | Show the badge | `boolean` | `true` |
| show-zero | Show numeric zero | `boolean` | `false` |
| variant | Appearance | `'outline' \| 'default'` | `default` |

### Badge Events

No component-specific events.

### Badge Slots

| Slot | Description | Prop |
| ------- | ---------------- | ---- |
| default | Fallback description text | - |
| content | Content displayed inside the badge | - |

### Badge Methods

No public methods.

### Usage notes

Props and slots match across platforms. Without a default slot and with an empty description, the badge renders independently inline. Omitting content displays a dot. Each library reads text direction from its own configuration and supplies its own theme colors and CSS prefix.
<!-- same-source-api:end -->

## Types

The component exports the following types

```ts
import type { BadgeInstance } from '@cedar-design/ui-vue'
```

### Color override boundaries

The bg-color fallback and danger fill use red backgrounds with white text: danger level 7 in light mode and level 4 in dark mode. Fixed neutral light gray and secondary/tertiary gray levels are intentional component colors. Override the border-color isolation ring to match the host surface. Callers must ensure contrast for custom color/text-color values.

## CSS Variables

The following CSS variables support customization with [ThemeProvider](#/en-US/theme-provider).

Filled badge text follows Button: primary, info, success, warning, danger and secondary use `content-on-dark`; tertiary uses `content-on-dark` in light mode and `content-on-bright` in dark mode. Default notification badges use red backgrounds and white text; the neutral background remains `#e0e0e0`.

Colored outline text and borders follow Button, using the matching `content-brand`, `content-info`, `content-success`, `content-warning` and `content-danger` semantic roles; secondary and tertiary outlines use `content-secondary` for readability. `variant-outline-bg-color` works for every status and defaults to transparent. The `color` prop overrides outline text and border; `text-color` overrides text further. Both preserve control through the background variable. Recheck contrast after customizing foreground or background.

```css
  --c-badge-bg-color: rgb(var(--c-danger-7));
}
```

Explicit inline styles and props that write the same CSS property take precedence over stylesheet defaults. After Teleport, ordinary CSS variables inherit from the actual mount location. When using ThemeProvider, follow its local-theme and popup configuration rules. Override the component variable directly for local styling; root-level aliases are not recalculated merely because a descendant system variable changes. Internal variables are not public APIs.

# Breadcrumb

Start with the basic example, then compare related settings before moving to controlled, asynchronous or combined use cases.

The default navigation landmark and ellipsis labels follow the current locale. Set aria-label on the root to customize the landmark name.

## Basic examples

### Basic usage

Example source: src/breadcrumb/__demos__/basic.vue

```vue
<template>
  <c-breadcrumb>
```

For routes with children, the parent remains a link and a separate button opens the menu. Selecting a child emits select(route, event) from the root; the application decides whether to navigate. Listen on individual manually composed BreadcrumbItem components for their select events.

## API

### Breadcrumb Props

| Prop | Description | Type | Default |
| --------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------- | ------ |
| max-count | Maximum ordinary breadcrumb items, excluding the overflow item; 0 means unlimited | `number` | `0` |
| routes | Route list | `BreadcrumbRoute[]` | `-` |
| separator | Separator text | `string \| number` | `/` |

### Breadcrumb Slots

| Slot | Description | Prop |
| ----------- | ---------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| default | Breadcrumb children | `-` |
| more-icon | Custom overflow icon | `omittedItems` `count` `start` `end` |
| item-render | Custom breadcrumb rendering when routes is provided | `route:BreadcrumbRoute`<br/>`routes:BreadcrumbRoute[]`<br/>`paths:string[]` |
| separator | Custom separator | `-` |

### Breadcrumb Events

| Event | Description | Arguments |
| --- | --- | --- |
| select | Emitted when a built-in dropdown child is selected in routes mode | `route: BreadcrumbRoute, event?: Event` |

The `more-icon` slot receives omitted route data only in routes mode. With manually composed default-slot items, omittedItems is empty; count, start and end still describe the omitted range.

### BreadcrumbItem Props

| Prop | Description | Type | Default |
| -------------- | ------------ | ----------------------------- | ------ |
| separator | Separator text | `string \| number` | `-` |
| href | Link URL | `string` | `-` |
| droplist | Dropdown menu content | `BreadcrumbRoute['children']` | `-` |
| dropdown-props | Menu props; open, onUpdate:open and onSelect are managed by the component | `MenuProps` | `-` |

### BreadcrumbItem Events

| Event | Description | Arguments |
| ------ | -------- | -------------- |
| click | Click event; omitted items do not emit it | `event: MouseEvent` |
| select | Fired when a built-in dropdown item is selected | `route: BreadcrumbRoute, event?: Event` |

### BreadcrumbItem Slots

| Slot | Description | Prop |
| --------- | -------------- | ---- |
| default | Item content | `-` |
| droplist | Custom dropdown menu | `-` |
| separator | Custom separator | `-` |

## Types

### BreadcrumbRoute

| Parameter | Description | Type | Default |
| -------- | ------------------------- | ------------------------------ | ------ |
| label | Breadcrumb label | `string` | `-` |
| path | Navigation path (`href` on the `a` element) | `string` |
| children | Dropdown menu items | `{label:string,path:string}[]` | `-` |

The component exports the following types

```ts
import type { BreadcrumbProps, BreadcrumbItemProps, BreadcrumbRoute } from '@cedar-design/ui-vue'
```

## Usage notes



- A nonempty `routes` array takes precedence over the default slot; an empty array falls back to the slot. Default route rendering links all items except the last, which has `aria-current="page"`. `item-render` controls links itself.
- Separator precedence: child slot → child prop → parent slot → parent prop. `0` and an empty string are supported.
- `max-count` is a nonnegative integer; 0 means unlimited. A value of 1 acts as 2 to preserve the first and current items. Positive fractions are rounded down and clamped to at least 2; negative or nonfinite values act as 0. Invalid values produce a development warning. Collapsing occurs only when the total exceeds the effective count plus 1; the overflow position does not trigger omitted items’ clicks, links or dropdowns.
- Built-in dropdown selection emits `select(route, event)`. Indices and separators update with dynamic insertion, removal, reordering and SSR.
- Custom attributes apply to the breadcrumb item content node.

## CSS Variables

<!-- component-css-variables:start -->

Use these variables to customize the component. Defaults may vary by the selector condition shown. Each variable applies to the corresponding size, variant and interaction states.

<div class="token-reference-table" style="max-width: 100%; overflow-x: auto;">

| Variable | Default / condition | Affected styles |
| --- | --- | --- |

| `--c-breadcrumb-link-text-color-hover` | `var(--c-sys-color-content-brand)` | `color` |
| `--c-breadcrumb-margin-dropdown-icon-left` | `var(--c-spacing-2)` | `margin-inline-start` |
| `--c-breadcrumb-margin-separator-horizontal` | `var(--c-spacing-2)` | `margin` |
| `--c-breadcrumb-padding-text-horizontal` | `var(--c-spacing-2)` | `margin`, `padding` |
| `--c-breadcrumb-separator-color` | `var(--c-color-text-4)` | `color` |
| `--c-breadcrumb-separator-font-size` | `inherit` | `font-size` |
| `--c-breadcrumb-separator-margin` | `0 var(--c-breadcrumb-margin-separator-horizontal)` | `margin` |
| `--c-breadcrumb-size-dropdown-icon` | `var(--c-size-3)` | `font-size` |
| `--c-breadcrumb-size-font-size` | `var(--c-font-size-body-3)` | `font-size` |
| `--c-breadcrumb-size-text-height` | `var(--c-size-6)` | `line-height` |
| `--c-breadcrumb-text-border-radius-hover` | `var(--c-border-radius-sm)` | `border-radius` |
| `--c-breadcrumb-text-color` | `var(--c-color-text-2)` | `color` |
| `--c-breadcrumb-text-color-active` | `var(--c-color-text-1)` | `color` |
| `--c-breadcrumb-touch-target-size` | `44px` | `min-height`, `min-width` |

</div>

Apply overrides to the rendered component root or the actual popup ancestor. For example, add the following class to that element and replace the value as needed:

```css
.component-theme {
  --c-breadcrumb-icon-color: var(--c-color-text-3);
}
```

Explicit inline styles and props that write the same CSS property take precedence over stylesheet defaults. After Teleport, ordinary CSS variables inherit from the actual mount location. When using ThemeProvider, follow its local-theme and popup configuration rules. Override the component variable directly for local styling; root-level aliases are not recalculated merely because a descendant system variable changes. Internal variables are not public APIs.

# Button

Both libraries use the same implementation and examples; package prefixes, themes and registration stay local.

## Basic examples

### Eight statuses

```vue
  "secondary",
  "tertiary",
  "info",
  "success",
  "warning",
  "danger",

  <c-space wrap size="12px">

    }}</c-button>
  </c-space>
```

## Appearance and states

### Four variants

<!-- demo-config-notes:start -->
#### Configuration reference for this comparison

| Configuration | Purpose | Related examples |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `variant` | Appearance; inherits from the button group when omitted, otherwise outline | Four variants, Colors, ripple and elevation |
| `size` | Size resolves from the button, then its group, then ConfigProvider, falling back to md | Four variants, Five sizes |
| `status` | Semantic color; inherits group, otherwise default | Four variants |
| `disabled` | Disabled; inherits group, explicit false overrides | Disabled buttons and links |
| `component` | Root tag; link attributes fall through | Disabled buttons and links |
| `loading` | Loading; blocks activation and navigation | Disabled buttons and links |
<!-- demo-config-notes:end -->

The `default` variant uses white text for primary, info, success, warning, danger and secondary solid fills.

Example source: src/button/__demos__/variants.vue

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { useDemoLocale as useInlineDemoLocale } from "../../__demos__/locale";
const inlineCopy = useInlineDemoLocale("buttonVariantsInline");

import { computed, ref } from "vue";

const variant = ref("default");
const size = ref("md");
const background = ref("navy");
const variants = ["default", "text", "outline", "tonal"];
const sizes = ["xs", "sm", "md", "lg", "xl"];
const statuses = [
  "default",
  "primary",
  "secondary",
  "tertiary",
  "info",
  "success",
  "warning",
  "danger",
];
const backgrounds = [
  {
    get label() {
      return inlineCopy.value.navy;
    },
    value: "navy",
    color: "#17224B",
  },
  {
    get label() {
      return inlineCopy.value.white;
    },
    value: "light",
    color: "#FFFFFF",
  },
  {
    get label() {
      return inlineCopy.value.lightGray;
    },
    value: "muted",
    color: "#F5F5F5",
  },
  {
    get label() {
      return inlineCopy.value.darkGray;
    },
    value: "dark",
    color: "#252525",
  },
];
const cardBackground = computed(
  () => backgrounds.find((item) => item.value === background.value)?.color,
);
</script>
<template>
  <c-space direction="column" block align="stretch" :size="16">
    <c-form layout="vertical" size="sm">
      <c-form-item label="Variant" field="variant">
        <c-radio-group
          v-model="variant"
          :options="variants"
          aria-label="Button variant"
          variant="button"
        />
      </c-form-item>
      <c-form-item label="Size" field="size">
        <c-radio-group
          v-model="size"
          :options="sizes"
          aria-label="Button size"
          variant="button"
        />
      </c-form-item>
      <c-form-item label="Background" field="background">
        <c-radio-group
          v-model="background"
          :options="backgrounds"
          aria-label="Button background"
          variant="button"
        />
      </c-form-item>
    </c-form>
    <c-card
      class="button-variant-card"
      :data-background="background"
      :elevation="false"
      :style="{ '--c-card-background': cardBackground }"
    >
      <c-space wrap>
        <c-button
          v-for="status in statuses"
          :key="status"
          :status="status"
          :variant="variant"
          :size="size"
          >{{ status }}</c-button
        >
      </c-space>
    </c-card>
  </c-space>
</template>
```

### Five sizes

Horizontal buttons and inputs of the same size share the default height and font size within each platform. Cedar heights are 24/28/32/36/44px; Maple heights are 32/40/48/56/64px. Horizontal button padding is 8/12/16/20/24px per side, with a 6px icon-label gap. Stacked buttons keep their separate content-based height. Component-level overrides remain independent.

Example source: src/button/__demos__/size.vue

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
const sizes = ["xs", "sm", "md", "lg", "xl"] as const;
</script>
<template>
  <c-space direction="column" :size="16">
    <c-space v-for="size in sizes" :key="size" align="center" wrap :size="12">
      <span>{{ size }}</span>
      <c-input
        :size="size"
        :aria-label="`Input ${size}`"
        placeholder="Input"
        style="width: 140px"
      />
      <c-button :size="size">Button</c-button>
      <c-button :size="size"
        ><template #icon><c-icon-search /></template>Search</c-button
      >
    </c-space>
  </c-space>
</template>
```

Cedar Button resolves size from its own prop, then its group, then ConfigProvider, falling back to md. Removing an override reveals the current provider value; provider changes update both button and loading-indicator sizing. Maple retains own/group/md sizing without a new global size provider.

## Icons and layout

### Icons and label layouts

<!-- demo-config-notes:start -->
#### Configuration reference for this comparison

| Configuration | Purpose | Related examples |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `status` | Semantic color; inherits group, otherwise default | Icons and label layouts |
| `variant` | Appearance; inherits from the button group when omitted, otherwise outline | Icons and label layouts |
| `size` | Size resolves from the button, then its group, then ConfigProvider, falling back to md | Icons and label layouts |

Use built-in icons to compare icon-only, inline and stacked labels across four variants and five sizes. Stacked buttons grow with content and keep at least 8px of top and bottom padding. Omit the default slot for icon-only buttons; round controls shape and stacked controls label layout.

Example source: src/button/__demos__/icons.vue

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { useDemoLocale as useInlineDemoLocale } from "../../__demos__/locale";
const inlineCopy = useInlineDemoLocale("buttonIconsInline");

import { ref } from "vue";

const sizes = ["xs", "sm", "md", "lg", "xl"] as const;
const variants = ["default", "text", "outline", "tonal"] as const;
const layouts = ["icon", "inline", "stacked"] as const;
const size = ref<(typeof sizes)[number]>("md");
const variant = ref<(typeof variants)[number]>("tonal");
const items = [
  { status: "default", icon: "plus", label: "Add" },
  { status: "primary", icon: "reply", label: "Reply" },
  { status: "info", icon: "info-circle", label: "Info" },
  { status: "success", icon: "check", label: "Confirm" },
  { status: "warning", icon: "delete", label: "Delete" },
  { status: "danger", icon: "close", label: "Close" },
] as const;
</script>
<template>
  <c-space direction="column" :size="16">
    <c-form layout="vertical" size="sm">
      <c-form-item label="Variant" field="variant">
        <c-radio-group
          v-model="variant"
          :options="variants"
          aria-label="Icon button variant"
          variant="button"
        />
      </c-form-item>
      <c-form-item label="Size" field="size">
        <c-radio-group
          v-model="size"
          :options="sizes"
          aria-label="Icon button size"
          variant="button"
        />
      </c-form-item>
    </c-form>
    <c-space
      v-for="layout in layouts"
      :key="layout"
      direction="column"
      :size="8"
    >
      <span>{{
        layout === "icon"
          ? inlineCopy.iconOnly
          : layout === "inline"
            ? inlineCopy.iconAndText
            : inlineCopy.stacked
      }}</span>
      <c-space wrap>
        <c-button
          v-for="item in items"
          :key="item.label"
          :status="item.status"
          :variant="variant"
          :size="size"
          :stacked="layout === 'stacked'"
          :round="layout === 'icon'"
          :aria-label="item.label"
        >
          <template #icon>
            <c-icon-plus v-if="item.icon === 'plus'" />
            <c-icon-reply v-else-if="item.icon === 'reply'" />
            <c-icon-info-circle v-else-if="item.icon === 'info-circle'" />
            <c-icon-check v-else-if="item.icon === 'check'" />
            <c-icon-delete v-else-if="item.icon === 'delete'" />
            <c-icon-close v-else-if="item.icon === 'close'" />
          </template>
          <template v-if="layout !== 'icon'" #default>{{
            item.label
          }}</template>
        </c-button>
      </c-space>
    </c-space>
  </c-space>
</template>
```

## Loading and action feedback

### Loading layouts and animations

<!-- demo-config-notes:start -->
#### Configuration reference for this comparison

| Configuration | Purpose | Related examples |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `loading` | Loading; blocks activation and navigation | Loading layouts and animations, Loading Appearance |
| `loading-size` | Indicator size; xs/sm/md/lg/xl map to 12/14/16/18/20px; numbers are px; follows button size when omitted; not used in line mode | Loading layouts and animations, Loading Appearance |
