```vue
      <c-button @click="reverse = !reverse">调整选项顺序</c-button>
    </c-space>
    <p>当前值：{{ JSON.stringify(value) }}</p>
    <p>方法返回值：{{ JSON.stringify(proposal) }}</p>
  </section>
</template>

<style scoped>

.group-methods-demo p { margin: 0; }
</style>
```

## Async options

### Async Options

Preview configuration: `edit-mode="direct"`, `:options="options"`, `:max="2"`.

Example source: src/checkbox/__demos__/async-options.vue

```vue
<script setup>
import { useDemoLocale as useInlineDemoLocale } from "../../__demos__/locale";
const inlineCopy = useInlineDemoLocale("checkboxAsyncOptionsInline");

import { onDeactivated, onUnmounted, ref, shallowRef } from "vue";

const value = ref(["remote"]);
const options = ref([]);
const loading = ref(false);
let pendingTimer;
const manual = ref(false);
const waiting = shallowRef([]);
const applied = ref(0);
const ignored = ref(0);
const changeCount = ref(0);
let version = 0;
let sequence = 0;

function cancelPending() {
  version++;
  if (pendingTimer !== undefined) {
    clearTimeout(pendingTimer);
  }
  pendingTimer = undefined;
  loading.value = false;
}

function load() {
  cancelPending();
  loading.value = true;
  const ticket = version;
  const id = ++sequence;
  const complete = () => {
    if (ticket !== version) {
      ignored.value++;
      return;
    }
    applied.value = id;
    options.value = [
      { label: "异步设备", value: "remote" },
      { label: "设备 A", value: "a" },
      { label: "设备 B", value: "b" },
      { label: "停用设备", value: "locked", disabled: true },
    ];
    pendingTimer = undefined;
    loading.value = false;
  };
  if (manual.value) {
    new Promise((resolve) => {
      waiting.value = [...waiting.value, { id, resolve }];
    }).then(complete);
  } else {
    pendingTimer = setTimeout(complete, 800);
  }
}

function settle(latest) {
  const jobs = [...waiting.value];
  const job = latest ? jobs.pop() : jobs.shift();
  waiting.value = jobs;
  job?.resolve();
}

function cleanup() {
  cancelPending();
  const jobs = waiting.value;
  waiting.value = [];
  jobs.forEach((job) => job.resolve());
}

function remove() {
  cancelPending();
  options.value = [];
}

onDeactivated(cleanup);
onUnmounted(cleanup);
</script>

<template>
  <c-space class="checkbox-async-demo" direction="column">
    <p>业务值独立于当前选项，加载或移除选项不会清空已选值：{{ value }}</p>
    <c-checkbox v-model="manual" edit-mode="direct" @change="remove">{{
      inlineCopy.manualResponses
    }}</c-checkbox>
    <c-space wrap>
      <c-button size="sm" @click="load">加载选项</c-button>
      <c-button size="sm" @click="remove">移除选项</c-button>
      <c-button
        size="sm"
        :disabled="waiting.length === 0"
        @click="settle(false)"
        >返回最早加载</c-button
      >
      <c-button size="sm" :disabled="waiting.length === 0" @click="settle(true)"
        >返回最新加载</c-button
      >
    </c-space>
    <p aria-live="polite">
      {{
        loading
          ? "加载中，可在完成前移除选项以取消本次加载。"
          : "加载完成后保留当前选值和键盘焦点。"
      }}
    </p>
    <c-checkbox-group
      v-model="value"
      edit-mode="direct"
      :options="options"
      :max="2"
      @change="changeCount++"
    />
    <p>用户变更次数：{{ changeCount }}</p>
    <p role="status">
      Applied: {{ applied }} · Ignored: {{ ignored }} · Pending:
      {{ waiting.length }}
    </p>
  </c-space>
</template>
```

## Native input attributes and keyboard cancellation

Native `id`, `form`, `required`, constraints, aria/data attributes and keyboard listeners belong to the actual input. Class/`style` and other shell attributes remain on the label. Generated native IDs are stable and unique, and an external label can target an explicit `id`. HTML `required` participates in native browser `form` validation, separately from Form business rules.

Once / Capture / Passive native listener modifiers stay on the input rather than firing from interactive slot children. Native preventDefault can veto Enter / Space activation and RadioGroup arrow navigation; canceled Space leaves no delayed release action. Checked, disabled, input type and group Tab navigation remain component-managed.

The nullable Checkbox model is preserved. checked in default / checkbox slots is always boolean, with null shown as false; rendering alone never proposes a new model.

## Usage notes

### Editing and confirmation

This component supports `edit-mode` with field > FormItem > Form precedence. When unset, it defaults to `direct` and preserves `direct` editing. Supported values: `direct / click / dblclick`. Non-direct modes open the editor through the field value trigger and keep one draft; v-model updates only after confirmation. Cancel, reset or enabling readPretty discards the draft.

Cedar uses edit-mode="click" / "dblclick" to open an editor popup near the field. Enter/F2 also opens it; cancel/Escape discards the draft, and confirmation commits it. readPretty is an independent reading setting, separate from readonly and disabled.

`before-commit(payload, done, context)` can guard saving the editor. FormItem validates the candidate first; invalid candidates keep the editor open. `open / default-open / update:open` control the editor. `#read="{ value, text }"` customizes read content. See the unified field presentation examples in Form.

`read-pretty` is an independent boolean alongside `readonly` and `disabled`. It inherits from field to FormItem to Form; explicit `false` overrides the parent. The default is `false`. Reading mode renders no editor.

`empty-value` accepts explicit `null` (or `() => null`). Clearing publishes `null` unchanged; omitted values preserve the existing default. Editors render `null` as blank without converting ordinary empty-string input to `null`. In popup editing, clearing changes the draft; confirm commits it and cancel preserves the original model.

The `options` prop accepts an array or `(query, { signal }) => array/Promise`. The component manages loading, cancellation and stale-result isolation; failures emit load-error. Single/multiple groups initialize with an empty-string query, searchable fields reload when the query changes, and root loading for tree fields remains independent of existing load-more child loading.

Public focus/blur methods are callable from initial mount. Focus opens an editable deferred editor and targets it after readiness; disabled, readonly, or reading fields do not open. Blur only blurs the current target without reopening. Stored methods never bind an old editor; closure, mode changes, deactivation, or unmount cancel queued calls.

CheckboxGroup checkAll/inverseAll change values only through an active editor. When a deferred editor is closed, deactivated, or unmounted, calls return an independent array copy of the current business value without opening the editor or publishing model changes.

## API

### Parameters, presentation clearing and mount-time boundaries

orientation accepts horizontal / vertical and falls back to horizontal after invalid-value diagnostics. max belongs to CheckboxGroup: valid values are finite nonnegative integers, zero forbids new choices, and omission is unlimited. Existing external values are never truncated. Invalid JavaScript callers retain the existing normalization after diagnostics: negatives become zero, fractions are floored, NaN is unlimited, and Infinity remains unlimited.

icon-size accepts positive lengths. Numbers and numeric strings use px, including positive fractions such as 0.5. Invalid, nonpositive or nonfinite values diagnose and fall back to the theme; the Divider minimum of 1 does not apply. Business styles determine the final resolved value of CSS expressions.

uninject-group-context decides group participation at mount. Changing it later does not reinject; change the key or remount. An isolated control still participates in Form. clearable / empty-value apply only to explicit presentation-layer clearing; native unchecking still proposes false or removes the array value and never uses empty-value. Ordinary event Promises do not participate in waiting; before-commit uses payload / done / context only when saving a deferred edit.

During an explicit options request both group roots announce aria-busy and emit one load-error on failure. No loading prop or extra graphic is added, and loading/failure never proposes a new model.

### Empty values and reading placeholders

`empty-values` recognizes empty data; `empty-value` keeps existing clear output. `empty-text` defaults to `'-'` under `read-pretty`, with Field > FormItem > Form precedence and custom read slots first. With explicit `empty-values`, built-in required uses the policy; custom validators receive original data. See the [shared guide](llms/en-US/guide/empty-values.md).

| Prop | Type | Default and scope |
| ------------ | ------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------- |
| empty-values | readonly unknown[] | Field > FormItem > Form > component-family default; replaces the whole list |
| empty-text | string | Field > FormItem > Form > '-'; explicit '' is valid |

These props belong to field presentation; pure panels do not gain reading mode. Form and FormItem provide inherited settings. The existing empty-value type and clear fallback remain component-specific.

`ChoiceValue = string | number | boolean`；`CheckboxModel = boolean | ChoiceValue[] | null`；`RadioModel = ChoiceValue | null`。

## Types

| ------------- | -------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- |

The component exports the following types

```ts
import type { CheckboxProps } from "@cedar-design/ui-vue";
```

### ChoiceFieldNames

`{ label?: string; value?: string; disabled?: string; readonly?: string; indeterminate?: string }`

Public types: `CheckboxOption`, `ChoiceFieldNames`, `CheckboxSlots` and `CheckboxGroupSlots`, consistently exported from root and subentries.

Public method type：`CheckboxGroupMethods`；`CheckboxGroupInstance` includes these methods.

### Reduced motion

Built-in CSS transitions follow `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`. Removing transitions does not change final visibility, selected/expanded state or event semantics. Applications control custom animations inside slots.

Explicit inline styles and props that write the same CSS property take precedence over stylesheet defaults. After Teleport, ordinary CSS variables inherit from the actual mount location. When using ThemeProvider, follow its local-theme and popup configuration rules. Override the component variable directly for local styling; root-level aliases are not recalculated merely because a descendant system variable changes. Internal variables are not public APIs.

<!-- component-css-variables:end -->

# Col

24-column Flex layout. Row manages gutters and alignment; Col manages spans, offsets, ordering and breakpoints. Use Grid for CSS Grid collapse and suffix items.

> **Choosing a layout**
>
> - Grid + GridItem: Use for form columns and card grids with consistent column widths, spans, responsive column counts, or collapsed rows and suffix items.
> - Row + Col: Use for 24-column Flex layouts that need horizontal/vertical alignment, wrapping control, fixed and flexible widths together, or responsive ordering. Row controls the row; Col controls width, offset and order.
> - Space: Use for simple groups of buttons, tags or text that only need spacing, direction and alignment. Use native Flex for more flexible width allocation.

## Basic examples

### Span and offset

Example source: src/col/__demos__/basic.vue

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { ref } from 'vue'
const span = ref(8)
const offset = ref(4)
</script>
<template><div>
  <div class="controls">Span<c-radio-group v-model="span"><c-radio v-for="value in [4, 8, 12]" :key="value" :value="value">{{ value }}</c-radio></c-radio-group></div>
  <div class="controls">Offset<c-radio-group v-model="offset"><c-radio v-for="value in [0, 4, 8]" :key="value" :value="value">{{ value }}</c-radio></c-radio-group></div>
  <c-row :gutter="12"><c-col :span="span" :offset="offset"><div class="cell">{{ span }} / +{{ offset }}</div></c-col><c-col :span="4"><div class="cell soft">4</div></c-col></c-row>
</div></template>

<style scoped>
.controls { display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; align-items: center; gap: 12px; }
.cell { box-sizing: border-box; padding: 12px; min-width: 0; border-radius: 4px; background: var(--c-color-primary); color: var(--c-color-white); text-align: center; overflow-wrap: anywhere; }
.soft { opacity: .7; }
</style>
```

## API

<!-- same-source-api:start -->
### Col Props

| Prop | Description | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| span | Column span; integer 0–24, with zero hiding the column | `number` | `24` |
| offset | Offset from the logical inline start; integer 0–24, with zero restoring it | `number` | `undefined` |
| order | Visual order; finite integer, including negative values; zero restores it | `number` | `undefined` |
| xs | Responsive span or object containing span, offset and order | `number / ColSizeDescriptor` | `undefined` |
| sm | Responsive span or object containing span, offset and order | `number / ColSizeDescriptor` | `undefined` |
| md | Responsive span or object containing span, offset and order | `number / ColSizeDescriptor` | `undefined` |
| lg | Responsive span or object containing span, offset and order | `number / ColSizeDescriptor` | `undefined` |
| xl | Responsive span or object containing span, offset and order | `number / ColSizeDescriptor` | `undefined` |
| xxl | Responsive span or object containing span, offset and order | `number / ColSizeDescriptor` | `undefined` |
| flex | Ratio, fixed length or CSS flex value | `number / string` | `undefined` |

### Col Events

| Event | Description |
| --- | --- |
| click | Native MouseEvent, emitted once per click |

### Col Slots

| Slot | Description |
| --- | --- |
| default | Layout content |

### Col Methods

| Method | Description |
| --- | --- |
<!-- same-source-api:end -->

The order example restores every column to `order: 0` when reverse is turned off. Responsive breakpoints use the browser viewport rather than the demo card width; widening the card alone does not activate a breakpoint. `span: 0` hides a column, and a matching larger breakpoint can restore it.

## Responsiveness and accessibility

Row resolves responsive gutter with JavaScript matchMedia, using xs for SSR and synchronizing the viewport after mounting. Col uses CSS media queries: SSR already emits all configured classes without waiting for measurement. Breakpoints use viewport width: xs is the base; sm ≥576, md ≥768, lg ≥992, xl ≥1200 and xxl ≥1600px. Only configured fields override earlier values. Offset starts at the logical inline edge and mirrors in RTL. Order affects visual positioning while preserving DOM, keyboard and assistive technology reading order.

Span, offset and their breakpoint fields accept integers from 0 through 24. A zero span hides the column; offset 24 shifts it by a full row width. Order accepts finite integers, including negative values and values above 24, subject to browser CSS order computation. Gutter accepts finite nonnegative numbers, six-breakpoint objects or exactly two entries [horizontal, vertical]. Development diagnostics report unknown breakpoints, invalid numbers and enum values. Invalid span falls back to 24; invalid offset/order is ignored; breakpoint objects retain valid fields; invalid gutter components fall back to zero.

## Imports

Grid contains only Grid.Item. Import the independent Row and Col components from the library root or their row/col subpaths; installing Grid does not register them. 

`flex` overrides column width while preserving `offset`, `order` and responsive configuration. `span: 0`, including breakpoint values, still hides the column; a matching nonzero span restores visibility while `flex` controls width. Removing `flex` restores the span width. Visual ordering does not change DOM or keyboard navigation `order`.

This component declares no independent public CSS variables. Use the configuration and layout APIs documented on this page.

Internal custom properties and measurement values are implementation details and are not customization APIs.

```vue
      <c-button @click="toggleAll({ expand: true, skipDisabled: true })">Expand all (skip disabled)</c-button>
      <c-button @click="toggleAll({ expand: false })">Collapse all</c-button>
      <c-button @click="toggleAll({ expand: false, skipDisabled: true })">Collapse all (skip disabled)</c-button>
    </c-space>
    <c-collapse ref="collapseRef" v-model="activeNames">
      <c-collapse-item title="Panel 1" name="1">
        <div>Content 1</div>
      </c-collapse-item>
      <c-collapse-item title="Panel 2" name="2">
        <div>Content 2</div>
      </c-collapse-item>
      <c-collapse-item title="Panel 3" name="3" disabled>
        <div>Content 3</div>
      </c-collapse-item>
      <c-collapse-item title="Panel 4" name="4" disabled>
        <div>Content 4</div>
      </c-collapse-item>
    </c-collapse>
  </c-space>
</template>
<script lang="ts" setup>
import { ref } from 'vue'

const collapseRef = ref<{
  toggleAll: (options: { expand: boolean | 'inverse'; skipDisabled?: boolean }) => void
}>()
const activeNames = ref<(string | number)[]>(['2', '4'])

const toggleAll = (options: { expand: boolean | 'inverse'; skipDisabled?: boolean }) => {
  collapseRef.value?.toggleAll(options)
}
</script>
```

## Reading direction

Inherits the nearest `dir="ltr|rtl"`, including runtime changes and local overrides. Header and expanded content inherit reading direction; changing direction preserves expansion. expand-icon-position left/right remain physical sides. Custom expansion graphics are not mirrored automatically.

## API

The main value uses ordinary `v-model`: `modelValue` is an array of expanded panel names, including in accordion mode. `defaultValue` initializes uncontrolled state only on creation; later changes do not reset it. Initialization does not emit `update:modelValue`. When `modelValue` is provided, the parent controls the state and its value is authoritative.

<!-- same-source-api:start -->

### Collapse Props

| Prop | Description | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| model-value | Expanded names; v-model | `(string \| number)[]` | `—` |
| default-value | Uncontrolled initial expanded names | `(string \| number)[]` | `[]` |
| accordion | Accordion mode; at most one open panel | `boolean` | `false` |
| show-expand-icon | Whether to show expansion icons; child items decide when omitted | `boolean` | `—` |
| expand-icon-position | Expand-icon position within the header: left or right, default left. Does not control content expansion direction | `'left' \| 'right'` | `'left'` |
| bordered | Whether to show border | `boolean` | `true` |
| divider | Show dividers | `boolean` | `true` |
| offset | Gap between expanded panels | `boolean` | `false` |
| destroy-on-hide | Destroy content when hidden | `boolean` | `false` |

Panel content is mounted eagerly by default. When either the parent or an item enables `destroy-on-hide`, closed content is destroyed after the closing transition; reopening during the transition preserves it. Changing this setting while closed takes effect immediately. An explicit parent `show-expand-icon` overrides the item setting.

### Collapse Events

| Event | Description | Arguments |
| --- | --- | --- |
| update:model-value | Request an expanded-name update | `(string \| number)[]` |
| change | Emitted when expanded panels change | `(string \| number)[]`, `Event` |

### Collapse Slots

| Slot | Description | Scope |
| --- | --- | --- |
| default | Panel list | `—` |

### Collapse Methods

| Method | Description |
| --- | --- |
| toggleAll | Expand or collapse all panels (no-op in accordion) |

<!-- same-source-api:end -->

The parent `expand-icon` slot is forwarded to items that do not provide their own icon. Scope: `expanded`, `disabled`, `position`. It is not rendered on the root node.

### CollapseItem Props

| Parameter | Description | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| name **(required)** | Unique panel identifier corresponding to a value in `modelValue` | `string \| number` | `—` |
| title | Panel title | `string` | `—` |
| heading-level | Heading level from 1 to 6, chosen for the page; omitted by default | `1–6` | `—` |
| region | Whether content is a region landmark | `boolean` | `true` |
| disabled | Whether disabled | `boolean` | `false` |
| show-expand-icon | Whether to show an expansion icon | `boolean` | `true` |
| destroy-on-hide | Destroy content when hidden | `boolean` | `false` |

Choose `heading-level` for the page structure; set `:region="false"` when many panels would create excessive region landmarks. `extra` sits outside the header button and can contain independent actions; avoid interactive controls in title and expand-icon slots. A right-side expand icon sits inside the header button, followed by `extra`.

### CollapseItem Slots

| extra | Extra content | `—` |

# Color Picker

Start with the basic example, then compare related settings before moving to controlled, asynchronous or combined use cases.

FormItem errors describe the inline panel or built-in trigger while preserving any existing `aria-describedby`. A custom trigger can bind the default slot’s `describedBy` value to its interactive element’s `aria-describedby`. Put the label’s `for` target ID on the interactive element itself. In custom-trigger mode, a ColorPicker `id` belongs to the popup; if supplied, use a different value to avoid duplicate IDs when it opens.

```vue
<ColorPicker :hide-trigger="false">
  <template #default="{ describedBy }">
    <button type="button" :aria-describedby="describedBy">Choose color</button>
  </template>
</ColorPicker>
```

During server rendering, the custom trigger slot does not yet support `v-for` and `v-memo` on the same node. Remove that node’s `v-memo` when SSR is required.

When a FormItem label has no explicit `for`, the inline panel is named as a group by that label, while the built-in trigger combines it with its localized action. A supplied `id` belongs to the built-in button; its name also combines the label and action when the label’s `for` matches that ID. Explicit `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` takes precedence. Give each field an explicit name when a FormItem contains multiple fields.

## Content and presentation

### Colors

<!-- demo-config-notes:start -->
#### Configuration reference for this comparison

| Configuration | Purpose | Related examples |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `default-value` | Default | Colors |
| `history-colors` | History colors | Colors |
| `show-history` | Show history colors | Colors |
| `show-preset` | Show preset colors | Colors |
<!-- demo-config-notes:end -->


- `default-value`: Default value (uncontrolled state)
- `history-colors`: Color array of historical colors
- `show-history`: Show history colors

History and presets accept HEX, HEX with alpha, RGB and RGBA. Selecting one updates both color and opacity; invalid entries leave the current color unchanged. Percentage RGB channels are converted and clamped to their valid ranges.

Use parenthesized RGB / RGBA functions with comma- or space-separated channels. Incomplete input and extra text are invalid. An invalid initial model falls back to opaque red.

`default-value` initializes the picker once. The parent owns a controlled `model-value`: selection proposes an update, and a rejected proposal restores the controlled color. External model synchronization does not emit `change`.
- `show-preset`: Show preset colors

Example source: src/color-picker/__demos__/colors.vue

```vue
<template>
  <c-color-picker
    defaultValue="#00BEBE"
    :historyColors="history"
    showHistory
    showPreset
    @open-change="addHistory" />
</template>

<script lang="ts" setup>
import { ref } from 'vue'

const history = ref(['#00BEBE'])
const addHistory = (visible, color) => {
  if (!visible) {
    const index = history.value.indexOf(color)
    if (index !== -1) {
      history.value.splice(index, 1)
    }
    history.value.unshift(color)
  }
}
</script>
```

When disabled, the palette and sliders leave the Tab order, and the inputs and format selector cannot be operated. Hue and opacity sliders support arrow keys and Home / End; color channels have localized accessible names.

`format` controls the output color format and initializes the panel's input mode. The panel selector changes the input mode independently. Later `format` changes affect output without resetting that mode or emitting change by themselves.

### Forwarded configuration precedence

Nested triggerProps fields such as disabled can override the corresponding popup settings supplied by ColorPicker. To disable the entire component, check both top-level props and nested configuration.

Drag listeners belong to the control's own view. KeepAlive deactivation or unmount ends the current gesture and releases listeners. Reactivation requires a new gesture; callbacks from the old gesture cannot change values.

# Color

Start with the basic example, then compare related settings before moving to controlled, asynchronous or combined use cases.

When disabled or readonly is omitted, Color inherits the corresponding FormItem and Form state. Explicit false overrides that inherited state. Disabled and readonly controls cannot open the color panel or change the color.

The default trigger is a native button and supports Tab, Enter and Space. A supplied `id` belongs to that button and can be targeted by a FormItem label’s `for`. When the label has no explicit `for`, or its `for` matches the button `id`, the button name combines the label with the localized “Choose color” action. A supplied `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` takes precedence; without a FormItem label the localized action is used. Custom trigger slots must provide their own accessible name and keyboard interaction.

## Basic examples

### Basic usage

- `show-text`: Show color value

Example source: src/color/__demos__/basic.vue

```vue
<template>
  <c-color v-model="value" show-text />
</template>

<script setup>
```

## API

### Empty values and reading placeholders

`empty-values` recognizes empty data; `empty-value` keeps existing clear output. `empty-text` defaults to `'-'` under `read-pretty`, with Field > FormItem > Form precedence and custom read slots first. With explicit `empty-values`, built-in required uses the policy; custom validators receive original data. See the [shared guide](llms/en-US/guide/empty-values.md).

| Prop | Type | Default and scope |
| ------------ | ------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------- |
| empty-values | readonly unknown[] | Field > FormItem > Form > component-family default; replaces the whole list |
| empty-text | string | Field > FormItem > Form > '-'; explicit '' is valid |

These props belong to field presentation; pure panels do not gain reading mode. Form and FormItem provide inherited settings. The existing empty-value type and clear fallback remain component-specific.

### Color Props

| Prop | Description | Type | Default |
| -------------------- | ------------------ | ---------------------------- | ------- |
| `model-value` | Bound value | `string` | `-` |
| `default-value` | Initial uncontrolled value | `string` | `undefined` |
| `format` | Color format | `hex \| rgb` | `-` |
| `size` | Size | `xs \| sm \| md \| lg \| xl` | `md` |
| `show-text` | Show color value | `boolean` | `false` |
| `show-history` | Show history colors | `boolean` | `false` |
| `show-preset` | Show preset colors | `boolean` | `false` |
| `disabled` | Disabled; inherits Form when omitted | `boolean` | `undefined` |
| `readonly` | Readonly; inherits Form when omitted | `boolean` | `undefined` |
| `disabled-alpha` | Disable alpha | `boolean` | `false` |
| `history-colors` | History colors | `string[]` | `undefined` |
| `preset-colors` | Preset colors | `string[]` | `undefined` |
| `empty-value` | Clear value or factory | `string \| null \| (() => string \| null)` | `undefined` |
| `color-picker-props` | Forwarded to ColorPicker | `Partial<ColorPickerProps>` | `{}` |

### Color Events

| Event | Description | Arguments |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `update:modelValue` | Update the field value | `(value)` |
| `change` | Notify a color change | `(value: string)` |
| `update:open` / `open-change` | Update or notify the field editor open state | `(open: boolean)` |

### Color Slots

| Slot | Description | Prop |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `default` | Custom color picker trigger | — |
| `read` | Custom reading content | `{ value, text }` |

### Editing and confirmation

This component supports `edit-mode` with field > FormItem > Form precedence. When unset, it defaults to `direct` and preserves `direct` editing. Supported values: `direct / click / dblclick`. Non-direct modes open the editor through the field value trigger and keep one draft; v-model updates only after confirmation. Cancel, reset or enabling readPretty discards the draft.

Cedar uses edit-mode="click" / "dblclick" to open an editor popup near the field. Enter/F2 also opens it; cancel/Escape discards the draft, and confirmation commits it. readPretty is an independent reading setting, separate from readonly and disabled.

`before-commit(value, { previousValue, signal })` can reject an overlay save. FormItem validates the candidate first and keeps the editor open on failure. `open / default-open / update:open` control the editor. Use `#read="{ value, text }"` to customize display. See the full field comparison in Form.

`read-pretty` is an independent boolean alongside `readonly` and `disabled`. It inherits from field to FormItem to Form; explicit `false` overrides the parent. The default is `false`. Reading mode renders no editor.

Drag listeners belong to the control's own view. KeepAlive deactivation or unmount ends the current gesture and releases listeners. Reactivation requires a new gesture; callbacks from the old gesture cannot change values.

Internal custom properties and measurement values are implementation details and are not customization APIs.

# Config Provider

Provide language, size, direction and shared content to descendants. Configuration is subtree-scoped by default. Maple separates language and styles through LocaleProvider and ThemeProvider, without a ConfigProvider component.

## Basic examples

### Basic usage

- `size`: ComponentSize

Example source: src/config-provider/__demos__/basic.vue

```vue
<template>
  <c-space direction="column">
    <c-button @click="large = !large">切换尺寸</c-button>
    <c-config-provider :size="large ? 'lg' : 'sm'">
      <c-space>
        <c-input placeholder="继承全局尺寸" />
        <c-button>继承尺寸</c-button>
      </c-space>
    </c-config-provider>
    <p role="status">当前尺寸：{{ large ? 'lg' : 'sm' }}</p>
  </c-space>
</template>
<script lang="ts" setup>
import { ref } from 'vue'
const large = ref(false)
</script>
```

## Shared content

### Empty states and loading indicators

Supported descendants consume empty/loading slots; the provider does not render them itself. The empty inner provider below inherits shared content, with local content or icon slots taking precedence. The empty component scope is a consumer-supplied identifier and need not equal a public component name.

Example source: src/config-provider/__demos__/content-overrides.en-US.vue

```vue
<template>
  <c-config-provider>
    <template #empty="{ component }"><p>No content ({{ component }})</p></template>
    <template #loading><span>◌</span></template>
    <c-config-provider>
      <c-space direction="column">
        <c-empty />
        <c-loading tip="Preparing content" />
      </c-space>
    </c-config-provider>
  </c-config-provider>
</template>
```

Use [ThemeProvider](llms/en-US/components/theme-provider.md) for themes. ConfigProvider handles locale, size, direction and shared content.

## API

### ConfigProvider Props

| Prop | Description | Type | Default |
| ---- | ---- | ---- | ---- |
| prefix-cls | Inherit the parent when omitted, with c at the root; custom prefixes require matching built styles | `string` | — |
| locale | Complete language pack; inherit the parent when omitted, or the global locale when the entire chain is unspecified | `CedarLang` | — |
| size | Default descendant size; inherit the parent when omitted, with component size taking precedence | `ComponentSize` (`xs` / `sm` / `md` / `lg` / `xl`) | — |
| global | Choose application-level injection during setup; static and intended for an application-lifetime root configuration | `boolean` | `false` |
| update-at-scroll | Inherit the parent when omitted, with false at the root; only supported popup consumers use this preference | `boolean` | — |
| scroll-to-close | Inherit the parent when omitted, with false at the root; does not actively close all popups | `boolean` | — |
| dir | Reading direction; inherits the source scope when omitted. Physical left/right placements keep their meaning. | `ReadingDirection` (`ltr` / `rtl`) | — |

### ConfigProvider Events

No declared events or public business instance methods. Native listeners fall through to the direction-carrying div; this is not a declared click event and listener Promises are not collected.

### ConfigProvider Slots

| Slot | Description | Prop |
| ------- | ---- | ---- |
| default | Subtree content | — |
| empty | Empty content for descendants supporting this configuration | `{ component: string }` |
| loading | Shared indicator consumed by Loading; a local icon takes precedence | — |

Nested providers inherit omitted prefix-cls, locale, size, update-at-scroll and scroll-to-close from the nearest parent; explicit false overrides remain effective. dir inherits through the reading-direction scope. locale remains a complete pack rather than a deep merge of partial packs. Size, language and scroll preferences update reactively. Keep prefix-cls fixed at initialization; changing a prefix requires matching styles and remounting the subtree.

empty/loading inherit independently and support dynamic additions, removals and fallback. The default subtree belongs only to its provider and never inherits parent content. Select, Cascader and TreeSelect read current empty content during rendering and retain complete node arrays; local empty slots win. Only an explicit theme claims document ownership; empty nested providers add no theme owner.

global chooses injection scope only during setup and cannot switch dynamically; other fields remain reactive while mounted. global=true installs application-level configuration without automatic restoration on Provider unmount or retroactive switching of consumers that already injected. Use it for application-lifetime roots; local or conditional content should keep global=false. Multiple global providers have no automatic reclamation priority.

## Types

The component exports the following types

```ts
import type { ConfigProviderProps, ConfigProviderInstance, ConfigProviderSlots } from '@cedar-design/ui-vue'
```

Component subpath entries also export these types and configProviderProps. The internal injection context is not a public configuration method.


## Reading direction

Use `<c-config-provider dir="rtl">` to scope right-to-left layout. Omit `dir` to inherit, or nest `dir="ltr"` for a local override. Native DOM `dir` containers work too. The provider renders a `display: contents` div to carry direction to ordinary descendants without adding a layout box; place it in an HTML context that permits a div. It does not change the document direction. The former boolean `rtl` option is replaced by `dir` before release. Physical left/right placements retain their meaning.

Internal custom properties and measurement values are implementation details and are not customization APIs.

## Numeric and animation boundaries

### Scientific notation and decimal floor

Precision is an integer from -292 to 292. Fractional and nonfinite precision falls back to 0; out-of-range integers are clamped. Unsupported inputs produce a development prop warning. String precision keeps the existing parseFloat conversion. Negative precision rounds at tens/hundreds and larger decimal places. The result is a number rounded toward negative infinity, without trailing-zero padding, and may use scientific notation. Changing precision only reformats the current value. IEEE-754 representability still applies; animation values are not decimal accounting values.

Example source: src/count-to/__demos__/decimal-floor.vue

```vue
<template>
  <c-space direction="column">
    <p>{{ inlineCopy.smallValue1234e7 }}</p>
    <c-count-to
      class="scientific-small"
      :from="-1.234e-7"
      :to="-1.234e-7"
      :precision="precision"
      :auto-start="false"
    />
    <c-button @click="precision = precision === 9 ? 8 : 9">{{
      inlineCopy.togglePrecision
    }}</c-button>
    <p role="status">
      Precision: {{ precision }} {{ inlineCopy.changesFormattingWithoutReplay }}
    </p>
    <p>{{ inlineCopy.largeValuePrecision23 }}</p>
    <c-count-to
      class="scientific-large"
      :from="-1.234e24"
      :to="-1.234e24"
      :precision="-23"
      :auto-start="false"
    />
    <p>{{ inlineCopy.floorTowardNegativeInfinity }}</p>
    <c-count-to
      class="negative-floor"
      :from="-12.351"
      :to="-12.351"
      :precision="2"
      :auto-start="false"
    />
  </c-space>
</template>
<script setup lang="ts">
import { useDemoLocale as useInlineDemoLocale } from "../../__demos__/locale";
const inlineCopy = useInlineDemoLocale("countToDecimalFloorInline");

import { ref } from "vue";
const precision = ref(9);
</script>
```

### Zero duration and replay

Example source: src/count-to/__demos__/zero-duration.vue

```vue
<template>
  <c-space direction="column">
    <c-count-to
      ref="counter"
      :from="0"
      :to="100"
      :duration="duration"
      @end="ends++"
    />
    <c-space>
      <c-button @click="duration = duration === 0 ? 600 : 0">{{
        inlineCopy.toggleDuration
      }}</c-button>
      <c-button @click="counter?.reset()">{{ inlineCopy.replay }}</c-button>
    </c-space>
    <p role="status">
      Duration: {{ duration }}ms; end: {{ ends }}. 0
      时长在下一帧完成，不占用持续动画帧。
    </p>
  </c-space>
</template>
<script setup lang="ts">
import { useDemoLocale as useInlineDemoLocale } from "../../__demos__/locale";
const inlineCopy = useInlineDemoLocale("countToZeroDurationInline");

import { ref } from "vue";
import type { CountToInstance } from "@cedar-design/ui-vue";
const counter = ref<CountToInstance>();
const duration = ref(0);
const ends = ref(0);
</script>
```

### Change easing and replay

Changing timing-function affects the next reset, including resets caused by from, to or duration changes. It does not restart the current animation. Pause/start resumes the existing curve; reset creates a fresh playback using the latest function. Clearing the function restores linear easing. A curve may reach the target early, but end still reports completion of the configured duration.

Example source: src/count-to/__demos__/easing-replay.vue

```vue
<template>
  <c-space direction="column">
    <c-count-to
      ref="counter"
      :to="100"
      :duration="1200"
      :timing-function="curve"
    />
    <c-space>
      <c-button @click="cubic = !cubic">{{ inlineCopy.changeCurve }}</c-button>
      <c-button @click="replay">{{ inlineCopy.replay }}</c-button>
    </c-space>
    <p role="status">
      Next: {{ cubic ? "ease-out cubic" : "linear" }}; current: {{ applied }}.
    </p>
    <p>{{ inlineCopy.changingTheCurveAppliesOn }}</p>
  </c-space>
</template>
<script setup lang="ts">
import { useDemoLocale as useInlineDemoLocale } from "../../__demos__/locale";
const inlineCopy = useInlineDemoLocale("countToEasingReplayInline");

import { computed, ref } from "vue";
import type { CountToInstance } from "@cedar-design/ui-vue";
const counter = ref<CountToInstance>();
const cubic = ref(false);
const applied = ref("linear");
const linear = (value: number) => value;
const easeOutCubic = (value: number) => 1 - Math.pow(1 - value, 3);
const curve = computed(() => (cubic.value ? easeOutCubic : linear));
function replay() {
  applied.value = cubic.value ? "ease-out cubic" : "linear";
  counter.value?.reset();
}
</script>
```

## Animation duration boundaries

Duration is a finite nonnegative number of milliseconds. Zero reaches the target on the next frame. Negative, NaN and infinite values produce development prop diagnostics and safely behave as zero without continuing to request animation frames. Pausing or unmounting before that frame cancels completion. String durations retain parseFloat conversion. reset reads auto-start again. end remains a notification; its listener Promise is not awaited.

## API

String `from`, `to`, `duration`, and `precision` values use parseFloat, so `10px` parses as 10. Invalid or non-finite endpoints produce a warning and use 0. If the difference between finite endpoints overflows, the animation completes on the next frame. `precision` floors the numeric result toward negative infinity without padding zeros and accepts integers in the range [-292, 292]. `auto-start` is read on mount or reset; calling start after completion does not replay until reset.

### CountTo Props

| Prop | Description | Type | Default |
| ----------------- | ------------------------ | ------------------------ | -------- |
| from | Start value | _number \| string_ | `0` |
| to | Target value | _number \| string_ | `0` |
| duration | Animation duration in milliseconds | _number \| string_ | `2000` |
| precision | Decimal precision | _number \| string_ | `0` |
| auto-start | Whether to start animation automatically | _boolean_ | `true` |
| timing-function | Animation easing function | _(v: number) => number_ | `-` |

### CountTo Events

| Event | Description | Callback arguments |
| ------ | -------------- | -------- |
| end | Triggered when animation ends | `-` |

### CountTo Slots

| Slot | Description | Prop |
| ------- | ---------- | ----------------- |
| default | Custom content | `value: number` |

### CountTo Methods

| Method | Description | Arguments | Returns |
| ------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------- | ---- | ------ |
| start | Start the animation | `-` | `-` |
| pause | Pause the animation | `-` | `-` |
| reset | Reset the animation; when `auto-start` is `true`, playback starts automatically after reset | `-` | `-` |


| `auto-start` | Whether to auto start count down | Manual |
| `format` | Display format | Manual |
<!-- demo-config-notes:end -->


- `format`: Controls the displayed format.

Example source: src/countdown/__demos__/manual.vue

```vue
<template>
  <c-space direction="column" align="flex-start">
    <c-countdown
      ref="countdownRef"
      :time="5000"
      :auto-start="false"
      format="ss.SSS"
      @end="handleEnd"
    />
    <c-space>
      <c-button status="primary" @click="countdownRef?.start()">开始</c-button>
      <c-button @click="countdownRef?.pause()">暂停</c-button>
      <c-button @click="countdownRef?.reset()">重置</c-button>
    </c-space>
  </c-space>
</template>

<script lang="ts" setup>
import { ref } from 'vue'
import { Message } from '@cedar-design/ui-vue'
import type { CountdownInstance } from '../index'

const countdownRef = ref<CountdownInstance>()

const handleEnd = () => {
  Message.info('end!')
}
</script>
```

## API

`time` is a duration rather than an absolute deadline; the remaining duration freezes while paused or deactivated by KeepAlive. The default slot receives the five fields days, hours, minutes, seconds, and milliseconds directly. `change` fires on reset and animation frames and may be frequent. `auto-start` is read on mount or reset; changing it alone does not start or pause. Repeated format tokens are all replaced. Omitted larger units accumulate into smaller units, so `SSS` alone can exceed three digits.

Pause and deactivation synchronize the displayed and slot values with the frozen remaining time without emitting another `change`. If the deadline has passed before the next frame, pausing displays zero and resuming emits `end` once.

### Countdown Props

| Prop | Description | Type | Default |
| ------------- | ------------------------------------------ | -------------------- | ------------ |
| `time` | Countdown duration in milliseconds | `number \| string` | `0` |
| `format` | Display format | `string` | `'HH:mm:ss'` |
| `auto-start` | Whether to auto start count down | `boolean` | `true` |

### format placeholders

| Format | Description |
| ----- | ------------- |
| `DD` | Day |
| `HH` | Hour |
| `mm` | Minute |
| `ss` | Seconds |
| `S` | Milliseconds: 1 digit |
| `SS` | Milliseconds: 2 digits |
| `SSS` | Milliseconds: 3 digits |

### Countdown Events

| Event | Description | Arguments |
| -------- | ---------------- | --------------------- |
| `change` | Emitted after countdown changed | `timeData: TimeData` |
| `end` | Emitted after countdown ended | `-` |

### Countdown Slots

| Slot | Description | Prop |
| --------- | ---------- | --------------------- |
| `default` | Custom content | `timeData: TimeData` |

### Countdown Methods

| Method | Description | Arguments | Returns |
| ------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------- | ---- | ------ |
| `start` | Start countdown | `-` | `-` |
| `pause` | Pause countdown | `-` | `-` |
| `reset` | Reset the countdown; when `auto-start` is `true`, it starts automatically after reset | `-` | `-` |

## Types

### TimeData

| Name | Description | Type |
| -------------- | -------- | -------- |
| `days` | Remain days | `number` |
| `hours` | Remain hours | `number` |
| `minutes` | Remain minutes | `number` |
| `seconds` | Remaining seconds | `number` |
| `milliseconds` | Remain milliseconds | `number` |

The component exports the following types

```ts
import type { CountdownProps, CountdownInstance, TimeData } from '@cedar-design/ui-vue'
```

## Usage notes



SSR renders the initial formatted time. Changing format while paused updates the display. The finish event fires once per round; reset starts another round. Unmounting cleans up animation frames.

### Disabled Parts

- `disabled-date`: Unselectable date
- `show-time`: Whether to increase time selection
- `disabled-time`: Unselectable time

Example source: src/date/picker/__demos__/disabled-parts.vue

```vue
<template>
  <c-date-picker style="margin: 0 24px 24px 0"
    :disabled-date="(current: any) => dayjs(current).isBefore(dayjs())"
  />
  <c-date-picker style="margin-right: 24px; margin-bottom: 24px"
    show-time
    :disabled-date="(current: any) => dayjs(current).isBefore(dayjs())"
    :disabled-time="getDisabledTime"
  />
</template>

<script lang="ts">
import { defineComponent } from 'vue'
import dayjs from 'dayjs'

export default defineComponent({
  setup() {
    function range(start: any, end: any) {
      const result = []
      for (let i = start; i < end; i++) {
        result.push(i)
      }
      return result
    }

    function getDisabledTime(date: any) {
      return {
        disabledHours: () => range(6, 24),
        disabledMinutes: () => range(30, 60),
        disabledSeconds: () => range(30, 60),
      }
    }
    return {
      dayjs,
      getDisabledTime,
    }
  },
})
</script>
```

## Reading direction

Inherits the nearest `dir="ltr|rtl"`, including runtime changes and local overrides. Calendar dates, months and years follow reading order; navigation icons mirror, while date values keep their meaning. In paged grids, Left/Right moves focus visually, Up/Down moves one row, and Home/End moves to the row boundary, skipping disabled items. Focus navigation does not select; Enter/Space keeps the existing selection behavior. Navigation is bounded by the displayed grid. Explicit `shortcuts-position="left|right"` remains physical; `bottom` stays below. Field popovers inherit their source direction.

## API

### DatePicker Props

Pure panels do not accept field/popup props such as open/default-open, popup-container, placement, trigger-props, placeholder, variant or clearable. Configure popups through Date/DateRange popup-props, and typing through input-editable. disable-confirm alone controls confirmation tools; 

| Prop | Description | Type | Default behavior |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `abbreviation` | Use abbreviated month-grid names; false uses full month names | `boolean` | `true` |
| `day-start-of-week` | First day of week for calendars, an integer from 0 to 6 | `DateWeekStart` | `0` |
| `default-picker-value` | Initial calendar viewport, read once; selected values take precedence over the current date | `DateSelection` | `undefined` |
| `default-value` | Initial uncontrolled value, read only at creation | `DateValue` | `undefined` |
| `disable-confirm` | Commit on selection; false retains draft for confirmation | `boolean` | `true` |
| `disabled` | Disable panel selection and commit | `boolean` | `false` |
| `disabled-date` | Return true to disable the date; side is start/end | `(date: Date, side: DateSide) => boolean`<br>`DateSide: 'end' \| 'start'` | `undefined` |
| `disabled-time` | Return disabled hour/minute/second lists for a date and endpoint | `(date: Date, side: DateSide) => DateDisabledTime`<br>`DateSide: 'end' \| 'start'` | `undefined` |
| `empty-value` | Clear output or synchronous factory, independent of emptyValues recognition | `DateValue \| null \| (() => DateValue \| null \| undefined)` | `undefined` |
| `format` | Display/text-input format; a function only formats without reverse text parsing | `string \| ((date: Date) => string)` | From precision/time settings |
| `max` | Inclusive maximum; a supplied invalid boundary is not silently ignored | `DateValue` | `undefined` |
| `min` | Inclusive minimum; a supplied invalid boundary is not silently ignored | `DateValue` | `undefined` |
| `model-value` | External date value; undefined is uncontrolled, null is explicitly empty | `DateValue \| null` | `undefined` |
| `picker-value` | Controlled calendar viewport, separate from selection; range viewports contain two dates | `DateSelection` | `undefined` |
| `preview-shortcut` | Preview shortcuts on hover/focus without committing | `boolean` | `true` |
| `readonly` | Readonly panel without candidate changes or commits | `boolean` | `false` |
| `shortcuts` | Shortcuts with values or on-demand synchronous value factories, optional format/disabled | `DateShortcut[]` | `[]` |
| `shortcuts-position` | Shortcut position | `left \| bottom \| right` | `bottom` |
| `show-current` | Highlight the current date without changing selection or model | `boolean` | `true` |
| `show-now-button` | Show the now action according to the actual panel range capabilities | `boolean` | `true` |
| `show-time` | Enable time precision/selection, with visible precision controlled by format | `boolean` | `false` |
| `time-picker-props` | Presentation options for the Cedar embedded time panel, excluding date model/rules | `DateTimePickerOptions` | `{}` |
| `time-zone` | IANA time zone; an invalid zone does not fall back to a valid selectable value | `string` | System local time zone |
| `type` | Date precision; Cedar includes week/quarter, while Maple supports date/month/year | `date \| month \| year \| week \| quarter` | `date` |
| `value-format` | Serialized model format: Date, timestamp or format tokens, independent of display format | `string` | From precision/time settings |

Desktop calendar capabilities, including shortcuts, footer and cell slots, remain in a separate presentation implementation.

### Shared date-family contract

| Prop | Description | Type | Default |
| ----------------- | ------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------ | ------- |
| `default-value` | Uncontrolled initial value, read once | DateValue / DateValue[] | — |
| `value-format` | Model and event value format: a date format string, Date, or timestamp | string | Follows type |
| `min` | Inclusive minimum date; string bounds use value-format | DateValue | — |
| `max` | Inclusive maximum date; string bounds use value-format | DateValue | — |
| `disabled-time` | Disabled times for the current date and endpoint | (date: Date, side: DateSide) => DateDisabledTime<br>`DateSide: 'end' \| 'start'` | — |
| `disable-confirm` | Commit immediately | boolean | true |

`DateValue = Date | string | number`. Clearing a single value produces undefined; clearing a range produces [].
The date argument of `disabledDate(date, side)` and `disabledTime(date, side)` is always a Date; side is start/end.
Time callbacks return numeric lists from `disabledHours()`, `disabledMinutes(hour)` and `disabledSeconds(hour, minute)`.
Invalid dates and incomplete/reversed ranges cannot be committed. Confirmation revalidates dynamic disabling rules. Locked range endpoints cannot be cleared or changed.
Nested panel props configure presentation only; they must not override top-level model-value, format, bounds, disabling rules or control events.

### DatePicker Events

| Event | Arguments |
| --- | --- |
| `update:modelValue` | `DatePickerEmits['update:modelValue']` |
| `change` | `DatePickerEmits['change']` |
| `select` | `DatePickerEmits['select']` |
| `confirm` | `DatePickerEmits['confirm']` |
| `update:pickerValue` | `DatePickerEmits['update:pickerValue']` |
| `picker-value-change` | `DatePickerEmits['picker-value-change']` |
| `select-shortcut` | `DatePickerEmits['select-shortcut']` |

Set `:disable-confirm="false"` to show confirmation tools. The `actions` slot provides `{ confirm, disabled }`; custom `actions` must still call confirm to validate.

### Complete standalone-panel contract

Complete properties, events, slots and instance boundaries match the standalone-panel sections in the main field documentation.

[Complete API](llms/en-US/components/date.md)

### Action scope

```ts
{ confirm: () => void; disabled: boolean; selectNow: () => void; nowDisabled: boolean }
```

# DateRange

A date range field. The bound model is an array; use DateRangePicker for a standalone panel.

## String range models

Set format="MM-DD" and value-format="MM-DD" to get ['09-10', '10-10'] directly. These values have no year; parsing uses the current year and cannot preserve cross-year ordering. For real bookings store YYYY-MM-DD and map the payload in application code. format only changes display, while value-format changes the model and events.

Without time-zone the browser-local time zone remains in effect. An explicit IANA time zone changes the civil-time interpretation of strings; Date/timestamp values preserve their instant. Editing one endpoint does not change an untouched endpoint's repeated-hour occurrence or milliseconds.

## Basic examples

### Basic

Example source: src/date-range/__demos__/basic.vue

```vue
</template>

const range = ref()
</script>
```

Toggle disabled, read-only and error states, then interact with the same instance. Recovery controls remain outside the target; error appearance alone does not validate data.

```vue
<script setup>
import { useDemoLocale } from "../../__demos__/locale";
const demoCopy = useDemoLocale("comparison");
import { reactive as __demoReactive } from "vue";
import { ref } from "vue";
const value = ref(["2026-10-23", "2026-10-25"]);
const __demoAppearance = __demoReactive({ variant: "filled", size: "md" });

import { computed as demoComputed, ref as demoRef } from "vue";
const demoCompareFields = [
  { name: "variant", values: ["filled", "outline", "standard"] },
  { name: "size", values: ["xs", "sm", "md", "lg", "xl"] },
];
const demoCompareAxis = demoRef("variant");
const demoComparedOptions = demoComputed(
  () =>
    demoCompareFields.find((field) => field.name === demoCompareAxis.value)
      ?.values ?? [],
);
</script>
<template>
  <c-space direction="column" :size="16">
    <c-form layout="vertical">
      <c-form-item layout="vertical" size="sm" label="variant">
        <c-radio-group
          v-model="__demoAppearance['variant']"
          aria-label="variant"
          :options="[
            { label: 'filled', value: 'filled' },
            { label: 'outline', value: 'outline' },
            { label: 'standard', value: 'standard' },
          ]"
          variant="button"
          size="sm"
        />
      </c-form-item>
      <c-form-item layout="vertical" size="sm" label="size">
        <c-radio-group
          v-model="__demoAppearance['size']"
          aria-label="size"
          :options="[
            { label: 'xs', value: 'xs' },
            { label: 'sm', value: 'sm' },
            { label: 'md', value: 'md' },
            { label: 'lg', value: 'lg' },
            { label: 'xl', value: 'xl' },
          ]"
          variant="button"
          size="sm"
        />
      </c-form-item>
    </c-form>
    <p class="demo-config-comparison-hint">{{ demoCopy.hint }}</p>
    <c-radio-group
      v-model="demoCompareAxis"
      :aria-label="demoCopy.configuration"
      :options="
        demoCompareFields.map((field) => ({
          label: field.name,
          value: field.name,
        }))
      "
    />
    <div class="demo-config-comparison">
      <section v-for="sample in demoComparedOptions" :key="String(sample)">
        <p>
          <code>{{ demoCompareAxis }}={{ sample }}</code>
        </p>
        <c-date-range
          v-model="value"
          value-format="YYYY-MM-DD"
          v-bind="{ ...__demoAppearance, [demoCompareAxis]: sample }"
        ></c-date-range>
      </section>
    </div>
  </c-space>
</template>
```

### Rejected Close

Example source: src/date-range/__demos__/rejected-close.vue

```vue
<script setup>
import { ref } from "vue";

const value = ref(["2026-09-22", "2026-09-24"]);
const open = ref(false);
const closeRequests = ref(0);
const commits = ref(0);

function requestOpen(next) {
  if (next) open.value = true;
  else closeRequests.value++;
}
</script>

<template>
  <c-space direction="column" size="12px">
    <p>
      关闭请求会被父级拒绝；修改起止日期后可再次确认，重复确认不应重复提交。
    </p>
    <c-date-range
      v-model="value"
      :open="open"
      @update:open="requestOpen"
      @change="commits++"
    >
      <template #actions="{ confirm, disabled }">
        <c-button :disabled="disabled" @click="confirm()">确认</c-button>
        <c-button @click="open = false">允许关闭</c-button>
      </template>
    </c-date-range>
    <span data-test="date-range-transaction-state"
      >值：{{ value.join(" ~ ") }}；提交：{{ commits }}；拒绝关闭：{{
        closeRequests
      }}</span
    >
  </c-space>
</template>
```

### Field Panel Tools

Example source: src/date-range/__demos__/field-panel-tools.vue

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { ref } from "vue";
import type { DateShortcut } from "@cedar-design/ui-vue";

const selected = ref(["2025-01-15", "2025-01-20"]);
const viewport = ref(["2025-01-01", "2025-02-01"]);
const acceptNavigation = ref(true);
const notice = ref("");
const shortcutNotice = ref("");
const shortcuts: DateShortcut[] = [
  { label: "下个月", value: ["2025-02-15", "2025-02-20"] },
  { label: "不可选", value: ["2025-03-01", "2025-03-05"], disabled: true },
];
function navigate(value: unknown) {
  if (
    acceptNavigation.value &&
    Array.isArray(value) &&
    value.length === 2 &&
    value.every((part) => typeof part === "string")
  )
    viewport.value = value;
}
function observe(_value: unknown, _dates: unknown, texts: unknown) {
  notice.value = String(texts);
}
function choose(shortcut: DateShortcut) {
  shortcutNotice.value = String(shortcut.label);
}
</script>

<template>
  <c-checkbox v-model="acceptNavigation"> 接受视口请求</c-checkbox>
  <c-date-range
    v-model="selected"
    :input-editable="false"
    format="DD/MM/YYYY"
    :date-range-picker-props="{ pickerValue: viewport, shortcuts }"
    @update:picker-value="navigate"
    @picker-value-change="observe"
    @select-shortcut="choose"
  />
  <p>选择模型：{{ selected }}；受控视口：{{ viewport }}</p>
  <p>视口通知：{{ notice }}；快捷项通知：{{ shortcutNotice }}</p>
  <p>
    导航不改变选择模型；拒绝视口请求后，日历仍显示原月份。快捷项先选择草稿，确认后提交。
  </p>
</template>
```

### Shared field loading

`loading` displays the shared field indicator. `loading-mode` is `default` (indicator) or `line` (an indeterminate bottom line); it defaults to `default`. Rendering belongs to FieldDecorator. Loading does not implicitly disable editing or change readonly. Set those states separately.

## Reading direction

Range values remain `[start, end]`; changing reading direction does not swap endpoints or commit drafts. Calendar range connections and boundary radii follow reading direction. In paged grids, Left/Right moves focus visually and Up/Down preserves date-row order. Maple endpoint editing and continuous range highlighting use different rendering paths. Explicit `shortcuts-position="left|right"` remains physical; popovers inherit the field's source direction.

## API

### Empty values and reading placeholders

`empty-values` recognizes empty data; `empty-value` keeps existing clear output. `empty-text` defaults to `'-'` under `read-pretty`, with Field > FormItem > Form precedence and custom read slots first. With explicit `empty-values`, built-in required uses the policy; custom validators receive original data. See the [shared guide](llms/en-US/guide/empty-values.md).

| Prop | Type | Default and scope |
| ------------ | ------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------- |
| empty-values | readonly unknown[] | Field > FormItem > Form > component-family default; replaces the whole list |
| empty-text | string | Field > FormItem > Form > '-'; explicit '' is valid |

These props belong to field presentation; pure panels do not gain reading mode. Form and FormItem provide inherited settings. The existing empty-value type and clear fallback remain component-specific.

### DateRange Props

`input-attrs` applies to the two direct input elements. For example, `:input-attrs="[{ 'aria-label': 'Departure' }, { 'aria-label': 'Return' }]"` names each endpoint. The field owns its value, disabled, readonly, placeholder, role and popup state; shared descriptions, per-input descriptions and form errors are merged for each input. Component errors take precedence; otherwise each input retains its `aria-invalid`. `RangeInputAttributes` is exported from the component and root entries and includes native attributes and `Once` event types.

When FormItem's `label-attrs.for` explicitly targets one input, unnamed range endpoints use the form label together with localized start/end names. Explicit accessible names supplied through `input-attrs` or the field take precedence. Older custom locales can provide `fieldPresentation.rangeStart` and `fieldPresentation.rangeEnd`; when absent, the existing date or time start/end labels are used.

| Prop | Description | Type | Default behavior |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `before-commit` | Explicit field-save guard using payload, done and context | `BeforeFieldCommit` | `undefined` |
| `blur-color` | Color while unfocused | `string` | Theme default |
| `clearable` | Allow clearing with disabled, readonly and pending guards | `boolean` | `true` |
| `date-range-picker-props` | Range-panel presentation options, with model/rules/type owned by the field | `DateRangePickerOptions` | `{}` |
| `default-open` | Initial uncontrolled opening, read only at creation | `boolean` | `false` |
| `default-value` | Initial uncontrolled value, read only at creation | `(DateValue \| undefined)[]` | `undefined` |
| `disable-confirm` | Commit on selection; false retains draft for confirmation | `boolean` | `false` |
| `disabled` | Disable all or lock start/end separately; fields inherit FormItem/Form when unset | `boolean \| boolean[]` | Inherited, finally false |
| `disabled-date` | Return true to disable the date; side is start/end | `(date: Date, side: DateSide) => boolean`<br>`DateSide: 'end' \| 'start'` | `undefined` |
| `disabled-time` | Return disabled hour/minute/second lists for a date and endpoint | `(date: Date, side: DateSide) => DateDisabledTime`<br>`DateSide: 'end' \| 'start'` | `undefined` |
| `edit-mode` | Field editing mode, inherited from FormItem/Form when unset | `FieldEditMode`<br>`'direct' \| 'click' \| 'dblclick'` | Inherited, finally direct |
| `empty-text` | Empty text in read-pretty mode | `string` | Inherited, finally '-' |
| `empty-value` | Clear output or synchronous factory, independent of emptyValues recognition | `(DateValue \| undefined)[] \| null \| (() => (DateValue \| undefined)[] \| null \| undefined)` | `undefined` |
| `empty-values` | Empty-value recognition list, replaced rather than merged | `readonly unknown[]` | Inherited/family default |
| `error` | Field error presentation, inherited when unset | `boolean` | Inherited, finally false |
| `focus-color` | Color while focused | `string` | Theme default |

| `hint` | Floating placeholder hint, suppressed by an outer Form label | `boolean` | `false` |

| `line` | Show the field border or underline | `boolean` | `true` |
| `loading` | Manual loading feedback, independent of event return values | `boolean` | `false` |
| `loading-mode` | Field loading presentation mode | `default \| line` | default |
| `max` | Inclusive maximum; a supplied invalid boundary is not silently ignored | `DateValue` | `undefined` |
| `min` | Inclusive minimum; a supplied invalid boundary is not silently ignored | `DateValue` | `undefined` |
| `model-value` | External date value; undefined is uncontrolled, null is explicitly empty | `(DateValue \| undefined)[] \| null` | `undefined` |
| `open` | Controlled field editor opening | `boolean` | `undefined` |
| `open-trigger-target` | Open by field or icon click, without restricting keyboard opening | `field \| icon` | field |
| `placeholder` | A range string applies to both endpoints, arrays configure each; omitted follows Locale | `string \| string[]` | `undefined` |
| `popup-container` | Editor container; false renders in place | `PopupContainer` | Shared container default |

| `readonly` | Readonly; fields allow focus/copy without value changes or opening editing | `boolean` | Inherited, finally false |
| `separator` | Separator text for joined/range display, including an empty string | `string` | ` ~ ` |
| `show-time` | Enable time precision/selection, with visible precision controlled by format | `boolean` | `false` |

| `text-color` | Content text color | `string` | Theme default |

| `type` | Date precision; Cedar includes week/quarter, while Maple supports date/month/year | `date \| month \| year \| week \| quarter` | `date` |

| `variant` | Field appearance | `filled \| outline \| standard` | `outline` |

### Shared date-family contract

| Prop | Description | Type | Default |
| ----------------- | ------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------- | ------- |
| `default-value` | Uncontrolled initial value, read once | DateValue / DateValue[] | — |
| `value-format` | Model and event value format: a date format string, Date, or timestamp | string | Follows type |
| `min` | Inclusive minimum date; string bounds use value-format | DateValue | — |
| `max` | Inclusive maximum date; string bounds use value-format | DateValue | — |
| `disabled-time` | Disabled times for the current date and endpoint | (date: Date, side: DateSide) => DateDisabledTime<br>`DateSide: 'end' \| 'start'` | — |
| `disable-confirm` | Commit immediately | boolean | false |
| `default-open` | Uncontrolled initial open state | boolean | false |
| `popup-props` | Trigger presentation options; cannot override owned visibility or date rules | object | {} |
| `popup-container` | Portal target; the top-level value wins, including false for inline rendering | string / HTMLElement / (() => HTMLElement) / false | — |

`DateValue = Date | string | number`. Clearing a single value produces undefined; clearing a range produces [].
The date argument of `disabledDate(date, side)` and `disabledTime(date, side)` is always a Date; side is start/end.

`disabled-date` restricts range endpoints. A range may cross disabled interior values; it is not scanned item by item or truncated automatically. This applies to dates, months and years. Interior disabled values remain gray. Changing pages preserves the selected start and clears hover preview; reverse selection is sorted chronologically.
Time callbacks return numeric lists from `disabledHours()`, `disabledMinutes(hour)` and `disabledSeconds(hour, minute)`.
Invalid dates and incomplete/reversed ranges cannot be committed. Confirmation revalidates dynamic disabling rules. Locked range endpoints cannot be cleared or changed.
Nested panel props configure presentation only; they must not override top-level model-value, format, bounds, disabling rules or control events.

### DateRange Events

See the complete field and panel event lists on this page.

Desktop supports keyboard editing. The default panel edits a draft before confirmation; disable-confirm commits directly. Escape or closing discards the draft. focus(index = 0) focuses a start/end input, and blur() closes the popup.

## Configuring the cleared value

`empty-value` defines the output of an existing clear action. Omission preserves the component fallback; supported types remain component-specific. It does not change empty-values recognition or Form reset defaults.

`empty-value` accepts explicit `null` (or `() => null`). Clearing publishes `null` unchanged; omitted values preserve the existing default. Editors render `null` as blank without converting ordinary empty-string input to `null`. In popup editing, clearing changes the draft; confirm commits it and cancel preserves the original model.

### Clearing in deferred editing

In deferred editing, clearing changes the draft; confirmation runs form validation and `beforeCommit` before publishing the configured `emptyValue`. Cancel restores the committed range. An untouched empty range or a half-selected range still requires complete endpoints; an explicit change from a non-empty range to an empty draft can be confirmed. Disabled/readonly fields and locked endpoints cannot be cleared. A rejected controlled open cannot publish a cleared model.

Public focus/blur methods are callable from initial mount. Focus opens an editable deferred editor and targets it after readiness; disabled, readonly, or reading fields do not open. Blur only blurs the current target without reopening. Stored methods never bind an old editor; closure, mode changes, deactivation, or unmount cancel queued calls.

Native range-input references apply string placeholders, including empty strings, to both endpoints and retain array labels by endpoint. Input placeholder visibility still follows hint. Readonly native inputs remain focusable and copyable while editing, opening and clearing are blocked. Global or endpoint disabled states take precedence over readonly. Existing omitted-placeholder defaults for each editing mode are preserved.

Native date-range references emit focus/blur without arguments: entering the input group emits focus, switching endpoints does not duplicate it, and leaving emits blur. Form receives each corresponding notification once under its existing rules. Readonly clicks still notify the original event without opening or editing. Disabled clicks do not notify or consume click.once early. Returning a Promise from an ordinary listener does not start busy state or block opening; asynchronous submission still uses explicit before-commit.

<!-- date-contract:start -->

### Values and formats

DateValue is string, number or native Date. Numbers are timestamps and 0 is not empty; modelValue=null is explicitly empty. Ranges retain broad arrays and incomplete endpoints rather than forcing a tuple; commits still validate completeness and validity. Maple general DatePicker/Date multiple selection does not widen Cedar single-value Props.

Tables list actual public properties. Inherited/precision-derived defaults describe resolved behavior; raw Props can be undefined. format controls display/text input and valueFormat controls the model protocol. Week/quarter display labels differ from model formats; function format has no reverse parser for text input.

Bounds are inclusive. Invalid supplied bounds block confirmation instead of being treated as omitted. Tightening rules does not clear the business model. disabledDate/disabledTime are explicit validation callbacks rather than asynchronous event tasks; time callbacks return disabled lists through DateDisabledTime.

| Event | Arguments |
| --- | --- |
| `update:modelValue` | `DateRangeEmits['update:modelValue']` |
| `change` | `DateRangeEmits['change']` |
| `select` | `DateRangeEmits['select']` |
| `clear` | `DateRangeEmits['clear']` |
| `click` | `DateRangeEmits['click']` |
| `focus` | `DateRangeEmits['focus']` |
| `blur` | `DateRangeEmits['blur']` |
| `update:open` | `DateRangeEmits['update:open']` |
| `open-change` | `DateRangeEmits['open-change']` |
| `update:pickerValue` | `DateRangeEmits['update:pickerValue']` |
| `picker-value-change` | `DateRangeEmits['picker-value-change']` |
| `select-shortcut` | `DateRangeEmits['select-shortcut']` |

Field value/viewport notifications use the corresponding public Emits tuples; DateChangeArgs contains value, date(s) and text(s). Listener Promises are not awaited and do not drive loading. beforeCommit uses payload/done/context, with value/previousValue in payload and signal/optional event in context; undefined waits for done.

### Panel event parameter types

Standalone panels have the seven events below, without the old preview event. Navigation uses picker-value-change and update:pickerValue. Navigation/shortcut hover-focus preview does not imply selection or commit. Confirmation only notifies when valid; select draft is separate from committed change.

| Event | Arguments |
| --- | --- |
| `update:modelValue` | `DateRangePickerEmits['update:modelValue']` |
| `change` | `DateRangePickerEmits['change']` |
| `select` | `DateRangePickerEmits['select']` |
| `confirm` | `DateRangePickerEmits['confirm']` |
| `update:pickerValue` | `DateRangePickerEmits['update:pickerValue']` |
| `picker-value-change` | `DateRangePickerEmits['picker-value-change']` |
| `select-shortcut` | `DateRangePickerEmits['select-shortcut']` |

### DateRangePicker Slots / Methods

Field default replaces the trigger; prefix/selected/suffix replace content, and ranges also support separator. Preserve names, endpoint distinctions and keyboard access when replacing native controls. read receives value/text, suffix-icon receives focus/popupOpen, and clear-icon receives guarded clear(event?), respecting emptyValue and disabled/readonly guards.

actions receives confirm/disabled/selectNow/nowDisabled, with both actions returning void. It has no Time-panel canConfirm/value arguments. disabled=true prevents confirmation. Standalone panels can replace the action region; the outer editing shell owns final saving in hosted editing, while the panel contributes auxiliary actions. Panel confirm is not the outer-save method.

Now capabilities follow the actual panel: Cedar single panels support it, while Cedar range panels have no now action. Maple range panels stage now for the active endpoint, preserve the other endpoint and still require confirmation. The presence of selectNow in scope does not imply every mode supports the action.

Cedar cell customizes a calendar cell with date and, for ranges, type=start/end; extra adds content. Maple Date/DatePicker page-calendar summaries support year({year}), month({year,month}), date({week,year,month,date}), range({choose}) and multiple({choose}) according to mode. Maple DateRange/DateRangePicker do not forward these single-panel summary slots, nor do scroll/line viewports promise them.

loading-icon is not wired to date fields or pure panels and is not available merely because the underlying decorator supports it. Field focus(index?)/blur() delegate to real controls. Cedar/direct-field blur closes the field popup; Maple range persistent-reference blur only clears its focus, without pretending to close the outer Drawer. Pure panels expose no focus/blur methods.

### Presentation configuration and ranges

datePickerProps/dateRangePickerProps configure presentation without overriding owned model/rules/type/control events; Maple internal range datePickerProps uses a calendar allowlist. popupProps retains a broad dictionary, with public DatePopupOptions/DateRangePopupOptions recommended and owner keys still filtered at runtime. Cedar timePickerProps configures embedded time presentation; Maple pickerProps configures wheels.

A range placeholder string applies to both endpoints; arrays configure each and missing entries are empty. readonly is separate from disabled; unset field state inherits Form. Cedar range-panel exchangeTime only handles reversed interactive candidates: true swaps their times, false retains endpoint times. It does not reorder external model/text/shortcut values. Maple does not expose this property.

```ts
  type DateRangeEmits, type DateRangePickerEmits, type DateValue, type DateSelection,
  type DateChangeArgs, type DateRules, type DateShortcut } from '@cedar-design/ui-vue'
```

# Date

Floating date panels use the visual viewport height so the full calendar is visible when space permits. Short windows scroll content while keeping actions visible. Override `--c-date-picker-popover-max-height` to adjust the limit (default `100dvh - 32px`).

A date field with a trigger. Use DatePicker for a standalone panel.

## String models and time zones

format controls display; value-format controls the model and events. Use YYYY-MM-DD for a date string or YYYY-MM for a month string. MM-DD has no year and parsing uses the current year, so retain a full date for cross-year ordering or explicit leap-year rules.

Omitting time-zone preserves browser-local behavior. With an IANA time zone, Date and timestamps represent instants while strings represent local civil times in that zone. Invalid DST times are rejected; newly entered repeated times resolve to the first occurrence. Untouched Date/timestamp range endpoints preserve their exact instant and hidden precision. Maple-only scroll/line views do not change Cedar panel defaults.

```vue
<script setup>
import { useDemoLocale } from "../../__demos__/locale";

  { name: "variant", values: ["filled", "outline", "standard"] },
```

```vue
const open = ref(false);

const commits = ref(0);

function requestOpen(next) {
  if (next) open.value = true;
  else closeRequests.value++;
}
</script>

<template>
  <c-space direction="column" size="12px">

      v-model="value"
      :open="open"
      @update:open="requestOpen"
      @change="commits++"
    >
      <template #actions="{ confirm, disabled }">
        <c-button :disabled="disabled" @click="confirm()">确认</c-button>
        <c-button @click="open = false">允许关闭</c-button>
      </template>
    </c-date>
```

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { ref } from "vue";
import type { DateShortcut } from "@cedar-design/ui-vue";

const selected = ref("2025-01-15");
const viewport = ref("2025-01-01");
const acceptNavigation = ref(true);
const notice = ref("");
const shortcutNotice = ref("");
const shortcuts: DateShortcut[] = [
  { label: "下个月", value: "2025-02-15" },
  { label: "不可选", value: "2025-03-01", disabled: true },
];
function navigate(value: unknown) {
  if (acceptNavigation.value && typeof value === "string")
    viewport.value = value;
}
function observe(_value: unknown, _dates: unknown, texts: unknown) {
  notice.value = String(texts);
}
function choose(shortcut: DateShortcut) {
  shortcutNotice.value = String(shortcut.label);
}
</script>

    @picker-value-change="observe"
    @select-shortcut="choose"
  />
```
