```vue
</template>
```

### Shared field loading

`loading` displays the shared field indicator. `loading-mode` is `default` (indicator) or `line` (an indeterminate bottom line); it defaults to `default`. Rendering belongs to FieldDecorator. Loading does not implicitly disable editing or change readonly. Set those states separately.

## Reading direction

Inherits the nearest `dir="ltr|rtl"`, including runtime changes and local overrides. Calendar dates, months and years follow reading order; navigation icons mirror, while date values keep their meaning. In paged grids, Left/Right moves focus visually, Up/Down moves one row, and Home/End moves to the row boundary, skipping disabled items. Focus navigation does not select; Enter/Space keeps the existing selection behavior. Navigation is bounded by the displayed grid. Explicit `shortcuts-position="left|right"` remains physical; `bottom` stays below. Field popovers inherit their source direction.

## Triggers and positioning

### Popup placement

The Date field prefers bottom-start below its input. Override the preferred side through popupProps.placement only when needed; the underlying Trigger positions it, not Popup or Popover. DatePicker is a standalone date panel with no input anchor. Configure popup placement on the Date field.

Public focus/blur methods are callable from initial mount. Focus opens an editable deferred editor and targets it after readiness; disabled, readonly, or reading fields do not open. Blur only blurs the current target without reopening. Stored methods never bind an old editor; closure, mode changes, deactivation, or unmount cancel queued calls.

<!-- date-contract:start -->

## API

### Empty values and reading placeholders

`empty-values` recognizes empty data; `empty-value` keeps existing clear output. `empty-text` defaults to `'-'` under `read-pretty`, with Field > FormItem > Form precedence and custom read slots first. With explicit `empty-values`, built-in required uses the policy; custom validators receive original data. See the [shared guide](llms/en-US/guide/empty-values.md).

| Prop | Type | Default and scope |
| ------------ | ------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------- |
| empty-values | readonly unknown[] | Field > FormItem > Form > component-family default; replaces the whole list |
| empty-text | string | Field > FormItem > Form > '-'; explicit '' is valid |

These props belong to field presentation; pure panels do not gain reading mode. Form and FormItem provide inherited settings. The existing empty-value type and clear fallback remain component-specific.

### Date Props

| Prop | Description | Type | Default behavior |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `before-commit` | Explicit field-save guard using payload, done and context | `BeforeFieldCommit` | `undefined` |
| `blur-color` | Color while unfocused | `string` | Theme default |
| `clearable` | Allow clearing with disabled, readonly and pending guards | `boolean` | `true` |

| `default-open` | Initial uncontrolled opening, read only at creation | `boolean` | `false` |
| `default-value` | Initial uncontrolled value, read only at creation | `DateValue` | `undefined` |

| `value-format` | Serialized model format: Date, timestamp or format tokens, independent of display format | `string` | From precision/time settings |
| `variant` | Field appearance | `filled \| outline \| standard` | `outline` |

### Shared date-family contract

| Prop | Description | Type | Default |
| ----------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------- | ------- |
| `default-value` | Uncontrolled initial value, read once | DateValue / DateValue[] | — |
| `value-format` | Model and event value format: a date format string, Date, or timestamp | string | Follows type |
| `min` | Inclusive minimum date; string bounds use value-format | DateValue | — |
| `max` | Inclusive maximum date; string bounds use value-format | DateValue | — |
| `disabled-time` | Disabled times for the current date and endpoint | (date: Date, side: DateSide) => DateDisabledTime<br>`DateSide: 'end' \| 'start'` | — |
| `disable-confirm` | Commit immediately | boolean | false |
| `default-open` | Uncontrolled initial open state | boolean | false |
| `popup-props` | Optional field-popup presentation settings. Placement defaults to bottom-start and is positioned automatically by the underlying Trigger; the preferred side can be overridden. No top-level placement prop; field state and rules cannot be overridden | object | {} |
| `popup-container` | Portal target; the top-level value wins, including false for inline rendering | string / HTMLElement / (() => HTMLElement) / false | — |

`DateValue = Date | string | number`. Clearing a single value produces undefined; clearing a range produces [].
The date argument of `disabledDate(date, side)` and `disabledTime(date, side)` is always a Date; side is start/end.
Time callbacks return numeric lists from `disabledHours()`, `disabledMinutes(hour)` and `disabledSeconds(hour, minute)`.
Invalid dates and incomplete/reversed ranges cannot be committed. Confirmation revalidates dynamic disabling rules. Locked range endpoints cannot be cleared or changed.
Nested panel props configure presentation only; they must not override top-level model-value, format, bounds, disabling rules or control events.

### Date Events

See the complete field and panel event lists on this page.

Desktop supports keyboard editing. The default panel edits a draft before confirmation; disable-confirm commits directly. Escape or closing discards the draft. focus(index = 0) focuses a start/end input, and blur() closes the popup.

| `type` | Date precision; Cedar includes week/quarter, while Maple supports date/month/year | `date \| month \| year \| week \| quarter` | `date` |
| `value-format` | Serialized model format: Date, timestamp or format tokens, independent of display format | `string` | From precision/time settings |

## Explicit time zones

`timeZone` accepts IANA names such as `Asia/Shanghai`. Date objects and millisecond timestamps represent instants; strings represent local time in the target zone. Display, typed input, min/max, shortcuts and disabling rules use the same protocol; event Date objects retain the actual instant. Omitting `timeZone` preserves local-zone behavior. Nonexistent daylight-saving times and invalid zones cannot be committed; repeated times use the first occurrence. Maple scroll / line are mobile calendar presentations; desktop retains its existing panel.

## Configuring the cleared value

`empty-value` defines the output of an existing clear action. Omission preserves the component fallback; supported types remain component-specific. It does not change empty-values recognition or Form reset defaults.

`empty-value` accepts explicit `null` (or `() => null`). Clearing publishes `null` unchanged; omitted values preserve the existing default. Editors render `null` as blank without converting ordinary empty-string input to `null`. In popup editing, clearing changes the draft; confirm commits it and cancel preserves the original model.

### Values and formats

DateValue is string, number or native Date. Numbers are timestamps and 0 is not empty; modelValue=null is explicitly empty. Ranges retain broad arrays and incomplete endpoints rather than forcing a tuple; commits still validate completeness and validity. Maple general DatePicker/Date multiple selection does not widen Cedar single-value Props.

Tables list actual public properties. Inherited/precision-derived defaults describe resolved behavior; raw Props can be undefined. format controls display/text input and valueFormat controls the model protocol. Week/quarter display labels differ from model formats; function format has no reverse parser for text input.

Bounds are inclusive. Invalid supplied bounds block confirmation instead of being treated as omitted. Tightening rules does not clear the business model. disabledDate/disabledTime are explicit validation callbacks rather than asynchronous event tasks; time callbacks return disabled lists through DateDisabledTime.

### Field event parameter types

| Event | Arguments |
| --- | --- |
| `update:modelValue` | `DateEmits['update:modelValue']` |
| `change` | `DateEmits['change']` |
| `select` | `DateEmits['select']` |
| `clear` | `DateEmits['clear']` |
| `click` | `DateEmits['click']` |
| `focus` | `DateEmits['focus']` |
| `blur` | `DateEmits['blur']` |
| `update:open` | `DateEmits['update:open']` |
| `open-change` | `DateEmits['open-change']` |
| `update:pickerValue` | `DateEmits['update:pickerValue']` |
| `picker-value-change` | `DateEmits['picker-value-change']` |
| `select-shortcut` | `DateEmits['select-shortcut']` |

Field value/viewport notifications use the corresponding public Emits tuples; DateChangeArgs contains value, date(s) and text(s). Listener Promises are not awaited and do not drive loading. beforeCommit uses payload/done/context, with value/previousValue in payload and signal/optional event in context; undefined waits for done.

### Panel event parameter types

Standalone panels have the seven events below, without the old preview event. Navigation uses picker-value-change and update:pickerValue. Navigation/shortcut hover-focus preview does not imply selection or commit. Confirmation only notifies when valid; select draft is separate from committed change.

| Event | Arguments |
| --- | --- |
| `update:modelValue` | `DatePickerEmits['update:modelValue']` |
| `change` | `DatePickerEmits['change']` |
| `select` | `DatePickerEmits['select']` |
| `confirm` | `DatePickerEmits['confirm']` |
| `update:pickerValue` | `DatePickerEmits['update:pickerValue']` |
| `picker-value-change` | `DatePickerEmits['picker-value-change']` |
| `select-shortcut` | `DatePickerEmits['select-shortcut']` |

### DatePicker Slots / Methods

Field default replaces the trigger; prefix/selected/suffix replace content, and ranges also support separator. Preserve names, endpoint distinctions and keyboard access when replacing native controls. read receives value/text, suffix-icon receives focus/popupOpen, and clear-icon receives guarded clear(event?), respecting emptyValue and disabled/readonly guards.

actions receives confirm/disabled/selectNow/nowDisabled, with both actions returning void. It has no Time-panel canConfirm/value arguments. disabled=true prevents confirmation. Standalone panels can replace the action region; the outer editing shell owns final saving in hosted editing, while the panel contributes auxiliary actions. Panel confirm is not the outer-save method.

Now capabilities follow the actual panel: Cedar single panels support it, while Cedar range panels have no now action. Maple range panels stage now for the active endpoint, preserve the other endpoint and still require confirmation. The presence of selectNow in scope does not imply every mode supports the action.

Cedar cell customizes a calendar cell with date and, for ranges, type=start/end; extra adds content. Maple Date/DatePicker page-calendar summaries support year({year}), month({year,month}), date({week,year,month,date}), range({choose}) and multiple({choose}) according to mode. Maple DateRange/DateRangePicker do not forward these single-panel summary slots, nor do scroll/line viewports promise them.

loading-icon is not wired to date fields or pure panels and is not available merely because the underlying decorator supports it. Field focus(index?)/blur() delegate to real controls. Cedar/direct-field blur closes the field popup; Maple range persistent-reference blur only clears its focus, without pretending to close the outer Drawer. Pure panels expose no focus/blur methods.

### Presentation configuration and ranges

datePickerProps/dateRangePickerProps configure presentation without overriding owned model/rules/type/control events; Maple internal range datePickerProps uses a calendar allowlist. popupProps retains a broad dictionary, with public DatePopupOptions/DateRangePopupOptions recommended and owner keys still filtered at runtime. Cedar timePickerProps configures embedded time presentation; Maple pickerProps configures wheels.

A range placeholder string applies to both endpoints; arrays configure each and missing entries are empty. readonly is separate from disabled; unset field state inherits Form. Cedar range-panel exchangeTime only handles reversed interactive candidates: true swaps their times, false retains endpoint times. It does not reorder external model/text/shortcut values. Maple does not expose this property.

```ts
import { Date as DateField, DatePicker, type DateProps, type DatePickerProps,
  type DateEmits, type DatePickerEmits, type DateValue, type DateSelection,
  type DateChangeArgs, type DateRules, type DateShortcut } from '@cedar-design/ui-vue'
```

```css
.component-theme {
  --c-date-picker-actions-padding: 8px 12px;
}
```

Explicit inline styles and props that write the same CSS property take precedence over stylesheet defaults. After Teleport, ordinary CSS variables inherit from the actual mount location. When using ThemeProvider, follow its local-theme and popup configuration rules. Override the component variable directly for local styling; root-level aliases are not recalculated merely because a descendant system variable changes. Internal variables are not public APIs.

# Descriptions

- `data`: Supplies the example data.

```vue
      <c-descriptions-item v-for="item of data" :key="item.label" :label="item.label" :span="item.span ?? 1">

      </c-descriptions-item>
    </c-descriptions>

  },

  },
  {

    value: 'Beijing',
  },
  {
    label: 'Hometown',
    value: 'Beijing',

</script>
```

## Reading direction

Inherits the nearest `dir="ltr|rtl"`, including runtime changes and local overrides. Labels and values follow reading order, with logical boundaries and default alignment. Changing direction does not reverse records, column definitions or span meanings.

## API

### Descriptions Props

| Prop | Description | Type | Default |
| ------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------ | :---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------: | :------------- |
| data | Description-list data | `DescData[]` | `[]` |
| column | Items per row. Responsive configuration is supported since 2.20.0; see Grid | `number \| ResponsiveValue` | `3` |
| title | Description-list title | `string` | `-` |
| layout | Description-list arrangement | `'horizontal' \| 'vertical' \| 'inline-horizontal' \| 'inline-vertical' \| 'inline-auto'` | `'horizontal'` |
| align | Text alignment | `TextAlign \| { label?: TextAlign; value?: TextAlign }`<br>`TextAlign: 'center' \| 'left' \| 'right'` | `'left'` |
| size | Description-list size | `'xs' \| 'sm' \| 'md' \| 'lg' \| 'xl'` | `-` |
| bordered | Whether to show border | `boolean` | `false` |
| label-style | Label styles | `CSSProperties` | `-` |
| value-style | Content styles | `CSSProperties` | `-` |
| table-layout | Table-style `layout-fixed`; setting `fixed` distributes widths evenly | `'auto' \| 'fixed'` | `'auto'` |
| aria-label | Accessible description-list label | `string` | `-` |

In data mode, slot `index` in `label` and `value` is the zero-based position in the original `data` array, independent of columns and layout.

Columns and each span must be finite positive integers, including responsive values. Invalid columns fall back to 3 and invalid spans to 1. The title slot names the table automatically; an explicit `aria-label` takes precedence. The default slot takes precedence over data even when empty.

### Descriptions Slots

| Slot | Description | Prop |
| ------ | :------: | ------------------------------------------------------ |
| default | Item list; takes precedence over data | - |
| value | Content | value: `string \| RenderFunction`<br>index: `number`<br>data: `DescData` |
| label | Label | label: `string \| RenderFunction`<br>index: `number`<br>data: `DescData` |
| title | Title | - |

### DescriptionsItem Props

| Prop | Description | Type | Default |
| ----- | -------- | :------: | :----- |
| span | Column span | `number` | `1` |
| label | Label | `string` | `-` |

### DescriptionsItem Slots

| Slot | Description | Prop |
| ------- | :--: | ---- |
| default | Content | - |
| label | Label | - |

## Types

Public types include `DescData`, `DescLayout`, `DescriptionsSlotScope`, `DescriptionsSlots`, and `DescriptionsItemSlots`.

### DescData

| Parameter | Description | Type | Default |
| ------ | -------- | -------------------------- | :----: |
| label | Label | `string \| RenderFunction` | `-` |
| value | Data | `string \| RenderFunction` | `-` |
| span | Column span | `number` | `-` |

The component exports the following types

```ts
import type { DescriptionsProps } from "@cedar-design/ui-vue";
```

```css

  --c-descriptions-border-color: var(--c-color-neutral-3);
}
```

Explicit inline styles and props that write the same CSS property take precedence over stylesheet defaults. After Teleport, ordinary CSS variables inherit from the actual mount location. When using ThemeProvider, follow its local-theme and popup configuration rules. Override the component variable directly for local styling; root-level aliases are not recalculated merely because a descendant system variable changes. Internal variables are not public APIs.

# Dialog

With `draggable` enabled, title inputs, textareas, buttons, links with href and editable content retain native pointer behavior and do not start a drag. The ordinary title area remains draggable. In non-centered mode, numeric `top=0` is supported just like the string `0px`.

A modal dialog with matching declarative and programmatic APIs.

## Basic examples

### Basic

Example source: src/dialog/__demos__/basic.vue

```vue
<template>
  <c-button @click="open = true">Open Dialog</c-button>

  <c-dialog
    v-model:open="open"
    title="Dialog Title"
    message="This is a basic component dialog."
    @confirm="Message.success('Confirmed')"
    @cancel="Message.info('Cancelled')"
  />
</template>

<script setup lang="ts">
import { Message } from "@cedar-design/ui-vue";
import { ref } from "vue";

const open = ref(false);
</script>
```

## Invocation and content

### Global

<!-- demo-config-notes:start -->
#### Configuration reference for this comparison

| Configuration | Purpose | Related examples |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `title` | Title | Confirm, Form, Simple |
| `type` | Status icon: `info`, `success`, `warning` or `error` | Confirm, Simple |
| `message` | Message content; the default slot is also supported | Confirm, Simple |
| `before-close` | Return a boolean/Promise or call done; the first completion wins | Form |
| `simple` | Compact layout with a centered footer | Simple |
<!-- demo-config-notes:end -->


Example source: src/dialog/__demos__/global.vue

```vue
<template>
  <c-space>
    <c-button @click="openBasic">Basic</c-button>
    <c-button @click="openDialog">Open</c-button>
    <c-button @click="openAndUpdate">Open and Update</c-button>
    <c-button @click="awaitAction">Await Action</c-button>
    <c-button @click="hideButtons">Hide Footer Buttons</c-button>
  </c-space>
</template>

<script setup lang="ts">
import { Dialog, Message } from "@cedar-design/ui-vue";

function openBasic() {
  Dialog.open("This dialog was opened from a string message.");
}

function openDialog() {
  Dialog.open({
    title: "Global Method",
    message: "This dialog was opened programmatically.",
  });
}

function openAndUpdate() {
  const instance = Dialog.open({
    title: "Submitting",
    message: "Processing the request…",
  });
  window.setTimeout(
    () =>
      instance.update({
        title: "Completed",
        message: "The request succeeded.",
      }),
    800,
  );
}

async function awaitAction() {
  const action = await Dialog.open("Choose an action to close this dialog.");
  if (action) Message.info(`Dialog action: ${action}`);
}

function hideButtons() {
  Dialog.open({
    title: "No Footer Buttons",
    message: "Click the overlay or press Esc to dismiss this dialog.",
    confirmButton: false,
    cancelButton: false,
  });
}
</script>
```

### Form

Example source: src/dialog/__demos__/form.vue

```vue
<template>
  <c-button @click="handleClick">Open Form Dialog</c-button>
  <c-dialog v-model:open="visible" title="Dialog Form" @cancel="handleCancel" :before-close="handleBeforeClose">
    <c-form :model="form">
      <c-form-item field="name" label="Name">
        <c-input v-model="form.name" />
      </c-form-item>
      <c-form-item field="post" label="Post">
        <c-select v-model="form.post">
          <c-option value="post1">Post1</c-option>
          <c-option value="post2">Post2</c-option>
          <c-option value="post3">Post3</c-option>
          <c-option value="post4">Post4</c-option>
        </c-select>
      </c-form-item>
    </c-form>
  </c-dialog>
</template>

<script lang="ts">
import { defineComponent, reactive, ref } from 'vue'

export default defineComponent({
  setup() {
    const visible = ref(false)
    const form = reactive({
      name: '',
      post: '',
    })

    const handleClick = () => {
      visible.value = true
    }

    const handleBeforeClose = ({ action }, done) => {
      if (action !== 'confirm') {
        done()
        return
      }

      window.setTimeout(() => {
        done()
      }, 2000)
    }

    const handleCancel = () => {
      visible.value = false
    }

    return {
      visible,
      form,
      handleClick,
      handleBeforeClose,
      handleCancel,
    }
  },
})
</script>
```

### Service popup containers

Function calls honor `popupContainer` from explicit configuration or `setDefaultOptions`, using the component's selector/HTMLElement resolution and missing/invalid-selector fallback to body. The default targets body; `false` renders inline in the service's own body host. `handle.update({ popupContainer })` moves the same dialog and preserves content state and app context. Closing removes teleported content and its service host, independently of notification callback results. A custom container controls DOM attachment; layout still follows Dialog positioning and its containing block.

Example source: src/dialog/__demos__/service-container.vue

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { useDemoLocale as useInlineDemoLocale } from "../../__demos__/locale";
const inlineCopy = useInlineDemoLocale("dialogServiceContainerInline");

import {
  computed,
  defineComponent,
  getCurrentInstance,
  h,
  onBeforeUnmount,
  ref,
  shallowRef,
} from "vue";
import Dialog from "..";
import Button from "../../button";
import Input from "../../input";
const first = ref<HTMLElement>();
const second = ref<HTMLElement>();
const active = shallowRef<ReturnType<typeof Dialog.open>>();
const context = getCurrentInstance()?.appContext;
const resultKey = ref<keyof typeof inlineCopy.value | undefined>("notOpened");
const rawResult = ref("");
const result = computed(() =>
  resultKey.value ? inlineCopy.value[resultKey.value] : rawResult.value,
);
function openSample() {
  if (!first.value) return;
  active.value?.close();
  const Content = defineComponent({
    setup() {
      const draft = ref("Draft"),
        location = ref("A");
      function move(to: "A" | "B") {
        const target = to === "A" ? first.value : second.value;
        if (target) {
          owned.update({ popupContainer: target });
          location.value = to;
        }
      }
      return () =>
        h("div", [
          h("p", inlineCopy.value.currentTarget + location.value),
          h(Input, {
            "aria-label": inlineCopy.value.serviceDraft,
            editMode: "direct",
            modelValue: draft.value,
            "onUpdate:modelValue": (value: string | null) => {
              draft.value = value ?? "";
            },
          }),
          h(
            "p",
            "切换挂载区域后，输入草稿仍保留。Moving the same dialog preserves its draft.",
          ),
          h(
            Button,
            { onClick: () => move("A") },
            () => inlineCopy.value.moveToA,
          ),
          h(
            Button,
            { onClick: () => move("B") },
            () => inlineCopy.value.moveToB,
          ),
        ]);
    },
  });
  const owned: ReturnType<typeof Dialog.open> = Dialog.open(
    {
      title: inlineCopy.value.serviceTarget,
      popupContainer: first.value,
      content: () => h(Content),
    },
    context,
  );
  active.value = owned;
  resultKey.value = "opened";
  void owned.then((action) => {
    if (active.value === owned) {
      active.value = undefined;
      resultKey.value = undefined;
      rawResult.value = String(action);
    }
  });
}
onBeforeUnmount(() => {
  active.value?.close();
  active.value = undefined;
});
</script>
<template>
  <c-space direction="column" :size="16">
    <c-button @click="openSample">{{ inlineCopy.openInA }}</c-button>
    <div
      ref="first"
      data-service-target="A"
      style="min-height: 64px; border: 1px dashed currentColor; padding: 12px"
    >
      {{ inlineCopy.targetA }}
    </div>
    <div
      ref="second"
      data-service-target="B"
      style="min-height: 64px; border: 1px dashed currentColor; padding: 12px"
    >
      {{ inlineCopy.targetB }}
    </div>
    <p role="status">{{ result }}</p>
  </c-space>
</template>
```

## Interaction and customization

### Draggable

<!-- demo-config-notes:start -->
#### Configuration reference for this comparison

| Configuration | Purpose | Related examples |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `unmount-on-close` | Unmount after closing | Custom Text, Advanced |
| `draggable` | Draggable | Draggable |
| `confirm-button-text` | Confirm button text | Custom Text |
| `cancel-button-text` | Cancel button text | Custom Text |
| `footer` | Whether to show the footer | Advanced |
| `type` | Status icon: `info`, `success`, `warning` or `error` | Advanced |
<!-- demo-config-notes:end -->


Example source: src/dialog/__demos__/draggable.vue

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { useDemoLocale as useInlineDemoLocale } from "../../__demos__/locale";
const inlineCopy = useInlineDemoLocale("dialogDraggableInline");

import { ref } from "vue";
const open = ref(false);
const draggable = ref(true);
const fullscreen = ref(false);
function keyboard(event: KeyboardEvent) {
  if (event.key.toLowerCase() === "d") {
    event.preventDefault();
    draggable.value = !draggable.value;
  } else if (event.key.toLowerCase() === "f") {
    event.preventDefault();
    fullscreen.value = !fullscreen.value;
  }
}
</script>
<template>
  <c-button @click="open = true">{{ inlineCopy.openDragExample }}</c-button>
  <c-dialog
    v-model:open="open"
    :draggable="draggable"
    :fullscreen="fullscreen"
    :title="inlineCopy.dragTitle"
    @keydown="keyboard"
    @confirm="open = false"
    @cancel="open = false"
  >
    <p>{{ inlineCopy.dragTheTitlePressD }}</p>
    <c-space wrap>
      <c-button @click="draggable = !draggable">{{
        draggable ? inlineCopy.disableDrag : inlineCopy.enableDrag
      }}</c-button>
      <c-button @click="fullscreen = !fullscreen">{{
        fullscreen ? inlineCopy.exitFullscreen : inlineCopy.fullscreen
      }}</c-button>
    </c-space>
    <p role="status">
      {{ draggable ? inlineCopy.dragEnabled : inlineCopy.dragStopped }}
    </p>
  </c-dialog>
</template>
```

## Async actions and closing

### Async

<!-- demo-config-notes:start -->
#### Configuration reference for this comparison

| Configuration | Purpose | Related examples |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `before-close` | Return a boolean/Promise or call done; the first completion wins | Async close, before hooks and callback compatibility |
| `title` | Title | Async |
| `message` | Message content; the default slot is also supported | Async |
<!-- demo-config-notes:end -->


Example source: src/dialog/__demos__/async.vue

```vue
<template>
  <c-space>
    <c-button @click="asyncOpen = true">Async Close</c-button>
    <c-button @click="loadingOpen = true">Button Loading</c-button>
  </c-space>

  <c-dialog
    v-model:open="asyncOpen"
    title="Async Close"
    message="Every action waits for the asynchronous task to finish."
    :before-close="beforeClose"
  />
  <c-dialog
    v-model:open="loadingOpen"
    title="Button Loading"
    message="The confirm button displays loading while the task is running."
    :before-close="buttonLoadingClose"
  />
</template>

<script setup lang="ts">
import { ref } from "vue";
import type { DialogAction } from "../types";

const asyncOpen = ref(false);
const loadingOpen = ref(false);

function beforeClose({ action: _action }: { action: DialogAction }, done: () => void) {
  window.setTimeout(done, 1000);
}

function buttonLoadingClose(
  { action }: { action: DialogAction },
  done: () => void,

) {
  if (action !== "confirm") {
    done();
    return;
  }

  window.setTimeout(() => {
    done();
  }, 1000);
}
</script>
```

### Guard Protocol

Example source: src/dialog/__demos__/en-US/guard-protocol.vue

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { ref } from "vue";
import type { DialogBeforeClose } from "@cedar-design/ui-vue";
const open = ref(false);
const mode = ref("promise");
const allowed = ref(false);
const status = ref("");
const check: DialogBeforeClose = (payload, done, { signal }) => {
  status.value = `Waiting: ${payload.action}`;
  if (mode.value === "done") {
    setTimeout(() => {
      status.value = allowed.value ? "Allowed" : "Rejected";
      done(!signal.aborted && allowed.value);
    }, 500);
    return;
  }
  return new Promise<boolean>((resolve) =>
    setTimeout(() => {
      status.value = allowed.value ? "Allowed" : "Rejected";
      resolve(!signal.aborted && allowed.value);
    }, 500),
  );
};
</script>
<template>
  <c-space direction="column" align="stretch">
    <c-switch v-model="allowed" />
    <c-form-item layout="vertical" size="sm" label="mode">
      <c-radio-group
        aria-label="mode"
        v-model="mode"
        :options="[
          { value: 'promise', label: 'Promise' },
          { value: 'done', label: 'done callback' },
        ]"
        variant="button"
        size="sm"
      />
    </c-form-item>
    <c-button @click="open = true">Open</c-button>
    <c-dialog
      v-model:open="open"
      :before-close="check"
      @guard-error="status = 'Error'"
    >
      <template #default
        ><c-button v-if="false" @click="open = true">Confirm action</c-button
        ><span v-else>Close with beforeClose</span></template
      >
    </c-dialog>
    <p role="status">{{ status }}</p>
  </c-space>
</template>
```

### Reading direction

Inherits the nearest `dir="ltr|rtl"` and supports runtime and nested overrides. Content, headings and action gaps use logical edges. Portals inherit their source direction. Direction changes preserve close, confirm, cancel and pending-state semantics.

## Reading direction

Inherits the nearest `dir="ltr|rtl"`, including runtime changes and local overrides. Content, titles and action spacing use logical start/end. External popovers inherit their source direction. Closing, confirmation, cancellation and uncommitted state are unchanged by direction switches.

## Usage notes

### Async operation feedback
Awaited before-* hooks show loading feedback and aria-busy. Rejection or failure restores interaction; repeated input does not start the same operation again. Ordinary event return Promises do not participate in loading.

Programmatic notification callbacks do not control task completion. Service selection/closing results settle independently of callback errors, and closing completion always releases the owned host. Exceptions still propagate through the caller or Vue error channel; returned Promises do not control loading or closing.

### Dragging and cancellation
Title dragging is controlled only by the initiating primary pointer. Disabling `draggable`, closing, entering fullscreen, losing pointer capture or owner-window focus, deactivation and unmount all end the gesture and release listeners and capture. Reenabling requires a new gesture; the previous pointer cannot resume it. Disabling preserves the current offset; fullscreen and the existing post-close reset restore defaults. Listeners belong to the title element's document.

## API

### Dialog Props

Dividers follow Card and are disabled by default. Enable them separately with `top-divider` and `bottom-divider`; each appears only when its corresponding header or footer exists. Dialog also supports these options in simple mode and service calls, using `topDivider` and `bottomDivider` in service configuration.

### Dialog Events

| Event | Description | Arguments |
| ------------ | ------------- | --------------- |
| `open` | When opened | `-` |
| `opened` | Opening transition completes | `-` |
| `close` | Closing begins | `-` |
| `closed` | Closing transition completes | `-` |
| `confirm` | Accepted confirm action | `Event` |
| `cancel` | Accepted cancel or close action | `Event` |
| `click-overlay` | `MouseEvent` | `MouseEvent` |
| `key-escape` | ESC | `KeyboardEvent` |

The `close` button, overlay, ESC and `close()` use `close` semantics without an additional `cancel` event.

Built-in buttons, overlay, Escape, footer methods and instance confirm()/cancel() request beforeClose. Instance close(), returned handle close(), Dialog.close() and parent open=false are direct commands that bypass guards; a controlled parent still decides whether to accept update:open(false). Direct closing retires pending guards so late results cannot close a reopened instance. close does not mean leave completion; observe closed/onClosed. Maple Popup close()/requestClose() instead return `Promise<boolean>` for guarded requests.

### Dialog Slots

| Slot | Description | Prop |
| --------- | ---- | ---------------------------- |
| `default` | Content | `-` |
| `title` | Title | `-` |
| `footer` | Footer | `cancel`, `confirm`, `close` |

Confirm and cancel buttons use Button's `default` status and `text` variant unless `confirmButtonProps` or `cancelButtonProps` overrides them.

### Dialog Methods

Function-based Dialog calls default to simple layout (`simple: true`) with the top-right close button hidden (`closable: false`). Explicit options or global defaults can override both.

## CSS Variables

Normal and simple modes grow with their content up to `90dvh`, falling back to `90vh` when unsupported. Beyond this height, only the body scrolls; the title and actions remain visible. Override the limit with `--c-dialog-max-height` or `dialogStyle.maxHeight`; fullscreen mode uses the full viewport height. In non-centered mode, the default top offset is capped at `5dvh`, falling back to `5vh`; an explicit `top` remains application-controlled.

Dialog public color variables have the same meanings as Maple: `--c-dialog-background` is the raised panel background (`surface-raised`); `--c-dialog-overlay-background` is the scrim; `--c-dialog-title-text-color` and `--c-dialog-content-text-color` are primary content; `--c-dialog-close-button-color` is the secondary action. `--c-dialog-status-{info|success|warning|danger}-color` uses readable content-info/success/warning/danger, not status fills. Business themes should override these component variables; shared themes should override the corresponding system variables. Borders, widths, spacing and layout retain desktop specifications.

The backdrop consumes `sys-color-scrim` through the Dialog component variable. Dialog uses its own backdrop variables. Set a per-instance backdrop variable via `overlay-style`; a variable on the panel (`dialog-style`) does not inherit to its sibling backdrop. Explicit `overlay-style.backgroundColor` wins. Teleported content needs variables on its actual DOM ancestors. Dark themes inherit the same semantic colors; geometry remains platform-specific. Status icons use readable content colors.

Variables are grouped by purpose: background/overlay-background for panel/scrim; border-* for panel/divider borders; title-* for title typography; content-* for body typography; actions-* for actions; close-button-* for the close button; status-* for semantic icons; simple-*/fullscreen-* for mode dimensions; animation-* for enter/leave motion. width/margin-top control ordinary panel layout. Internal drag/position variables are not public customization points.

<!-- component-css-variables:start -->

```css
  --c-dialog-actions-button-gap: var(--c-sys-space-6);
}
```

Explicit inline styles and props that write the same CSS property take precedence over stylesheet defaults. After Teleport, ordinary CSS variables inherit from the actual mount location. When using ThemeProvider, follow its local-theme and popup configuration rules. Override the component variable directly for local styling; root-level aliases are not recalculated merely because a descendant system variable changes. Internal variables are not public APIs.

# Divider

Separate content sections in lists and layouts.

Inherits the nearest `dir="ltr|rtl"`. Horizontal text start/end follows reading order; vertical start/end remains top/bottom. Inset controls along-line indentation and spacing controls perpendicular margins. Paired horizontal inset and vertical spacing uses logical start/end. Vertical borders use inline start; hairline, border type and aria-orientation retain their meaning. Direction changes preserve content nodes.

## Basic examples

### Basic Usage

Separate adjacent content sections.

Example source: src/divider/__demos__/basic.vue

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { useDemoLocale as useInlineDemoLocale } from "../../__demos__/locale";
const inlineCopy = useInlineDemoLocale("dividerBasicInline");
</script>
<template>
  <div>
    <p>{{ inlineCopy.before }}</p>
    <c-divider />
    <p>{{ inlineCopy.after }}</p>
  </div>
</template>
```

## Content and layout

### Content height and minimum thickness

Explicit thickness accepts finite numbers greater than or equal to 1. hairline still takes priority, using half the theme width. Values below 1 (including zero and negative values), and non-finite values, are ignored and use the theme width; development builds warn.

Multiline descriptions and custom content occupy their full height, including spacing=0. Subsequent content stays below the divider.

Example source: src/divider/__demos__/content-flow.vue

```vue
    <h4>{{ inlineCopy.minimumExplicitWidth }}</h4>
    <div class="flow-sample">

        :spacing="0"
        :description="inlineCopy.contentStaysInNormalFlow"
      />
      <p>{{ inlineCopy.followingContent }}</p>
    </div>
    <h4>{{ inlineCopy.multilineContent }}</h4>
    <div class="flow-sample">
      <c-divider
```

## Usage notes

### Configuration

Presets read the active platform theme. Text spacing is 16px on desktop and 8px on mobile.

## API

### Divider Props

| Prop | Description | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `orientation` | Horizontal/vertical orientation of the divider itself, default horizontal; does not control text alignment | `horizontal` \| `vertical` | `horizontal` |
| `type` | Line style | `solid` \| `dashed` \| `dotted` \| `double` | `solid` |
| `text-align` | Text position along the line; start/end follow logical direction | `start` \| `center` \| `end` | `center` |
| `description` | Description text; the default slot takes priority | `string` | — |
| `inset` | Inset along the line: left/right horizontally, top/bottom vertically | `DividerSize` | — |
| `spacing` | Outer spacing across the line: top/bottom horizontally, left/right vertically | `DividerSize` | `md` |
| `thickness` | Finite line width of at least 1px; omission uses the 1px theme default; hairline takes precedence | `number` | — |
| `hairline` | Scale the theme line width by half; 0.5px with the default theme | `boolean` | `false` |
| `color` | Line color; defaults to the theme border color | `string` | — |
| `opacity` | Opacity of the entire divider, including text, from 0 to 1; zero preserves layout | `number` | — |

### Spacing values

`DividerSize = number | string | [number | string] | [number | string, number | string]`

`inset` controls the ends of the line; `spacing` controls the outer gap between the line and adjacent content. Both accept presets `xs`, `sm`, `md`, `lg`, `xl`, a number in px, a CSS length, or an array. A scalar or single-item array applies to both ends; `[start, end]` sets each end separately. Array entries are lengths, not preset names.

| Direction | inset array order | spacing array order |
| --- | --- | --- |
| horizontal | Inline start/end inset; right/left in RTL | Top/bottom margin |
| vertical | Top/bottom inset | Inline start/end margin; right/left in RTL |

`inset` has no inset by default; `spacing` defaults to the platform’s `md` spacing. Presets use platform theme tokens, so pixel values may differ.


Development checks cover orientation, text-align, type, spacing shape, thickness and opacity. Invalid enums use defaults; invalid inset produces no indentation, invalid spacing falls back to md, and invalid opacity does not override styles. opacity must be finite and within 0–1. Arrays accept one or two lengths and no preset names. Finite negative margins and CSS var/calc expressions remain supported; browsers parse their CSS syntax.

### Divider Slots

| Slot | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `default` | Custom divider content; overrides description |

<!-- Source: src/drawer/README.en-US.md; locale: en-US; page: /en/components/drawer/ -->

# Drawer

A side panel with declarative and programmatic APIs and cancellable before-close operations.

The default header associates its `title` slot with the dialog through a stable, unique title id. Text and render-function service titles follow the same rule; simultaneous service roots do not reuse title ids. An explicit `ariaLabel` takes precedence, and a plain `title` prop can still name the dialog. Hidden or fully custom headers do not reference unrendered titles; provide `ariaLabel` explicitly.

`DrawerConfig` supports the same `dir`, `ariaLabel`, `closeButtonAriaLabel` and `overlayAnimationName` as the component. Guard errors notify `onGuardError(error, action)`. Retired `beforeConfirm` / `beforeCancel` have been replaced by `beforeClose`; changing a guard does not reopen a closed drawer.

## Basic examples

### Basic

Example source: src/drawer/__demos__/basic.vue

```vue
<template>
  <c-button status="primary" @click="handleClick">Open Drawer</c-button>
  <c-drawer v-model:open="visible" :width="340" @confirm="handleConfirm" @cancel="handleCancel" unmount-on-close>
    <template #title>Title</template>
    <div>
      You can customize modal body text by the current situation. This modal will be closed immediately once you press
      the OK button.
    </div>
  </c-drawer>
</template>

<script lang="ts" setup>
import { ref } from 'vue'
const visible = ref(false)

const handleClick = () => {
  visible.value = true
}
const handleConfirm = () => {
  visible.value = false
}
const handleCancel = () => {
  visible.value = false
}
</script>
```

## Sizing and positioning

### Drawer size and placement

<!-- demo-config-notes:start -->
#### Configuration reference for this comparison

| Configuration | Purpose | Related examples |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `unmount-on-close` | Unmount content after the closing transition | Drawer size and placement |
| `placement` | Side of the containing area where the drawer appears, default right. It is not anchored to a button and does not perform popup collision flipping | Drawer size and placement |
| `popup-container` | Portal container | Popup Container |
<!-- demo-config-notes:end -->


Open each drawer separately to compare placement and occupied space. Nesting, containers and guards remain separate.

Example source: src/drawer/__demos__/position-size-comparison.vue

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { useDemoLocale } from "../../__demos__/locale";
const demoCopy = useDemoLocale("drawerPositionSizeComparison");
import { ref } from "vue";
import { proxyRefs as demoProxyRefs } from "vue";

const scene1 = demoProxyRefs(
  (() => {
    const visibleSmall = ref(false);

    const visibleMedium = ref(false);

    const visibleLarge = ref(false);

    const handleClickSmall = () => {
      visibleSmall.value = true;
    };

    const handleClickMedium = () => {
      visibleMedium.value = true;
    };

    const handleClickLarge = () => {
      visibleLarge.value = true;
    };

    const handleConfirm = () => {
      visibleSmall.value = false;
      visibleMedium.value = false;
      visibleLarge.value = false;
    };

    const handleCancel = () => {
      visibleSmall.value = false;
      visibleMedium.value = false;
      visibleLarge.value = false;
    };
    return {
      visibleSmall,
      visibleMedium,
      visibleLarge,
      handleClickSmall,
      handleClickMedium,
      handleClickLarge,
      handleConfirm,
      handleCancel,
    };
  })(),
);

const scene2 = demoProxyRefs(
  (() => {
    const visible = ref(false);

    const position = ref("right");

    const handleClick = () => {
      visible.value = true;
    };

    const handleConfirm = () => {
      visible.value = false;
    };

    const handleCancel = () => {
      visible.value = false;
    };
    return { visible, position, handleClick, handleConfirm, handleCancel };
  })(),
);
</script>

<template>
  <div class="demo-comparison">
    <section
      class="demo-comparison-case demo-comparison-case--1"
      data-comparison-scene="size"
    >
      <h4>{{ demoCopy.size }}</h4>
      <c-space>
        <c-button status="primary" @click="scene1.handleClickSmall"
          >sm Drawer</c-button
        >
        <c-button status="primary" @click="scene1.handleClickMedium"
          >md Drawer</c-button
        >
        <c-button status="primary" @click="scene1.handleClickLarge"
          >lg Drawer</c-button
        >
      </c-space>
      <c-drawer
        v-model:open="scene1.visibleSmall"
        :width="280"
        @confirm="scene1.handleConfirm"
        @cancel="scene1.handleCancel"
        unmount-on-close
      >
        <template #title>Title</template>
        <div>
          You can customize modal body text by the current situation. This modal
          will be closed immediately once you press the OK button.
        </div>
      </c-drawer>
      <c-drawer
        v-model:open="scene1.visibleMedium"
        :width="420"
        @confirm="scene1.handleConfirm"
        @cancel="scene1.handleCancel"
        unmount-on-close
      >
```

## Closing and async control

### Guard Protocol

Example source: src/drawer/__demos__/en-US/guard-protocol.vue

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { ref } from "vue";
import type { DrawerBeforeClose } from "@cedar-design/ui-vue";
const open = ref(false);
const mode = ref("promise");
const allowed = ref(true);
const status = ref("");
function waitForDecision(signal: AbortSignal) {
  return new Promise<boolean>((resolve) => {
    const abort = () => { clearTimeout(timer); signal.removeEventListener('abort', abort); resolve(false) }
    const timer = setTimeout(() => {
      signal.removeEventListener('abort', abort)
      if (signal.aborted) { resolve(false); return }
      status.value = allowed.value ? 'Allowed' : 'Rejected'
      resolve(allowed.value)
    }, 500)
    signal.addEventListener('abort', abort, { once: true })
    if (signal.aborted) abort()
  })
}
const check: DrawerBeforeClose = (payload, done, { signal }) => {
  status.value = `Waiting: ${payload.action}`
  const decision = waitForDecision(signal)
  if (mode.value === 'done') { void decision.then(value => done(value)); return }
  return decision
}
</script>
<template>
  <c-space direction="column" align="stretch">
    <c-form-item layout="vertical" label="Allow closing"><c-switch v-model="allowed" aria-label="Allow closing" /></c-form-item>
    <c-form-item layout="vertical" size="sm" label="mode">
      <c-radio-group
        aria-label="mode"
        v-model="mode"
        :options="[
          { value: 'promise', label: 'Promise' },
          { value: 'done', label: 'done callback' },
        ]"
        variant="button"
        size="sm"
      />
    </c-form-item>
    <c-button @click="open = true">Open</c-button>
    <c-drawer
      v-model:open="open"
      :before-close="check"
      @guard-error="status = 'Error'"
    >
      <p>The guard waits briefly before closing. Turn off the switch to reject once, then enable it here and retry.</p>
      <c-form-item layout="vertical" label="Allow closing"><c-switch v-model="allowed" aria-label="Allow closing inside drawer" /></c-form-item>
      <c-button @click="open = false; status = 'Closed directly'">Close directly</c-button>
      <p role="status">{{ status }}</p>
    </c-drawer>
    <p role="status">{{ status }}</p>
  </c-space>
</template>
```

Promise and done share a single completion state: false/done(false) rejects; true/done() allows; a resolved Promise&lt;void&gt; allows. The first completion wins. Errors emit guard-error; cancellation/unmount invalidates late completion. Synchronous void retains the callback protocol and waits for done on these close/confirm guards.


Cancellable hooks use `(payload, done, context)`: closure payloads contain `{ action }`, change/commit payloads contain `{ value, previousValue }`, and Popup uses `{ reason }`. Context provides `signal` and an optional original `event`. Return a boolean/Promise, or call done()/done(false). Synchronous void waits for done; Promise&lt;void&gt; allows the operation. First completion wins. Pending state controls loading/disabled automatically. Cancellation invalidates stale results. Button refs are not exposed.

## Reading direction

Inherits the nearest `dir="ltr|rtl"`, including runtime changes and local overrides. Drawer placement left/right remain physical sides, so entrance/exit follows the corresponding screen edge. Header, content and footer inherit reading direction. Direction changes do not commit or clear content.

## Usage notes

### Async operation feedback
Awaited before-* hooks show loading feedback and aria-busy. Rejection or failure restores interaction; repeated input does not start the same operation again. Ordinary event return Promises do not participate in loading.

## API

### Drawer Props

Dividers follow Card and are disabled by default. Enable them separately with `top-divider` and `bottom-divider`; each appears only when its corresponding header or footer exists. Service calls also support these options as `topDivider` and `bottomDivider`.

| --- | --- | --- | --- |

| bottom-divider | Divider between the content and footer | `boolean` | `false` |
| dir | Reading direction; inherits the source scope when omitted. Physical left/right placements keep their meaning. | `ReadingDirection` (`ltr` / `rtl`) | — |
| open **(v-model)** | Controlled visibility | `boolean` | - |

| placement | Side of the containing area where the drawer appears, default right. It is not anchored to a button and does not perform popup collision flipping | `'top' \| 'right' \| 'bottom' \| 'left'` | `'right'` |
| title | Title | `string` | - |
| overlay | Show the overlay | `boolean` | `true` |
| overlay-class | Custom overlay classes | `string` | - |

### Drawer Events

| Event | Description | Arguments |
| --- | --- | --- |
| update:open | Request a visibility update | `boolean` |
| confirm / cancel | Accepted confirm or cancel action | `Event` |
| open / close | Opening or closing begins | - |
| opened / closed | Opening or closing transition completes | - |
| click-overlay | Click the topmost overlay | `MouseEvent` |
| key-escape | Escape reaches the topmost drawer | `KeyboardEvent` |
| guard-error | Notifies when beforeClose throws or rejects; remains open and clears waiting | `(error: unknown, action: DrawerAction)` |

### Drawer Slots

`default`, `header`, `title`, `footer`. The `footer` slot receives `confirm`, `cancel` and `close` methods.

Footer confirm/cancel/close, built-in controls, overlay and Escape are beforeClose requests; instance confirm()/cancel() are guarded too. Instance close(), Drawer.open() handle close() and parent open=false are direct commands for completion or explicit exit, bypassing the guard without extra confirm/cancel. Controlled close() still only requests update:open(false); a rejecting parent remains authoritative. Direct closing aborts pending guards and invalidates late results. close() returns void and does not await leave; use closed/onClosed for completion.

Both Dialog implementations share this policy. Maple Popup close()/requestClose() and external model closing are awaitable guard requests returning `Promise<boolean>`; they are not Drawer direct-close commands. Popup destruction remains parent-owned. The demo Close directly action keeps an exit without changing Allow closing or pretending the guard approved.

### Imperative calls

`Drawer.open(config)` uses camelCase options such as `cancelButtonText`, `beforeClose` and `closeOnRouteChange`. Notifications use `onConfirm`, `onCancel`, `onOpen`, `onOpened`, `onClose`, `onClosed`, `onClickOverlay` and `onKeyEscape`.

```ts
import type { DrawerAction, DrawerConfig, DrawerProps } from '@cedar-design/ui-vue'
```

## CSS Variables

Built-in fade and four-direction slide disable transitions and initial displacement under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`. Adapt custom animations to the reduced-motion preference in your application.

Panel bg uses surface-raised; overlay-bg uses sys-color-scrim; header-text-color/content-text-color use content-primary, with the close button inheriting header-text-color; border-color uses border-default. Drawer keeps its existing geometry, motion and stacking defaults. Drawer is a Cedar component; Maple does not define empty same-name variables.

overlay-style sets instance scrim variables; drawer-style sets panel variables. These sibling nodes do not inherit variables from one another. Set global system theme variables on a real common ancestor. Explicit background props take precedence over variable consumption.

<!-- component-css-variables:start -->

Apply overrides to the rendered component root or the actual popup ancestor. For example, add the following class to that element and replace the value as needed:

```css
.component-theme {

}
```

Explicit inline styles and props that write the same CSS property take precedence over stylesheet defaults. After Teleport, ordinary CSS variables inherit from the actual mount location. When using ThemeProvider, follow its local-theme and popup configuration rules. Override the component variable directly for local styling; root-level aliases are not recalculated merely because a descendant system variable changes. Internal variables are not public APIs.

```vue
.ellipsis-demo { display: flex; flex-direction: column; align-items: flex-start; gap: 12px; }
.ellipsis-demo p { margin: 0; }
</style>
```

### Controlled expansion

Example source: src/ellipsis/__demos__/controlled.vue

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { ref } from 'vue'
const expanded = ref(false)
</script>

<template>
  <div class="ellipsis-demo">
    <c-button @click="expanded = !expanded">外部切换: {{ expanded }}</c-button>
    <c-ellipsis
      style="width: 240px; max-width: 100%"
      :line-clamp="2"
      expand-trigger="click"
      :tooltip="false"
      v-model:expand="expanded"
    >
      这是一段较长的说明文字，用于展示有限宽度内的省略效果。点击或使用键盘可以展开查看完整内容，再次操作可以收起。容器宽度改变时，文本会根据新的空间重新排版。
    </c-ellipsis>
  </div>
</template>

<style scoped>

.ellipsis-demo p { margin: 0; }
</style>
```

## Usage notes

### Rows and content boundaries

expand-trigger supports only click. Invalid values produce Vue prop validation warnings in development and do not enable button semantics, click or keyboard expansion. line-clamp accepts finite numbers or numeric strings of at least one row and floors decimals. Values below one, nonfinite values and invalid strings warn and fall back to ordinary single-line mode, clearing old multiline styles. Prefer plain text or inline content without independent interactions. The default Tooltip still does not detect actual overflow and remains focusable with Tab when enabled. Custom tooltip content and controlled expansion remain unchanged.

## API

### Ellipsis Props

| Prop | Description | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `expand` | Controlled expansion | `boolean` | `undefined` |
| `default-expand` | Initial uncontrolled expansion | `boolean` | `false` |
| `expand-trigger` | Enable click / Enter / Space toggling | `'click'` | `—` |
| `line-clamp` | Positive line count; omitted or invalid means single line | `number \| string` | `—` |
| `tooltip` | Tooltip configuration; false disables it | `boolean \| TooltipProps` | `true` |

Providing `expand` makes the component request updates from its parent rather than changing controlled state. When omitted, internal state is used, initialized once by `default-expand`. Tooltip follows its own width and trigger defaults; display does not depend on measured overflow. Touch callers can include `click` in `tooltip.trigger` explicitly. External class/style/width apply directly to the text node.

### Ellipsis Events / Slots

- `update:expand(expand: boolean)`: the new state requested by user interaction; external updates do not emit it.
- `default`: body text.
- `tooltip-content`: tooltip content. Without it, tooltip.content takes precedence, then body text; content is not concatenated twice.
- Keyboard: expandable text supports Enter / Space; tooltip-enabled text is focusable with Tab. No public instance methods.

## Types

```ts
import type { EllipsisProps, EllipsisInstance, EllipsisExpandTrigger } from '@cedar-design/ui-vue'
```

### Imports and event types

The subentry default component and the named components from the subentry and root are the same component. Props includes actual listener parameters. Events remain notifications and do not await returned Promises. Use only the documented instance methods.

```ts
import Ellipsis, { Ellipsis as NamedEllipsis } from '@cedar-design/ui-vue/ellipsis'
import { Ellipsis as RootEllipsis } from '@cedar-design/ui-vue'
import type { EllipsisProps, EllipsisInstance } from '@cedar-design/ui-vue'
import type { EllipsisProps as SubEllipsisProps } from '@cedar-design/ui-vue/ellipsis'
const options: EllipsisProps = { 'onUpdate:expand': (expanded: boolean) => String(expanded) }
```

<!-- component-css-variables:start -->

Use these variables to customize the component. Defaults may vary by the selector condition shown. Each variable applies to the corresponding size, variant and interaction states.

<div class="token-reference-table" style="max-width: 100%; overflow-x: auto;">

| Variable | Default / condition | Affected styles |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--c-ellipsis-focus-color` | `var(--c-sys-color-action-primary)` | `outline` |
| `--c-ellipsis-focus-offset` | `2px` | `outline-offset` |
| `--c-ellipsis-focus-width` | `2px` | `outline` |

</div>

```css

  --c-ellipsis-focus-color: var(--c-sys-color-action-primary);
}
```

Explicit inline styles and props that write the same CSS property take precedence over stylesheet defaults. After Teleport, ordinary CSS variables inherit from the actual mount location. When using ThemeProvider, follow its local-theme and popup configuration rules. Override the component variable directly for local styling; root-level aliases are not recalculated merely because a descendant system variable changes. Internal variables are not public APIs.

| Slot | Description | Prop |

## Types

The component exports the following types

```ts
import type { EmptyImageSize, EmptyProps } from '@cedar-design/ui-vue'
```

ConfigProvider's `empty` slot can replace Empty content when no custom content is supplied; it is not a public Empty prop.

Local default, image and extra slots, or nonempty image-url/description, take precedence over the global replacement, including dynamic additions and removals. A global replacement owns the entire Empty content: show-icon, show-description and image-size control only the local template and do not rewrite provider nodes. Bubbling clicks from replacement content emit Empty click once, including multiple roots and nested Empty, with recursion protection.

# Field Decorator

Start with the basic example, then compare related settings before moving to controlled, asynchronous or combined use cases.

Focused inputs do not draw an additional outer outline. Existing variant borders, underlines or backgrounds provide focus feedback. This applies to consumers including Input, Textarea, Date and Time.

Input, textarea and numeric-input carets use `currentColor`, matching the current input text. Error state does not override caret color separately.

`--c-field-caret-color` defaults to `currentColor` and controls Input, InputNumber and Textarea carets without changing text color.

## Basic examples

### Control Sizes

## Loading and waiting

### Shared field loading

`loading` displays the shared field indicator. `loading-mode` is `default` (indicator) or `line` (an indeterminate bottom line); it defaults to `default`. Rendering belongs to FieldDecorator. Loading does not implicitly disable editing or change readonly. Set those states separately.

 Example source: src/field-decorator/__demos__/loading.vue

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { ref } from 'vue'
const busy = ref(true)
const mode = ref<'default' | 'line'>('line')
const text = ref('加载时仍可编辑')
</script>
<template>
  <c-space direction="column" :size="16">
    <c-space><c-switch v-model="busy" />加载状态</c-space>
    <c-radio-group v-model="mode" :options="['default', 'line']" variant="button" aria-label="字段加载布局" />
    <c-form layout="vertical">
      <c-form-item label="文本"><c-input v-model="text" :loading="busy" :loading-mode="mode" /></c-form-item>
      <c-form-item label="多行文本"><c-textarea v-model="text" :loading="busy" :loading-mode="mode" /></c-form-item>
      <c-form-item label="选择"><c-select edit-mode="direct" :options="[{ label: '选项', value: 'a' }]" :loading="busy" :loading-mode="mode" /></c-form-item>
      <c-form-item label="日期"><c-date edit-mode="direct" :loading="busy" :loading-mode="mode" /></c-form-item>
    </c-form>
    <p>加载展示由同一个 FieldDecorator 实现，不隐式禁用输入；需要禁止操作时单独设置 disabled 或 readonly。</p>
  </c-space>
</template>
```

## Usage notes

### Error and disabled borders

Changing `tag` rebinds size observation to the current root and content nodes. KeepAlive deactivation releases observation and queued measurements; a frame from an earlier activation cannot change current layout.

## API

### FieldDecorator Props

The floating hint leaves a gap in the outline, aligned with the content column. Adjust the space on either side through `hint-space`.

| Prop | Type | Default / meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `loading` | `boolean` | `false`; show loading without changing disabled or readonly |
| `loading-mode` | `'default' \| 'line'` | `default`; indicator or bottom progress line |
| `tag` | `'div' \| 'span'` | `div`; wrapper element |
| `value` | `unknown` | Checks only whether content is empty |
| `id` | `string` | Native control id associated with the floating label |
| `title` | `string` | Native title tooltip |
| `size` | `ComponentSize`<br>`'xs' \| 'sm' \| 'md' \| 'lg' \| 'xl'` | `md`; implements all five sizes |
| `variant` | `'outline' \| 'filled' \| 'standard'` | `outline` |
| `placeholder` | `string` | Floating label text |
| `hint` | `boolean` | `false` |
| `hint-center` | `boolean` | `true`; use false for multiline controls |
| `line` | `boolean` | `true`; whether to show a border or underline |
| `focused` | `boolean` | Consumer-supplied focus state |
| `composing` | `boolean` | Keep the label floated during IME composition |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | Consumer-supplied disabled state after merging Form / Group state |
| `readonly` | `boolean` | Consumer-supplied read-only state after merging Form / Group state |
| `error` | `boolean` | Consumer-supplied error state after merging Form / Group state |
| `clearable` | `boolean` | `false`; whether clearing is allowed |
| `text-color` | `string` | Custom per-instance text color; prefer tokens for static themes |
| `focus-color` | `string` | Custom per-instance focused color; prefer tokens for static themes |
| `blur-color` | `string` | Custom per-instance unfocused color; prefer tokens for static themes |
| `cursor` | `string` | Custom caret |

### FieldDecorator Slots / Events

`default` contains a native input, tags or display content. `prefix` / `suffix` contain adornments. `clear-icon` receives `clear(event?)`; a custom button should call it. Clearing does not bubble to open the selection panel.

`loading-icon` replaces the indicator icon only when `loading=true` and `loading-mode=default`; `line` mode renders no icon. `fieldLoadingProps` contains `loading` and `loadingMode`; `fieldLoadingModes`, `FieldLoadingMode`, and `FieldLoadingProps` are exported from the component and root entry points.

`clear(event)` asks the consumer to update the value; `mousedown(event)` lets the consumer manage focus. The wrapper does not mutate the model itself.

Style semantics use `--c-field-*` / `--mp-field-*`, declared in each library's `style/token.less`. Implementations are not shared across libraries. Consumers must not draw a second border.

### Error and disabled borders

Prefix these suffixes with `--c-field-` / `--mp-field-`: `variant-outline-border-color-error` controls outline error borders; `variant-standard-line-color-error` controls standard error underlines; `variant-standard-line-color-disabled` controls standard disabled underlines and defaults to system border-subtle. # Filter Form

Start with the basic example, then compare related settings before moving to controlled, asynchronous or combined use cases.

## Basic examples

### Basic usage

Actions reserve space according to their actual width and keep the expand/collapse control and action buttons on one line. When collapsed, actions sit at the right of the first row. When expanded, fields use the full column layout and actions sit at the right of the last row, moving to a new row if needed. One- and two-column layouts retain a separate action row.

Preview configuration: `v-model:collapsed="collapsed"`, `:fields="fields"`, `:rules="rules"`.

Example source: src/filter-form/__demos__/basic.vue

```vue
<template>
  <c-filter-form
    v-model="filter"
    v-model:collapsed="collapsed"
    :fields="fields"
    :rules="rules"
  >
    <template #actions>
      <c-button variant="outline" :elevation="false" @click="reset">重置</c-button>
      <c-button status="primary" :elevation="false" @click="search">搜索</c-button>
    </template>
  </c-filter-form>
  <pre class="demo-filter-json">{{ filter }}</pre>
  <p role="status">{{ result }}</p>
</template>

<script lang="ts" setup>
import { ref } from 'vue'
import {
  Cascader,
  DateRange,
  Input,
  Select,
  type FilterFormField,
} from '@cedar-design/ui-vue'

const collapsed = ref(true)
const result = ref('尚未搜索')
const filter = ref<Record<string, unknown>>({
  region: undefined,
  status: undefined,
  keyword: '',
  timeRange: undefined,
})

const options = {
  status: [
    { label: '待处理', value: 'pending' },
    { label: '进行中', value: 'doing' },
    { label: '已完成', value: 'done' },
  ],
  owner: [
    { label: '张三', value: 'zhang' },
    { label: '李四', value: 'li' },
  ],
}

const rules = {
  keyword: [{ maxLength: 50, message: '最多 50 个字符' }],
}

const fields: FilterFormField[] = [
  {
    component: Cascader,
    field: 'region',
    label: '地区',
    props: {
      clearable: true,
      placeholder: '请选择地区',
      pathMode: true,
      variant: 'outline',
      options: [
        {
          value: 'beijing',
          label: '北京',
          children: [
            { value: 'chaoyang', label: '朝阳' },
            { value: 'haidian', label: '海淀' },
          ],
        },
        {
          value: 'shanghai',
          label: '上海',
          children: [{ value: 'huangpu', label: '黄浦' }],
        },
      ],
    },
  },
  {
    component: Select,
    field: 'status',
    label: '状态',
    props: { variant: 'outline', clearable: true, placeholder: '全部', options: options.status },
  },
  {
    component: Select,
    field: 'owner',
    label: '负责人',
    props: { variant: 'outline', clearable: true, placeholder: '全部', options: options.owner },
  },
  {
    component: Input,
    field: 'keyword',
    label: '关键词',
    autoEmitChange: false,
    props: { variant: 'outline', clearable: true, placeholder: '回车或失焦触发' },
  },
  {
    component: DateRange,
    field: 'timeRange',
    label: '时间范围',
    gridItemProps: { span: 2 },
    props: { variant: 'outline', valueFormat: 'timestamp', clearable: true, showTime: true },
  },
]

function search() {
  result.value = `搜索条件：${JSON.stringify(filter.value)}`
}

function reset() {
  result.value = '已重置'
  filter.value = {
    region: undefined,
    status: undefined,
    keyword: '',
    timeRange: undefined,
  }
}
</script>

<style scoped>
.demo-filter-json {
```

## Async and dynamic data

### Async Options

<!-- demo-config-notes:start -->
#### Configuration reference for this comparison

| Configuration | Purpose | Related examples |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `fields` | Filter-item schema | Async Options |
| `collapsible` | Whether expanding/collapsing is enabled | Async Options |
<!-- demo-config-notes:end -->


Preview configuration: `:fields="fields"`, `:collapsed="false"`, `:collapsible="false"`.

Example source: src/filter-form/__demos__/async-options.vue

```vue
<template>
  <c-space direction="column" style="width: 100%">
    <c-alert>
      异步加载选项后，通过 computed 更新字段的 props.options。
    </c-alert>
    <c-filter-form
      v-model="filter"
      :fields="fields"
      :collapsed="false"
      :collapsible="false"
    >
      <template #actions>
        <c-space>
          <c-button @click="reset">重置</c-button>
          <c-button status="primary" @click="search">搜索</c-button>
        </c-space>
      </template>
    </c-filter-form>
  </c-space>
  <p role="status">{{ result }}</p>
</template>

<script lang="ts" setup>
import { computed, onMounted, onUnmounted, ref } from 'vue'
import {
  Input,
  Select,
  type FilterFormField,
} from '@cedar-design/ui-vue'

const filter = ref<Record<string, unknown>>({
  category: undefined,
  tag: undefined,
  name: '',
})

const options = ref<Record<string, unknown>>({
  category: [],
  tag: [],
})

const fields = computed<FilterFormField[]>(() => [
  {
    component: Select,
    field: 'category',
    label: '分类',
    props: { clearable: true, placeholder: '请选择', options: options.value.category },
  },
  {
    component: Select,
    field: 'tag',
    label: '标签',
    props: { clearable: true, multiple: true, placeholder: '请选择', options: options.value.tag },
  },
  {
    component: Input,
    field: 'name',
    label: '名称',
    props: { clearable: true },
  },
])

let timer: ReturnType<typeof setTimeout>
onUnmounted(() => clearTimeout(timer))

onMounted(() => {
  timer = setTimeout(() => {
    options.value = {
      category: [
        { label: '组件', value: 'component' },
        { label: '工具', value: 'tool' },
      ],
      tag: [
        { label: '推荐', value: 'hot' },
        { label: '新品', value: 'new' },
      ],
    }
  }, 800)
})

const result = ref('尚未搜索')
function search() {
  result.value = `搜索条件：${JSON.stringify(filter.value)}`
}

function reset() {
  filter.value = {
    category: undefined,
    tag: undefined,
    name: '',
  }
}
</script>
```

## API

### Value and default value

Use ordinary `v-model`. `modelValue` is the filter-fields object. `defaultValue` initializes uncontrolled state once; later changes do not reset it. Explicit binding takes precedence, and initialization emits no `update:modelValue`.

Input updates the internal mirror before notifying the parent. If the parent does not accept the update, the input remains visible locally; a different external model replaces the mirror. `collapsed` likewise updates locally before notification and accepts later external changes. To reject an input, explicitly provide a new model object.

### FilterForm Props

| Prop | Description | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| model-value **(v-model)** | Form values; uses default-value when omitted | `Record<string, unknown>` | `undefined` |
| default-value | Initial values read only at creation | `Record<string, unknown>` | `{}` |
| fields | Filter-item schema | `FilterFormField[]` | `[]` |
| field-map | Optional field-component registry | `FilterFormFieldMap` | `{}` |
| rules | Forwarded Form validation rules | object | - |
| collapsed **(v-model)** | Whether to collapse extra items | boolean | `true` |
| collapsible | Whether expanding/collapsing is enabled | boolean | `true` |
| cols | Responsive column count | number \| object | `{ xs:1, sm:2, md:3, lg:3, xl:4, xxl:5 }` |
| grid-props | Forwarded Grid properties, taking precedence over matching container settings | `Record<string, unknown>` | - |
| change-debounce | change debounce in milliseconds; 0 notifies immediately; negative or nonfinite values fall back to 500 | number | `500` |

### FilterFormFieldRegistration Events

| Event | Description | Arguments |
| --- | --- | --- |
| update:model-value | Immediate value snapshot notification on input | `(value: Record<string, unknown>) => void` |
| update:collapsed | Local expand/collapse notification | `(collapsed: boolean) => void` |
| change | Debounced input notification and immediate Enter notification; with autoEmitChange=false, blur or Enter notifies | `(value: Record<string, unknown>, field: string) => void` |

Events are notifications only; listener Promises are not collected and do not drive loading state.

### FilterFormFieldRegistration Slots

| Slot | Description |
| --- | --- |
| actions | Actions such as search/reset beside expand/collapse; no scoped arguments; available with collapsible=false |

### FilterFormFieldRegistration Instance Properties

| Prop | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| formRef | `FormInstance \| undefined` | Inner Form instance after mounting; supports Form methods such as validate, clearValidate and resetFields |

`formRef` is an instance property. Calling the inner Form `resetFields` restores its recorded initial values locally without emitting FilterForm `update:modelValue` or `change`. To reset the complete filter, replace the bound business model; for example:

```ts
const makeInitialModel = () => ({ keyword: '', createdAt: new Date() })
const model = ref(makeInitialModel())
const resetFilters = () => { model.value = makeInitialModel() }
```

Use search/reset buttons with `type="button"` in `actions` and manage the model and queries in business handlers. The container exposes no additional reset/search methods or task execution entry point.

## Types

### FilterFormField

| Prop | Description | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| component | Vue component or a key in `fieldMap` | `string \| Component` | - |
| field | Form field path | string | - |
| label | Label | string | - |
| visible | Whether to render | boolean | `true` |
| autoEmitChange | Whether input emits change while editing | boolean | `true` |
| props | Props forwarded to the field component | object | - |
| gridItemProps | GridItem props | object | - |
| formItemProps | FormItem props | object | - |

### FilterFormFieldRegistration

| Prop | Description | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| component | Field component | Component | - |
| defaultProps | Default props | object | - |

Field properties merge in order: registration `defaultProps`, `field` `props`, then the container-owned `modelValue`, with later values taking precedence. `gridItemProps` passes through to GridItem. `formItemProps` can override the FormItem `field` and `label`, but does not change the schema `field` path used for model writes. `grid-props` can also override Grid settings such as `cols` and `collapsed`; avoid conflicting container state.

```ts
import type {
  FilterFormProps,
  FilterFormInstance,
  FilterFormEmits,
  FilterFormSlots,
  FilterFormExpose,
  FilterFormField,
  FilterFormFieldMap,
  FilterFormFieldRegistration,
} from '@cedar-design/ui-vue'
```

Grid column spacing is controlled by `grid-props.colGap` in numeric px. There is no same-name CSS override, ensuring numerical Grid measurements match actual spacing.

Changing changeDebounce reschedules the pending snapshot using the new delay; zero notifies immediately. Enter cancels the pending task before notifying the current value. External reset or a different model replacement cancels stale snapshots, while accepting the same update:modelValue proposal does not cancel change. KeepAlive deactivation and unmount cancel pending notifications; reactivation accepts new input.

Filter models use the existing Form data-snapshot policy. Date values, plain objects and arrays are copied independently; Map, Set, BigInt and cyclic references retain their data kinds instead of converting dates to strings or collections to empty objects. Mutating a plain-object or Date event snapshot does not alter the parent model or later internal snapshots. Identity semantics such as Map keys follow the existing Form policy. Functions, DOM nodes, WeakMap/WeakSet, Promises and instances with private state are outside the deeply isolated filter-data contract.

field supports the same dot and bracket paths as FormItem. Writes create missing object containers and preserve sibling fields. Prebuild array containers in default-value or model-value when an array is required. Existing intermediate values must be objects or arrays; input does not replace incompatible scalar structures. Existing local-mirror, debounce and accepted-echo behavior for model updates and change notifications is preserved.

## CSS Variables
