### IconPark custom projects

You can use the **SVG Symbol JS** or **Web Component JS** generated by an IconPark custom project directly. Exporting individual SVG files or generating a Vue component for every icon is optional. These are SVG resource mechanisms, separate from loading text fonts with `@font-face`.

The public `@icon-park/vue-next` component package and your custom project's JS are separate resource sources. Installing the public package does not automatically include your team's uploaded or maintained icons.

| Approach | Resource source | Rendering | Loading unit |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| SVG Symbol JS | Custom project script | `svg` / `use` in the default slot | The icon collection in that file |
| Web Component JS | Custom project script | A custom element in the default slot | Depends on the generated implementation; do not assume individual icon loading |
| Individual SVG Vue components | Local files or a component package | Vue components in the default slot | Imported modules, subject to build configuration |

SVG Symbol is a suitable starting point: it reuses the Icon container without configuring Vue custom element recognition.

**Current API:** `CIcon` does not have a `symbol` prop and does not download, register or inject IconPark resources. The examples below use the existing default slot. `name` only resolves icon components registered in the current Vue application; it does not resolve Symbol IDs or Web Component icon names. Default slot content takes precedence over `name`.

#### SVG Symbol: load the project script

Copy the **SVG Symbol** script URL from your custom project and load it once in the application's HTML entry, such as `index.html` in a Vite application:

```html
<!-- Example path: replace with your project URL or a locally deployed copy -->
<script src="/icons/project-symbol.js" defer></script>
```

After execution, the script should inject an SVG collection containing `symbol` nodes into the page. The application owns the resource URL and decides whether to use a remote URL or a deployed static file. The component library does not embed business project URLs. Load the script type you chose; using the same collection does not require loading both script variants.

#### SVG Symbol: reference an icon

Suppose the script injects `<symbol id="project-home" viewBox="0 0 48 48">`. You can render it as follows. Paths and IDs in these examples are placeholders; use the values in your generated output.

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { Icon as CIcon } from '@cedar-design/ui-vue'
import '@cedar-design/ui-vue/icon/style'
</script>

<template>
  <c-icon :size="24" color="#1677ff">
    <svg width="1em" height="1em" aria-hidden="true">
      <use href="#project-home" />
    </svg>
  </c-icon>
</template>
```

`href` uses the complete Symbol ID with a leading `#`. Display names, the library's `name` prop and IconPark icon names may differ from the Symbol ID. Do not invent or strip prefixes; inspect `symbol[id]` in developer tools. This references resources injected into the current page: do not use `href="project.js#project-home"`.

`size` sets the container's font size, and the inner SVG follows it through `1em`. `rotate` and `spin` affect the entire container. Without an explicit `size`, normal Icon size inheritance applies. Preserve the generated Symbol's `viewBox` to avoid clipping or incorrect scaling.

#### An application wrapper for shorter usage

Create an application component named `ProjectIcon.vue` if you want to pass an ID as a prop. This requires neither a library API change nor a generated Vue file for each icon:

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { Icon as CIcon } from '@cedar-design/ui-vue'
import '@cedar-design/ui-vue/icon/style'

defineProps<{ symbol: string }>()
</script>

<template>
  <c-icon>
    <svg width="1em" height="1em" aria-hidden="true">
      <use :href="`#${symbol}`" />
    </svg>
  </c-icon>
</template>
```

Use it in the application:

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import ProjectIcon from './ProjectIcon.vue'
</script>

<template>
  <ProjectIcon symbol="project-home" :size="24" color="#1677ff" />
</template>
```

Here, `symbol` belongs to the application wrapper and excludes `#`. Undeclared attributes such as `size`, `color`, `rotate` and `spin` fall through to the single `CIcon` root. Forward `$attrs` explicitly if you add multiple roots or disable `inheritAttrs`. The existing `transition` prop only animates `CIcon`'s `name` changes; it does not animate Symbol reference changes inside the slot.

#### Web Component: script and compiler configuration

Alternatively, load your project's **Web Component JS** and place its registered element in the slot. The following assumes the generated element is named `iconpark-icon` and uses a `name` attribute. Confirm element names, attributes and theme support against your project's generated usage instructions.

```html
<!-- Application HTML entry; use the Web Component variant here -->
<script src="/icons/project-web-component.js" defer></script>
```

Configure the build that compiles Vue SFCs containing this tag to recognize the custom element. For Vite:

```ts
import { defineConfig } from 'vite'
import vue from '@vitejs/plugin-vue'

export default defineConfig({
  plugins: [
    vue({
      template: {
        compilerOptions: {
          isCustomElement: (tag) => tag === 'iconpark-icon',
        },
      },
    }),
  ],
})
```

Merge this into the existing Vue plugin configuration instead of adding a duplicate plugin. `isCustomElement` is a compile-time setting; setting only `app.config.compilerOptions` does not replace this configuration when using a build tool. Configure the library build when the tag is wrapped inside library source, or the application build when application source uses the tag directly.

```vue
<template>
  <c-icon :size="24" color="#1677ff">
    <iconpark-icon name="project-home" size="1em"></iconpark-icon>
  </c-icon>
</template>
```

This example uses the application's existing `c-icon` import or registration. The outer `CIcon` does not automatically forward theme, stroke width or other attributes to slot content. Set supported attributes directly on the custom element. If it uses Shadow DOM, external `.c-icon svg` rules cannot directly style its inner SVG; use the element's supported attributes, inherited styles or CSS variables.

#### Size, color and multicolor icons

| Setting | Behavior and limitations |
| --- | --- |
| `size` | Symbol examples inherit through `1em`; check the Web Component's own sizing API |
| `color` | Works only when the graphic uses `currentColor` or supports corresponding inheritance |
| Fixed `fill` / `stroke` | Colors embedded in the graphic are not automatically overridden by the container's `color` |
| Multicolor icons | Preserve their colors; avoid forcing a single `fill` or `stroke` across all paths |
| Themes and stroke width | Depend on generated output; public Vue icon package props do not automatically apply to project scripts |

#### On-demand loading and bundle size

Importing components on demand and loading icon resources are independent. Slot usage does not make `CIcon` depend on the entire IconPark package, and existing Resolver imports still work. The Resolver does not load resources based on a `use` ID.

A Symbol script that injects a collection loads that entire file. If it contains 200 icons and a page references three, all 200 are still downloaded and injected. `href="#project-home"` selects a graphic; it does not request an individual icon. A static script is outside the application's module tree-shaking analysis, and string IDs do not automatically remove unused Symbols.

| Goal | Approach |
| --- | --- |
| Small collection reused across pages | Load once at application entry and reuse the browser cache by file version |
| Large collection with distinct business modules | Split resources into shared and module collections; load each when its route or module needs it |
| Render the page before loading icons | Manage loading, failure and placeholder states in the application; show icons when resources are ready |
| Require individual icons to participate in tree shaking | Use separate SVG modules or Vue components and verify package exports and actual build output |

Remote JS is outside the library's npm package but still contributes to application download size. Updating the project requires updating generated resources and their cache versions. The component library's build size alone does not describe page cost.

#### Loading order, SSR and accessibility

- Make static resources available when icons are needed. For dynamic loading, wait for successful script execution. For Web Components, `customElements.whenDefined('iconpark-icon')` can additionally wait for registration; it neither downloads the script nor automatically settles on a resource loading failure.
- Load each resource once per application instead of inserting a script on every component mount. Keep Symbol IDs unique across collections to avoid conflicting references.
- Do not execute scripts requiring `window`, `document` or `customElements` on the server. Use HTML scripts or client lifecycle loading. When rendering conditionally, keep server and initial client placeholders consistent. Icons remain invisible until their resources exist; strict first-paint requirements need server-inlined Symbols or individual SVGs.
- Use `aria-hidden="true"` for decorative SVGs. Give standalone informative SVGs `role="img"` and an accessible name. Give icon-only buttons an `aria-label` on the button itself.

#### Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Check |
| --- | --- |
| Blank icon | Successful script execution, correct script variant, exact ID and nonzero container size |
| `Failed to resolve component: iconpark-icon` | Compile-time `isCustomElement` configuration for the source containing the tag |
| Color does not change | Fixed graphic colors or the Web Component's supported color interface |
| Size does not follow `CIcon` | Inner SVG / element sizing through `1em` and any fixed pixel dimensions |
| Old icon after a project update | Current script version and browser / CDN caching |
| Works locally but fails after deployment | Resource base paths, network requests, CSP `script-src` and script execution errors |
| Wrong icon with multiple collections | Symbol ID collisions, duplicate scripts and the unique IDs in actual output |

References: [Vue and Web Components](https://vuejs.org/guide/extras/web-components), [SVG use element](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/SVG/Reference/Element/use).

### Dynamic Name

- `size`: Controls the component size.

Example source: src/icon/__demos__/dynamic-name.vue

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { getCurrentInstance, ref } from "vue";
import {
  IconArrowLeft,
  IconArrowRight,
  IconCheckCircle,
  IconInfoCircle,
  IconRefresh,
  IconSearch,
} from "@cedar-design/icons-vue";
const iconName = ref("arrow-left");
const app = getCurrentInstance()?.appContext.app;
const icons = {
  IconArrowLeft,
  IconArrowRight,
  IconCheckCircle,
  IconInfoCircle,
  IconRefresh,
  IconSearch,
};
for (const [name, component] of Object.entries(icons)) {
  if (app && !app.component(name)) {
    app.component(name, component);
  }
}
function toggle() {
  iconName.value =
    iconName.value === "arrow-left" ? "arrow-right" : "arrow-left";
}
</script>
<template>
  <p>
    name 是已注册图标的名称。本例提供
    arrow-left、arrow-right、check-circle、info-circle、refresh、search；默认插槽存在时优先显示插槽内容。
  </p>
  <div class="icon-name-demo">
    <c-space wrap align="center" :size="24">
      <c-button @click="toggle">切换图标</c-button>
      <c-icon :name="iconName" :size="32" :transition="300" />
    </c-space>
  </div>
</template>
```

## API

### Standalone icon styles and usage boundaries

Resolver auto-imports include the lightweight rotation styles for standalone icons. With `importStyle: false`, applications must import those styles. The UI Icon style entry also includes them; loading every icon is unnecessary.

When manually importing standalone SVG components, import this stylesheet once in your application entry when using `spin`:

```ts
import '@cedar-design/icons-vue/style.css'
```

`rotate` and `spin` can be combined; built-in rotation respects reduced motion. `transition` controls registered-name changes only, using milliseconds as a number or numeric string, such as `200` / `"200"`; it does not parse `"200ms"` / `"1s"`. The default slot owns content and skips name-`transition` animation. Removing it immediately shows the latest name. Custom `animation-class` should avoid overriding the `transform` used for continuous rotation and should implement reduced-motion behavior.

`name` only resolves icons explicitly registered in the current application before rendering; it does not download resources. Registration after mount does not refresh an existing icon automatically. The container's native `title` is not forwarded to its SVG. Set `title` on standalone icons for image naming, and use an accessibly named Button for actions. `click` is a notification supporting Vue `.once`; listener Promises do not manage waiting. `stroke-*` affects strokes only; filled or fixed multicolor artwork may not respond.


### Icon Props

| Prop | Description | Type | Default |
| --------------- | ---------------------- | ---------------- | ------ |
| name | Explicitly registered icon name | string | - |
| size | `inherit` | number \| string | - |
| color | Icon color | string | - |
| rotate | Rotation angle | number | - |
| spin | Whether to rotate continuously | boolean | false |
| transition | Name-change animation duration in ms | number \| string | 0 |
| animation-class | Custom transition animation class | string | - |

### IconXxx Props

| Prop | Description | Type | Default |
| --------------- | ---------- | ------------------------------------------ | ------- |
| size | `inherit` | number \| string | - |
| color | Icon color | string | - |
| rotate | Rotation angle | number | - |
| spin | Whether to rotate | boolean | false |
| title | Accessible title | string | - |
| stroke-width | Stroke width | number | 4 |
| stroke-linecap | Stroke line cap | 'butt' \| 'round' \| 'square' | 'butt' |
| stroke-linejoin | Stroke line join | 'bevel' \| 'inherit' \| 'miter' \| 'round' | 'miter' |

## Usage notes



Only resolves icons registered in the current application. Repeated name changes display the latest requested icon, and unmounting stops pending switches.

Icons inherit the host font size on both platforms. For a fixed 20px icon, set size="20" or icon-size explicitly. The size prop overrides the variable; color inherits from the host by default.

## CSS Variables

<!-- component-css-variables:start -->

Use these variables to customize the component. Defaults may vary by the selector condition shown. Each variable applies to the corresponding size, variant and interaction states.

<div class="token-reference-table" style="max-width: 100%; overflow-x: auto;">

| Variable | Default / condition | Affected styles |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--c-icon-size` | `inherit` | `font-size` |
| `--c-icon-spin-duration` | `1s` | `animation` |

</div>

Apply overrides to the rendered component root or the actual popup ancestor. For example, add the following class to that element and replace the value as needed:

```css
.component-theme {
  --c-icon-size: inherit;
}
```

Explicit inline styles and props that write the same CSS property take precedence over stylesheet defaults. After Teleport, ordinary CSS variables inherit from the actual mount location. When using ThemeProvider, follow its local-theme and popup configuration rules. Override the component variable directly for local styling; root-level aliases are not recalculated merely because a descendant system variable changes. Internal variables are not public APIs.

<!-- component-css-variables:end -->

### Motion

Built-in motion follows prefers-reduced-motion: reduce: content and state feedback remain, while decorative spinning, shimmer and ripples stop. Icon name changes display the latest value immediately and cancel unfinished phases, keeping CSS and JS durations aligned. Callers must adapt custom animation classes. Ripple duration/cleanup follows Ripple documentation; its historical 250ms rule is not an Icon duration limit.

### Imperative Preview

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
const images = ['/cat.jpg', '/cat2.jpg']
let handle: { next: () => void; close: () => void } | undefined

function previewSingle() {
  imagePreview(images[0])
}

function previewMultiple() {
  handle = imagePreview({ images, modelValue: 1 })
}

function next() {
  handle?.next()
}

function close() {
  handle?.close()
}
</script>

<template>
```

## Lifecycle

### Track Lifecycle

Preview configuration: `v-model:open="open"`, `:images="images"`, `:loop="loop"`, `name="Replace images / 换图"`.

Example source: src/image/__demos__/track-lifecycle.vue

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { useDemoLocale as useInlineDemoLocale } from "../../__demos__/locale";
const inlineCopy = useInlineDemoLocale("imageTrackLifecycleInline");

import { ImagePreviewAction as CImagePreviewAction } from "../index";

import { ref } from "vue";
const active = ref(true);
const open = ref(false);
const current = ref(1);
const loop = ref(true);
const images = ref(["/cat.jpg", "/cat2.jpg"]);
function replaceImages() {
  images.value = [...images.value].reverse();
}
</script>
<template>
  <div>
    <c-button @click="open = true">{{ inlineCopy.open }}</c-button>
    <c-button @click="active = !active">{{ inlineCopy.activate }}</c-button>
    <c-button @click="loop = !loop">{{ inlineCopy.loop }}</c-button>
    <c-button @click="replaceImages">{{ inlineCopy.replaceImages }}</c-button>
    <p>
      {{ inlineCopy.current }} {{ current }}. Navigate across the loop edge;
      deactivate, close or replace images. Old work must not replay.
    </p>
    <KeepAlive>
      <c-image-preview-group
        v-if="active"
        v-model:open="open"
        v-model="current"
        :images="images"
        :loop="loop"
      >
        <template #actions>
          <c-image-preview-action
            :name="inlineCopy.replaceImages2"
            @click="replaceImages"
            >换图</c-image-preview-action
          >
          <c-image-preview-action
            :name="inlineCopy.deactivate"
            @click="active = false"
            >停用</c-image-preview-action
          >
        </template>
      </c-image-preview-group>
    </KeepAlive>
  </div>
</template>
```

### Controller Lifecycle

Preview configuration: `v-model:open="open"`, `:src="source"`, `interaction="touch"`, `:keyboard="true"`.

Example source: src/image/__demos__/controller-lifecycle.vue

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { useDemoLocale as useInlineDemoLocale } from "../../__demos__/locale";
const inlineCopy = useInlineDemoLocale("imageControllerLifecycleInline");

import { ImagePreviewAction as CImagePreviewAction } from "../index";

import { ref } from "vue";
const open = ref(false);
const active = ref(true);
const source = ref("/cat.jpg");
const presses = ref(0);
const switchSource = () => {
  source.value = source.value === "/cat.jpg" ? "/cat2.jpg" : "/cat.jpg";
};
</script>
<template>
  <div>
    <c-button @click="open = true">{{ inlineCopy.open }}</c-button>
    <c-button @click="active = !active">{{ inlineCopy.activate }}</c-button>
    <p>
      {{ inlineCopy.longPresses }} {{ presses }}. Cancel or deactivate; old
      input must not replay.
    </p>
    <KeepAlive>
      <c-image-preview
        v-if="active"
        v-model:open="open"
        :src="source"
        interaction="touch"
        :keyboard="true"
        @long-press="presses++"
      >
        <template #actions>
          <c-image-preview-action
            :name="inlineCopy.switchSource"
            @click="switchSource"
            >换图</c-image-preview-action
          >
          <c-image-preview-action
            :name="inlineCopy.deactivate"
            @click="active = false"
            >停用</c-image-preview-action
          >
        </template>
      </c-image-preview>
    </KeepAlive>
  </div>
</template>
```

## Reading direction

Inherits the nearest `dir="ltr|rtl"`, including runtime changes and local overrides. Previous/next preview navigation, horizontal keys and swipes follow reading direction without reversing the value array. Direction changes cancel unfinished gestures while preserving the current image, zoom and rotation. Images and zoomed drag coordinates are not mirrored automatically. Image indices retain LTR numeric display.

## API

ImagePreviewGroup binds a one-based image number through ordinary `v-model`; `defaultValue` initializes the uncontrolled index. Panel opening uses `v-model:open` and `defaultOpen` independently. Programmatic preview options also use modelValue/`defaultValue` and onUpdate:modelValue.

### Image Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| src | string | - | Thumbnail source |
| preview-src | string | - | Preview URL, falling back to src |
| fallback-src | string | - | One fallback after a source error |
| width | string \| number | - | Root width; numbers are px |
| height | string \| number | - | Root height; numbers are px |
| object-fit | ImageFit | fill | Image fitting mode |
| object-position | string | 50% 50% | Native object position |
| radius | string \| number | 0 | Root border radius |
| alt | string | - | Image alternative text; empty is preserved |
| title | string | - | Image title and footer title |
| description | string | - | Footer text and alt fallback |
| load-description | string | - | Last alt fallback |
| hide-footer | boolean \| 'never' | false | Hide footer, or show it in every load state |
| footer-position | 'inner' \| 'outer' | inner | Footer position |
| footer-class | string \| array \| object | - | Footer classes |
| lazy | boolean | false | Use native image lazy loading |
| img-props | ImgHTMLAttributes | - | Thumbnail element attributes |
| previewed-img-props | ImgHTMLAttributes | - | Single preview image attributes |
| show-loader | boolean | false | Show default loader while loading |
| ripple | boolean | false | Enable ripple |
| block | boolean | true | Render block layout |
| preview-disabled | boolean | false | Disable image preview |
| open | boolean | `-` | Controlled standalone preview state Supports `v-model:open`. |
| default-open | boolean | false | Initial uncontrolled preview state |
| preview-props | `Partial<ImagePreviewProps>` | - | Standalone preview options |
| popup-container | string \| HTMLElement \| false | body | Preview mount target |

### Image Events

| Event | Description | Arguments |
| --- | --- | --- |
| update:open | Preview state request | open: boolean |
| open-change | Preview state request | open: boolean |
| click | Image activation | event: Event |
| load | Image resource loaded | event: Event |
| error | Image resource failed | event: Event |

### Image Slots

| Slot | Description | Scope |
| --- | --- | --- |
| extra | Footer content | - |
| placeholder | Loading placeholder; takes precedence over loader | - |
| loader | Custom loading indicator | - |
| error | Error content | - |
| error-icon | Default error icon replacement | - |
| preview-actions | Standalone preview toolbar extra actions | - |

### ImagePreview Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| src | string | - | Preview image URL |
| open | boolean | `-` | Controlled preview state Supports `v-model:open`. |
| default-open | boolean | false | Initial uncontrolled state |
| interaction | 'auto' \| 'desktop' \| 'touch' | auto | Interaction mode |
| popup-container | string \| HTMLElement \| false | body | Preview mount target |
| lock-scroll | boolean | true | Lock background scrolling |
| closable | boolean | true | Show separate close button |
| overlay-closable | boolean | true | Allow backdrop to close |
| esc-to-close | boolean | true | Allow Escape to close |
| image-prevent-default | boolean | false | Prevent image context menu |
| default-scale | number | 1 | Initial and reset scale |
| min-scale | number | 0.5 | Lower scale bound |
| max-scale | number | 8 | Upper scale bound |
| scale-step | number | 0.5 | Zoom increment |
| wheel-zoom | boolean | desktop | Enable wheel zoom; automatic when omitted |
| keyboard | boolean | desktop | Enable preview keyboard shortcuts |
| draggable | boolean | true | Enable pointer gestures |
| keep-drag-offset | boolean | false | Keep offset when scale returns to 1 or less |
| show-toolbar | boolean | true | Show toolbar and its actions slot |
| actions-layout | ImagePreviewActionName[] | desktop defaults / touch [] | Ordered toolbar actions |
| previewed-img-props | ImgHTMLAttributes | - | Preview image element attributes |

### ImagePreview Events

| Event | Description | Arguments |
| --- | --- | --- |
| update:open | Preview state request | open: boolean |
| open-change | Preview state request | open: boolean |
| open / opened | Open transition start / end | - |
| close / closed | Close transition start / end | - |
| key-escape | Escape notification | - |
| long-press | Long press notification | - |
| prev / next | Navigation requests | - |

### ImagePreview Slots

| Slot | Description | Scope |
| --- | --- | --- |
| image | Replace the preview image | { src, scale, rotate, translateX, translateY, moving, previewedImgProps } |
| actions | Additional toolbar actions | - |
| close-icon | Separate close button icon | - |
| overlay | Preview overlay content | - |
| extra | Extra preview content | - |

When `images` is omitted or `undefined`, the group collects previewable child Images in DOM order; updating a child URL preserves its identity and position. An explicitly supplied array is the source, and `[]` means no images. Set it back to `undefined` to resume child collection. In array mode use the group `open` / `to` methods to select an image; child Images do not map themselves to array indices.

Public indices start at 1. The displayed index is clamped when data shrinks, and child reordering preserves the selected image identity. A controlled `modelValue` receives an update request when adjustment is needed; its owner can accept or reject it. No preview content is shown when the list is empty; the open state remains, so content may reappear when images return.

A previewable image exposes a named button action supporting Tab, Enter and Space. When preview closes, focus is restored to its opener when possible if focus is still in the preview or has fallen to the document body. The action is absent when preview is disabled or the image has failed. Explicit `alt=""` stays empty; a previewable decorative image still has a separately named preview action. When `alt` is omitted, `imgProps.alt`, `description`, then `loadDescription` supply the fallback.

When keyboard shortcuts are enabled, only the topmost preview handles arrow keys and Space. Inputs, editable regions and other interactive controls retain their own key behavior.

### ImagePreviewGroup Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| open | boolean | `-` | Controlled preview state Supports `v-model:open`. |
| default-open | boolean | false | Initial uncontrolled state |
| interaction | 'auto' \| 'desktop' \| 'touch' | auto | Interaction mode |
| popup-container | string \| HTMLElement \| false | body | Preview mount target |
| lock-scroll | boolean | true | Lock background scrolling |
| closable | boolean | true | Show separate close button |
| overlay-closable | boolean | true | Allow backdrop to close |
| esc-to-close | boolean | true | Allow Escape to close |
| image-prevent-default | boolean | false | Prevent image context menu |
| default-scale | number | 1 | Initial and reset scale |
| min-scale | number | 0.5 | Lower scale bound |
| max-scale | number | 8 | Upper scale bound |
| scale-step | number | 0.5 | Zoom increment |
| wheel-zoom | boolean | desktop | Enable wheel zoom; automatic when omitted |
| keyboard | boolean | desktop | Enable preview keyboard shortcuts |
| draggable | boolean | true | Enable pointer gestures |
| keep-drag-offset | boolean | false | Keep offset when scale returns to 1 or less |
| show-toolbar | boolean | true | Show toolbar and its actions slot |
| actions-layout | ImagePreviewActionName[] | desktop defaults / touch [] | Ordered toolbar actions |
| images | string[] | - | Explicit images; undefined collects children, [] is empty |
| model-value | number | `-` | Controlled image number, starting at 1 Supports `v-model`. |
| default-value | number | 1 | Initial image number, starting at 1 |
| loop | boolean | false | Wrap when navigating |

### ImagePreviewGroup Events

| Event | Description | Arguments |
| --- | --- | --- |
| update:open | Preview state request | open: boolean |
| open-change | Preview state request | open: boolean |
| update:modelValue | Image number request | imageNumber: number |
| change | Image number change request | imageNumber: number, previousImageNumber: number |
| open / opened | Open transition start / end | - |
| close / closed | Close transition start / end | - |
| key-escape | Escape notification | - |
| long-press | Long press notification | imageNumber: number |

### ImagePreviewGroup Slots

| Slot | Description | Scope |
| --- | --- | --- |
| default | Child images | - |
| close-icon | Separate close button icon | - |
| indicator | Image count display | { imageNumber, length } |
| extra | Extra preview content | { url } |
| actions | Additional toolbar actions | { url } |

### ImagePreviewAction Props (2.17.0)

| Parameter | Description | Type | Default |
| -------- | -------- | --------- | :-----: |
| name | Name | `string` | `-` |
| disabled | Whether disabled | `boolean` | `false` |

### ImagePreviewGroup Methods

| Method | Description |
| --- | --- |
| open(imageNumber = 1) | Request open at a 1-based image number |
| close() | Request close |
| prev() / next() | Navigate one image |
| to(imageNumber) | Navigate to a 1-based image number |
| reset() | Reset current preview transforms |
| zoomTo(scale) | Set finite scale within bounds |
| zoomIn() / zoomOut() | Change scale by scale-step |
| rotateLeft() / rotateRight() | Rotate by 90 degrees |
| toggleFullscreen() | Toggle fullscreen; returns the browser Promise or undefined when unsupported |

`Image.showPreview()` requests the current image preview. The `imagePreview`, `previewImage`, and `ImagePreviewFn` service accepts a URL, URL array, or options and returns `ImagePreviewHandle | undefined` (for example during SSR). Its handle offers the 12 Group operations; paging operations have no effect for a single image. The service also exposes `close()`, `setDefaultOptions()`, and `resetDefaultOptions()`. Native `lazy` is browser-scheduled and does not promise automatic retries.

Scale parameters must be finite and positive; invalid min/max/default/step values fall back to 0.5/8/1/0.5. If max is below min it resolves to min. Initial and reset scales are clamped, changes to bounds clamp the current value, and `zoomTo` ignores nonfinite input. `close` in `actionsLayout` is a toolbar action, independent of the separate button controlled by `closable`.

### Image Methods

| Method | Description |
| --- | --- |
| showPreview() | Request the current image preview when available |

### ImagePreviewAction Slots

| Slot | Description | Scope |
| --- | --- | --- |
| default | Action button content | - |

## Types

```ts
import type { ImageInstance } from "@cedar-design/ui-vue";
import { imagePreview } from "@cedar-design/ui-vue";
```

### ImagePreview Methods

Replacing an imperative preview disposes the previous instance and invokes its `onClosed` once, just like normal closure. Use this callback to release owned resources such as Object URLs. Old handles never close newer previews. If `onClosed` synchronously opens a new preview, that newer call wins and the interrupted outer call returns `undefined`.

| Method | Description |
| --- | --- |
| open() | Request open |
| close() | Request close |
| reset() | Reset scale, rotation and offset |
| zoomTo(scale) | Set finite scale within bounds |
| zoomIn() / zoomOut() | Change scale by scale-step |
| rotateLeft() / rotateRight() | Rotate by 90 degrees |
| toggleFullscreen() | Toggle fullscreen; returns the browser Promise or undefined when unsupported |

## FAQ

### `image-preview` prop notes

1. Set `keyboard` to `true` to enable preview shortcuts independently of `actions-layout`. Escape is controlled by `esc-to-close`.

- `esc`: close the preview
- `left`: previous image
- `right`: next image
- `up`: zoom in
- `down`: zoom out
- `space`: restore original size

2. `defaultScale` sets the initial zoom ratio. For example, 1.5 initially displays the image at 1.5 times its original size.

3. `scaleStep` sets the zoom increment for wheel, double-click and toolbar actions.

### Image-preview group numbering

`modelValue/defaultValue` start at `1`. `open(imageNumber = 1)` and `to(imageNumber)` use the same numbering; invalid/noninteger values are ignored. `prev()/next()` retain this numbering at loop boundaries. Model events are `update:modelValue(imageNumber)`; navigation emits `change(imageNumber, previousImageNumber)`, while external assignments do not. Long press emits `long-press(imageNumber)`; the indicator slot receives `{ imageNumber, length }`. Internal array indices remain zero-based.

Root `class` and `style` merge with the Image wrapper. Use `img-props.class/style` to `style` the inner image. Preview `open-change` is a Vue notification event: each state transition emits once, `.once` uses Vue event semantics, and returned Promises do not control loading. The typed `onOpenChange` listener uses this same event path.

<!-- Source: src/infinite-scroll/README.en-US.md; locale: en-US; page: /en/components/infinite-scroll/ -->

# Infinite Scroll

Start with the basic example, then compare related settings before moving to controlled, asynchronous or combined use cases.

## Basic examples

### List

- `status`: Selects the semantic state.

Example source: src/infinite-scroll/__demos__/list.vue

```vue
<template>
  <div ref="scroller" class="infinite-scroll-demo">
    <c-infinite-scroll
      v-model:status="status"
      :target="scroller"
      :bottom-offset="32"
      @load="fetchData"
    >
      <c-list :data="data" :scrollbar="false">
        <template #header>Infinite list</template>
        <template #item="{ item }">
          <c-list-item>{{ item }}</c-list-item>
        </template>
      </c-list>
    </c-infinite-scroll>
  </div>
</template>

<script lang="ts" setup>
import { onBeforeUnmount, onDeactivated, ref } from "vue";
import type { InfiniteScrollStatus } from "@cedar-design/ui-vue";

const scroller = ref<HTMLElement>();
const page = ref(0);
const data = ref<string[]>([]);
const status = ref<InfiniteScrollStatus>("idle");
let timer: ReturnType<typeof window.setTimeout> | undefined;

const fetchData = () => {
  window.clearTimeout(timer);
  timer = window.setTimeout(() => {
    timer = undefined;
    const start = data.value.length;
    data.value.push(
      ...Array.from(
        { length: 8 },
        (_, index) => `Cedar list item ${start + index + 1}`,
      ),
    );
    page.value += 1;
    status.value = page.value >= 5 ? "finished" : "idle";
  }, 600);
};
onBeforeUnmount(() => window.clearTimeout(timer));
onDeactivated(() => {
  window.clearTimeout(timer);
  timer = undefined;
  if (status.value === "loading") {
    status.value = "idle";
  }
});
</script>

<style scoped>
.infinite-scroll-demo {
  max-height: 320px;
  overflow-y: auto;
}
</style>
```

## Content and presentation

### Error

<!-- demo-config-notes:start -->
#### Configuration reference for this comparison

| Configuration | Purpose | Related examples |

<!-- demo-config-notes:end -->


- `status`: Selects the semantic state.

Example source: src/infinite-scroll/__demos__/error.vue

```vue
<template>
  <div ref="scroller" class="infinite-scroll-demo">
    <c-infinite-scroll
      v-model:status="status"
      :target="scroller"
      @load="fetchData"
      @retry="fetchData"
    >
      <c-list :data="data" :scrollbar="false">
        <template #item="{ item }">
          <c-list-item>{{ item }}</c-list-item>
        </template>
      </c-list>

      <template #error="{ retry }">
        加载失败，<c-button
          variant="text"
          size="sm"
          status="primary"
          @click="retry"
          >点击重试</c-button
        >
      </template>
    </c-infinite-scroll>
  </div>
</template>

<script lang="ts" setup>
import { onBeforeUnmount, onDeactivated, ref } from "vue";
import type { InfiniteScrollStatus } from "@cedar-design/ui-vue";

const scroller = ref<HTMLElement>();
const data = ref<string[]>([]);
const status = ref<InfiniteScrollStatus>("idle");
let failedOnce = false;
let timer: ReturnType<typeof window.setTimeout> | undefined;

const fetchData = () => {
  window.clearTimeout(timer);
  timer = window.setTimeout(() => {
    timer = undefined;
    if (!failedOnce && data.value.length === 8) {
      failedOnce = true;
      status.value = "error";
      return;
    }

    const start = data.value.length;
    data.value.push(
      ...Array.from(
        { length: 8 },
        (_, index) => `Cedar list item ${start + index + 1}`,
      ),
    );
    status.value = data.value.length >= 32 ? "finished" : "idle";
  }, 600);
};
onBeforeUnmount(() => window.clearTimeout(timer));
onDeactivated(() => {
  window.clearTimeout(timer);
  timer = undefined;
  if (status.value === "loading") {
    status.value = "idle";
  }
});
</script>

<style scoped>
.infinite-scroll-demo {
  max-height: 320px;
  overflow-y: auto;
}
</style>
```

## Lifecycle and edge cases

### Scheduler Lifecycle

<!-- demo-config-notes:start -->
#### Configuration reference for this comparison

| Configuration | Purpose | Related examples |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `status` | Pagination state; supports `v-model:status` | Scheduler Lifecycle |
| `target` | Scroll container; defaults to the nearest scrolling ancestor | Scheduler Lifecycle |
| `immediate` | Whether to check immediately after mounting and resolving the scroll container | Scheduler Lifecycle |
<!-- demo-config-notes:end -->


- `status`: Selects the semantic state.

Example source: src/infinite-scroll/__demos__/scheduler-lifecycle.vue

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { useDemoLocale as useInlineDemoLocale } from "../../__demos__/locale";
const inlineCopy = useInlineDemoLocale(
  "infiniteScrollSchedulerLifecycleInline",
);

import { ref } from "vue";
import type { InfiniteScrollStatus } from "@cedar-design/ui-vue";
const first = ref<HTMLElement>();
const second = ref<HTMLElement>();
const alternate = ref(false);
const active = ref(true);
const status = ref<InfiniteScrollStatus>("idle");
const loads = ref(0);
const load = () => {
  loads.value++;
  status.value = "finished";
};
</script>
<template>
  <div>
    <c-button @click="alternate = !alternate">{{
      inlineCopy.switchTarget
    }}</c-button>
    <c-button @click="active = !active">{{ inlineCopy.activate }}</c-button>
    <c-button @click="status = 'idle'">{{
      inlineCopy.newStatusCycle
    }}</c-button>
    <p>
      {{ inlineCopy.loads }} {{ loads }}{{ inlineCopy.oldChecksMustNotReplay }}
    </p>
    <div ref="first" style="height: 100px; overflow: auto">
      <div style="height: 300px">Target A</div>
    </div>
    <div ref="second" style="height: 100px; overflow: auto">
      <div style="height: 300px">Target B</div>
    </div>
    <KeepAlive>
      <c-infinite-scroll
        v-if="active"
        v-model:status="status"
        :target="alternate ? second : first"
        :immediate="false"
        @load="load"
      >
        <div>{{ inlineCopy.detector }}</div>
      </c-infinite-scroll>
    </KeepAlive>
  </div>
</template>
```

When `target` is a selector, its element must exist when binding occurs. `check()` uses the current binding and does not resolve the selector again; pass the element or change `target` to rebind. Accept the emitted `loading` via `v-model:status`, then set `idle`, `error`, or `finished` when the request settles; assigning the original `idle` alone does not release the request lock. A negative numeric offset requires scrolling past the bottom. String offsets are resolved as CSS widths: negative lengths fall back to zero, and percentages use the measurement element’s CSS containing-block width.

## API

### InfiniteScroll Props

| Parameter | Description | Type | Default |
| ------------- | -------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------- | -------- |
| status | Pagination state; supports `v-model:status` | `'idle' \| 'loading' \| 'error' \| 'finished'` | `'idle'` |
| bottom-offset | Distance-to-bottom threshold; numbers are px, strings are CSS lengths | `string \| number` | `0` |
| immediate | Whether to check immediately after mounting and resolving the scroll container | `boolean` | `true` |
| disabled | Pause loading and retry | `boolean` | `false` |
| target | Scroll container; defaults to the nearest scrolling ancestor | `string \| HTMLElement` | `-` |

### InfiniteScroll Events

| Event | Description | Arguments |
| ------------- | -------------------------- | --------- |
| update:status | Requests pagination status `loading` | `loading` |
| load | Emitted when idle and the threshold is reached | - |
| retry | Emitted when retry is invoked in the error state | - |

`retry` does not also emit `load`. Both events may call the same business request function.

### InfiniteScroll Methods

| Method | Description |
| ------ | ---------------------------- |
| check | Immediately check whether the loading threshold is reached |
| retry | Request a retry in the `error` state |

### InfiniteScroll Slots

| Slot | Description | Prop |
| -------- | ---------------- | ------------------- |
| default | Observed content | - |
| loading | Pagination loading state | - |
| error | Pagination error state | `retry: () => void` |
| finished | All-pages-loaded state | - |

The default error area retries on click. `finished` is terminal; detection resumes only when the parent resets `status` to `idle`.

```ts
  InfiniteScrollInstance,
  InfiniteScrollMethods,
  InfiniteScrollProps,
  InfiniteScrollStatus,
} from "@cedar-design/ui-vue";
```

Override the component variable directly for local styling; root-level aliases are not recalculated merely because a descendant system variable changes. Internal variables are not public APIs.

<!-- component-css-variables:end -->

# InputNumber

Numeric editing with bounds and formatting.

## Reading direction

The numeric input inherits its source `dir`; step buttons follow reading order. Values, precision and vertical keys retain their meaning: ArrowUp increases and ArrowDown decreases. Neither values nor display strings are reversed.

## Basic examples

### Basic usage

Example source: src/input-number/__demos__/field-basic.vue

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { ref } from "vue";
const value = ref<number | undefined>(12);
const disabled = ref(false);
const readonly = ref(false);
const clearable = ref(true);
const hint = ref(false);
</script>
<template>
  <div class="number-demo">
    <div class="number-demo__options">
      <c-checkbox v-model="disabled" edit-mode="direct">禁用</c-checkbox>
      <c-checkbox v-model="readonly" edit-mode="direct">只读</c-checkbox>
      <c-checkbox v-model="clearable" edit-mode="direct">可清空</c-checkbox>
      <c-checkbox v-model="hint" edit-mode="direct">浮动提示</c-checkbox>
    </div>
    <c-input-number
      v-model="value"
      :disabled="disabled"
      :readonly="readonly"
      :clearable="clearable"
      :hint="hint"
      placeholder="数量"
    />
    <output>业务数值：{{ value ?? "空值" }}</output>
  </div>
</template>
```

## Appearance and layout

### Appearance Lab

<!-- demo-config-notes:start -->

#### Configuration reference for this comparison

| Configuration | Purpose | Related examples |
| ------------- | --------------------------- | ------------------------------------ |
| `size` | All five sizes implemented; inheritable | Control Sizes, Field Options |
| `variant` | Field variant; inherits InputGroup | Control Sizes, Field Options |
| `placeholder` | Placeholder | Control Sizes, Field Options |
| `min` | Minimum | Appearance Lab |
| `max` | Maximum | Appearance Lab |
| `mode` | Step-button layout | Field Modes |

<!-- demo-config-notes:end -->


- `min`: Sets the lower bound.
- `max`: Sets the upper bound.

Example source: src/input-number/__demos__/appearance-lab.vue

```vue
<script setup>
```

## Numeric input and formatting

### Quantity Controls

<!-- demo-config-notes:start -->

#### Configuration reference for this comparison

| Configuration | Purpose | Related examples |
| ----------- | ---------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------- |
| `clearable` | Allow clearing an editable field | Quantity Controls, Format Slots, Number Boundaries |
| `mode` | Step-button layout | Quantity Controls, Format Slots |
| `min` | Minimum | Quantity Controls, Number Boundaries |
| `max` | Maximum | Quantity Controls, Number Boundaries |
| `step` | Positive finite step; scientific notation supported | Quantity Controls, Number Boundaries |
| `formatter` | Display formatting only; does not change the number | Format Slots, Number Boundaries |

<!-- demo-config-notes:end -->


- `min`: Sets the lower bound.
- `max`: Sets the upper bound.
- `step`: Controls the allowed increment.
- `disabled`: Prevents user interaction.

Example source: src/input-number/__demos__/quantity-controls.vue

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { useDemoLocale } from "../../__demos__/locale";
import { computed, onBeforeUnmount, ref, shallowRef } from "vue";

const copy = useDemoLocale("quantityControls");
const value = ref<number | null | undefined>(2);
const disableInput = ref(true);
const disableIncrement = ref(false);
const disableDecrement = ref(false);
const incrementButton = ref(true);
const decrementButton = ref(true);
const press = ref(true);
const lastStep = ref("—");
function handleStep(next: number, direction: string) {
  lastStep.value = `${direction}: ${next}`;
}
const approved = ref<number | null | undefined>(2);
const blocked = ref(false);
const pending = ref(false);
const statusKey = ref<
  "waiting" | "cancelled" | "approved" | "rejected" | "failed"
>();
const proposedValue = shallowRef<unknown>();
const status = computed(() => {
  if (!statusKey.value) return "—";
  return statusKey.value === "waiting"
    ? copy.value.waiting(proposedValue.value)
    : copy.value[statusKey.value];
});
const decision = shallowRef<((allowed: boolean) => void) | undefined>();
const fail = shallowRef<(() => void) | undefined>();
function beforeCommit(
  { value: next }: { value: unknown },
  _done: (allow?: boolean) => void,
  { signal }: { signal: AbortSignal },
) {
  pending.value = true;
  proposedValue.value = next;
  statusKey.value = "waiting";
  return new Promise<void | false>((resolve, reject) => {
    const cleanup = () => {
      signal.removeEventListener("abort", cancel);
      pending.value = false;
      decision.value = undefined;
      fail.value = undefined;
    };
    const cancel = () => {
      cleanup();
      statusKey.value = "cancelled";
      resolve(false);
    };
    signal.addEventListener("abort", cancel, { once: true });
    decision.value = (allowed) => {
      cleanup();
      statusKey.value = allowed ? "approved" : "rejected";
      resolve(allowed ? undefined : false);
    };
    fail.value = () => {
      cleanup();
      statusKey.value = "failed";
      reject(new Error(copy.value.requestError));
    };
  });
}
onBeforeUnmount(() => decision.value?.(false));
</script>

<template>
  <div class="quantity-controls-demo">
    <h4>
      {{ copy.title }}
    </h4>
    <c-space wrap>
      <c-checkbox v-model="disableInput" edit-mode="direct">{{
        copy.buttonsOnly
      }}</c-checkbox>
      <c-checkbox v-model="disableIncrement" edit-mode="direct">{{
        copy.disableIncrease
      }}</c-checkbox>
      <c-checkbox v-model="disableDecrement" edit-mode="direct">{{
        copy.disableDecrease
      }}</c-checkbox>
      <c-checkbox v-model="incrementButton" edit-mode="direct">{{
        copy.showIncrease
      }}</c-checkbox>
      <c-checkbox v-model="decrementButton" edit-mode="direct">{{
        copy.showDecrease
      }}</c-checkbox>
      <c-checkbox v-model="press" edit-mode="direct">{{
        copy.longPress
      }}</c-checkbox>
    </c-space>
    <c-input-number
      v-model="value"
      edit-mode="direct"
      mode="button"
      :aria-label="copy.quantityInput"
      :disable-input="disableInput"
      :disable-increment="disableIncrement"
      :disable-decrement="disableDecrement"
      :increment-button="incrementButton"
      :decrement-button="decrementButton"
      :press="press"
      :min="0"
      :max="10"
      @step="handleStep"
    />
    <p role="status">{{ copy.acceptedStep }}：{{ lastStep }}</p>
    <h4>
      {{ copy.asyncTitle }}
    </h4>
    <p>
      {{ copy.asyncHint }}
    </p>
    <c-input-number
      v-model="approved"
      edit-mode="direct"
      mode="button"
      clearable
      :aria-label="copy.asyncInput"
      :before-commit="beforeCommit"
      loading-mode="line"
      :disabled="blocked"
    />
    <c-space wrap>
      <c-button :disabled="!pending" @click="decision?.(true)">{{
        copy.approve
      }}</c-button>
      <c-button :disabled="!pending" @click="decision?.(false)">{{
        copy.reject
      }}</c-button>
      <c-button :disabled="!pending" @click="fail?.()">{{
        copy.simulateFailure
      }}</c-button>
      <c-button @click="approved = 10">{{ copy.externalValue }}</c-button>
      <c-button @click="blocked = !blocked">{{
        blocked ? copy.enable : copy.disable
      }}</c-button>
    </c-space>
    <p role="status">
      {{ status }}；{{ copy.committedValue }}：{{ approved ?? "—" }}
    </p>
  </div>
</template>
```

### Empty markers and valid zero

Configure empty-values and empty-value when an API uses -1 for missing data. Initially the input is blank while the model remains -1. Set it to 0 to see a valid zero; clearing returns -1. A second field clears to a valid 0, showing that clear output need not mean missing data.

Example source: src/input-number/__demos__/en-US/empty-value.vue

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { reactive, ref } from "vue";
const model = reactive({ quantity: -1 as number | null | undefined });
const restored = ref<number | null | undefined>(12);
</script>
<template>
  <c-space direction="column">
    <p>
      -1 means missing and renders blank; 0 remains a valid number. Clearing
      produces -1.
    </p>
    <c-form :model="model" layout="vertical">
      <c-form-item field="quantity" label="Quantity">
        <c-input-number
          v-model="model.quantity"
          edit-mode="direct"
          clearable
          :empty-values="[null, undefined, -1]"
          :empty-value="-1"
        />
      </c-form-item>
    </c-form>
    <c-space wrap>
      <c-button @click="model.quantity = 0">Set to 0</c-button>
      <c-button @click="model.quantity = -1">Set to -1</c-button>
    </c-space>
    <p>
      Current model: <output>{{ String(model.quantity) }}</output>
    </p>
    <p>This field clears to 0 without treating 0 as missing.</p>
    <c-form layout="vertical">
      <c-form-item label="Clear restores valid zero">
        <c-input-number
          v-model="restored"
          edit-mode="direct"
          clearable
          :empty-value="0"
        />
        <output>{{ String(restored) }}</output>
      </c-form-item>
    </c-form>
  </c-space>
</template>
```

```vue
}
</script>
<template>
  <div class="number-demo">
    <label>父组件接受更新
```

### Shared field loading

`loading` displays the shared field indicator. `loading-mode` is `default` (indicator) or `line` (an indeterminate bottom line); it defaults to `default`. Rendering belongs to FieldDecorator. Loading does not implicitly disable editing or change readonly. Set those states separately.

## Composition input

IME composition preserves the native text being entered; external model updates do not replace it before completion. Existing formatting and controlled-owner acceptance apply afterward. Queued restoration from an earlier input cannot replace a later edit's text or caret. Numeric updates still follow model-event, with unchanged blur/Enter commit timing.

## Usage notes

### Editing and confirmation

This component supports `edit-mode` with field > FormItem > Form precedence. When unset, it defaults to `direct` and preserves `direct` editing. Supported values: `direct / click / dblclick`. Non-direct modes open the editor through the field value trigger and keep one draft; v-model updates only after confirmation. Cancel, reset or enabling readPretty discards the draft.

Cedar uses edit-mode="click" / "dblclick" to open an editor popup near the field. Enter/F2 also opens it; cancel/Escape discards the draft, and confirmation commits it. readPretty is an independent reading setting, separate from readonly and disabled.



`read-pretty` is an independent boolean alongside `readonly` and `disabled`. It inherits from field to FormItem to Form; explicit `false` overrides the parent. The default is `false`. Reading mode renders no editor.

`--c-field-caret-color` sets the shared caret color, defaulting to `currentColor`. `--c-input-number-caret-color` overrides this component and defaults to `var(--c-field-caret-color)`.

Explicit beforeCommit waiting uses the existing loadingMode indicator and sets aria-busy on the actual input. Manual loading remains business-owned and does not imply readonly; beforeCommit guards retain their existing interaction lock. Notification return Promises, including change/step, do not control waiting.

Deferred `change` preserves the real confirmation event when available (for example, the save button). Programmatic editor handoff has no DOM event, so its second argument is optional. The event target can be the confirmation control rather than the input. `change` is a notification: its returned Promise is not awaited; use `before-commit` to approve asynchronous saves.

Public focus/blur methods are callable from initial mount. Focus opens an editable deferred editor and targets it after readiness; disabled, readonly, or reading fields do not open. Blur only blurs the current target without reopening. Stored methods never bind an old editor; closure, mode changes, deactivation, or unmount cancel queued calls.

## API

### Empty values and reading placeholders

`empty-values` recognizes empty data; `empty-value` keeps existing clear output. `empty-text` defaults to `'-'` under `read-pretty`, with Field > FormItem > Form precedence and custom read slots first. With explicit `empty-values`, built-in required uses the policy; custom validators receive original data. See the [shared guide](llms/en-US/guide/empty-values.md).

| Prop | Type | Default and scope |
| ------------ | ------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------- |
| empty-values | readonly unknown[] | Field > FormItem > Form > component-family default; replaces the whole list |
| empty-text | string | Field > FormItem > Form > '-'; explicit '' is valid |

These props belong to field presentation; pure panels do not gain reading mode. Form and FormItem provide inherited settings. The existing empty-value type and clear fallback remain component-specific.

### Clear output

`empty-value` defines the output of an existing clear action. Omission preserves the component fallback; supported types remain component-specific. It does not change empty-values recognition or Form reset defaults.

`empty-value` accepts explicit `null` (or `() => null`). Clearing publishes `null` unchanged; omitted values preserve the existing default. Editors render `null` as blank without converting ordinary empty-string input to `null`. In popup editing, clearing changes the draft; confirm commits it and cancel preserves the original model.

### InputNumber Props

| Prop | Description | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| empty-value | Clear output, falling back to undefined when omitted | `number \| null \| undefined \| (() => number \| null \| undefined)` | `undefined` |
| model-value | Controlled numeric value including null; uses internal state when omitted | `number \| null` | `undefined` |
| default-value | Initial uncontrolled numeric value, read at creation | `number` | `undefined` |
| disable-input | Disable typing while retaining step buttons and arrow-key stepping | `boolean` | `false` |
| disable-increment | Disable incrementing through buttons and arrow keys | `boolean` | `false` |
| disable-decrement | Disable decrementing through buttons and arrow keys | `boolean` | `false` |
| increment-button | Show the increment button | `boolean` | `true` |
| decrement-button | Show the decrement button | `boolean` | `true` |
| press | Repeat stepping while held; approval-enabled operations do not repeat requests | `boolean` | `true` |
| mode | Step-button layout | `'embed' \| 'button' \| 'input'` | `'embed'` |
| precision | Explicit precision is an integer from 0 to 100, at least the decimal places required by step | `number` | `undefined` |
| step | Positive finite step size | `number` | `1` |
| disabled | Disabled state; can inherit from Form | `boolean` | `-` |
| error | Error state; can inherit from FormItem | `boolean` | `-` |
| max | Maximum commit bound, allowing positive infinity | `number` | `Infinity` |
| min | Minimum commit bound, allowing negative infinity | `number` | `-Infinity` |
| formatter | Editor display formatter without changing the numeric model | `InputNumberFormatter` | `undefined` |
| parser | Parse user-edited text once per edit | `InputNumberParser` | `undefined` |
| placeholder | Hint text | `string` | `-` |
| size | Input size | `'xs' \| 'sm' \| 'md' \| 'lg' \| 'xl'` | `'md'` |
| variant | Field appearance | `'filled' \| 'outline' \| 'standard'` | `'outline'` |
| hint | Whether hint text floats | `boolean` | Inherits when unset; defaults to `false` when used independently |
| clearable | Whether to allow the input to be cleared | `boolean` | `false` |
| model-event | Model notification timing; change always denotes a commit | `'change' \| 'input'` | `'change'` |
| readonly | Readonly state; can inherit from Form | `boolean` | `-` |
| input-attrs | Additional native attributes; the component owns controlled value, state, ARIA bounds, and component events | `Record<string, unknown>` | `undefined` |
| edit-mode | Editor mode; inherits FormItem/Form | `direct / click / dblclick` | `undefined` |
| read-pretty | Reading presentation; inherits FormItem/Form | `boolean` | `undefined` |
| empty-values | Empty-value recognition set; an explicit set replaces inherited values | `readonly unknown[]` | Inherited component-family policy |
| empty-text | Empty reading text, inherited from FormItem/Form | `string` | `'-'` |
| before-commit | Direct commit and deferred save approval: (payload, done, context) | `BeforeFieldCommit` | `undefined` |
| open | Controlled editor visibility in deferred modes | `boolean` | `undefined` |
| default-open | Uncontrolled initial editor visibility; creation-only | `boolean` | `false` |
| popup-container | Deferred editor portal target; false renders in place | `PopupContainer` | `undefined` |
| loading | Loading presentation; keeps the input editable | `boolean` | `false` |
| loading-mode | Loading layout: default indicator or bottom line | `default / line` | `default` |

Min may be finite or -Infinity; max may be finite or Infinity. Negative values and 0 are valid. Invalid individual bounds use Vue prop-validation diagnostics and fall back to their unbounded defaults. An inverted range diagnoses both bounds and becomes unbounded, without swapping values. Input commits, stepping, and ARIA share the effective bounds; clear markers still follow empty-value.

Approved clearing notifies **clear → input → update:modelValue → change**. Clear is an action notification and is not emitted after a veto. A target equal to the current model does not invent change. The default clear value is undefined; explicit empty-value may provide null or another supported numeric value.

`before-commit(payload, done, context)` receives `{ value, previousValue }`; context provides `signal`. Synchronous void waits for done; true, done(), or fulfilled `Promise<void>` allows the operation. False, done(false), `Promise<false>`, throwing, or rejection cancels. Direct mode approves changed model values before committing, stepping, or clearing; `model-event="input"` also approves before publishing, without repeated approval for the same value. Pending work announces aria-busy and locks typing/stepping. External model/configuration/state changes or deactivation/unmount cancel stale work. Direct approval errors preserve the value and notify `commit-error`; deferred editing approves once at final confirmation and uses the existing panel feedback. With approval enabled, holding a button does not start repeated requests. Ordinary listener Promises are not approval tasks.

### InputNumber Events

| Event | Parameters / Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| update:modelValue | `number \| null \| undefined` | Model update proposal |
| update:open | `boolean` | Editor visibility request |
| open-change | `boolean` | Editor visibility change notification |
| input | `value: number \| null \| undefined, text: string, event: Event` | Parsed numeric value and display text from user editing |
| change | `value: number \| null \| undefined, event?: Event` | Numeric commit; deferred source event may be absent |
| clear | `event: Event` | Approved clear action notification, preceding value notifications |
| step | `value: number, direction: 'plus' \| 'minus', event: Event` | Step notification after changing the value |
| commit-error | `error: unknown` | Direct approval error notification; a boolean veto is not an error |
| keydown | `event: KeyboardEvent` | Native keyboard notification with synchronous preventDefault support |
| focus | `event: FocusEvent` | Native editor receives focus |
| blur | `event: FocusEvent` | Native editor loses focus |

### InputNumber Slots

| Slot | Parameters / Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| read | `{ value: number \| null \| undefined; text: string }` | Custom reading content |
| prefix | `-` | Inner prefix |
| suffix | `-` | Inner suffix |
| prepend | `-` | Outer leading content |
| append | `-` | Outer trailing content |
| plus | `-` | Increment button content |
| minus | `-` | Decrement button content |
| clear-icon | `{ clear(event?: Event): void }` | Clear icon or button |

### InputNumber Methods

| Method / property | Parameters / Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| focus | `focus(options?: FocusOptions): void` | Focus the mounted editor |
| blur | `blur(): void` | Blur the mounted editor |
| select | `select(): void` | Select all text in the mounted editor |
| inputRef | `HTMLInputElement \| undefined` | Reference to the mounted native numeric input |

# InputTag

Editable tag values with controlled array models. FormItem error messages are associated with the input alongside any existing `aria-describedby`.

Tags wrap automatically and scroll inside the input after three rows. Candidates appear only for a non-empty query that meets `min-search-length`; focusing an empty input does not open the panel, and no dropdown arrow is shown by default.

## Reading direction

Tags follow reading order while their source array stays unchanged. With empty input, Backspace removes the last closable value; Enter adds a tag. Composition does not submit or delete tags.

## Basic examples

### Basic usage

Example source: src/input-tag/__demos__/basic.vue

```vue
</template>
```

## Data and options

### Search and select tags

Type or paste at least two characters to search; a sole enabled result is committed automatically and multiple results require selection.

Example source: src/input-tag/__demos__/search-options.vue

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { useDemoLocale as useInlineDemoLocale } from "../../__demos__/locale";
const inlineCopy = useInlineDemoLocale("inputTagSearchOptionsInline");

import { ref } from "vue";

const tags = ref<string[]>([]);
const singleTag = ref<string | null>(null);
const error = ref("");
const people = [
  { value: "alice", label: "Alice · 设计" },
  { value: "alan", label: "Alan · 产品" },
  { value: "bob", label: "Bob · 开发" },
];

// 模拟服务端搜索；真实请求可把 signal 传入 fetch。
async function searchPeople(
  query: string,
  { signal }: { signal: AbortSignal },
) {
  await new Promise<void>((resolve, reject) => {
    const cancel = () => {
      clearTimeout(timer);
      reject(new DOMException("Aborted", "AbortError"));
    };
    const timer = setTimeout(() => {
      signal.removeEventListener("abort", cancel);
      resolve();
    }, 350);
    if (signal.aborted) cancel();
    else signal.addEventListener("abort", cancel, { once: true });
  });
  error.value = "";
  return people.filter((person) => person.value.includes(query.toLowerCase()));
}
</script>

<template>
  <c-space direction="column" style="width: 100%" :size="12">
    <p>
      输入或粘贴至少两个字符，输入 al 选择多个结果中的一项；输入 bob
      自动提交唯一结果。
    </p>
    <p>
      Type or paste at least two characters. Choose an “al” result, or type
      “bob” to commit the only result.
    </p>
    <c-input-tag
      v-model="tags"
      :options="searchPeople"
      :min-search-length="2"
      :search-delay="250"
      auto-commit-single
      unique-value
      :placeholder="inlineCopy.searchAccounts"
      :aria-label="inlineCopy.searchAccounts"
      @load-error="error = inlineCopy.searchFailed"
    />
    <p v-if="error" role="alert">{{ error }}</p>
    <p>{{ inlineCopy.savedIDs }} {{ JSON.stringify(tags) }}</p>
    <p>单值模式：选择新账号替换旧值；无匹配时按回车保存输入。</p>
    <c-input-tag
      v-model="singleTag"
      :multiple="false"
      :options="searchPeople"
      :min-search-length="2"
      :search-delay="250"
      auto-commit-single
      :placeholder="inlineCopy.singleAccount"
      :aria-label="inlineCopy.singleAccount"
    />
    <p>{{ inlineCopy.singleID }} {{ JSON.stringify(singleTag) }}</p>
  </c-space>
</template>
```

When `options` is supplied, typing or pasting searches only after `min-search-length` is reached. Arrays filter locally by label; loaders receive the query and `{ signal }`, and remote results are not filtered again. Composition completes before searching; shortening the query or blurring cancels pending work. Enter selects a highlighted candidate, or creates the typed value when a completed search returns no candidates. Loading, failed searches, and disabled matches never create a tag. `auto-commit-single` defaults to false and commits only the sole enabled result of the current search. Selected values are saved in the model. Resolve labels from current `options`, then `fallback-option`, the instance cache, and finally the raw value. Use `options` or `fallback-option` to restore labels after remounting.

Selected tags display their label by default. Use `format-label` to format the text and `#label="{ data }"` for custom content. Slots take priority over formatting; neither changes search matching or the model. Read mode uses formatted text; use `#read` to customize read content.
