| `--c-steps-navigation-padding-left` | `var(--c-spacing-8)` | `padding-inline-start` |
| `--c-steps-node-font-weight` | `var(--c-font-weight-500)` | `font-weight` |
| `--c-steps-size-md` | `var(--c-size-7)` | `height`, `inset-inline-start`, `line-height`, `margin-inline-start`, `margin-top`, `padding`, `padding-inline-end`, `top`, `width` |
| `--c-steps-size-md-arrow` | `var(--c-size-18)` | `border-bottom`, `border-inline-start`, `border-top`, `height`, `inset-inline-end`, `padding-inline-start` |
| `--c-steps-size-md-description-font-size` | `var(--c-font-size-body-1)` | `font-size` |
| `--c-steps-size-md-icon-font-size` | `var(--c-size-4)` | `font-size` |
| `--c-steps-size-md-item-icon-margin-left` | `calc((var(--c-steps-label-vertical-content-width) - var(--c-steps-size-md)) / 2)` | `inset-inline-start`, `margin-inline-start` |
| `--c-steps-size-md-title-font-size` | `var(--c-font-size-title-1)` | `font-size` |
| `--c-steps-size-sm` | `var(--c-size-6)` | `height`, `inset-inline-start`, `line-height`, `margin-inline-start`, `padding`, `padding-inline-end`, `top`, `width` |
| `--c-steps-size-sm-arrow` | `var(--c-size-10)` | `border-bottom`, `border-inline-start`, `border-top`, `height`, `inset-inline-end`, `padding-inline-start` |
| `--c-steps-size-sm-description-font-size` | `var(--c-font-size-body-1)` | `font-size` |
| `--c-steps-size-sm-icon-font-size` | `var(--c-font-size-body-3)` | `font-size` |
| `--c-steps-size-sm-item-icon-margin-left` | `calc((var(--c-steps-label-vertical-content-width) - var(--c-steps-size-sm)) / 2)` | `inset-inline-start`, `margin-inline-start` |
| `--c-steps-size-sm-title-font-size` | `var(--c-font-size-body-3)` | `font-size` |
| `--c-steps-transition-duration-1` | `var(--c-transition-duration-1)` | `transition` |
| `--c-steps-transition-timing-function-linear` | `var(--c-transition-timing-function-linear)` | `transition` |
| `--c-steps-vertical-item-min-height` | `90px` | `min-height` |

</div>

Apply overrides to the rendered component root or the actual popup ancestor. For example, add the following class to that element and replace the value as needed:

```css
.component-theme {
  --c-steps-arrow-item-description-color-error: var(--c-sys-color-surface-default);
}
```

Explicit inline styles and props that write the same CSS property take precedence over stylesheet defaults. After Teleport, ordinary CSS variables inherit from the actual mount location. When using ThemeProvider, follow its local-theme and popup configuration rules. Override the component variable directly for local styling; root-level aliases are not recalculated merely because a descendant system variable changes. Internal variables are not public APIs.

## Responsive layout and composition

### Breakpoints

Preview configuration: `:columns="columns"`, `:data="rows"`, `:pagination="false"`.

Example source: src/style/atomic-css/__demos__/breakpoints.vue

```vue
<template>
  <c-space direction="column" fill size="md">
    <div class="hint">
      缩小浏览器窗口可观察当前命中的断点；类名形如
      <code>sm:c-bg-info</code>。
    </div>
    <div class="box">
      <div class="label">当前 ≥</div>
      <strong class="value">{{ active }}</strong>
    </div>
    <c-table :columns="columns" :data="rows" :pagination="false" />
  </c-space>
</template>

<script lang="ts" setup>
import { computed, onMounted, onUnmounted, ref } from "vue";

const width = ref(typeof window !== "undefined" ? window.innerWidth : 0);

const onResize = () => {
  width.value = window.innerWidth;
};

onMounted(() => {
  width.value = window.innerWidth;
  window.addEventListener("resize", onResize);
});

onUnmounted(() => {
  window.removeEventListener("resize", onResize);
});

const active = computed(() => {
  const w = width.value;
  if (w >= 1920) return "xl (1920px)";
  if (w >= 1200) return "lg (1200px)";
  if (w >= 992) return "md (992px)";
  if (w >= 768) return "sm (768px)";
  return "base (< sm)";
});

const columns = [
  { title: "前缀", dataIndex: "prefix" },
  { title: "最小宽度", dataIndex: "min" },
  { title: "示例类", dataIndex: "cls" },
];

const rows = [
  { prefix: "sm:", min: "768px", cls: "sm:c-bg-info" },
  { prefix: "md:", min: "992px", cls: "md:c-bg-warning" },
  { prefix: "lg:", min: "1200px", cls: "lg:c-bg-danger" },
  { prefix: "xl:", min: "1920px", cls: "xl:c-bg-success" },
];
</script>

<style scoped lang="scss">
.hint {
  font-size: 13px;
  color: var(--c-color-text-3);
}

.box {
  display: flex;
  align-items: baseline;
  gap: 8px;
  padding: 12px 16px;
  border-radius: 4px;
  background: var(--c-color-primary);
  color: #fff;
}

.label {
  opacity: 0.85;
  font-size: 13px;
}

.value {
  font-size: 18px;
}
</style>
```

## UnoCSS

### Installation

```shell
pnpm add -D @cedar-design/preset-unocss-vue unocss
```

### Configuration

```js
// uno.config.ts
import { defineConfig } from "unocss";
import { presetCedar } from "@cedar-design/preset-unocss-vue";

export default defineConfig({
  presets: [presetCedar()],
});
```

Optional `presetCedar({ colors, fontSize, breakpoints })`; `false` disables a section.

### Load theme variables first

```js
import "@cedar-design/ui-vue/style";
// Or import a theme stylesheet containing --c-* variables
```

---

## Tailwind CSS

### Installation

```shell
pnpm add -D @cedar-design/preset-tailwindcss-vue tailwindcss
```

### Tailwind v3

```js
// tailwind.config.js
import { presetCedar } from "@cedar-design/preset-tailwindcss-vue";

export default {
  content: ["./index.html", "./src/**/*.{vue,js,ts,jsx,tsx}"],
  presets: [presetCedar()],
};
```

### Tailwind v4

```js
// tailwind.config.js
import { presetCedar } from "@cedar-design/preset-tailwindcss-vue";

export default {
  presets: [presetCedar()],
};
```

```css
/* src/style.css */
@import "tailwindcss";
@config '../tailwind.config.js';
```

---

See [Common patterns](llms/en-US/components/style/atomic-usage.md) for all Flex/spacing/sizing/overflow/radius classes. Only utilities mapped to Cedar tokens are listed below.

## Optional configuration

```js
presetCedar({
  colors: true, // or false / partial key overrides
  fontSize: true, // false disables it; custom fontSize maps are accepted
  // Uno:
  breakpoints: true,
  // TW:
  // screens: true,
});
```

### Custom theme mapping

`colors`/`fontSize` may override part of the defaults; omitted keys retain default mappings:

```js
presetCedar({
  colors: {
    primary: "var(--app-color-brand)",
    danger: "var(--app-color-error)",
  },
  fontSize: {
    md: "15px",
  },
});
```

`false` disables the corresponding Cedar theme mapping. Generator-native utilities may still exist but are independent of Cedar variables.

---

## Corresponding Maple configuration

Maple's UnoCSS preset includes `presetUno` with an `mp-` prefix:

```js
import { defineConfig } from "unocss";
import { presetMaple } from "@nio-pow/preset-unocss";

export default defineConfig({
  presets: [presetMaple()],
});
```

Both Maple UnoCSS/Tailwind presets generate `mp-bg-primary`, `mp-text-primary` and `mp-border mp-border-primary` without unprefixed aliases.

Tailwind `prefix` is global; one Tailwind instance should not load Cedar/Maple presets with different prefixes simultaneously.

---

## Notes

- The preset includes the framework's full atomic classes with `c-` prefixes, e.g. `c-flex`/`c-p-16`.
- Classes must start with `c-`, e.g. `c-bg-primary`; no unprefixed aliases.
- Choose UnoCSS or Tailwind CSS; do not enable both generators in one app.
- Cedar/Maple share theme key names. Even with different UnoCSS utility prefixes, avoid merging both themes in one config or matching colors may overwrite by preset order.

---

### Breakpoints

Preview configuration: `:columns="columns"`, `:data="rows"`, `:pagination="false"`.

Example source: src/style/atomic-css/__demos__/breakpoints.vue

```vue
<template>
  <c-space direction="column" fill size="md">
    <div class="hint">
      缩小浏览器窗口可观察当前命中的断点；类名形如
      <code>sm:c-bg-info</code>。
    </div>
    <div class="box">
      <div class="label">当前 ≥</div>
      <strong class="value">{{ active }}</strong>
    </div>
    <c-table :columns="columns" :data="rows" :pagination="false" />
  </c-space>
</template>

<script lang="ts" setup>
import { computed, onMounted, onUnmounted, ref } from "vue";

const width = ref(typeof window !== "undefined" ? window.innerWidth : 0);

const onResize = () => {
  width.value = window.innerWidth;
};

onMounted(() => {
  width.value = window.innerWidth;
  window.addEventListener("resize", onResize);
});

onUnmounted(() => {
  window.removeEventListener("resize", onResize);
});

const active = computed(() => {
  const w = width.value;
  if (w >= 1920) return "xl (1920px)";
  if (w >= 1200) return "lg (1200px)";
  if (w >= 992) return "md (992px)";
  if (w >= 768) return "sm (768px)";
  return "base (< sm)";
});

const columns = [
  { title: "前缀", dataIndex: "prefix" },
  { title: "最小宽度", dataIndex: "min" },
  { title: "示例类", dataIndex: "cls" },
];

const rows = [
  { prefix: "sm:", min: "768px", cls: "sm:c-bg-info" },
  { prefix: "md:", min: "992px", cls: "md:c-bg-warning" },
  { prefix: "lg:", min: "1200px", cls: "lg:c-bg-danger" },
  { prefix: "xl:", min: "1920px", cls: "xl:c-bg-success" },
];
</script>

<style scoped lang="scss">
.hint {
  font-size: 13px;
  color: var(--c-color-text-3);
}

.box {
  display: flex;
  align-items: baseline;
  gap: 8px;
  padding: 12px 16px;
  border-radius: 4px;
  background: var(--c-color-primary);
  color: #fff;
}

.label {
  opacity: 0.85;
  font-size: 13px;
}

.value {
  font-size: 18px;
}
</style>
```

# Style Elevation

Start with the basic example, then compare related settings before moving to controlled, asynchronous or combined use cases.

## Basic examples

### Class

Preview configuration: `:columns="columns"`, `:data="data"`, `:pagination="false"`.

Example source: src/style/elevation/__demos__/class.vue

```vue
<template>
  <c-space direction="column" fill size="lg">
    <c-table :columns="columns" :data="data" :pagination="false" />
  </c-space>
</template>
<script lang="ts" setup>
import { h } from "vue";
import { Message } from "@cedar-design/ui-vue";

const columns = [
  {
    title: "Class",
    dataIndex: "class",
    render: (data) => {
      return h(
        "div",
        {
          style: {
            cursor: "pointer",
          },
          onClick: () => {
            navigator.clipboard
              .writeText(data.record.class)
              .then(() => {
                Message.success("copy success");
              })
              .catch(() => {
                Message.fail("copy fail");
              });
          },
        },
        data.record.class,
      );
    },
  },
  {
    title: "Properties",
    dataIndex: "properties",
  },
];

const data = Array.from({ length: 25 }, (_, i) => ({
  class: `c-elevation--${i}`,
  properties: `Material elevation level ${i}`,
}));
</script>
```

```vue
<template>
  <c-table :columns="columns" :data="data" :pagination="false" />

<script lang="ts" setup>
import { h } from "vue";
import { Message } from "@cedar-design/ui-vue";

const columns = [
  {
    title: "Class",
    dataIndex: "class",
    render: (data) => {
      return h(
        "div",
        {
          style: {
            cursor: "pointer",
          },
          onClick: () => {
            navigator.clipboard
              .writeText(data.record.class)
              .then(() => {
                Message.success("copy success");
              })
              .catch((err) => {
                Message.fail("copy fail");
              });
          },
        },
        data.record.class,
      );
    },
  },
  {
    title: "Effective CSS",
    dataIndex: "effective",
    render: (data) => {
      return h("div", {
        innerHTML: `<div>${data.record.effective?.replaceAll("\n", "<br/>")}</div>`, // 等效于 v-html
      });
    },
  },
];
const data = [
  {
    class: "c-text-left",
    properties: "text-align: left !important;",
    effective: "text-align: left !important;",
  },
  {
    class: "c-text-center",
    properties: "text-align: center !important;",
    effective: "text-align: center !important;",
  },
  {
    class: "c-text-right",
    properties: "text-align: right !important;",
    effective: "text-align: right !important;",
  },
  {
    class: "c-text-justify",
    properties: "text-align: justify !important;",
    effective: "text-align: justify !important;",
  },
];
</script>
```

<!-- Source: src/switch/README.en-US.md; locale: en-US; page: /en/components/switch/ -->

# Switch

The same scenarios, parameters and interactions as Cedar. Only component prefixes differ; themes and site shells remain independent.

## Reading direction

Switch inherits source dir: its unchecked handle starts at inline start and moves toward inline end when checked. Space/Enter still toggle. Direction changes do not modify values; disabled, readonly and loading states block commits.

## Basic examples

### Controlled and default value

Example source: src/switch/__demos__/basic.vue

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { ref } from 'vue'
const enabled = ref(false)
</script>

<template>
  <c-space wrap
    ><c-switch v-model="enabled" aria-label="Enable notifications" /><output>{{ enabled }}</output
    ><c-switch :default-value="true" aria-label="Initially enabled"
  /></c-space>
</template>
```

## Appearance and states

### Appearance configuration comparison

Choose a dimension to compare all its values side by side while keeping other settings and content identical. Change the other settings to inspect combinations; input specimens share one model.

Example source: src/switch/__demos__/appearance-lab.vue

```vue
<script setup>
import { useDemoLocale } from "../../__demos__/locale";
const demoCopy = useDemoLocale("comparison");
import { reactive as __demoReactive } from "vue";
import { ref } from "vue";
const value = ref(false);
const __demoAppearance = __demoReactive({ variant: "circle", size: "md" });

import { computed as demoComputed, ref as demoRef } from "vue";
const demoCompareFields = [
  { name: "variant", values: ["circle", "round", "line", "tonal"] },
  { name: "size", values: ["sm", "md", "lg"] },
];
const demoCompareAxis = demoRef("variant");
const demoComparedOptions = demoComputed(
  () =>
    demoCompareFields.find((field) => field.name === demoCompareAxis.value)
      ?.values ?? [],
);
</script>
<template>
  <c-space direction="column" :size="16">
    <c-form layout="vertical">
      <c-form-item layout="vertical" size="sm" label="variant">
        <c-radio-group
          v-model="__demoAppearance['variant']"
          aria-label="variant"
          :options="[
            { label: 'circle', value: 'circle' },
            { label: 'round', value: 'round' },
            { label: 'line', value: 'line' },
            { label: 'tonal', value: 'tonal' },
          ]"
          variant="button"
          size="sm"
        />
      </c-form-item>
      <c-form-item layout="vertical" size="sm" label="size">
        <c-radio-group
          v-model="__demoAppearance['size']"
          aria-label="size"
          :options="[
            { label: 'sm', value: 'sm' },
            { label: 'md', value: 'md' },
            { label: 'lg', value: 'lg' },
          ]"
          variant="button"
          size="sm"
        />
      </c-form-item>
    </c-form>
    <p class="demo-config-comparison-hint">{{ demoCopy.hint }}</p>
    <c-radio-group
      v-model="demoCompareAxis"
      :aria-label="demoCopy.configuration"
      :options="
        demoCompareFields.map((field) => ({
          label: field.name,
          value: field.name,
        }))
      "
    />
    <div class="demo-config-comparison">
      <section v-for="sample in demoComparedOptions" :key="String(sample)">
        <p>
          <code>{{ demoCompareAxis }}={{ sample }}</code>
        </p>
        <c-switch
          v-model="value"
          v-bind="{ ...__demoAppearance, [demoCompareAxis]: sample }"
        ></c-switch>
      </section>
    </div>
  </c-space>
</template>

<style scoped>
.demo-config-comparison {
  display: grid;
  grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fit, minmax(min(100%, 220px), 1fr));
  gap: 20px;
  min-width: 0;
  max-width: 100%;
}
.demo-config-comparison > section {
  min-width: 0;
}
.demo-config-comparison p {
  margin: 0 0 8px;
}
</style>
```

#### Configuration reference for this comparison

| Configuration | Purpose | Related examples |
| ----------------- | -------------- | ---------------------- |

| `unchecked-color` | Unchecked track color | Custom colors |

## Interaction and control

### Interaction state comparison

<!-- demo-config-notes:start -->

#### Configuration reference for this comparison

| Configuration | Purpose | Related examples |
| --------------- | --------------------------------------------------------- | -------------- |
| `disabled` | Disable interaction, including inherited form disabled state | Interaction state comparison |
| `readonly` | Read only; focus and click remain available without toggling | Interaction state comparison |
| `variant` | Appearance | Loading |
| `loading` | Loading; blocks clicks and changes | Loading |
| `default-value` | Initial uncontrolled value; falls back to uncheckedValue | Loading |
| `size` | Size; omitted value follows platform rules below | Focus and event order |

<!-- demo-config-notes:end -->


Toggle disabled, read-only and error states, then interact with the same instance. Recovery controls remain outside the target; error appearance alone does not validate data.

Example source: src/switch/__demos__/state-lab.vue

```vue
<script setup>
import { reactive as __demoReactive } from "vue";
import { ref } from "vue";
const value = ref(false);
const __demoState = __demoReactive({ disabled: false, readonly: false });
</script>
<template>
  <c-space direction="column" :size="16">
    <c-space wrap>
      <c-checkbox v-model="__demoState['disabled']">disabled</c-checkbox>
      <c-checkbox v-model="__demoState['readonly']">readonly</c-checkbox>
    </c-space>
    <c-switch v-model="value" v-bind="__demoState"></c-switch>
  </c-space>
</template>
```

### Loading

Example source: src/switch/__demos__/loading.vue

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
const variants = ['circle', 'round', 'line', 'tonal'] as const
</script>

<template>
  <c-space wrap
    ><template v-for="variant in variants" :key="variant"
      ><c-switch :variant="variant" loading :aria-label="variant + ' off'" /><c-switch
        :variant="variant"
        :default-value="true"
        loading
        :aria-label="variant + ' on'" /></template
  ></c-space>
</template>
```

### Focus and event order

Example source: src/switch/__demos__/events.vue

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { ref } from 'vue'
const value = ref(false)
const events = ref<string[]>([])
function record(name: string) {
  events.value = [...events.value.slice(-7), name]
}
</script>

<template>
  <p>Use Tab to focus, then Space or Enter to toggle.</p>
  <c-switch
    v-model="value"
    size="md"
    aria-label="Event sequence"
    @focus="record('focus')"
    @blur="record('blur')"
    @click="record('click')"
    @update:model-value="record(`update: ${$event}`)"
    @change="record(`change: ${$event}`)"
  />
  <p aria-live="polite">{{ events.join(' → ') || 'No events yet' }}</p>
  <c-button @click="events = []">Clear events</c-button>
</template>
```

### Custom values and events

## Async and dynamic data

### Async allow, deny and rejection

Example source: src/switch/__demos__/switch-interception.vue

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { ref } from 'vue'
const result = ref('Ready')
const wait = () => new Promise<void>((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, 500))
async function allow() {
  await wait()
  result.value = 'Allowed'
  return true
}
async function deny() {
  await wait()
  result.value = 'Blocked'
  return false
}
async function reject() {
  await wait()
  result.value = 'Rejected'
  throw new Error('Demo rejection')
}
</script>

<template>
  <c-space direction="column">
    <label>Allow after 500ms <c-switch :before-change="allow" aria-label="Async allow" /></label>
    <label>Return false <c-switch :before-change="deny" aria-label="Async deny" /></label>
    <label>Reject Promise <c-switch :before-change="reject" aria-label="Async rejection" /></label>
    <output aria-live="polite">{{ result }}</output>
  </c-space>
</template>
```

## Usage notes

### Configuration

Use the CSS Variables table below to customize dimensions and colors.

## API

### Empty values and reading placeholders

`empty-values` recognizes empty data; `empty-value` keeps existing clear output. `empty-text` defaults to `'-'` under `read-pretty`, with Field > FormItem > Form precedence and custom read slots first. With explicit `empty-values`, built-in required uses the policy; custom validators receive original data. See the [shared guide](llms/en-US/guide/empty-values.md).

| Prop | Type | Default and scope |
| ------------ | ------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------- |
| empty-values | readonly unknown[] | Field > FormItem > Form > component-family default; replaces the whole list |
| empty-text | string | Field > FormItem > Form > '-'; explicit '' is valid |

These props belong to field presentation; pure panels do not gain reading mode. Form and FormItem provide inherited settings. The existing empty-value type and clear fallback remain component-specific.

### Value and default value

Use ordinary `v-model`. `modelValue` is the actual switch value and matches checkedValue/uncheckedValue types. `defaultValue` initializes uncontrolled state once; later changes do not reset it. Explicit binding takes precedence, with no initialization `update:modelValue`.

<!-- same-source-api:start -->

### Switch Props

| Prop | Meaning | Type | Default |
| ---------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------- |
| model-value | Controlled value; managed internally when omitted | string / number / boolean | undefined |
| default-value | Initial uncontrolled value; falls back to uncheckedValue | string / number / boolean | undefined |
| clearable | Show clearing in popup editing | boolean | false |
| empty-value | Value committed after clearing; accepts a value or factory | SwitchValue \| null \| (() => SwitchValue \| null) | undefined |
| empty-values | Empty-value recognition list; fully replaces inherited configuration | readonly unknown[] | Inherits the field empty-value policy |
| empty-text | Reading placeholder; field > FormItem > Form | string | - |
| edit-mode | Editing mode; inherits FormItem/Form when unset. See editing-mode guidance for platform-specific values | FieldEditMode<br>`'direct' \| 'click' \| 'dblclick'` | undefined |
| read-pretty | Plain reading display, independent of readonly | boolean | undefined |
| before-commit | Cancelable interceptor before saving the editor | BeforeFieldCommit | undefined |
| open | Controlled editor open state | boolean | undefined |
| default-open | Initial uncontrolled editor state | boolean | false |
| popup-container | Editor mount container | PopupContainer | undefined |
| checked-value | Checked value | string / number / boolean | true |
| unchecked-value | Unchecked value | string / number / boolean | false |
| variant | Appearance | circle / round / line / tonal | circle |
| size | Size; omitted value follows platform rules below | sm / md / lg | undefined |
| disabled | Disable interaction, including inherited form disabled state | boolean | undefined |
| readonly | Read only; focus and click remain available without toggling | boolean | undefined |
| loading | Loading; blocks clicks and changes | boolean | false |
| before-change | Switch interceptor, not an event | (payload, done, context) => boolean / void / Promise<boolean / void> | — |
| checked-text | Checked label | string | — |
| unchecked-text | Unchecked label | string | — |
| checked-color | Checked track color | string | — |
| unchecked-color | Unchecked track color | string | — |
| loading-color | Loading-icon color | string | — |
| ripple | Click ripple | boolean | true |
| handle-elevation | Thumb elevation: true means level 2; numbers are integer-clamped to 0–24 | boolean / number | true |

before-change uses (payload, done, context). Return true, call done(), or fulfill a Promise with a non-false result to allow switching. Return false, call done(false), throw, fulfill with false or reject to cancel. Synchronous void waits for done; fulfilled `Promise<void>` allows. Waiting automatically shows loading and blocks duplicate input. In deferred editing, confirmation is disabled while waiting; closing the editor still cancels the operation. Exceptions cancel permission without adding an error event.
Pending results become stale after unmount, KeepAlive deactivation, external value updates or changes to disabled/readonly/loading.
Controlled mode only requests updates. Selection changes after the parent updates model-value. Without model-value, internal state is used.

### Switch Events

| Event | Arguments and timing |
| ------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------- |
| click | (event: Event), before interception when clicking is allowed |
| update:model-value | (nextValue: SwitchValue), after switching is allowed and before change |
| change | (nextValue: SwitchValue, event?: Event), once per commit |
| focus | (event: FocusEvent), on focus |
| blur | (event: FocusEvent), on blur |

Supports Enter/Space without repeated toggles on key repeat. disabled/loading emit neither click nor value changes; readonly may emit click without running the interceptor.
External model-value updates do not emit an extra change.

### Switch Slots

| Slot | Description | Prop |
| -------------- | ---------------------------------------------------- | ---- |
| checked | Checked label; overrides checked-text; hidden for line/sm | — |
| unchecked | Unchecked label; overrides unchecked-text; hidden for line/sm | — |
| checked-icon | Checked thumb icon; replaced while loading | — |
| unchecked-icon | Unchecked thumb icon; replaced while loading | — |

### Switch Methods

No public methods.

### Usage notes

Props, event arguments and slots match. Cedar inherits omitted size from Form/global settings: xs/sm map to sm; lg/xl map to lg. Maple defaults to md. Both inherit disabled/readonly from field > FormItem > Form, with explicit false overriding the parent. Form integration is local to each platform.
<!-- same-source-api:end -->

## Types

SwitchProps, SwitchVariant, SwitchSize, SwitchValue, SwitchBeforeChange and SwitchInstance are exported from both root and component entries.

## Inheriting Form disabled state

The default disabled=undefined means inheritance, resolved as local ?? FormItem ?? Form ?? false. Explicit false remains effective, allowing one field to stay enabled while unspecified fields follow Form. Form disabled is the form-wide default, not a lock preventing child overrides.

`empty-value` accepts explicit `null` (or `() => null`). Clearing publishes `null` unchanged; omitted values preserve the existing default. Editors render `null` as blank without converting ordinary empty-string input to `null`. In popup editing, clearing changes the draft; confirm commits it and cancel preserves the original model.

```vue
<c-switch v-model="flag" :before-change="beforeChange" />
```

```ts
const beforeChange = (payload, done, context) => {
  canChange(payload.value, { previousValue: payload.previousValue, signal: context.signal })
    .then((allowed) => done(allowed), () => done(false));
};
```

Cancellable hooks use `(payload, done, context)`: closure payloads contain `{ action }`, change/commit payloads contain `{ value, previousValue }`, and Popup uses `{ reason }`. Context provides `signal` and an optional original `event`. Return a boolean/Promise, or call done()/done(false). Synchronous void waits for done; Promise&lt;void&gt; allows the operation. First completion wins. Pending state controls loading/disabled automatically. Cancellation invalidates stale results. Button refs are not exposed.

### Async operation feedback

Awaited before-* hooks show loading feedback and aria-busy. Rejection or failure restores interaction; repeated input does not start the same operation again. Ordinary event return Promises do not participate in loading.

Deferred `change` preserves the real confirmation event when available (for example, the save button). Programmatic editor handoff has no DOM event, so its second argument is optional. The event target can be the confirmation control rather than the input. `change` is a notification: its returned Promise is not awaited; use `before-commit` to approve asynchronous saves.

When using ThemeProvider, follow its local-theme and popup configuration rules. ### Motion

Built-in motion follows `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`. Reduced motion does not prevent loading-state or close-event updates.

### Track and handle colors

| Variable suffix: --c-switch- | Default system role | Responsibility |
| ----------------------- | ----------------- | ---------------------------------------- |
| track-background | content-secondary | Ordinary unchecked solid track |
| track-active-background | content-brand | Checked track and keyboard-focus ring |
| track-error-background | content-danger | Interactive error track and tonal error border |
| handle-background | surface-default | Ordinary/checked/error thumb fill |
| handle-color | content-brand | Ordinary/checked/error thumb icon color |
| text-color | surface-default | Text on a solid track |
| checked-text-color | switch-text-color | Checked-track text; error retains existing foreground precedence |
| tonal-track-background | surface-muted | Tonal unchecked-track background |
| tonal-border-color | content-secondary | Tonal unchecked border and thumb fill |
| tonal-text-color | content-secondary | Tonal unchecked-track text |
| tonal-handle-color | surface-default | Tonal unchecked-thumb icon |

Defaults use the corresponding system roles, such as var(--c-sys-color-content-secondary). Unchecked tonal uses tonal-text-color / tonal-handle-color; override both ordinary and tonal foregrounds when customizing every variant. Interactive error state uses paired text/handle colors, while disabled / loading suppresses error colors. Keep foregrounds readable on custom track colors.

# Table Column Manager

Start with the basic example, then compare related settings before moving to controlled, asynchronous or combined use cases.

## Basic examples

### Basic usage

- `options`: Supplies the available options.

Example source: src/table-column-manager/__demos__/basic.vue

```vue
<template>
  <c-space>
    <c-button @click="openDrawer = true">抽屉中管理列</c-button>
    <c-button @click="openDialog = true">弹窗中管理列</c-button>
  </c-space>

  <c-table-column-manager
    v-model:open="openDrawer"
    v-model="items"
    :columns="columns"
    :options="columnDefinitions"
    :fallback-item="fallbackItem"
    @confirm="applyResult"
  />

  <c-dialog v-model:open="openDialog" title="列管理" :width="720" :body-padding="false" unmount-on-close>
    <div style="height: 480px">
      <c-table-column-manager
        inline
        v-model="items"
        :columns="columns"
        :options="columnDefinitions"
      />
    </div>
  </c-dialog>

  <pre style="margin-top: 16px; font-size: 12px">
items: {{ items }}
columns: {{ columns.map((c) => c.dataIndex).join(', ') }}</pre
  >
</template>

<script setup lang="ts">
import { ref } from 'vue'
import type {
  ColumnDefinition,
  ColumnDefinitions,
  ColumnManagerItem,
  ColumnManagerResult,
  TableColumnData,
} from '@cedar-design/ui-vue'

const openDrawer = ref(false)
const openDialog = ref(false)

const items = ref<ColumnManagerItem[]>([
  { dataIndex: 'connectorId', fixed: 'left' },
  { dataIndex: 'connectorName' },
  { dataIndex: 'deviceName' },
])

const columns = ref<TableColumnData[]>([
  { dataIndex: 'connectorId', title: '枪ID', width: 100, fixed: 'left' },
  { dataIndex: 'connectorName', title: '枪名称', width: 120 },
  { dataIndex: 'deviceName', title: '设备名称', width: 120 },
])

const columnDefinitions = ref<ColumnDefinitions>([
  {
    title: '基本信息',
    key: 'basic',
    children: [
      {
        dataIndex: 'connectorId',
        title: '枪ID',
        required: true,
        tip: '必选列',
      },
      {
        dataIndex: 'connectorName',
        title: '枪名称',
      },
      {
        dataIndex: 'areaCompany',
        title: '区域公司区域公司区域公司区域公司区域公司区域公司',
        tip: '区域公司说明',
      },
    ],
  },
  {
    title: '设备信息',
    key: 'device',
    children: [
      { dataIndex: 'deviceId', title: '设备ID' },
      { dataIndex: 'deviceName', title: '设备名称' },
      { dataIndex: 'lockStatus', title: '地锁' },
    ],
  },
  { dataIndex: 'workingStatus', title: '工作状态' },
  { dataIndex: 'connectStatus', title: '连接状态' },
])

const fallbackItem = (dataIndex: string): ColumnDefinition => {
  return { dataIndex, title: dataIndex }
}

const applyResult = (result: ColumnManagerResult) => {
  columns.value = result.columns
  items.value = result.items
}
</script>
```

```vue
    </c-space>

    <c-table
      v-model:columns="columns"
      extra-column
      column-resizable
      :data="data"
      :pagination="false"
      :bordered="{ cell: true, headerCell: true }"
      :fit="fit"

      size="xs"
      @column-resize="handleColumnResize"
    >
      <template #extra-column-header>
        <c-button variant="text" size="xs" aria-label="管理列" @click="open">
          <c-icon-settings />
        </c-button>
      </template>
      <template #extra-column-cell />

      <template #header-cell-actions="{ column, dataIndex }">
        <HeaderAction :data-index="dataIndex" :column="column" />
      </template>

      <template #priority="{ record }">
        <c-tag :color="priorityColor(record.priority)" size="sm">{{
          record.priority
        }}</c-tag>
      </template>
      <template #status="{ record }">

          record.status
        }}</c-tag>
      </template>
    </c-table>

    <!-- 列管理抽屉 + 插入/编辑弹窗 -->
    <c-table-column-manager v-bind="managerProps" />
  </c-space>

<script lang="ts" setup>

    tableLayout.value = val ? "fixed" : "auto";
```

## Async catalog and search

### Remote

Preview configuration: `v-model:columns="columns"`, `:data="data"`, `:pagination="false"`, `size="xs"`.

Example source: src/table-column-manager/__demos__/remote.vue

```vue
<template>
  <c-space direction="column" size="md">
    <c-alert type="info" :show-icon="false">
      弹窗候选列由 <code>columnSource.search</code> 远程搜索；恢复缓存遇到本地未知列时，通过
      <code>columnSource.resolve</code> 批量反显。远程接口只返回 dataIndex、title 和分组信息。
    </c-alert>

    <div class="demo-toolbar">
      <c-button status="secondary" size="sm" @click="open">远程管理列</c-button>
      <c-link @click="resetToDefault">恢复本地默认列</c-link>
    </div>

    <c-table v-model:columns="columns" :data="data" :pagination="false" size="xs" />
    <c-table-column-manager v-bind="managerProps" />
  </c-space>
</template>

<script setup lang="ts">
import { onMounted, ref } from 'vue'
import { useTableColumnManager } from '@cedar-design/ui-vue'
import type { ColumnDefinition, ColumnDefinitionSource, ManagedTableColumn } from '@cedar-design/ui-vue'

const defaultColumns: ManagedTableColumn[] = [
  { dataIndex: 'id', title: '编号', width: 100, fixed: 'left', manager: { required: true } },
  { dataIndex: 'name', title: '名称', minWidth: 180 },
]

// 模拟服务端保存的轻量字段目录。
const remoteFields: Array<ColumnDefinition & { group?: string }> = [
  { dataIndex: 'id', title: '编号', group: '基础信息' },
  { dataIndex: 'name', title: '名称', group: '基础信息' },
  { dataIndex: 'owner', title: '负责人', group: '基础信息' },
  { dataIndex: 'remoteConfig1', title: '远程配置 1', group: '远程配置' },
  { dataIndex: 'remoteConfig2', title: '远程配置 2', group: '远程配置' },
  { dataIndex: 'remoteStatus', title: '远程状态', group: '远程配置' },
]

const wait = (duration: number) => new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, duration))
const groupDefinitions = (items: typeof remoteFields) =>
  [...new Set(items.map((item) => item.group ?? '其他'))].map((group) => ({
    key: group,
    title: group,
    children: items
      .filter((item) => (item.group ?? '其他') === group)
      .map(({ group: _group, ...definition }) => definition),
  }))

const columnSource: ColumnDefinitionSource = {
  async search({ keyword }) {
    await wait(300)
    const normalized = keyword.trim().toLowerCase()
    const matched = normalized
      ? remoteFields.filter(
          (item) => item.title.toLowerCase().includes(normalized) || item.dataIndex.toLowerCase().includes(normalized)
        )
      : remoteFields
    return { items: groupDefinitions(matched), total: matched.length }
  },
  async resolve(dataIndexes) {
    await wait(200)
    const keys = new Set(dataIndexes)
    return remoteFields.filter((item) => keys.has(item.dataIndex)).map(({ group: _group, ...item }) => item)
  },
}

const { columns, managerProps, open, restore, resetToDefault } = useTableColumnManager({
  defaultColumns,
  columnSource,
  columnDefaults: { width: 140, ellipsis: true },
  createColumn: (definition) =>
    definition.dataIndex === 'remoteStatus'
      ? { dataIndex: definition.dataIndex, title: definition.title, width: 110 }
      : { dataIndex: definition.dataIndex, title: definition.title },
})

onMounted(async () => {
  // 模拟缓存中包含一个不在本地 defaultColumns 里的远程列。
  await restore({
    version: 2,
    items: [{ dataIndex: 'id', fixed: 'left' }, { dataIndex: 'name' }, { dataIndex: 'remoteConfig2' }],
  })
})

const data = ref([
  {
    id: 'T-001',
    name: '远程字段示例',
    owner: '张三',
    remoteConfig1: '配置 A',
    remoteConfig2: '配置 B',
    remoteStatus: '已同步',
  },
])
</script>

<style scoped>
.demo-toolbar {
  display: flex;
  align-items: center;
  gap: 12px;
}
</style>
```

## API

### State and persistence structure

Column order, titles and fixed positions are stored together in `items`. The component/`useTableColumnManager` do not cache state. Business code may persist
the following state to localStorage, Pinia or a server:

```ts
const state: ColumnManagerState = {
  version: 2,
  items: [
    { dataIndex: 'id', fixed: 'left', width: 120 },
    { dataIndex: 'name', title: 'User name' },
  ],
  layout: [],
}
```



```ts
const { state, restore } = useTableColumnManager({ defaultColumns, columnDefinitions })
const storageReady = ref(false)

onMounted(async () => {
  const raw = window.localStorage.getItem(STORAGE_KEY)
  if (raw) await restore(JSON.parse(raw))
  storageReady.value = true
})

watch(
  state,
  (value) => {
    if (!storageReady.value) return
    window.localStorage.setItem(STORAGE_KEY, JSON.stringify(value))
  },
  { deep: true }
)
```

`restore()` validates versions, removes stale/duplicate columns, cleans invalid widths/layouts, adds `required` columns and repairs fixed-region ordering.
`state` records only user-renamed titles and widths changed through `handleColumnResize`. Debounce server persistence in business code if needed.

### Default columns and candidate definitions

`defaultColumns` supplies complete initial Table columns and the reset baseline. `columnDefinitions` supplies popup candidates only and may contain just
`dataIndex`, `title`, grouping and hints:

```ts
const defaultColumns: ManagedTableColumn[] = [
  {
    title: 'Basic information',
    children: [
      {
        dataIndex: 'id',
        title: 'ID',
        fixed: 'left',
        width: 120,
        manager: { required: true },
      },
      { dataIndex: 'name', title: 'Name', minWidth: 180 },
    ],
  },
]

const columnDefinitions: ColumnDefinitions = [
  {
    key: 'base',
    title: 'Basic information',
    children: [
      { dataIndex: 'id', title: 'ID' },
      { dataIndex: 'name', title: 'Name' },
      { dataIndex: 'remark', title: 'Notes', tip: 'Optional column' },
    ],
  },
]

const manager = useTableColumnManager({
  defaultColumns,
  columnDefinitions,
  columnDefaults: { width: 140, ellipsis: true },
  createColumn: (definition) => ({ dataIndex: definition.dataIndex, title: definition.title }),
})
```

- `defaultColumns` determines initial display, reset, default width, fixed position, slots, rendering and `manager.required`.
- `columnDefinitions` determines popup candidates, not Table rendering configuration.
- `columnDefaults` supplies common Table defaults for new ordinary columns.
- `createColumn` handles a few candidates requiring special width, slots or rendering.
- For remote data, `columnSource.search` searches and `columnSource.resolve` restores unknown selected columns. `restore()` then returns a Promise.

Prefer passing either `columnDefinitions` or `columnSource`. For compatibility, if both are supplied, local definitions take precedence for the catalog; remote `search` still runs but does not replace local definitions, while remote `resolve` can still restore unknown columns. Remote `search` requests one page at a time; it does not automatically use `nextCursor` or paginate using `total`. Return the complete catalog from the application source when all candidates are needed.

`restore()` always returns a Promise and rejects if remote `resolve` fails; the caller handles that failure. State stores only the version, leaf columns, and optional layout; keep functions such as `render` in `defaultColumns` or an application registry. Opening the panel creates a draft from the current columns, closing discards the draft, and confirming applies it. A `required` default column cannot be removed and is restored if missing; `resetToDefault()` restores default columns.

### TableColumnManager Props

| Parameter | Description | Type | Default |
| ------------- | ---------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------- | ---------- |
| model-value | Complete ordered selected-column state, including titles/fixed positions | `ColumnManagerItem[]` | `-` |
| default-value | Initial uncontrolled selected state | `ColumnManagerItem[]` | `-` |
| columns | Current Table columns; assembled back into full definitions on confirmation | `TableColumnData[]` | `[]` |
| registry-columns | Full registry of hidden default columns, preserving render configuration when restored | `TableColumnData[]` | `-` |
| column-defaults | Default configuration for newly added ordinary columns | `Partial<TableColumnData>` | `-` |
| create-column | Construct a new column from its catalog definition | `(definition: ColumnCatalogItem) => TableColumnData` | `-` |
| options | Left-side column definitions | `ColumnDefinitions` | `[]` |
| load-options | Asynchronously load column definitions | `() => Promise<ColumnDefinitions>` | `-` |
| remote-search | Remote search; hides top select-all when provided | `(keyword: string) => Promise<void>` | `-` |
| fallback-item | Resolve display for values absent from definitions | `(dataIndex: string) => ColumnDefinition \| undefined` | `-` |
| insert-at | Insertion context determining where new columns land | `{ dataIndex: string; side: 'left' \| 'right' }` | `-` |
| open | Drawer visibility; `v-model:open` | `boolean` | `-` |
| drawer-title | Drawer title | `string` | `自定义列` |
| drawer-width | Drawer width | `number \| string` | `720` |
| inline | Render only the inline panel without a drawer | `boolean` | `false` |
| placeholder | Search placeholder | `string` | `-` |

### TableColumnManager Events

| Event | Description | Arguments |
| ----------------- | ------------------------------- | --------------------- |
| update:model-value | Complete selected-state changes | `ColumnManagerItem[]` |
| update:open | Drawer visibility changes | `boolean` |
| confirm | Assembled result after drawer/dialog confirmation | `ColumnManagerResult` |
| change | Selection, order, fixed-position or title changes | `ColumnManagerItem[]` |
| load-error | Current catalog load or remote search failed | `error: unknown, source: 'catalog' \| 'search'` |

### TableColumnManager Methods

| Method | Description | Returns |
| ----------- | ------------------------ | --------------------- |
| getResult | Assemble Table columns from current selection | `ColumnManagerResult` |
| loadCatalog | Manually invoke `loadOptions` | `Promise<void>` |
| resetInitialKeys | Reset the baseline for identifying new columns to the current selection | `void` |

### `useTableColumnManager`

Recommended with `c-table`. Returns `columns`, `state`, `restore`, `managerProps`, `HeaderAction` and others.
`HeaderAction` obtains context directly through `inject`; templates only need:

```vue
<template #header-cell-actions="{ column, dataIndex }">
  <HeaderAction :data-index="dataIndex" :column="column" />
</template>
```

`headerActions` configures visible header-action keys; all are shown by default.

The following members are returned; read `Ref` / `ComputedRef` via `.value` in scripts:

| Member | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `columns`、`leafColumns`、`state` | Current table columns, leaf-column summary, and persistable state |
| `managerVisible`、`managerRef`、`managerProps` | Panel visibility, instance reference, and pre-bound props/events |
| `open`、`close`、`confirm` | Open and create a draft, close, and confirm changes |
| `insertColumns`、`getInsertableItems` | Insert columns at an anchor and retrieve available candidates |
| `getEditInitialValues`、`applyEdit` | Get initial edit values and apply title/group changes |
| `freezeColumn`、`removeColumn` | Freeze or unfreeze columns and remove removable columns |
| `resetToDefault`、`restore`、`handleColumnResize` | Reset, restore persisted state, and save width changes |
| `headerActions`、`columnActions`、`HeaderAction` | Available header actions, pre-bound actions, and header button component |
| `openInsert`、`insertVisible`、`insertSide`、`insertableItems`、`insertSelected`、`handleInsertConfirm` | Insert dialog entry, state, and confirmation method |
| `openEdit`、`editVisible`、`editGroupTitle`、`editColumnTitle`、`handleEditConfirm` | Edit dialog entry, state, and confirmation method |

Header-action behavior:

- Insert left/right: new columns enter the anchor's first-level group, preserving group titles/`colspan`. If the anchor is fixed, new columns inherit its fixed position.
- Fix/unfix: reorder leaf columns so fixed columns collect at the left/right edge.
- Edit columns: edit first-level group titles and column names; adjacent equal-name groups merge automatically.

Required rules need declaration only in `defaultColumns`. Transfer, clearing and header deletion all follow them:

```ts
{
  dataIndex: 'priority',
  title: 'Priority',
  manager: { required: true },
  fixed: 'left',
  width: 120,
  slotName: 'priority',
}
```

`columnDefinitions` need not duplicate width, fixed-position or required rules. User-resized widths persist in `items[].width`.

### Extra-column width

`c-table` `extra-column`, e.g. a settings control, defaults to 28px. Override with `extraColumn: { width: number }`.

### Utility functions in the column-management package

`buildColumnsResult` / `stateFromColumns` / `applyColumnEdit` / `applyColumnFixed` / `applyInsertToLayout` / `mapLeafColumns` support external assembly, group editing, fixed reordering and insertion. Traverse `columns` in business code for flat leaf lists; Table exports are unnecessary.

Catalog loading and remote search have separate pending states; an older task cannot release a newer wait. `loadOptions` runs on creation, loader replacement, and explicit `loadCatalog` calls. Current failures emit `load-error` with `source` identifying catalog or search; superseded requests do not emit. A manual `loadCatalog` call still rejects for the caller to handle; automatic loading and search report failures through the event. Notification listener Promises do not drive loading. Hook catalog loading and remote search use the latest catalog generation; restore has its own generation and newer column edits or unmount invalidate older results.

<!-- Source: src/table/README.en-US.md; locale: en-US; page: /en/components/table/ -->

# Table

The active sorted column exposes ascending or descending order through `aria-sort`. Inputs and buttons inside custom headers retain their own keyboard and click behavior.

Default row selection controls use the row key in their accessible names, and the select-all control uses a localized name. An explicit selection column title takes precedence.

When a height constraint, sticky header, or virtual list splits the table into multiple native tables, the data and summary tables include semantic headers in the same table, associated with cells through `headers`. The data table’s semantic header reflects the current sort; the summary table uses separate summary data and does not claim that its rows are sorted. An explicit `headers` on the `td` slot takes precedence; the caller is responsible for referencing valid headers in the same table. Adding, removing, or replacing structural `thead`, `tbody`, `tr`, `th`, and `td` slots updates the table; associated semantic headers also follow `th` changes. Virtual tables support a custom `tbody`; automatic virtual row counts and indices are omitted because the custom container may change the row structure. Content slots such as empty state, footer, summary cells, and named columns also support dynamic insertion, removal, and replacement. Screen-reader and complex custom-header acceptance is still pending; verify the target environment and provide accessible alternatives where needed.

## Basic examples

### Basic usage

Example source: src/table/__demos__/basic.vue

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
const columns = [
```

## Column widths, layout and fixed columns

### Column width scenarios

<!-- demo-config-notes:start -->
#### Configuration reference for this comparison

| Configuration | Purpose | Related examples |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `columns` | Column info of the table | Column width scenarios, Fixed columns, Grouped headers with fixed columns |
| `data` | Table data | Column width scenarios, Fixed columns, Grouped headers with fixed columns |
| `pagination` | Pagination properties configuration | Column width scenarios, Layout, sizing and column resizing |
| `bordered` | Whether to show border | Grouped headers with fixed columns, Layout, sizing and column resizing |
| `sticky-pagination` | Sticky pagination relative to the page/outer scroller; numeric values are bottom offsets in px | Column width scenarios |
| `row-selection` | Table row selector configuration | Column width scenarios |
<!-- demo-config-notes:end -->


Container width and column width are separate settings. Use `style="width: 100%"` or `style="width: 480px"` for the container, and `columns[].width` / `minWidth` for individual columns. No `scroll.x` or `scroll.y` configuration is required.

Horizontal scrolling needs a definite available width around the table. In flex or grid layouts, set `min-width: 0` or an explicit width on the item containing the table when needed to prevent its content from expanding ancestors.

Compare seven combinations and switch between 100%, 480px and 360px to observe recalculation and horizontal overflow.

| Configuration | Distribution with default `table-layout="fixed"`, `fit=true` |
| --- | --- |
| No column width | Each column starts at 80px and shares remaining space proportionally |
| `minWidth` | Base width of a flexible column; overflow preserves this width |
| `width` plus flexible columns | Explicit widths remain exact; flexible columns share remaining space in proportion to their base widths |
| Every column has `width` | Preserve widths on overflow; proportionally enlarge ordinary data columns when they do not fill the container |
| `fit=false` | Still fill the container; distribute remaining space proportionally across ordinary data columns |
| Selection / extra columns | Preserve selection operation width; exclude the extra column from proportional expansion |

Flexible columns have no explicit `width`. `minWidth` does not turn an explicit-width column into a flexible column. These distribution rules apply to `fixed` layout.

Example source: src/table/__demos__/column-width-scenarios.vue

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { ref } from 'vue'
import type { TableColumnData } from '@cedar-design/ui-vue'

const tableWidth = ref('100%')
const data = [{ key: '1', name: '设备巡检', owner: '张三', status: '进行中' }]
const base: TableColumnData[] = [
  { title: '任务', dataIndex: 'name' },
  { title: '负责人', dataIndex: 'owner' },
  { title: '状态', dataIndex: 'status' },
]
const scenarios = [
  { title: '不指定列宽', description: '每列以 80px 为基础，均分剩余空间。', columns: base },
  { title: '全部使用 minWidth', description: '按 160 : 80 : 80 的基础宽度比例分配剩余空间。', columns: base.map((column, index) => ({ ...column, minWidth: index === 0 ? 160 : 80 })) },
  { title: '定宽列与弹性列混合', description: '负责人、状态各保持 120px，任务列吸收剩余空间。', columns: base.map((column, index) => ({ ...column, ...(index === 0 ? { minWidth: 160 } : { width: 120 }) })) },
  { title: '全部指定 width', description: '列宽之和不足容器时，Cedar 按比例放大普通数据列以铺满容器。', columns: base.map((column, index) => ({ ...column, width: index === 0 ? 160 : 80 })) },
  { title: '列宽之和超出容器', description: '三列各 280px，保留列宽并自动出现横向滚动条，无需 scroll.x。', columns: base.map(column => ({ ...column, width: 280 })) },
  { title: '左右固定列与混合列宽', description: '左右各固定 140px、120px，中间列 minWidth 为 440px；无需 scroll.x，底部粘性滚动条随表格悬浮显示。', columns: [{ ...base[0], width: 140, fixed: 'left' as const }, { ...base[1], minWidth: 440 }, { ...base[2], width: 120, fixed: 'right' as const }], sticky: true },
  { title: '选择列、弹性列与扩展列', description: '选择列保持 40px，扩展列保持 28px，任务列分配剩余空间。', columns: base.map((column, index) => ({ ...column, ...(index === 0 ? { minWidth: 160 } : { width: 120 }) })), operations: true },
]
</script>

<template>
  <div class="column-width-scenarios">
    <c-radio-group v-model="tableWidth" type="button" aria-label="表格宽度">
      <c-radio value="480px">定宽 480px</c-radio>
      <c-radio value="100%">100% 宽度</c-radio>
      <c-radio value="360px">窄屏 360px</c-radio>
    </c-radio-group>
    <section v-for="scenario in scenarios" :key="scenario.title">
      <h4>{{ scenario.title }}</h4>
      <p>{{ scenario.description }}</p>
      <c-table
        :columns="scenario.columns"
        :data="data"
        :style="{ width: tableWidth }"
        :pagination="scenario.sticky ? { pageSize: 5 } : false"
        :sticky-pagination="scenario.sticky ? 0 : false"
        :row-selection="scenario.operations ? { width: 40 } : undefined"
        :extra-column="scenario.operations"
      />
    </section>
  </div>
</template>

<style scoped>
.column-width-scenarios { width: 640px; max-width: 100%; }
.column-width-scenarios > section { margin-top: 24px; }
h4 { margin: 0 0 8px; }
p { margin: 0 0 12px; }
</style>
```

### Layout, sizing and column resizing

Compare the same columns by switching layout, fit, grouped headers, resizing and container width in one table.

| Configuration | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| `table-layout="fixed"` (default) | Computed widths are written to `<col>`; long content does not stretch columns arbitrarily |
| `table-layout="auto"` | The browser allocates actual widths based on content; fixed-column offsets use measured widths |
| `column-resizable` | Resize handles appear only in `fixed` layout; resized widths participate in recalculation |
| `max-height` or column `ellipsis` | Force `fixed` layout |

An explicit `width` stays exact with flexible columns and `fit=true`. If every column has a width, or `fit=false`, proportional expansion still fills the container.

Example source: src/table/__demos__/column-sizing-playground.vue

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { useDemoLocale } from "../../__demos__/locale";
import { computed, ref } from "vue";
import type { TableColumnData } from "@cedar-design/ui-vue";

const copy = useDemoLocale("columnSizingPlayground");
const layout = ref<"fixed" | "auto">("fixed");
const fit = ref(true);
const grouped = ref(false);
const resizable = ref(false);
const narrow = ref(false);

const columns = computed<TableColumnData[]>(() => {
  const flat: TableColumnData[] = [
    {
      title: copy.value.labels.priority,
      dataIndex: "priority",
      width: 100,
      fixed: "left",
    },
    { title: copy.value.labels.name, dataIndex: "name", minWidth: 200 },
    { title: copy.value.labels.owner, dataIndex: "owner", minWidth: 120 },
    {
      title: copy.value.labels.status,
      dataIndex: "status",
      width: 100,
      fixed: "right",
    },
  ];
  return grouped.value
    ? [
        { title: copy.value.labels.task, children: flat.slice(0, 2) },
        { title: copy.value.labels.people, children: flat.slice(2) },
      ]
    : flat;
});
const data = computed(() => [
  {
    key: "1",
    priority: "P0",
    name: copy.value.inspectionTask,
    owner: "Alex",
    status: copy.value.active,
  },
  {
    key: "2",
    priority: "P1",
    name: copy.value.longTask,
    owner: "Lee",
    status: copy.value.done,
  },
]);
</script>

<template>
  <div class="column-sizing-playground">
    <c-space wrap>
      <c-radio-group v-model="layout" type="button" aria-label="table-layout">
        <c-radio value="fixed">fixed</c-radio>
        <c-radio value="auto">auto</c-radio>
      </c-radio-group>
      <c-checkbox v-model="fit">fit：{{ copy.labels.fit }}</c-checkbox>
      <c-checkbox v-model="grouped">{{ copy.labels.grouped }}</c-checkbox>
      <c-checkbox v-model="resizable">{{ copy.labels.resizable }}</c-checkbox>
      <c-checkbox v-model="narrow">{{ copy.labels.narrow }}</c-checkbox>
    </c-space>
    <p>{{ copy.labels.hint }}</p>
    <p v-if="resizable" role="status">
      {{ layout === "fixed" ? copy.labels.drag : copy.labels.auto }}
    </p>
    <c-table
      :columns="columns"
      :data="data"
      :pagination="false"
      :style="{ width: narrow ? '420px' : '100%' }"
      :table-layout="layout"
      :fit="fit"
      :column-resizable="resizable"
      :bordered="{ cell: true }"
    />
  </div>
</template>

<style scoped>
.column-sizing-playground {
  width: 760px;
  max-width: 100%;
}
p {
  margin: 12px 0;
}
</style>
```

### Automatic scrolling and height

Horizontal overflow follows computed total column width and available container width. Use `height` for a fixed body height or `max-height` for a shrinking body that scrolls when needed. Without either constraint, the page or outer container owns vertical scrolling. Sticky positioning is controlled separately by `sticky-header` / `sticky-pagination`. With horizontal overflow and sticky pagination enabled, hovering over Table or focusing inside Table reveals the synchronized bottom scrollbar.

See the next group for height, header and pagination combinations.

### Span Method

```vue
<template>
  <c-space direction="column" size="lg" style="width: 100%">
    <c-table :columns="columns" :data="data" :span-method="spanMethod" />
    <c-table :columns="columns" :data="data" :span-method="dataSpanMethod" :bordered="{ wrapper: true, cell: true }" />

<script lang="ts" setup>
const spanMethod = ({ rowIndex, columnIndex }) => {
  if (rowIndex === 1 && columnIndex === 1) {
    return {
      rowspan: 2,
      colspan: 3,
    }
  }
}
const dataSpanMethod = ({ record, column }) => {
  if (record.name === 'Alisa Ross' && column.dataIndex === 'salary') {
    return {
      rowspan: 2,
    }
  }
}
const spanMethodAll = ({ rowIndex, columnIndex }) => {
  if (rowIndex === 1 && columnIndex === 0) {
    return { rowspan: 2 }
  }

  if (rowIndex === 1 && columnIndex === 2) {
    return {
      rowspan: 2,
      colspan: 3,
    }
  }
}
const columns = [
  {
    title: 'Name',
    dataIndex: 'name',
  },
  {
    title: 'Salary',
    dataIndex: 'salary',
  },
  {
    title: 'Address',
    dataIndex: 'address',
  },
  {
    title: 'Email',
    dataIndex: 'email',
  },
]
const data = [

    key: '1',
```

### Summary

```vue
<template>
  <c-table :columns="columns" :data="data" :summary="true" :summary-span-method="spanMethod" />
  <c-table :columns="columns" :data="data" :height="200" :expandable="expandable" :summary="summary">
    <template #summary-cell="{ column, record, rowIndex }">
      <div :style="getColorStyle(column, record)">{{ record[column.dataIndex] }}</div>
    </template>
  </c-table>
</template>

<script lang="ts" setup>
import { reactive } from 'vue'
const expandable = {
  title: 'Expand',
  width: 80,
}
const columns = reactive([
  {
    title: 'Name',
    dataIndex: 'name',
    fixed: 'left',
    width: 140,
  },
  {
    title: 'Salary',
    dataIndex: 'salary',

      if (record.salary > 100000) {
        return {
          backgroundColor: 'rgb(var(--brand-6))',
          color: '#fff',
        }
      }
    },
  },
  {
    title: 'Data1',
    dataIndex: 'data1',
    minWidth: 300,
  },
  {
    title: 'Data2',
    dataIndex: 'data2',
    minWidth: 300,
  },
])
const data = reactive([
  {
    key: '1',
    name: 'Jane Doe',
    salary: 23000,
    data1: 10,
    data2: 8,
    expand: 'Expand Content',
  },
  {
    key: '2',
    name: 'Alisa Ross',
    salary: 25000,
    data1: 9,
    data2: -12,
  },
  {
    key: '3',
    name: 'Kevin Sandra',
    salary: 22000,
    data1: 15,
    data2: -2,
  },
  {
    key: '4',
    name: 'Ed Hellen',
    salary: 17000,
    data1: 2,
    data2: 3,
  },
  {
    key: '5',
    name: 'William Smith',
    salary: 27000,
    data1: 11,
    data2: 0,
  },
])

const summary = ({ columns, data }) => {
  let countData = {
    salary: 0,
    data1: 0,
    data2: 0,
  }
  data.forEach((record) => {
    countData.salary += record.salary
    countData.data1 += record.data1
    countData.data2 += record.data2
  })

  return [
    {
      name: 'Avg',
      salary: countData.salary / data.length,
      data1: countData.data1 / data.length,
      data2: countData.data2 / data.length,
    },
    {
      name: 'Sum',
      salary: countData.salary,
      data1: countData.data1,
      data2: countData.data2,
    },
  ]
}

const getColorStyle = (column, record) => {
  if (['data1', 'data2'].includes(column.dataIndex)) {
    return { color: record[column.dataIndex] > 0 ? 'red' : 'green' }
  }
  return undefined
}

const spanMethod = ({ rowIndex, columnIndex }) => {
  if (rowIndex === 0 && columnIndex === 1) {
    return {
      colspan: 2,
    }
  }
}
</script>
```

### Sticky header, pagination and horizontal scrolling

Example source: src/table/__demos__/en-US/sticky-layout.vue

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { ref } from 'vue'
const pageScroll = ref(false)
const custom = ref(false)
const external = ref(false)
const pagerHost = ref<HTMLElement>()
const page = ref(1)
const rows = Array.from({ length: 160 }, (_, index) => ({ key: index + 1, name: `User ${index + 1}`, city: 'Shanghai', email: `user${index + 1}@example.com`, description: `Rightmost field ${index + 1}` }))
const columns = [{ title: 'Name', dataIndex: 'name', width: 200 }, { title: 'City', dataIndex: 'city', width: 200 }, { title: 'Email', dataIndex: 'email', width: 360 }, { title: 'Description', dataIndex: 'description', width: 480 }]
</script>
<template>
 <c-space direction="column">
  <c-space>
   <c-checkbox v-model="pageScroll">Page scrolling</c-checkbox>
   <c-checkbox v-model="custom">Custom pagination</c-checkbox>
   <c-checkbox v-model="external">Move footer outside Table</c-checkbox>
  </c-space>
  <p>The outer container scrolls; Table has no height or vertical scroll setting. Switch to page scrolling to verify the same header/footer.</p>
  <p role="status">Page: {{ page }}</p>
  <div :class="['sticky-table-demo', { 'sticky-table-demo--page': pageScroll }]">
   <c-table
    :columns="columns" :data="rows"
    :sticky-header="0" :sticky-pagination="0"
    :pagination="{ modelValue: page, pageSize: 40, container: external ? pagerHost : undefined }"
    @page-change="page = $event"
   >
    <template v-if="custom" #pagination="{ page: current, pageSize, total, onChange }">
     <c-space>
      <c-button :disabled="current <= 1" @click="onChange(current - 1)">Previous</c-button>
      <span>{{ current }} / {{ Math.max(1, Math.ceil(total / pageSize)) }}</span>
      <c-button :disabled="current * pageSize >= total" @click="onChange(current + 1)">Next</c-button>
     </c-space>
    </template>
   </c-table>
   <div ref="pagerHost" class="sticky-table-pagination-host" />
  </div>
 </c-space>
</template>
<style scoped>
.sticky-table-demo { max-height: 420px; overflow: auto; isolation: isolate; }
.sticky-table-demo--page { max-height: none; overflow: visible; }
.sticky-table-pagination-host { display: contents; }
</style>
```

sticky-header and sticky-pagination follow the page or outer scroll container. A numeric zero enables the feature with zero offset. This differs from using height/max-height to constrain internal body scrolling. Avoid an extra overflow:hidden ancestor that interrupts sticky positioning.

Built-in sticky pagination keeps a synchronized horizontal rail above the pagination in the same sticky footer. The rail follows body scroll in both directions, and is omitted when content fits. The horizontal rail remains reachable above sticky pagination.

| Property | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| pagination=true | Built-in pagination with its defaults |
| pagination={ pageSize, total, ... } | Configure built-in pagination; total does not fetch server data |
| pagination=false | No built-in pagination UI or slicing; the caller owns the current-page rows |
| sticky-header=true or number | Stick the header; a number sets its top offset |
| sticky-pagination=true or number | Stick the pagination and horizontal rail; a number sets its bottom offset |
| style="width: 100%" | Set the table container width; column widths determine horizontal overflow automatically |

For external pagination, pass pagination=false and render a separate Pagination component. Slice local data before passing it to Table, or request a server page. The business layout owns positioning and scrollbar clearance in that mode. The example switches between built-in sticky pagination and this fully external mode.

### Replace pagination content inside the managed footer

The pagination slot receives { page, pageSize, total, onChange, onPageSizeChange }. Render a business pagination component there to replace the built-in widget while Table keeps data slicing and the scrollbar-above-pagination layout. Keep this content in normal flow inside the footer. pagination=false instead disables the entire built-in pagination protocol.

`--c-table-sticky-scrollbar-height` sets the minimum horizontal rail height (16px by default); intrinsic sizing also reserves the native scrollbar height.

### Mount pagination externally

`pagination.container` accepts a CSS selector or HTMLElement. Omitting it keeps the footer inside Table. Only placement changes: page state, slicing, events and the sticky horizontal rail remain managed by Table. No slot or separate pager state is required. Keep the host in the same scroll context and use display: contents when needed. The target must exist; a selector target can be created later in the same render batch. SSR hosts must handle Teleport output. Give asynchronously loaded tables separate pagination targets and inject each target’s Teleport content into its corresponding host. A shared target can misassociate content or events when the server and client hydrate async branches in different orders. pagination=false still disables Table pagination and slicing entirely.

```vue
<c-table
  :data="rows" :columns="columns"
  :sticky-header="0" :sticky-pagination="0"
  :pagination="{ pageSize: 10, total: 500, container: '#table-pagination' }"
/>
<div id="table-pagination" style="display: contents" />
```

The sticky layout demo provides an outer scrolling container. Table itself has no height/max-height or vertical scroll limit. Toggle page scrolling, custom pagination, and an external footer host. The Table-owned footer groups the synchronized horizontal scrollbar and the pagination slot, and moves them together when pagination.container is set. The external host must remain in the intended scrolling/layout boundary; arbitrary destinations do not remove CSS sticky constraints.

Sticky pagination suppresses the internal horizontal thumb/native scrollbar and reuses the shared Scrollbar in embed mode above the footer. It appears while the pointer is over Table or keyboard focus is inside Table, including when the footer is mounted externally; dragging, track clicks and trackpad scrolling remain synchronized. Vertical scrolling remains owned by the demo container unless Table height/max-height is explicitly set.

### Sort And Filter

When the initial server render of Cedar Table must apply a default filter, pass the columns through `:columns` and set `filterable.defaultFilteredValue`. Columns declared with `<c-table-column>` do not guarantee filtered rows in the server HTML.

- `columns`: Column info of the table
- `data`: Table data
- `filter-icon-align-left`: Whether the filter icon is aligned to the left

Example source: src/table/__demos__/sort-and-filter.vue

### Editable Form

- `columns`: Column info of the table
- `data`: Table data

Example source: src/table/__demos__/editable-form.vue

```vue
<template>
  <c-table :columns="columns" :data="data">
    <template #name="{ rowIndex }">
      <c-input v-model="data[rowIndex].name" />
    </template>
    <template #province="{ rowIndex }">
      <c-form-item layout="vertical" hide-label>
        <c-select
          v-model="data[rowIndex].province"
          @change="() => handleChange(rowIndex)"
        >
          <c-option v-for="value of Object.keys(options)">{{ value }}</c-option>
        </c-select>
      </c-form-item>
    </template>
    <template #city="{ rowIndex }">
      <c-form-item layout="vertical" hide-label>
        <c-select
          :options="options[data[rowIndex].province] || []"
          v-model="data[rowIndex].city"
        />
      </c-form-item>
    </template>
  </c-table>
  <!-- support from v2.25.0  -->
  <c-table :columns="columns" :data="data" style="margin-top: 20px">
    <template #name="{ record, rowIndex }">
      <c-input v-model="record.name" />
    </template>
    <template #province="{ record, rowIndex }">
      <c-form-item layout="vertical" hide-label>
        <c-select
          v-model="record.province"
          @change="
            () => {
              record.city = '';
            }
          "
        >
          <c-option v-for="value of Object.keys(options)">{{ value }}</c-option>
        </c-select>
      </c-form-item>
    </template>
    <template #city="{ record, rowIndex }">
      <c-form-item layout="vertical" hide-label>
        <c-select
          :options="options[record.province] || []"
          v-model="record.city"
        />
      </c-form-item>
    </template>
  </c-table>
</template>

import { reactive } from "vue";
const options = {

    title: "Salary",
    dataIndex: "salary",

    title: "Address",

  {
    title: "Province",
    dataIndex: "province",
    slotName: "province",

  {
    title: "City",
    dataIndex: "city",
    slotName: "city",
  },
  {
    title: "Email",
    dataIndex: "email",

];
```

## Column management and rendering

### Column Manager Basic

<!-- demo-config-notes:start -->
#### Configuration reference for this comparison

| Configuration | Purpose | Related examples |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `columns` | Column info of the table | Column Manager Basic, Custom Filter, Custom Rendering |
| `data` | Table data | Column Manager Basic, Custom Filter, Custom Rendering |
| `pagination` | Pagination properties configuration | Column Manager Basic |
| `size` | The size of the table | Column Manager Basic |
| `row-class` | Class for table-row elements | Customize Table Elements |
<!-- demo-config-notes:end -->


- `columns`: Column info of the table
- `data`: Table data
- `pagination`: Pagination properties configuration
- `size`: The size of the table

Example source: src/table/__demos__/column-manager-basic.vue

```vue
<template>
  <c-space wrap justify="flex-end" style="margin-bottom: 8px">
    <c-link @click="visible = true">列管理</c-link>
  </c-space>

  <c-table
    v-model:columns="columns"
    :data="data"
    :pagination="false"
    size="xs"
  />

  <c-drawer
    v-model:open="visible"
    title="列管理"
    :width="720"
    unmount-on-close
    @confirm="handleConfirm"
  >
    <div style="height: calc(100vh - 120px)">
      <c-table-column-manager
        ref="mgrRef"
        v-model="items"
        :columns="columns"
        :options="columnDefinitions"
      />
    </div>
  </c-drawer>
</template>

<script setup lang="ts">
import { ref, watch } from "vue";
import { stateFromColumns } from "@cedar-design/ui-vue";
import type {
  ColumnDefinitions,
  TableColumnData,
  TableColumnManagerInstance,
} from "@cedar-design/ui-vue";

const visible = ref(false);
const mgrRef = ref<TableColumnManagerInstance>();
const items = ref([]);

const columns = ref<TableColumnData[]>([
  { dataIndex: "name", title: "姓名", width: 120 },
  { dataIndex: "salary", title: "薪资", width: 100 },
  { dataIndex: "address", title: "地址", width: 180 },
]);

const columnDefinitions: ColumnDefinitions = [
  {
    title: "基础",
    key: "basic",
    children: [
      { dataIndex: "name", title: "姓名", required: true },
      { dataIndex: "salary", title: "薪资" },
      { dataIndex: "email", title: "邮箱" },
      { dataIndex: "address", title: "地址" },
    ],
  },
];

watch(visible, (val) => {
  if (!val) return;
  const state = stateFromColumns(columns.value, columnDefinitions);
  items.value = state.items;
});

const handleConfirm = () => {
  const result = mgrRef.value?.getResult?.();
  if (result) columns.value = result.columns;
  visible.value = false;
};

const data = ref([
  { name: "Jane", salary: 23000, address: "London", email: "jane@example.com" },
  {
    name: "Alisa",
    salary: 25000,
    address: "Paris",
    email: "alisa@example.com",
  },
]);
</script>
```

Example source: src/table/__demos__/custom-table-columns.vue

```vue
<template>
  <c-space wrap size="12px" justify="flex-end" style="margin-bottom: 8px">
    <c-link @click="open">列管理</c-link>
    <c-link @click="resetColumns">重置列</c-link>
  </c-space>

  <c-table
    v-model:columns="columns"
    :data="data"
    :pagination="false"
    size="xs"
  />

  <c-table-column-manager v-bind="managerProps" />
</template>

<script lang="ts" setup>
import { onMounted, ref, watch } from "vue";
import { useTableColumnManager } from "@cedar-design/ui-vue";
import type { ColumnDefinitions, ManagedTableColumn } from "@cedar-design/ui-vue";

const STORAGE_KEY = "cedar-demo-table-columns";
let storage: Storage | undefined;
const storageReady = ref(false);

const defaultColumns: ManagedTableColumn[] = [
  {
    dataIndex: "connectorId",
    title: "枪ID",
    width: 100,
    fixed: "left",
    manager: { required: true },
  },
  { dataIndex: "connectorName", title: "枪名称", width: 120 },
  {
    dataIndex: "deviceName",
    title: "设备名称",
    width: 140,
    manager: { required: true },
  },
];

const columnDefinitions: ColumnDefinitions = [
  {
    title: "枪基本信息",
    key: "connectorBasicInfo",
    children: [
      {
        dataIndex: "connectorId",
        title: "枪ID",
        tip: "必选列",
      },
      { dataIndex: "connectorName", title: "枪名称" },
      { dataIndex: "connectorNo", title: "枪序号" },
      { dataIndex: "workingStatus", title: "工作状态" },
      { dataIndex: "connectStatus", title: "连接状态" },
      { dataIndex: "parkNo", title: "停车位" },
    ],
  },
  {
    title: "桩基本信息",
    key: "chargerBasicInfo",
    children: [
      { dataIndex: "deviceId", title: "设备ID" },
      {
        dataIndex: "deviceName",
        title: "设备名称",
        tip: "必选规则来自 defaultColumns",
      },
      { dataIndex: "lockStatus", title: "地锁" },
      { dataIndex: "ratedVoltage", title: "额定电压" },
    ],
  },
  {
    title: "其他信息",
    key: "other",
    children: [
      { dataIndex: "batteryStatus", title: "电池状态" },
      { dataIndex: "temperature", title: "温度" },
      { dataIndex: "current", title: "电流" },
      { dataIndex: "power", title: "功率" },
      { dataIndex: "action", title: "操作" },
    ],
  },
];

const { columns, state, restore, managerProps, open, resetToDefault } =
  useTableColumnManager({
    defaultColumns,
    columnDefinitions,
    columnDefaults: { width: 110, ellipsis: true },
    createColumn: (definition) => ({
      dataIndex: definition.dataIndex,
      title: definition.title,
      ...(definition.dataIndex === "action"
        ? { width: 100, fixed: "right" }
        : {}),
    }),
  });

onMounted(async () => {
  storage = window.localStorage;
  try {
    const raw = storage.getItem(STORAGE_KEY);
    if (raw) await restore(JSON.parse(raw));
  } catch {
    storage.removeItem(STORAGE_KEY);
  } finally {
    storageReady.value = true;
  }
});

watch(
  state,
  (value) => {
    if (!storageReady.value) return;
    storage?.setItem(STORAGE_KEY, JSON.stringify(value));
  },
  { deep: true },
);

const resetColumns = () => {
  try {
    storage?.removeItem(STORAGE_KEY);
  } catch {
    // ignore
  }
  resetToDefault();
};

const data = ref([
  {
    connectorId: "1",
    connectorName: "Jane Doe",
    connectorNo: "001",
    workingStatus: "正常",
    connectStatus: "连接中",
    parkNo: "A1",
    deviceId: "D001",
    deviceName: "Device A",
    lockStatus: "解锁",
    ratedVoltage: "220V",
    batteryStatus: "良好",
    temperature: "36",
    current: "10A",
    power: "2kW",
    action: "详情",
  },
]);
</script>
```

### Custom Rendering

- `columns`: Column info of the table
- `data`: Table data

Once at least one `<c-table-column>` is registered, declared columns replace the `columns` prop. Without registered columns, the `columns` prop remains in use.

Column headings use the Table named slot identified by `titleSlotName`, then the column `title` slot, then the `title` value. Cells use the column `cell` slot, then `render`, then the Table named slot identified by `slotName`, then the data at `dataIndex`. Prefer one content source per location.

Example source: src/table/__demos__/custom-rendering.vue

```vue
      </c-table-column>

</template>
```

## Async and large datasets

### Load More

<!-- demo-config-notes:start -->
#### Configuration reference for this comparison

| Configuration | Purpose | Related examples |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `columns` | Column info of the table | Load More, Column Manager Async, Virtual List Props |
| `data` | Table data | Load More, Column Manager Async, Virtual List Props |
| `pagination` | Pagination properties configuration | Column Manager Async, Virtual List Props |
| `load-more` | Load children asynchronously; call done(children), or done() to allow retry | Load More |
| `size` | The size of the table | Column Manager Async |
| `row-selection` | Table row selector configuration | Virtual List Props |
