### Shared field loading

`loading` displays the shared field indicator. `loading-mode` is `default` (indicator) or `line` (an indeterminate bottom line); it defaults to `default`. Rendering belongs to FieldDecorator. Loading does not implicitly disable editing or change readonly. Set those states separately.

## Reading direction

Range values stay `[start, end]`. LTR/RTL changes affect layout without swapping endpoints or changing cross-day meaning. Time columns and start/end panels follow reading order. Left/Right moves focus visually, including across endpoints. Cedar Up/Down moves focus and Enter/Space selects; Maple Up/Down retains wheel selection semantics. Existing draft/confirmation configuration is preserved, and popovers inherit source field direction.

## API

### Empty values and reading placeholders

`empty-values` recognizes empty data; `empty-value` keeps existing clear output. `empty-text` defaults to `'-'` under `read-pretty`, with Field > FormItem > Form precedence and custom read slots first. With explicit `empty-values`, built-in required uses the policy; custom validators receive original data. See the [shared guide](llms/en-US/guide/empty-values.md).

| Prop | Type | Default and scope |
| ------------ | ------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------- |
| empty-values | readonly unknown[] | Field > FormItem > Form > component-family default; replaces the whole list |
| empty-text | string | Field > FormItem > Form > '-'; explicit '' is valid |

These props belong to field presentation; pure panels do not gain reading mode. Form and FormItem provide inherited settings. The existing empty-value type and clear fallback remain component-specific.

### Popup configuration and field notifications

`popup-props` configures local Trigger positioning/appearance, e.g. `{ placement: 'top-start' }`, without overriding field open, disabled, trigger or other state/interaction. Top-level `popup-container`, including false, takes precedence. `input-editable` defaults to true and can disable desktop typing. `time-range-picker-props`, including class/style, controls panel appearance. Panel and popup configuration uses the declared props; id/aria-* fall through to the field.

`click(event)` notifies only clicks on non-disabled fields. Readonly may notify without expanding. Closing consistently listens to `open-change(false)`, a close request that controlled open still requires the parent to accept. Neither platform has a field close event; a close request is not a value commit.

`suffix-icon` receives `focus: boolean` and `popupOpen: boolean`. `focus(index = 0)` focuses start (0) or end (1) without committing; `blur()` removes focus and requests closing.

A `placeholder` string applies to both endpoints; arrays provide start/end text, with missing entries empty. Explicit empty strings do not fall back to default text.

### TimeRange Props

`input-attrs` applies to the two direct input elements. For example, `:input-attrs="[{ 'aria-label': 'Departure' }, { 'aria-label': 'Return' }]"` names each endpoint. The field owns its value, disabled, readonly, placeholder, role and popup state; shared descriptions, per-input descriptions and form errors are merged for each input. Component errors take precedence; otherwise each input retains its `aria-invalid`. `RangeInputAttributes` is exported from the component and root entries and includes native attributes and `Once` event types.

When FormItem's `label-attrs.for` explicitly targets one input, unnamed range endpoints use the form label together with localized start/end names. Explicit accessible names supplied through `input-attrs` or the field take precedence. Older custom locales can provide `fieldPresentation.rangeStart` and `fieldPresentation.rangeEnd`; when absent, the existing date or time start/end labels are used.

| Prop | Description | Type | Default behavior |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `before-commit` | Explicit field-save guard using payload, done and context | `BeforeFieldCommit` | `undefined` |
| `blur-color` | Color while unfocused | `string` | Theme default |
| `clearable` | Allow clearing with disabled, readonly and pending guards | `boolean` | `true` |
| `default-open` | Initial uncontrolled opening, read only at creation | `boolean` | `false` |
| `default-value` | Initial uncontrolled value, read only at creation | `TimeValue[]` | `undefined` |
| `disable-confirm` | Commit a valid selection immediately; fields also request closing | `boolean` | `false` |
| `disabled` | Disable interaction; fields inherit FormItem/Form when unset | `boolean` | Inherited, finally false |
| `disabled-hours` | Return disabled hours in the 0–23 clock | `() => number[]` | `undefined` |
| `disabled-minutes` | Return disabled minutes for the selected hour | `(hour?: number) => number[]` | `undefined` |
| `disabled-seconds` | Return disabled seconds for the selected hour and minute | `(hour?: number, minute?: number) => number[]` | `undefined` |
| `edit-mode` | Field editing mode, inherited from FormItem/Form when unset | `FieldEditMode`<br>`'direct' \| 'click' \| 'dblclick'` | Inherited, finally direct |
| `empty-text` | Empty text in read-pretty mode | `string` | Inherited, finally '-' |
| `empty-value` | Clear output or factory, independent of empty-value recognition | `TimeValue[] \| null \| (() => TimeValue[] \| null \| undefined)` | `undefined` |
| `empty-values` | Empty-value recognition list, replaced rather than merged | `readonly unknown[]` | Inherited/family default |
| `error` | Field error presentation, inherited when unset | `boolean` | Inherited, finally false |
| `focus-color` | Color while focused | `string` | Theme default |
| `format` | String parsing, display and output format; 12-hour defaults include a | `string` | From use12Hours |
| `hide-disabled-options` | Hide disabled time options; clocks retain tick positions | `boolean` | `false` |
| `hint` | Floating placeholder hint, suppressed by an outer Form label | `boolean` | `false` |
| `input-editable` | Allow text input without removing panel selection | `boolean` | `true` |
| `input-attrs` | Native attributes for the start and end inputs, in order; per-input names override shared names | `RangeInputAttributes[]` | `undefined` |
| `line` | Show the field border or underline | `boolean` | `true` |
| `loading` | Manual loading feedback, independent of event return values | `boolean` | `false` |
| `loading-mode` | Field loading presentation mode | `default \| line` | `default` |
| `max` | Maximum inclusive clock time in HH:mm or HH:mm:ss | `string` | `undefined` |
| `min` | Minimum inclusive clock time in HH:mm or HH:mm:ss | `string` | `undefined` |
| `model-value` | External value; numbers and Dates retain their input kind, while normal commits output formatted strings | `TimeRangeModelValue` | `undefined` |
| `open` | Controlled field editor opening | `boolean` | `undefined` |
| `open-trigger-target` | Open by field or icon click, without restricting keyboard opening | `field \| icon` | `field` |
| `placeholder` | Placeholder text; ranges also accept start/end arrays | `string \| string[]` | `undefined` |
| `popup-container` | Editor container; false renders in place | `PopupContainer` | Shared container default |
| `popup-props` | Popup presentation options, excluding model, state and owned events | `TimePopupPresentationProps` | `{}` |
| `read-pretty` | Read-pretty presentation without an editor, independent of readonly | `boolean` | Inherited, finally false |
| `readonly` | Readonly; fields allow focus/copy without value changes or opening editing | `boolean` | Inherited, finally false |
| `separator` | Range separator text, including an empty string | `string` | ` ~ ` |
| `show-next-day` | Ranges only: allow an earlier end time as next day without swapping endpoints | `boolean` | `false` |
| `size` | Five sizes, following field Form inheritance | `ComponentSize`<br>`'xs' \| 'sm' \| 'md' \| 'lg' \| 'xl'` | Inherited, finally md |
| `step` | Hour/minute/second steps from midnight; invalid steps fall back to 1 | `TimeStep` | Effective steps are all 1 |
| `text-color` | Content text color | `string` | Theme default |
| `time-range-picker-props` | Range-panel presentation options; model, rules and state remain owned by the field | `TimePanelPresentationProps` | `{}` |
| `use12-hours` | 12-hour panel; disabled-hour callbacks still use 0–23 | `boolean` | `false` |
| `variant` | Field appearance | `filled \| outline \| standard` | `outline` |

### Editing and confirmation

This component supports `edit-mode` with field > FormItem > Form precedence. When unset, it defaults to `direct` and preserves `direct` editing. Supported values: `direct / click / dblclick`. Non-direct modes open the editor through the field value trigger and keep one draft; v-model updates only after confirmation. Cancel, reset or enabling readPretty discards the draft.

Cedar uses edit-mode="click" / "dblclick" to open an editor popup near the field. Enter/F2 also opens it; cancel/Escape discards the draft, and confirmation commits it. readPretty is an independent reading setting, separate from readonly and disabled.

`before-commit(payload, done, context)` can guard saving the editor. FormItem validates the candidate first; invalid candidates keep the editor open. `open / default-open / update:open` control the editor. `#read="{ value, text }"` customizes read content. See the unified field presentation examples in Form.

Inline date/time fields retain their existing confirmation policy. In click/dblclick editors, internal panels hide confirmation tools, and the edit layer supplies one confirm/cancel pair. Standalone DatePicker, DateRangePicker, TimePicker and TimeRangePicker retain panel APIs/confirmation and do not inherit Form field presentation.

`read-pretty` is an independent boolean alongside `readonly` and `disabled`. It inherits from field to FormItem to Form; explicit `false` overrides the parent. The default is `false`. Reading mode renders no editor.

### Forwarded configuration boundaries

The time field manages open/defaultOpen, disabled, trigger, closeOnClickReference, preventFocus and visibility updates. An explicit top-level popup-container takes precedence over nested configuration; popupClass is merged. Inline presentation fixes popupOffset=4, and Maple also fixes unmountOnClose=true, so those nested fields may not control the final values.

### TimeRangePicker Props

| Prop | Description | Type | Default behavior |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `default-value` | Initial uncontrolled value, read only at creation | `TimeValue[]` | `undefined` |
| `disable-confirm` | Commit a valid selection immediately; fields also request closing | `boolean` | `false` |
| `disabled` | Disable panel selection and confirmation | `boolean` | `false` |
| `disabled-hours` | Return disabled hours in the 0–23 clock | `() => number[]` | `undefined` |
| `disabled-minutes` | Return disabled minutes for the selected hour | `(hour?: number) => number[]` | `undefined` |
| `disabled-seconds` | Return disabled seconds for the selected hour and minute | `(hour?: number, minute?: number) => number[]` | `undefined` |
| `format` | String parsing, display and output format; 12-hour defaults include a | `string` | From use12Hours |
| `hide-disabled-options` | Hide disabled time options; clocks retain tick positions | `boolean` | `false` |
| `max` | Maximum inclusive clock time in HH:mm or HH:mm:ss | `string` | `undefined` |
| `min` | Minimum inclusive clock time in HH:mm or HH:mm:ss | `string` | `undefined` |
| `model-value` | Panel external value, seeding draft and accepting later changes | `TimeValue[]` | `undefined` |
| `readonly` | Readonly panel without draft changes or confirmation | `boolean` | `false` |
| `show-next-day` | Ranges only: allow an earlier end time as next day without swapping endpoints | `boolean` | `false` |
| `step` | Hour/minute/second steps from midnight; invalid steps fall back to 1 | `TimeStep` | Effective steps are all 1 |
| `use12-hours` | 12-hour panel; disabled-hour callbacks still use 0–23 | `boolean` | `false` |

## Configuring the cleared value

`empty-value` defines the output of an existing clear action. Omission preserves the component fallback; supported types remain component-specific. It does not change empty-values recognition or Form reset defaults.

`empty-value` accepts explicit `null` (or `() => null`). Clearing publishes `null` unchanged; omitted values preserve the existing default. Editors render `null` as blank without converting ordinary empty-string input to `null`. In popup editing, clearing changes the draft; confirm commits it and cancel preserves the original model.

Public focus/blur methods are callable from initial mount. Focus opens an editable deferred editor and targets it after readiness; disabled, readonly, or reading fields do not open. Blur only blurs the current target without reopening. Stored methods never bind an old editor; closure, mode changes, deactivation, or unmount cancel queued calls.

During deferred editing, clearing retains the configured valid empty-value and confirmation submits that empty value; null is not replaced by midnight. A newly created empty wheel panel may initialize a visible candidate without selecting or committing a model. Later explicit empty drafts in that panel are not automatically refilled. Reopening and cancelling does not publish another value.

### Field notifications and public types

Field update:modelValue/change use TimeModelValue (TimeRangeModelValue for ranges). Normal selections commit formatted strings; explicit clears retain configured null, timestamps, Date objects or range arrays accepted by the property. Auxiliary dates may be undefined; clearing a range to an empty array also yields an empty auxiliary array. Clear does not emit select. Select remains a formatted user draft, which may be incomplete for a range.

Exports TimeEmits, TimeModelValue, TimeReadScope, TimeSuffixIconScope, TimeSlots, TimeActionsScope and TimeExpose, plus TimeRangeEmits, TimeRangeModelValue, TimeRangeReadScope, TimeRangeSlots, TimeRangeActionsScope and TimeRangeExpose. Import each from the root or its component entry. Instances include the public Expose contract.

Field read receives { value, text } with a nullable model; suffix-icon receives { focus, popupOpen }; clear-icon receives a guarded clear(event?). Range fields also support separator. Cedar direct mode supports a default custom trigger, while Maple does not. Neither platform currently forwards field loading-icon, so types do not promise it. actions/extra operate on panel drafts: Cedar forwards them in direct mode; Maple forwards them during deferred editing, not direct mode. Inner confirm is not the outer final-save entry.

<!-- time-contract:start -->

### Defaults and format

Inherited, format-derived and effective-step defaults describe resolved behavior; raw Props may be undefined. Without format, the default is HH:mm:ss, or hh:mm:ss a with use12Hours=true. Bounds use 24-hour clock times, separate from Date-family valueFormat/time-zone rules.

### Field event and slot parameter types

Events notify only; listener Promises are not collected. update:modelValue and change include null, 0, Date or range arrays allowed by the clearing policy. select reports formatted draft rather than saving. Field update:open/open-change are opening requests; initialization does not notify automatically.

| Event | Arguments |
| --- | --- |
| `update:modelValue` | `TimeRangeModelValue` |
| `change` | `TimeRangeModelValue, (Date \| undefined)[] \| undefined` |
| `select` | `(string \| undefined)[] \| undefined, (Date \| undefined)[] \| undefined` |
| `clear` | `()` |
| `click` | `Event` |
| `focus` | `()` |
| `blur` | `()` |
| `update:open` | `boolean` |
| `open-change` | `boolean` |

Field focus(index?)/blur() target the actual input or trigger without changing model. read receives value/text, suffix-icon receives focus/popupOpen, and clear-icon receives guarded clear(event?). prefix, selected, suffix and extra are unscoped; ranges also have separator. Cedar direct mode has a custom default trigger slot; Maple does not.

actions/extra belong to panel draft: Cedar direct forwards them, Maple direct does not, and deferred editing forwards them. Panel confirm() is not the outer field final-save entry point. Pure panels have actions/extra, without field read/clear-icon/loading-icon slots. Standalone panels expose no ref.confirm() method; custom confirmation uses actions.confirm.

### Panel event parameter types

Arguments are tuples from the corresponding public event type. Date arguments are parsed from formatted clock times and do not promise to preserve an input Date calendar day.

| Event | Arguments |
| --- | --- |
| `update:modelValue` | `TimeRangePickerEmits['update:modelValue']` |
| `change` | `TimeRangePickerEmits['change']` |
| `select` | `TimeRangePickerEmits['select']` |
| `confirm` | `TimeRangePickerEmits['confirm']` |

### Panel Events

Pure-panel business events are update:modelValue, change, select and confirm. select reports candidates; valid confirmation notifies confirm, while update:modelValue/change only occur for an actual value change. Field opening, clearing and focus events do not belong to pure panels.

Complete panel actions scope below; extra has no arguments.

```ts
import type { TimeValue } from '@cedar-design/ui-vue'
type PanelActionsScope = { confirm: () => boolean; canConfirm: boolean; value: Array<TimeValue | undefined> | undefined }
```

### Explicit save guard

beforeCommit(payload, done, context) belongs to field saving. payload contains value/previousValue; context has signal and optional event. Returning undefined waits for done, while boolean/Promise results settle by their result. FormItem validates candidates first; failure retains draft. Ordinary select/change/confirm/click listener returns do not use this task protocol.

### Type imports

```ts
import { TimeRange, TimeRangePicker, type TimeRangeProps, type TimeRangeEmits,
  type TimeRangeSlots, type TimeRangeInstance, type TimeRangePickerProps,
  type TimeRangePickerEmits, type TimeRangePickerSlots } from '@cedar-design/ui-vue'
```

# Time

`Time` is a time field with an input and popup; `TimePicker` is an embedded panel without a trigger. This page demonstrates both with shared values and rules. Use the field in forms and the panel in custom layouts. Range selection uses [`TimeRange`](llms/en-US/components/time-range.md).


A time field with a separate draft and confirmation step.

```ts
import type { TimeProps, TimeInstance } from "@cedar-design/ui-vue";
```

`empty-value` accepts explicit `null` (or `() => null`). Clearing publishes null unchanged; omitted values preserve the existing default. Editors render null as blank without converting ordinary empty-string input to null. In popup editing, clearing changes the draft; confirm commits it and cancel preserves the original model.

The examples above compare shared formats, steps and bounds. The following examples focus on panel selection and confirmation. Input, clearing and popup controls belong to `Time`; the panel manages its own draft.

### Step

- `format`: Controls the displayed format.
- `step`: Controls the allowed increment.

Example source: src/time/__demos__/step.vue

```vue
<script setup>
import { computed, ref } from "vue";
const value = ref("09:30:00");
const coarse = ref(false);
const fiveHours = ref(false);
const blockAfternoon = ref(false);
const accept = ref(true);
const proposals = ref(0);
const disabledHours = () => (blockAfternoon.value ? [15] : []);
function update(next) {
  proposals.value++;
  if (accept.value) value.value = next;
}
const step = computed(() => ({
  hour: fiveHours.value ? 5 : 1,
  minute: coarse.value ? 30 : 15,
  second: 10,
}));
</script>

<template>
  <c-space
    class="time-step-demo"
    direction="column"
    :size="12"
    style="width: 100%"
  >
    <c-checkbox v-model="fiveHours"> 十二小时显示 + 5 小时步长</c-checkbox>
    <c-checkbox v-model="coarse"> 切换为 30 分钟步长</c-checkbox>
    <c-checkbox v-model="blockAfternoon"> 禁用 15 点（03 PM）</c-checkbox>
    <c-checkbox v-model="accept"> 父级接受更新</c-checkbox>
    <p>确认时按当前步长重新校验；切换规则不会自动修改已提交值。</p>
    <c-time
      :model-value="value"
      format="HH:mm:ss"
      :use12-hours="fiveHours"
      :step="step"
      :disabled-hours="disabledHours"
      style="width: 100%; max-width: 360px"
      @update:model-value="update"
    />
    <span>{{ value }}</span>
    <span role="status">提议次数：{{ proposals }}</span>
  </c-space>
</template>
```

### Selection Events

- `readonly`: Displays the current value without allowing edits.
- `disabled`: Prevents user interaction.
- `format`: Controls the displayed format.

Example source: src/time/__demos__/selection-events.vue

```vue
<script setup>
import { formatDemoTime } from "../../__demos__/locale";
import { ref } from "vue";

const value = ref("09:00");
const immediate = ref(false);
const readonly = ref(false);
const disabled = ref(false);
const events = ref([]);
function record(name, value, dates) {
  const times = Array.isArray(dates)
    ? dates.map((date) => (date == null ? undefined : formatDemoTime(date)))
    : dates == null
      ? undefined
      : formatDemoTime(dates);
  events.value = [
    JSON.stringify({ event: name, value: value ?? null, time: times ?? null }),
    ...events.value,
  ].slice(0, 5);
}
</script>

<template>
  <c-space direction="column" size="12px" style="width: 100%">
    <c-checkbox v-model="readonly"> 只读：可聚焦，不可修改</c-checkbox>
    <c-checkbox v-model="disabled"> 禁用：释放焦点，不可修改</c-checkbox>
    <c-checkbox v-model="immediate"> 选择后立即提交</c-checkbox>
    <p>select 记录草稿，change 记录提交；取消不改模型，清除返回 undefined。</p>
    <c-time
      v-model="value"
      :disable-confirm="immediate"
      :readonly="readonly"
      :disabled="disabled"
      format="HH:mm"
      clearable
      @select="(value, dates) => record('select', value, dates)"
      @change="(value, dates) => record('change', value, dates)"
      @clear="record('clear')"
      @click="record('click')"
      @open-change="(open) => record('open-change', open)"
      @focus="record('focus')"
      @blur="record('blur')"
    />
    <span>模型: {{ value === undefined ? "undefined" : value }}</span>
    <c-button variant="outline" @click="value = '15:30'"
      >从外部替换模型</c-button
    >
    <small>外部替换会更新反显，不触发 select 或 change。</small>
    <div
      v-for="(event, index) in events"
      :key="index"
      style="overflow-wrap: anywhere"
    >
      {{ event }}
    </div>
  </c-space>
</template>
```

### Shared field loading

`loading` displays the shared field indicator. `loading-mode` is `default` (indicator) or `line` (an indeterminate bottom line); it defaults to `default`. Rendering belongs to FieldDecorator. Loading does not implicitly disable editing or change readonly. Set those states separately.

## Reading direction

Inherits the nearest `dir="ltr|rtl"`; direction changes do not modify time or commit drafts. Hour, minute and second columns follow reading order, with Left/Right moving focus visually between columns. Cedar Up/Down and Home/End move focus within the current column, Enter/Space selects, and disabled options are skipped. Maple wheels retain Up/Down and Home/End selection behavior. Existing confirmation configuration determines immediate commits. Popovers inherit source field direction.

## API

### Empty values and reading placeholders

`empty-values` recognizes empty data; `empty-value` keeps existing clear output. `empty-text` defaults to `'-'` under `read-pretty`, with Field > FormItem > Form precedence and custom read slots first. With explicit `empty-values`, built-in required uses the policy; custom validators receive original data. See the [shared guide](llms/en-US/guide/empty-values.md).

| Prop | Type | Default and scope |
| ------------ | ------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------- |
| empty-values | readonly unknown[] | Field > FormItem > Form > component-family default; replaces the whole list |
| empty-text | string | Field > FormItem > Form > '-'; explicit '' is valid |

These props belong to field presentation; pure panels do not gain reading mode. Form and FormItem provide inherited settings. The existing empty-value type and clear fallback remain component-specific.

### Popup configuration and field notifications

`popup-props` configures local Trigger positioning/appearance, e.g. `{ placement: 'top-start' }`, without overriding field state/interaction such as open, disabled or trigger. Top-level `popup-container`, including false, takes precedence. `input-editable` defaults to true and can disable desktop typing. `time-picker-props`, including class/style, controls panel appearance. Panel and popup configuration uses the declared props; id/aria-* fall through to the field.

`click(event)` notifies only clicks on non-disabled fields. Readonly may notify without expanding. Closing consistently listens to `open-change(false)`, a close request that controlled open still requires the parent to accept. Neither platform has a field close event; a close request is not a value commit.

The field icon slot is `suffix-icon` with `focus: boolean` and `popupOpen: boolean`. `focus(index = 0)` focuses an endpoint without committing; `blur()` removes focus and requests closing.

### Time Props

| Prop | Description | Type | Default behavior |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `before-commit` | Explicit field-save guard using payload, done and context | `BeforeFieldCommit` | `undefined` |

| `variant` | Field appearance | `filled \| outline \| standard` | `outline` |

### Editing and confirmation

This component supports `edit-mode` with field > FormItem > Form precedence. When unset, it defaults to `direct` and preserves `direct` editing. Supported values: `direct / click / dblclick`. Non-direct modes open the editor through the field value trigger and keep one draft; v-model updates only after confirmation. Cancel, reset or enabling readPretty discards the draft.

Cedar uses edit-mode="click" / "dblclick" to open an editor popup near the field. Enter/F2 also opens it; cancel/Escape discards the draft, and confirmation commits it. readPretty is an independent reading setting, separate from readonly and disabled.

`before-commit(payload, done, context)` can guard saving the editor. FormItem validates the candidate first; invalid candidates keep the editor open. `open / default-open / update:open` control the editor. `#read="{ value, text }"` customizes read content. See the unified field presentation examples in Form.

Inline date/time fields retain their existing confirmation policy. In click/dblclick editors, internal panels hide confirmation tools, and the edit layer supplies one confirm/cancel pair. Standalone DatePicker, DateRangePicker, TimePicker and TimeRangePicker retain panel APIs/confirmation and do not inherit Form field presentation.

`read-pretty` is an independent boolean alongside `readonly` and `disabled`. It inherits from field to FormItem to Form; explicit `false` overrides the parent. The default is `false`. Reading mode renders no editor.

### Forwarded configuration boundaries

The time field manages open/defaultOpen, disabled, trigger, closeOnClickReference, preventFocus and visibility updates. An explicit top-level popup-container takes precedence over nested configuration; popupClass is merged. Inline presentation fixes popupOffset=4, and Maple also fixes unmountOnClose=true, so those nested fields may not control the final values.

| `hide-disabled-options` | Hide disabled time options; clocks retain tick positions | `boolean` | `false` |

## Configuring the cleared value

`empty-value` defines the output of an existing clear action. Omission preserves the component fallback; supported types remain component-specific. It does not change empty-values recognition or Form reset defaults.

`empty-value` accepts explicit `null` (or `() => null`). Clearing publishes `null` unchanged; omitted values preserve the existing default. Editors render `null` as blank without converting ordinary empty-string input to `null`. In popup editing, clearing changes the draft; confirm commits it and cancel preserves the original model.

Public focus/blur methods are callable from initial mount. Focus opens an editable deferred editor and targets it after readiness; disabled, readonly, or reading fields do not open. Blur only blurs the current target without reopening. Stored methods never bind an old editor; closure, mode changes, deactivation, or unmount cancel queued calls.

During deferred editing, clearing retains the configured valid empty-value and confirmation submits that empty value; null is not replaced by midnight. A newly created empty wheel panel may initialize a visible candidate without selecting or committing a model. Later explicit empty drafts in that panel are not automatically refilled. Reopening and cancelling does not publish another value.

### Field notifications and public types

Field update:modelValue/change use TimeModelValue (TimeRangeModelValue for ranges). Normal selections commit formatted strings; explicit clears retain configured null, timestamps, Date objects or range arrays accepted by the property. Auxiliary dates may be undefined; clearing a range to an empty array also yields an empty auxiliary array. Clear does not emit select. Select remains a formatted user draft, which may be incomplete for a range.

Exports TimeEmits, TimeModelValue, TimeReadScope, TimeSuffixIconScope, TimeSlots, TimeActionsScope and TimeExpose, plus TimeRangeEmits, TimeRangeModelValue, TimeRangeReadScope, TimeRangeSlots, TimeRangeActionsScope and TimeRangeExpose. Import each from the root or its component entry. Instances include the public Expose contract.

Field read receives { value, text } with a nullable model; suffix-icon receives { focus, popupOpen }; clear-icon receives a guarded clear(event?). Range fields also support separator. Cedar direct mode supports a default custom trigger, while Maple does not. Neither platform currently forwards field loading-icon, so types do not promise it. actions/extra operate on panel drafts: Cedar forwards them in direct mode; Maple forwards them during deferred editing, not direct mode. Inner confirm is not the outer final-save entry.

<!-- time-contract:start -->

### Defaults and format

Inherited, format-derived and effective-step defaults describe resolved behavior; raw Props may be undefined. Without format, the default is HH:mm:ss, or hh:mm:ss a with use12Hours=true. Bounds use 24-hour clock times, separate from Date-family valueFormat/time-zone rules.

### Field event and slot parameter types

Events notify only; listener Promises are not collected. update:modelValue and change include null, 0, Date or range arrays allowed by the clearing policy. select reports formatted draft rather than saving. Field update:open/open-change are opening requests; initialization does not notify automatically.

| Event | Arguments |
| --- | --- |
| `update:modelValue` | `TimeModelValue` |
| `change` | `TimeModelValue, Date \| undefined` |
| `select` | `string \| undefined, Date \| undefined` |
| `clear` | `()` |
| `click` | `Event` |
| `focus` | `()` |
| `blur` | `()` |
| `update:open` | `boolean` |
| `open-change` | `boolean` |

Field focus(index?)/blur() target the actual input or trigger without changing model. read receives value/text, suffix-icon receives focus/popupOpen, and clear-icon receives guarded clear(event?). prefix, selected, suffix and extra are unscoped; ranges also have separator. Cedar direct mode has a custom default trigger slot; Maple does not.

actions/extra belong to panel draft: Cedar direct forwards them, Maple direct does not, and deferred editing forwards them. Panel confirm() is not the outer field final-save entry point. Pure panels have actions/extra, without field read/clear-icon/loading-icon slots. Standalone panels expose no ref.confirm() method; custom confirmation uses actions.confirm.

### Panel event parameter types

Arguments are tuples from the corresponding public event type. Date arguments are parsed from formatted clock times and do not promise to preserve an input Date calendar day.

| Event | Arguments |
| --- | --- |
| `update:modelValue` | `TimePickerEmits['update:modelValue']` |
| `change` | `TimePickerEmits['change']` |
| `select` | `TimePickerEmits['select']` |
| `confirm` | `TimePickerEmits['confirm']` |

### Panel Events

Pure-panel business events are update:modelValue, change, select and confirm. select reports candidates; valid confirmation notifies confirm, while update:modelValue/change only occur for an actual value change. Field opening, clearing and focus events do not belong to pure panels.

Complete panel actions scope below; extra has no arguments.

```ts
import type { TimeValue } from '@cedar-design/ui-vue'
type PanelActionsScope = { confirm: () => boolean; canConfirm: boolean; value: TimeValue | Array<TimeValue | undefined> | undefined }
```

### Explicit save guard

beforeCommit(payload, done, context) belongs to field saving. payload contains value/previousValue; context has signal and optional event. Returning undefined waits for done, while boolean/Promise results settle by their result. FormItem validates candidates first; failure retains draft. Ordinary select/change/confirm/click listener returns do not use this task protocol.

### Type imports

```ts
import { Time, TimePicker, type TimeProps, type TimeEmits,
  type TimeSlots, type TimeInstance, type TimePickerProps,
  type TimePickerEmits, type TimePickerSlots } from '@cedar-design/ui-vue'
```

<!-- time-contract:end -->

Apply overrides to the rendered component root or the actual popup ancestor. For example, add the following class to that element and replace the value as needed:

```css

  --c-time-picker-border-color: var(--c-color-neutral-3);
}
```

Explicit inline styles and props that write the same CSS property take precedence over stylesheet defaults. After Teleport, ordinary CSS variables inherit from the actual mount location. When using ThemeProvider, follow its local-theme and popup configuration rules. Override the component variable directly for local styling; root-level aliases are not recalculated merely because a descendant system variable changes. Internal variables are not public APIs.

# Timeline

Start with the basic example, then compare related settings before moving to controlled, asynchronous or combined use cases.

## Basic examples

### Basic usage

- `reverse`: Whether reverse order

Example source: src/timeline/__demos__/basic.vue

```vue
<template>
  <div :style="{ marginBottom: '40px' }">
    <c-typography-text :style="{ verticalAlign: 'middle', marginRight: '8px' }"> Reverse </c-typography-text>
    <c-radio-group @change="onChange" :style="{ marginBottom: '30px' }" v-model="isReverse">
      <c-radio :value="false">No Reverse</c-radio>
      <c-radio :value="true">Reverse</c-radio>
    </c-radio-group>
  </div>
  <c-timeline :reverse="isReverse">
    <c-timeline-item label="2017-03-10">The first milestone</c-timeline-item>
    <c-timeline-item label="2018-05-12">The second milestone</c-timeline-item>
    <c-timeline-item label="2020-09-30">The third milestone</c-timeline-item>
  </c-timeline>
</template>

<script lang="ts" setup>
import { ref } from 'vue'

const isReverse = ref(false)

const onChange = (bool) => {
  isReverse.value = bool
}
</script>
```

Example source: src/timeline/__demos__/pending.vue

```vue
<template>
  <c-row align="center" :style="{ marginBottom: '24px' }">
    <c-checkbox :checked="pendingProps.orientation === 'horizontal'" @change="(v) => onChange({ orientation: v ? 'horizontal' : 'vertical' })">
      horizontal &nbsp; &nbsp;
    </c-checkbox>
    <c-checkbox :checked="!!pendingProps.reverse" @change="(v) => onChange({ reverse: v })">
      reverse &nbsp; &nbsp;
    </c-checkbox>
    <c-checkbox
      :checked="!!pendingProps.pending"
      @change="(v) => onChange({ pending: v ? 'This is a pending dot' : false })"
    >
      pending &nbsp; &nbsp;
    </c-checkbox>
    <c-checkbox :checked="!!pendingProps.hasPendingDot" @change="(v) => onChange({ hasPendingDot: v })">
      custom pendingDot
    </c-checkbox>
  </c-row>
  <c-timeline v-bind="pendingProps">
    <template v-if="pendingProps.hasPendingDot" #dot>
      <c-icon-fire :style="{ color: '#e70a0a' }" />
    </template>
    <c-timeline-item label="2017-03-10" dotColor="#52C419"> The first milestone </c-timeline-item>
    <c-timeline-item label="2018-05-12" dotColor="#F5222D"> The second milestone </c-timeline-item>
    <c-timeline-item label="2020-09-30">The third milestone</c-timeline-item>
  </c-timeline>
  <c-timeline>
    <template #pending>Waiting for the next milestone</template>
  </c-timeline>
</template>

<script lang="ts" setup>
import { ref } from 'vue'

const pendingProps = ref({})

const onChange = (newProps) => {
  pendingProps.value = {
    ...pendingProps.value,
    ...newProps,
  }
}
</script>
```

## API

### Timeline Props

| Parameter | Description | Type | Default |
| -------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------- | :----------: |
| reverse | Whether reverse order | `boolean` | `false` |
| orientation | Horizontal/vertical axis of the timeline line, default vertical; constrains valid item sides | `'horizontal' \| 'vertical'` | `'vertical'` |
| mode | The display mode of Timeline | `'left' \| 'right' \| 'top' \| 'bottom' \| 'alternate'` | `'left'` |
| pending | Append a pending item; true has no text, and a string is displayed as its content. | `boolean\|string` | `-` |
| label-position | Position of label text | `'relative' \| 'same'` | `'same'` |

### Timeline Slots

| Slot | Description | Prop |
| ------ | :------: | ---- |
| default | Timeline items | - |
| dot | Pending item icon | - |
| pending | Pending item content; adding this slot appends an item and takes precedence over the pending prop text | - |

### TimelineItem Props

| Parameter | Description | Type | Default |
| ---------- | ---------------------------- | --------------------------------- | :-------: |
| dot-color | Node color | `string` | `-` |
| dot-type | Node type: outlined/filled circle | `'hollow' \| 'solid'` | `'solid'` |
| line-type | Timeline line style: solid/dashed/dotted | `'solid' \| 'dashed' \| 'dotted'` | `'solid'` |
| line-color | Timeline color | `string` | `-` |
| label | Label text | `string` | `-` |
| content-placement | Current per-item side relative to the timeline in alternate mode: left/right for vertical and top/bottom for horizontal. Constrained by mode and orientation | `TimelineItemContentPlacement`<br>`'left' \| 'right' \| 'bottom' \| 'top'` | `-` |

Use `content-placement` for the physical side of the content: top/bottom in horizontal layouts and left/right in vertical layouts. `mode` controls the arrangement.

### TimelineItem Slots

| Slot | Description | Prop | Version |
| ------ | :--------: | ---- | :----- |
| default | Item content | - |  |
| dot | Custom node | - |  |
| label | Custom label | - | 2.50.0 |

## Types

The component exports the following types

```ts
import type { TimelineProps, TimelineItemProps, TimelineSlots, TimelineItemSlots, TimelineMode, TimelineLabelPosition, TimelineDotType, TimelineLineType, TimelineItemContentPlacement, TimelineInstance, TimelineItemInstance } from '@cedar-design/ui-vue'
```

## Reading direction and keyboard interaction

Timeline inherits its container's reading direction. Horizontal nodes and connectors follow LTR/RTL. `reverse` independently controls visual reversal; direction changes do not mutate node data or automatically change `reverse`.

Explicit vertical `mode="left"` / `mode="right"` and item physical sides retain their meaning; `alternate` continues alternating. Labels and custom content inherit text direction normally.

Apply overrides to the rendered component root or the actual popup ancestor. For example, add the following class to that element and replace the value as needed:

```css
.component-theme {
  --c-timeline-content-text-color: var(--c-color-text-1);
}
```

Explicit inline styles and props that write the same CSS property take precedence over stylesheet defaults. After Teleport, ordinary CSS variables inherit from the actual mount location. When using ThemeProvider, follow its local-theme and popup configuration rules. Override the component variable directly for local styling; root-level aliases are not recalculated merely because a descendant system variable changes. Internal variables are not public APIs.

# Tooltip

SSR limitation: a trigger slot node using both `v-for` and `v-memo` can make server rendering fail. Remove `v-memo` from that slot node when rendering on the server; ordinary `v-for` remains supported. The same limitation can affect the `content` slot; remove `v-memo` there for server rendering.

Start with the basic example, then compare related settings before moving to controlled, asynchronous or combined use cases.

```vue
<script setup>

const demoCopy = useDemoLocale("comparison");

const __demoAppearance = __demoReactive({ status: "default", size: "md" });

import { computed as demoComputed, ref as demoRef } from "vue";
const demoCompareFields = [
  {
    name: "status",
    values: ["default", "primary", "info", "success", "warning", "danger"],
  },
  { name: "size", values: ["xs", "md"] },
];

  () =>
    demoCompareFields.find((field) => field.name === demoCompareAxis.value)
      ?.values ?? [],
);

            { label: 'info', value: 'info' },
            { label: 'success', value: 'success' },
            { label: 'warning', value: 'warning' },
            { label: 'danger', value: 'danger' },

      :aria-label="demoCopy.configuration"
      :options="
        demoCompareFields.map((field) => ({
```

## Directive options type

`TooltipOptions` can be imported from the root or `@cedar-design/ui-vue/tooltip`; it contains required `content` and optional `placement`.

## API

### Tooltip Props

Tooltip inherits Trigger positioning, container, controlled state, and `close` policies. Its defaults are `hide-empty=true` and `auto-fit-transform-origin=true`; an omitted `animation-name` uses the Tooltip animation. Empty content hides only the tooltip and does not change `open`; component nodes count as content even when they render no content, producing an empty tooltip and description relationship. Conditionally render the component node in the slot when its content may be empty. The instance exposes seven methods: `open`, `close`, `resize`, `allowClose`, `getReference`, `focusReference`, and `setReference`.

| Prop | Description | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| content | Hint content | `string` | — |
| status | Panel intent | `default \| primary \| info \| success \| warning \| danger` | `default` |
| size | Implemented sizes | `xs \| md` | `md` |
| color | Background color | `string` | — |
| text-color | Custom text color | `string` | — |
| trigger | Interaction | `TriggerEvent \| TriggerEvent[]`<br>`TriggerEvent: 'manual' \| 'hover' \| 'click' \| 'focus' \| 'contextMenu'` | `['hover', 'focus']` |
| placement | Preferred popup side relative to the trigger, default top. With the default auto-fit-position enabled, Trigger may flip and constrain it to the viewport when space is limited; this is not a fixed final position | `TriggerPlacement`<br>`'left' \| 'right' \| 'bottom' \| 'top' \| 'top-start' \| 'top-end' \| 'bottom-start' \| 'bottom-end' \| 'left-start' \| 'left-end' \| 'right-start' \| 'right-end'` | `top` |
| show-arrow | Show the arrow | `boolean` | `true` |
| popup-offset | Main-axis distance | `number` | `10` |
| unmount-on-close | Unmount after close | `boolean` | `true` |

Events: `update:open`, `open-change`, `open`, `opened`, `close`, `closed`, `click-outside`. Slots: `default`, `content`. Exposes `open`, `close`, `resize`, `allowClose`, `getReference`, `setReference` and `focusReference`.

Tooltip content has `role="tooltip"` and its ID is added to the actual reference’s `aria-describedby` while open. Existing and reference-attrs descriptions are merged without duplicates; closing, changing references or unmounting removes the tooltip ID and preserves existing descriptions.

## Usage notes

Use `color` to customize the background and `size="xs"` for the smallest size. There is no `backgroundColor` or boolean `xs` prop.

### Configuration

These are actual :root defaults. Prefer component variables for business customization; internal positioning variables are not public API.

With Teleport, variables must be in the actual popup scope, for example through `popup-style`. Trigger-button variables do not automatically inherit into popups.

## CSS Variables

All built-in themes use opacity 1. Colored solid text follows Button on-dark in both light/dark modes. Maple dark mode retains 4px radius, 14px font and 8px/16px vertical/horizontal padding. Neutral surfaces remain dark in both modes. `color` sets content/arrow backgrounds; `text-color` sets text. Explicit content-style/arrow-style override their respective nodes. Recheck custom colors/opacity.

<!-- component-css-variables:start -->

Use these variables to customize the component. Defaults may vary by the selector condition shown. Each variable applies to the corresponding size, variant and interaction states.

<div class="token-reference-table" style="max-width: 100%; overflow-x: auto;">

| Variable | Default / condition | Affected styles |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--c-tooltip-animation-duration` | `var(--c-sys-motion-duration-standard)` | `transition` |
| `--c-tooltip-background` | `var(--c-sys-color-surface-tooltip)` | `background-color` |

```css
  --c-tooltip-background: var(--c-sys-color-surface-tooltip);
}
```

Explicit inline styles and props that write the same CSS property take precedence over stylesheet defaults. After Teleport, ordinary CSS variables inherit from the actual mount location. When using ThemeProvider, follow its local-theme and popup configuration rules. Override the component variable directly for local styling; root-level aliases are not recalculated merely because a descendant system variable changes. Internal variables are not public APIs.

<!-- Source: src/transfer/README.en-US.md; locale: en-US; page: /en/components/transfer/ -->

# Transfer

Start with the basic example, then compare related settings before moving to controlled, asynchronous or combined use cases.

When omitted, `disabled` and `readonly` inherit from FormItem / Form; explicit false overrides the corresponding state. Both block transfers, sorting, renaming and custom header clear actions. Readonly still allows asynchronous options to load for display. When the target list changes from empty to populated, enabled drag sorting attaches to the list.

Items use their own checkboxes or action buttons without an extra inert row focus stop. Icon-only clear and target action menu controls are native buttons with localized names.

Within FormItem, the transfer group uses the FormItem label when no label `for` is specified; a caller-provided `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` takes precedence. The form error describes the group instead of being repeated on every internal option. Caller-provided `role` and `aria-describedby` remain intact. For multiple fields in one FormItem, use separate FormItems or give each field an explicit name.

When a target value is absent from the current data, the target list still displays its label, falling back to its value. Updating data alone does not change the model. Disabled or required status cannot be inferred for a missing item; keep the corresponding option in data when those restrictions are needed.

## Basic examples

### Basic usage

- `data`: Data of the transfer
- `default-value`: The default value in the target selection box (uncontrolled state)

```vue
<template>
  <c-transfer :data="data" :default-value="value" />
</template>

<script lang="ts" setup>
const data = Array(8)
  .fill(undefined)
  .map((_, index) => ({
    value: `option${index + 1}`,
    label: `Option ${index + 1}`,
  }))
const value = [{ value: 'option1' }, { value: 'option3' }, { value: 'option5' }]
</script>
```

### Grouped

```vue
<template>
  <div style="height: 520px">
```

### Tree

- `data`: Data of the transfer
- `default-value`: The default value in the target selection box (uncontrolled state)

Example source: src/transfer/__demos__/tree.vue

```vue
<template>
  <c-transfer :data="transferData" :default-value="value">
    <template #source="{ data, selectedKeys, onSelect }">
      <c-tree
        :checkable="true"
        checked-strategy="child"
        :checked-values="selectedKeys"
        :data="getTreeData(data)"
        @check="onSelect"
      />
    </template>
  </c-transfer>
</template>

<script lang="ts" setup>
const treeData = [
  {
    label: 'Trunk 0-0',
    value: '0-0',
    children: [
      {
        label: 'Leaf 0-0-1',
        value: '0-0-1',
      },
      {
        label: 'Branch 0-0-2',
        value: '0-0-2',
        children: [
          {
            label: 'Leaf 0-0-2-1',
            value: '0-0-2-1',
          },
          {
            label: 'Leaf 0-0-2-2',
            value: '0-0-2-2',
          },
        ],
      },
    ],
  },
  {
    label: 'Trunk 0-1',
    value: '0-1',
    children: [
      {
        label: 'Branch 0-1-1',
        value: '0-1-1',
        children: [
          {
            label: 'Leaf 0-1-1-1',
            value: '0-1-1-1',
          },
          {
            label: 'Leaf 0-1-1-2',
            value: '0-1-1-2',
          },
        ],
      },
      {
        label: 'Leaf 0-1-2',
        value: '0-1-2',
      },
    ],
  },
]

const getTransferData = (treeData = [], transferDataSource = []) => {
  treeData.forEach((item) => {
    if (item.children) getTransferData(item.children, transferDataSource)
    else transferDataSource.push({ label: item.label, value: item.value })
  })
  return transferDataSource
}

const getTreeData = (data = []) => {
  const values = data.map((item) => item.value)

  const travel = (_treeData = []) => {
    const treeDataSource = []
    _treeData.forEach((item) => {
      if (item.children || values.includes(item.value)) {
        treeDataSource.push({ label: item.label, value: item.value, children: travel(item.children) })
      }
    })
    return treeDataSource
  }

  return travel(treeData)
}

const transferData = getTransferData(treeData)

const value = [{ value: '0-0-2-1' }]
</script>
```

## API

### Empty values and reading placeholders

`empty-values` recognizes empty data; `empty-value` keeps existing clear output. `empty-text` defaults to `'-'` under `read-pretty`, with Field > FormItem > Form precedence and custom read slots first. With explicit `empty-values`, built-in required uses the policy; custom validators receive original data. See the [shared guide](llms/en-US/guide/empty-values.md).

| Prop | Type | Default and scope |
| ------------ | ------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------- |
| empty-values | readonly unknown[] | Field > FormItem > Form > component-family default; replaces the whole list |
| empty-text | string | Field > FormItem > Form > '-'; explicit '' is valid |

These props belong to field presentation; pure panels do not gain reading mode. Form and FormItem provide inherited settings. The existing empty-value type and clear fallback remain component-specific.

| model-value **(v-model)** | Complete ordered target-side state | `TransferTargetItem[] \| null` | `-` |
| default-value | Complete uncontrolled target-side state | `TransferTargetItem[]` | `[]` |

### Editing and confirmation

This component supports `edit-mode` with field > FormItem > Form precedence. When unset, it defaults to `direct` and preserves `direct` editing. Supported values: `direct / click / dblclick`. Non-direct modes open the editor through the field value trigger and keep one draft; v-model updates only after confirmation. Cancel, reset or enabling readPretty discards the draft.

Cedar uses edit-mode="click" / "dblclick" to open an editor popup near the field. Enter/F2 also opens it; cancel/Escape discards the draft, and confirmation commits it. readPretty is an independent reading setting, separate from readonly and disabled.

`before-commit(value, { previousValue, signal })` can reject an overlay save. FormItem validates the candidate first and keeps the editor open on failure. `open / default-open / update:open` control the editor. Use `#read="{ value, text }"` to customize display. See the full field comparison in Form.

`read-pretty` is an independent boolean alongside `readonly` and `disabled`. It inherits from field to FormItem to Form; explicit `false` overrides the parent. The default is `false`. Reading mode renders no editor.

`data` accepts an array or (query, { signal }) => array/Promise. The component manages loading, cancellation and stale-result isolation; failures emit load-error. Single/multiple groups initialize with an empty query; searchable fields reload when queries change. Tree root loading is independent of existing load-more child loading.

## Reading direction and keyboard interaction

Transfer maintains selection directly through candidate-list checkboxes. Candidates sit at inline start and selections at inline end: candidates are right and selections left in RTL. Headings, search, clear/action spacing and joined radii follow direction.

Direction changes do not modify `modelValue`, selection order, search queries or frozen state. Vertical list dragging keeps its order semantics. Remove buttons are keyboard-operable; required and disabled items cannot be removed. Frozen `left/right` values retain their existing business grouping rather than swapping with reading direction.

Apply overrides to the rendered component root or the actual popup ancestor. For example, add the following class to that element and replace the value as needed:

```css

  --c-transfer-border-color: var(--c-color-neutral-3);
}
```

Explicit inline styles and props that write the same CSS property take precedence over stylesheet defaults. After Teleport, ordinary CSS variables inherit from the actual mount location. When using ThemeProvider, follow its local-theme and popup configuration rules. Override the component variable directly for local styling; root-level aliases are not recalculated merely because a descendant system variable changes. Internal variables are not public APIs.

# TreeSelect

A tree-backed selection field with explicit search fields and controlled selection.

## Reading direction

Inherits source dir. Horizontal keys expand, enter children, return or collapse according to reading direction; vertical keys and Home/End keep logical order. Search uses the actual active match. Values and multiple-value arrays are not reversed. Portaled content retains source direction in custom containers.

## Basic examples

### Basic

Example source: src/tree-select/__demos__/basic.vue

```vue
<template>
  <c-space direction="column">
    <c-tree-select v-model="value" :data="data" :tree-props="{ defaultExpandAll: true }" selectable="leaf" clearable placeholder="选择部门" />
    <p role="status">当前部门：{{ value || '未选择' }}</p>
  </c-space>
</template>
<script setup lang="ts">
import { ref } from 'vue'
const value = ref<string>()
const data = [
  { value: 'product', label: '产品中心', children: [
    { value: 'design', label: '设计部' },
    { value: 'engineering', label: '研发部' },
  ] },
  { value: 'operations', label: '运营中心', children: [
    { value: 'support', label: '客户服务部' },
    { value: 'locked', label: '归档部门（禁用）', disabled: true },
  ] },
]
</script>
```

### Checkbox multiple selection

Select a parent to check its available children. `tree-checked-strategy="child"` publishes leaf identities; disabled nodes remain unavailable.

Example source: src/tree-select/__demos__/en-US/multiple.vue

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { ref } from 'vue'
import type { TreeNodeData } from '@cedar-design/ui-vue'

const value = ref<string[]>(['design'])
const data: TreeNodeData[] = [
  { value: 'product', label: 'Product', children: [
    { value: 'design', label: 'Design' },
    { value: 'engineering', label: 'Engineering' },
  ] },
  { value: 'operations', label: 'Operations', children: [
    { value: 'support', label: 'Support' },
    { value: 'locked', label: 'Archived department (disabled)', disabled: true },
  ] },
]
</script>
<template>
  <c-space direction="column" fill>
    <c-tree-select v-model="value" :data="data" :tree-props="{ defaultExpandAll: true }" multiple tree-checkable tree-checked-strategy="child" clearable placeholder="Select departments" />
    <p role="status">Selected departments: {{ value.join(', ') || 'None' }}</p>
    <c-tree-select v-model="value" :data="data" multiple tree-checkable read-pretty />
  </c-space>
</template>
```

## Data and options

### Search Matching

<!-- demo-config-notes:start -->

#### Configuration reference for this comparison

| Configuration | Purpose | Related examples |
| -------------------- | ---------------------- | ------------------------------------------------ |
| `data` | Data | Search Matching, Retain the query after selecting |
| `filterable` | Whether to allow searching | Search Matching, Retain the query after selecting |
| `case-sensitive` | Case-sensitive built-in search | Search Matching |
| `multiple` | Whether to support multiple selection | Retain the query after selecting |
| `retain-input-value` | Keep search text after selecting an option | Retain the query after selecting |

<!-- demo-config-notes:end -->


Example source: src/tree-select/__demos__/search-matching.vue

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { computed, ref } from "vue";
const value = ref("");
const mode = ref("label");
const caseSensitive = ref(false);
const modes = [
  { value: "label", label: "默认：只匹配 label" },
  { value: "both", label: "配置：value 或 label" },
];
const options = [
  { value: "USER_A", label: "Apple" },
  { value: "USER_B", label: "Banana" },
];
const searchFields = computed<("label" | "value")[]>(() =>
  mode.value === "both" ? ["value", "label"] : ["label"],
);
</script>
<template>
  <c-space direction="column" align="stretch" fill>
    <c-form-item layout="vertical" size="sm" label="匹配字段">
      <c-radio-group
        v-model="mode"
        aria-label="匹配字段"
        :options="modes"
        variant="button"
        size="sm"
      />
    </c-form-item>
    <c-space
      ><c-switch v-model="caseSensitive" /><span>区分大小写</span></c-space
    >
    <c-tree-select
      v-model="value"
      :data="options"
      :case-sensitive="caseSensitive"
      :search-fields="searchFields"
      filterable
      placeholder="输入 Apple、apple 或 USER_A"
    />
    <p>
      默认搜索 label，不区分大小写；配置两字段后，USER_A 和 Apple
      都能找到同一个选项。
    </p>
  </c-space>
</template>
```

### Retain the query after selecting

Type Al, then select Alice: the selected model contains Alice in both examples. Without retain-input-value the search text becomes empty; with it enabled, Al remains so Alan is still easy to select next. This does not control the selected label or whether the field is searchable. filterable enables searching.

Example source: src/tree-select/__demos__/en-US/retain-input-value.vue

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { ref } from 'vue'
const cleared = ref<string[]>([])
const retained = ref<string[]>([])
const clearQuery = ref('')
const retainedQuery = ref('')
const data = [{ value: 'alice', label: 'Alice' }, { value: 'alan', label: 'Alan' }, { value: 'bob', label: 'Bob' }]
</script>
<template>
  <c-space direction="column">
    <p>Type Al and select Alice. Both fields select Alice; only the remaining query text differs.</p>
    <c-tree-select v-model="cleared" v-model:input-value="clearQuery" :data="data" filterable multiple placeholder="Clear query after selecting" />
    <output>Selected: {{ cleared }}; query: {{ JSON.stringify(clearQuery) }}</output>
    <c-tree-select v-model="retained" v-model:input-value="retainedQuery" :data="data" filterable multiple retain-input-value placeholder="Keep query after selecting" />
    <output>Selected: {{ retained }}; query: {{ JSON.stringify(retainedQuery) }}</output>
  </c-space>
</template>
```

The candidate `data` prop accepts an array or `(query, { signal }) => array/Promise`. Components own loading, cancellation and stale results, and emit load-error on failure. Choice groups initialize with an empty query; searchable fields load when queries change. Root tree loaders remain independent of existing load-more child loading.

With open-trigger-target="icon", use the input area to edit or copy and the suffix button to open. Existing text remains copyable when editing or search is disabled.

## API

### Empty values and reading placeholders

`empty-values` recognizes empty data; `empty-value` keeps existing clear output. `empty-text` defaults to `'-'` under `read-pretty`, with Field > FormItem > Form precedence and custom read slots first. With explicit `empty-values`, built-in required uses the policy; custom validators receive original data. See the [shared guide](llms/en-US/guide/empty-values.md).

| Prop | Type | Default and scope |
| ------------ | ------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------- |
| empty-values | readonly unknown[] | Field > FormItem > Form > component-family default; replaces the whole list |
| empty-text | string | Field > FormItem > Form > '-'; explicit '' is valid |

These props belong to field presentation; pure panels do not gain reading mode. Form and FormItem provide inherited settings. The existing empty-value type and clear fallback remain component-specific.

### TreeSelect Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| need-confirm | `boolean` | Single `false`; multiple `true` | Applies only to overlay editing. Single selection commits and closes on choice by default; true keeps a draft until confirmation. Multiple selection defaults to confirmation. Submission still runs form validation and before-commit; rejection keeps the editor open. |
| model-value | TreeSelectValue | undefined | Controlled value: node identity, label value, homogeneous arrays or null. |
| default-value | TreeSelectValue | undefined | Uncontrolled initial value, read only at creation. |
| data | readonly TreeNodeData[] / `OptionsLoader<TreeNodeData>` | undefined | Root candidate array or (query, { signal }) loader. |
| multiple | boolean | false | Enable multiple selection and determine default searching when filterable is omitted. |
| label-in-value | boolean | false | Publish label-value objects; an explicit label takes precedence over the candidate name. |
| tree-checkable | boolean | false | Use tree checkboxes and a multiple-value model; this flag alone does not enable searching. |
| tree-check-strictly | boolean | false | Check parent and child nodes independently. |
| tree-checked-strategy | 'all' / 'parent' / 'child' | 'all' | Display strategy for linked checks, following Tree rules. |
| filterable | boolean | undefined | Explicit values take precedence; the default follows multiple, not tree-checkable. |
| retain-input-value | boolean | false | Retain search text after selection. |
| input-value | string | undefined | Controlled search text, independent of the selected value. |
| default-input-value | string | '' | Initial uncontrolled search text. |
| case-sensitive | boolean | false | Case-sensitive built-in node searching; custom callbacks take precedence. |
| search-fields | readonly OptionSearchField[]<br>`OptionSearchField: 'label' \| 'value'` | ['label'] | Built-in search fields, mapped through field-names. |
| filter-tree-node | (searchKey, nodeData) => boolean | undefined | Custom node filtering callback. |
| disable-filter | boolean | false | Disable internal node filtering for data already filtered by the application. |
| field-names | TreeFieldNames | undefined | Business node field mapping; identities must be unique across the tree. |
| load-more | (nodeData) => `Promise<void>` | undefined | Lazy node loading using the Tree loading protocol. |
| fallback-option | boolean / function | true | Synchronous node fallback for missing candidates; false hides unmatched values. |
| selectable | boolean / leaf / function | true | Node selection policy; leaf allows only leaf nodes. |
| tree-props | `Partial<TreeProps>` | undefined | Internal tree configuration; managed top-level fields take precedence; TreeSelectTreeOptions checks the boundary. |
| trigger-props | `Partial<TriggerProps>` | undefined | Candidate popup configuration; top-level opening and mounting policies take precedence. |
| dropdown-style | CSSProperties | undefined | Candidate content style. |
| dropdown-class-name | string / string[] | undefined | Additional candidate content classes. |
| scrollbar | boolean / ScrollbarProps | true | Candidate-area scrollbar configuration. |
| show-header-on-empty | boolean | false | Retain header content when candidates are empty. |
| show-footer-on-empty | boolean | false | Retain footer content when candidates are empty. |
| placeholder | string | undefined | Placeholder for the default selection field. |
| size | ComponentSize<br>`'xs' \| 'sm' \| 'md' \| 'lg' \| 'xl'` | undefined | Selection field size, inherited from group and form when omitted. |
| border | boolean | true | The default field uses filled; false switches to standard. |
| max-tag-count | number | undefined | Maximum displayed selected tags; omission or 0 leaves the count unlimited. |
| disabled | boolean | undefined | Disable editing; inherited from the form when omitted. |
| readonly | boolean | undefined | Readonly, inherited from the form when omitted; distinct from pure reading. |
| error | boolean | undefined | Error state, inherited from the form when omitted. |
| loading | boolean | false | Field and candidate waiting feedback; pauses selection, clearing, removal and confirmation while retaining search and closing. |
| loading-mode | 'default' / 'line' | 'default' | Field indicator or bottom loading line; does not change the popup loader scope. |
| clearable | boolean | false | Allow clearing; deferred modes first update the draft. |
| empty-value | TreeSelectProps['emptyValue'] | undefined | Clear result override: node value, array, null or factory; omission preserves existing rules. |
| empty-values | readonly unknown[] | undefined | Empty-value recognition, inherited through field, FormItem and Form. |
| empty-text | string | undefined | Default empty reading text; defaults to a dash after inheritance; custom read takes precedence. |
| read-pretty | boolean | undefined | Common pure-reading state, inherited from the form when omitted. |
| edit-mode | direct / click / dblclick | undefined | Editing entry, inherited from the form when omitted, otherwise direct. |
| before-commit | BeforeFieldCommit | undefined | Before confirmation, calls ({ value, previousValue }, done, { signal }); complete with a boolean, Promise or done; synchronous undefined waits for done. |
| open | boolean | undefined | Controlled candidate popup or deferred editor state. |
| default-open | boolean | false | Initial uncontrolled open state. |
| popup-container | PopupContainer | undefined | Top-level mount target: selector, HTMLElement or false. |
| open-trigger-target | 'field' / 'icon' | 'field' | Open editing from the field or only its icon; keyboard entry remains available. |

### TreeSelect Events

| Event | Arguments | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| update:modelValue / change | TreeSelectValue / undefined | Selected value publication; deferred drafts do not trigger it. |
| update:inputValue / input-value-change / search | string | Input text and search notifications. |
| update:open / open-change | boolean | Candidate popup or editor open notifications. |
| keydown | KeyboardEvent | Field keyboard event; `preventDefault()` suppresses internal keyboard handling. |
| clear | — | Clear action notification; deferred modes still require confirmation. |
| load-error | error: unknown, node?: TreeNodeData | The current root data source or node loadMore failed; node failures include the original node. Listener Promises are not awaited. |

### TreeSelect Slots

| Slot | Prop | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| trigger | — | Replace the default field trigger content. |
| read | TreeSelectReadScope | Common reading { value, text }; text is the formatted value and is empty for empty values; empty-text affects default reading only. |
| label | { data: SelectionFieldItem } | Selected item content in the default field. |
| selected / prefix / suffix | — | Selected area, prefix and suffix of the default field, consistent with Select. |
| clear-icon | { clear(event?) } | Custom clear node; call clear for the standard clear action. |
| arrow-icon | { focus, menuOpen } | Default field arrow with real focus and open state. |
| loading-icon / search-icon | — | Default field loading or search icon; line mode does not show a loading icon. |
| header / footer | — | Candidate content header and footer; corresponding props control visibility when empty. |
| loader / empty | — | Candidate panel waiting and empty content; loader is separate from the field loading-icon. |
| tree-slot-label / tree-slot-extra | node: TreeNodeData, status: TreeSelectNodeStatus | Forward Tree node label and extra content; node data is the first argument and status the second. |
| tree-slot-* | Parameters of the corresponding Tree slot | Other Tree slots are forwarded using the corresponding protocol. |

### TreeSelect Methods

| Method | Returns | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| refresh() | `Promise<void>` | Reload the current data source without opening the editor. |
| focus() / blur() | void | Operate the current default field input; deferred modes use the common editing entry. |

### Public types

TreeSelectProps is inferred from actual props. TreeSelectValue, TreeSelectLabelValue, TreeSelectReadScope, TreeSelectNodeStatus, TreeSelectEmits, TreeSelectSlots and TreeSelectExpose are available from the root and tree-select entry points. There is no default editor replacement slot; use tree-slot-label for node content.

### Editing and confirmation

Cedar uses edit-mode="click" / "dblclick" to open an editor popup near the field. Enter/F2 also opens it; cancel/Escape discards the draft, and confirmation commits it. readPretty is an independent reading setting, separate from readonly and disabled.

### In-place editing and keyboard precedence

`click`/`dblclick` use Form's editing inheritance. Hover/focus shows an edit icon that opens editing directly. disabled, readonly and readPretty hide edit entries. Panel clicks change only the draft.

While open, arrows navigate visible enabled nodes; Left/Right collapse/expand or move to parents/children; Home/End reach first/last nodes. Enter selects/checks the current node, or toggles an unselectable branch. Search prioritizes matching nodes; multiple selection uses Tree checking rules. Esc first closes the panel, retaining the draft and restoring input focus. With the panel closed, Enter saves and Esc cancels editing. Compare AutoComplete/PeopleSelect in Form's unified field-presentation examples.

Checkboxes in a multiple-selection tree do not create separate Tab stops. Pointer selection retains input focus, and nodes expose checked and mixed states through `aria-checked`.

Duplicate expansion requests for the same asynchronously loaded node are merged. Replacing nodes, closing editors or resetting Form invalidates old requests so they cannot expand/check nodes. Arrows can enter loaded children immediately. Query/candidate changes clear old filters before Enter can choose stale options. Field confirmation still validates before asynchronous commit.

### Node fields and business values

Nodes default to `{ value, label, children }`. `value` is a tree-wide unique string/number, including `0`; `label` is display content. Map other backend fields with `fieldNames: { value: 'id', label: 'text', children: 'items' }` without changing backend data. Declarative child `name`, Vue `:key` and Table `rowKey` retain separate meanings.

Tree's standalone state uses `selectedValues/defaultSelectedValues`, `checkedValues/defaultCheckedValues`, `halfCheckedValues` and `expandedValues/defaultExpandedValues`, updated through the matching named v-models. The half-checked collection in the `check` event is `halfCheckedValues`. The node content slot is `label`; TreeSelect forwards it as `tree-slot-label`. `scrollIntoView({ value })` locates a node by business value, while an explicit `index` remains the virtual list's zero-based array index. Opening the virtual list scrolls to the active item; its reference is not exposed while it is unmounted and is restored after remounting.

### Search configuration

Use `filterable` for searching; omission follows only `multiple`. Enabling `tree-checkable` alone creates a `multiple`-value model without enabling searching; set `filterable` explicitly. `retain-input-value` independently retains search text after selection and defaults to false.

Replace the old `allow-search` with `filterable`. Replace `{ retainInputValue: true }` with `filterable` plus `retain-input-value`.

### Search fields

`searchFields` / `search-fields` is a readonly `('label' | 'value')[]`, defaulting to `['label']`. Multiple fields use OR matching, case-insensitive by default. `['value', 'label']` searches codes and names; fieldNames maps semantic fields to business fields. An empty array matches no items for a nonempty query. Values are compared as strings; object traversal, object values and pinyin matching require a custom callback. A custom callback takes precedence and decides case handling itself. Remote results use the existing protocol for disabling local filtering. Cascader retains path semantics and checks the configured fields on each path node.

## Configuring the cleared value

`empty-value` defines the output of an existing clear action. Omission preserves the component fallback; supported types remain component-specific. It does not change empty-values recognition or Form reset defaults.

Refresh can retry the component-owned asynchronous option source before the editor opens, using the existing AbortSignal, loading, and load-error protocol without opening the editor; static arrays do not create extra requests.

### Input and open button

The native combobox and separate open button both announce aria-haspopup=tree. While the panel is visible, the same aria-controls points to the actual tree. Expanded state stays synchronized; disabled/readonly and open-trigger-target rules remain in force.

### Selection actions during loading

While manual loading or the current candidate request is active, selection fields preserve existing values and pause selection, clearing and tag removal. Blocked actions neither notify nor submit a model. Search text remains editable and disabled/readonly are not changed; set them separately to prevent searching.

Deferred editor clearing and confirmation are unavailable while loading; cancellation and closing remain available. Actions return to their normal state after both the manual flag and current request finish, still respecting disabled options. Loading on free-text fields such as Input and AutoComplete continues to allow text editing and clearing.

# Tree

Start with the basic example, then compare related settings before moving to controlled, asynchronous or combined use cases.

## Basic examples

### Basic usage

- `data`: Pass in `data` to generate the corresponding tree structure
- `default-expanded-values`: Nodes expanded by default
- `default-selected-values`: Tree node selected by default

Example source: src/tree/__demos__/basic.vue
