### Control

- `checkable`: Whether to add a checkbox before the node, function format is supported since `2.27.0`
- `selected-values`: Selected tree node
- `checked-values`: Tree node with check box selected
- `expanded-values`: Expanded node

Example source: src/tree/__demos__/control.vue

```vue
<template>
  <c-button-group style="margin-bottom: 20px">
    <c-button status="primary" @click="toggleChecked">
      {{ checkedValues?.length ? 'deselect all' : 'select all' }}
    </c-button>
    <c-button status="primary" @click="toggleExpanded">
      {{ expandedValues?.length ? 'fold' : 'unfold' }}
    </c-button>
  </c-button-group>
  <c-tree
    :checkable="true"
    v-model:selected-values="selectedValues"
    v-model:checked-values="checkedValues"
    v-model:expanded-values="expandedValues"
    @select="onSelect"
    @check="onCheck"
    @expand="onExpand"
    :data="treeData" />
</template>

<script lang="ts" setup>
import { ref } from 'vue'

const allCheckedValues = ['0-0', '0-0-1', '0-0-2', '0-0-2-1', '0-1', '0-1-1', '0-1-2']
const allExpandedValues = ['0-0', '0-1', '0-0-2']
const selectedValues = ref([])
const checkedValues = ref([])
const expandedValues = ref([])

function toggleChecked() {
  checkedValues.value = checkedValues?.value.length ? [] : allCheckedValues
}

function toggleExpanded() {
  expandedValues.value = expandedValues?.value.length ? [] : allExpandedValues
}

function onSelect(newSelectedValues, event) {
  console.log('select: ', newSelectedValues, event)
}

function onCheck(newCheckedValues, event) {
  console.log('check: ', newCheckedValues, event)
}

function onExpand(newExpandedValues, event) {
  console.log('expand: ', newExpandedValues, event)
}

const treeData = [
  {
    label: 'Trunk 0-0',
    value: '0-0',
    children: [
      {
        label: 'Leaf 0-0-1',
        value: '0-0-1',
      },
      {
        label: 'Branch 0-0-2',
        value: '0-0-2',
        children: [
          {
            label: 'Leaf 0-0-2-1',
            value: '0-0-2-1',
          },
        ],
      },
    ],
  },
  {
    label: 'Trunk 0-1',
    value: '0-1',
    children: [
      {
        label: 'Leaf 0-1-1',
        value: '0-1-1',
      },
      {
        label: 'Leaf 0-1-2',
        value: '0-1-2',
      },
    ],
  },
]
</script>
```

### Checked Strategy

- `checkable`: Whether to add a checkbox before the node, function format is supported since `2.27.0`
- `checked-values`: Tree node with check box selected
- `checked-strategy`: Customized backfill method <br/> all: return all selected nodes <br/> parent: return only parent node when both parent and child nodes are selected <br/> child: return only child nodes
- `data`: Pass in `data` to generate the corresponding tree structure

Example source: src/tree/__demos__/checked-strategy.vue

```vue
<template>
  <c-radio-group
    type="button"
    v-model="checkedStrategy"
    @change="
      (value) => {
        checkedValues = []
      }
    "
  >
    <c-radio v-for="item in strategyOptions" :key="item?.value" :value="item?.value">
      {{ item?.label }}
    </c-radio>
  </c-radio-group>
  <br />
  <c-typography-text style="margin: 24px 0; display: inline-block">
    Current: {{ checkedValues?.join(' , ') }}
  </c-typography-text>
  <br />
  <c-tree :checkable="true" v-model:checked-values="checkedValues" :checked-strategy="checkedStrategy" :data="treeData" />
</template>

<script lang="ts" setup>
import { ref } from 'vue'

const checkedValues = ref([])
const checkedStrategy = ref('all')

const treeData = [
  {
    label: 'Trunk 0-0',
    value: '0-0',
    children: [
      {
        label: 'Leaf',
        value: '0-0-1',
      },
      {
        label: 'Branch 0-0-2',
        value: '0-0-2',
        children: [
          {
            label: 'Leaf',
            value: '0-0-2-1',
          },
        ],
      },
    ],
  },
  {
    label: 'Trunk 0-1',
    value: '0-1',
    children: [
      {
        label: 'Branch 0-1-1',
        value: '0-1-1',
        children: [
          {
            label: 'Leaf',
            value: '0-1-1-1',
          },
          {
            label: 'Leaf',
            value: '0-1-1-2',
          },
        ],
      },
      {
        label: 'Leaf',
        value: '0-1-2',
      },
    ],
  },
]

const strategyOptions = [
  {
    value: 'all',
    label: 'show all',
  },
  {

    label: 'show parent',
```

### Render Extra

- `block-node`: Whether the node occupies a row
- `checkable`: Whether to add a checkbox before the node, function format is supported since `2.27.0`
- `selectable`: Whether to support selection, function format is supported since `2.27.0`
- `check-strictly`: Whether to cancel the parent-child node association

Example source: src/tree/__demos__/render-extra.vue

```vue
<template>
  <div style="width: 500px; padding: 2px; overflow: auto">
    <c-space wrap>
      <c-checkbox v-model="leafChecksOnly">Leaf checkboxes only</c-checkbox>
      <c-checkbox v-model="leafSelectionOnly">Leaf selection only</c-checkbox>
      <c-checkbox v-model="strict">Strict checks</c-checkbox>
      <c-tag>Checked: {{ checkedValues.join(', ') || '-' }}</c-tag>
      <c-tag>Selected: {{ selectedValues.join(', ') || '-' }}</c-tag>
    </c-space>
    <c-tree
      :block-node="true"
      :checkable="leafChecksOnly ? isLeafNode : true"
      :selectable="leafSelectionOnly ? isLeafNode : true"
      :check-strictly="strict"
      :data="treeData"
      @check="keys => checkedValues = keys"
      @select="keys => selectedValues = keys"
    >
      <template #extra="nodeData">
        <c-button
          variant="text"
          size="xs"
          :aria-label="'Add child to ' + nodeData.title + ' (' + nodeData.key + ')'"
          style="position: absolute; right: 8px; top: 2px"
          @click.stop="onIconClick(nodeData)"
        >
          <template #icon><c-icon-plus /></template>
        </c-button>
      </template>
    </c-tree>
  </div>
</template>

<script lang="ts" setup>
import { ref } from 'vue'

const leafChecksOnly = ref(false)
const leafSelectionOnly = ref(false)
const strict = ref(false)
const checkedValues = ref<(string | number)[]>([])
const selectedValues = ref<(string | number)[]>([])
const isLeafNode = (_node: unknown, info: { isLeaf: boolean }) => info.isLeaf

function onIconClick(nodeData) {
  const children = nodeData.children || []
  children.push({
    label: 'new tree node',
    value: nodeData.key + '-' + (children.length + 1),
  })
  nodeData.children = children

  treeData.value = [...treeData.value]
}

const treeData = ref([
  {
    label: 'Trunk',
    value: '0-0',
    children: [
      {
        label: 'Leaf',
        value: '0-0-1',
      },
      {
        label: 'Branch',
        value: '0-0-2',
        children: [
          {
            label: 'Leaf',
            value: '0-0-2-1',
          },
        ],
      },
    ],
  },
  {
    label: 'Trunk',
    value: '0-1',
    children: [
      {
        label: 'Branch',
        value: '0-1-1',
        children: [
          {
            label: 'Leaf',
            value: '0-1-1-1',
          },
          {
            label: 'Leaf',
            value: '0-1-1-2',
          },
        ],
      },
      {
        label: 'Leaf',
        value: '0-1-2',
      },
    ],
  },
])
</script>
```

### Draggable

- `draggable`: Whether it can be dragged
- `block-node`: Whether the node occupies a row
- `checkable`: Whether to add a checkbox before the node, function format is supported since `2.27.0`
- `data`: Pass in `data` to generate the corresponding tree structure

Example source: src/tree/__demos__/draggable.vue

```vue
<template>
  <c-checkbox v-model="checked" style="margin-bottom: 20px"> checkable </c-checkbox>
  <c-tree class="tree-demo" draggable blockNode :checkable="checked" :data="treeData" @drop="onDrop" />
</template>

<script lang="ts" setup>
import { ref } from 'vue'

const defaultTreeData = [
  {
    label: 'Trunk 0-0',
    value: '0-0',
    children: [
      {
        label: 'Leaf 0-0-1',
        value: '0-0-1',
      },
      {
        label: 'Branch 0-0-2',
        value: '0-0-2',
        disableCheckbox: true,
        children: [
          {
            draggable: false,
            label: 'Leaf 0-0-2-1 (Drag disabled)',
            value: '0-0-2-1',
          },
        ],
      },
    ],
  },
  {
    label: 'Trunk 0-1',
    value: '0-1',
    children: [
      {
        label: 'Branch 0-1-1',
        value: '0-1-1',
        checkable: false,
        children: [
          {
            label: 'Leaf 0-1-1-1',
            value: '0-1-1-1',
          },
          {
            label: 'Leaf 0-1-1-2',
            value: '0-1-1-2',
          },
        ],
      },
      {
        label: 'Leaf 0-1-2',
        value: '0-1-2',
      },
    ],
  },
]

const treeData = ref(defaultTreeData)
const checkedValues = ref([])
const checked = ref(false)

function onDrop({ dragNode, dropNode, dropPosition }) {
  const data = treeData.value
  const loop = (data, key, callback) => {
    data.some((item, index, arr) => {
      if (item.key === key) {
        callback(item, index, arr)
        return true
      }
      if (item.children) {
        return loop(item.children, key, callback)
      }
      return false
    })
  }

  loop(data, dragNode.key, (_, index, arr) => {
    arr.splice(index, 1)
  })

  if (dropPosition === 0) {
    loop(data, dropNode.key, (item) => {
      item.children = item.children || []
      item.children.push(dragNode)
    })
  } else {
    loop(data, dropNode.key, (_, index, arr) => {
      arr.splice(dropPosition < 0 ? index : index + 1, 0, dragNode)
    })
  }
}
</script>
```

## Async data and virtualization

### Load More

<!-- demo-config-notes:start -->
#### Configuration reference for this comparison

| Configuration | Purpose | Related examples |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `data` | Pass in `data` to generate the corresponding tree structure | Load More, Virtual |
| `load-more` | A callback for loading data asynchronously, returning a `Promise` | Load More |
| `block-node` | Whether the node occupies a row | Virtual |
| `checkable` | Add a checkbox before nodes | Virtual |

<!-- demo-config-notes:end -->


- `data`: Pass in `data` to generate the corresponding tree structure
- `load-more`: A callback for loading data asynchronously, returning a `Promise`

Example source: src/tree/__demos__/load-more.vue

```vue
<template>
  <c-tree :data="treeData" :load-more="loadMore" />
</template>

<script lang="ts" setup>
import { ref } from 'vue'

const treeData = ref([
  {
    label: 'Trunk 0-0',
    value: '0-0',
  },
  {
    label: 'Trunk 0-1',
    value: '0-1',
    children: [
      {
        label: 'Branch 0-1-1',
        value: '0-1-1',
      },
    ],
  },
])

const loadMore = (nodeData) => {
  return new Promise((resolve) => {
    setTimeout(() => {
      nodeData.children = [{ label: `leaf`, value: `${nodeData.value}-1`, isLeaf: true }]
      resolve()
    }, 1000)
  })
}
</script>
```

### Virtual

- `block-node`: Whether the node occupies a row
- `checkable`: Whether to add a checkbox before the node, function format is supported since `2.27.0`
- `data`: Pass in `data` to generate the corresponding tree structure
- `virtual-list-props`: Pass virtual list properties, pass in this parameter to turn on virtual scrolling, [VirtualListProps](#VirtualListProps)

Example source: src/tree/__demos__/virtual.vue

```vue
<template>
  <c-button status="primary" :style="{ marginBottom: '20px' }" @click="scrollIntoView">
    Scroll to 0-0-2-2, i.e. the 26th.
  </c-button>
  <c-tree
    ref="treeRef"
    blockNode
    checkable
    :data="treeData"
    :virtualListProps="{
      height: 200,
    }" />
</template>

<script lang="ts" setup>
import { ref } from 'vue'

function loop(path = '0', level = 2) {
  const list = []
  for (let i = 0; i < 10; i += 1) {
    const key = `${path}-${i}`
    const treeNode: {
      label: string
      value: string
      children?: ReturnType<typeof loop>
    } = {
      label: key,
      key,
    }

    if (level > 0) {
      treeNode.children = loop(key, level - 1)
    }

    list.push(treeNode)
  }
  return list
}

const treeRef = ref()
const treeData = loop()
const scrollIntoView = () => {
  treeRef.value && treeRef.value.scrollIntoView({ value: '0-0-2-2' })
}
</script>
```

| selectable | Whether selection is supported | `boolean\| ((    node: TreeNodeData,    info: {      level: number;      isLeaf: boolean;    }  ) => boolean)` | `true` |
| check-strictly | Whether to cancel the parent-child node association | `boolean` | `false` |
| checked-strategy | Customized backfill method <br/> all: return all selected nodes <br/> parent: return only parent node when both parent and child nodes are selected <br/> child: return only child nodes | `'all' \| 'parent' \| 'child'` | `'all'` |
| default-selected-values | Tree node selected by default | `Array<string \| number>` | `-` |

| field-names | Specify the field name in the node data | `TreeFieldNames` | `-` |
| show-line | Whether to display the connection line | `boolean` | `false` |

| draggable | Whether it can be dragged | `boolean` | `false` |

| only-check-leaf | When enabled, checkedValues is only for checked leaf nodes, and the status of the parent node is determined by the child node.(Only valid when checkable and checkStrictly is false) | `boolean` | `false` |
| animation | Whether to enable expand transition animation | `boolean` | `true` |
| action-on-node-click | The action triggered when the node is clicked | `'expand'` | `-` |

### Tree Events

| Event | Description | Arguments |
| ---------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| update:selectedValues | Selected node values updated | `TreeNodeValue[]` |
| update:checkedValues | Checked node values updated | `TreeNodeValue[]` |
| update:halfCheckedValues | Half-checked node values updated | `TreeNodeValue[]` |
| update:expandedValues | Expanded node values updated | `TreeNodeValue[]` |
| select | Emitted when a tree node is clicked | selectedValues: `Array<string \| number>`<br>data: `{ selected?: boolean; selectedNodes: TreeNodeData[]; node?: TreeNodeData; e?: Event; }` |
| check | Emitted when a node checkbox is clicked. `halfCheckedValues`/`halfCheckedNodes` are supported since `2.19.0` | checkedValues: `Array<string \| number>`<br>data: `{ checked?: boolean; checkedNodes: TreeNodeData[]; node?: TreeNodeData; e?: Event; halfCheckedValues: (string \| number)[]; halfCheckedNodes: TreeNodeData[]; }` |
| expand | Expand/collapse | expandKeys: `Array<string \| number>`<br>data: `{ expanded?: boolean; expandedNodes: TreeNodeData[]; node?: TreeNodeData; e?: Event; }` |
| load-error | Current node async load failed | error: `unknown`<br>node: `TreeNodeData` |
| drag-start | Node drag starts | ev: `DragEvent`<br>node: `TreeNodeData` |
| drag-end | Node drag ends | ev: `DragEvent`<br>node: `TreeNodeData` |
| drag-over | Node enters a drop target | ev: `DragEvent`<br>node: `TreeNodeData` |
| drag-leave | Node leaves a drop target | ev: `DragEvent`<br>node: `TreeNodeData` |
| drop | Node is dropped on a target | data: `{ e: DragEvent; dragNode: TreeNodeData; dropNode: TreeNodeData; dropPosition: number; }` |

### Tree Slots

| Slot | Description | Prop |
| ------------- | :----------------: | -------------------- |
| label | Node content | node: `TreeNodeData` |
| extra | Render additional node content | Receives `TreeNodeData` directly |
| drag-icon | Custom drag icon | node: `TreeNodeData` |
| loading-icon | Custom loading icon | TreeNodeData |
| switcher-icon | Custom switcher icon | TreeNodeData |
| icon | Custom node icon | node: `TreeNodeData` |

Template slots `label`, `extra`, `switcher-icon`, and `loading-icon` receive the original `node` object; `icon` and `drag-icon` receive an object containing `node` and `node` state. State includes `loading`, `checked`, `selected`, `indeterminate`, `expanded`, and `isLeaf`.

### Five densities and icons

xs/sm/md/lg/xl consume their icon-size, font-size, line-height and title-padding-vertical. Icon sizes also determine expansion-button/indent geometry; show-line follows the matching line height.

| Variable | Default |
| --- | --- |
| `--c-tree-size-xl-icon-size` | `var(--c-size-4)` |
| `--c-tree-size-xl-font-size` | `var(--c-sys-font-size-lg)` |
| `--c-tree-size-xl-line-height` | `var(--c-size-xl)` |
| `--c-tree-size-xl-title-padding-vertical` | `12px` |

### Node fields and business values

Nodes default to `{ value, label, children }`. `value` is a tree-wide unique string/number, including `0`; `label` is display content. Map other backend fields with `fieldNames: { value: 'id', label: 'text', children: 'items' }` without changing backend data. Declarative child `name`, Vue `:key` and Table `rowKey` retain separate meanings.

Independent Tree state uses `selectedValues/defaultSelectedValues`, `checkedValues/defaultCheckedValues`, `halfCheckedValues` and `expandedValues/defaultExpandedValues`, updated through corresponding named v-models. `check` event indeterminate sets use `halfCheckedValues`. Node content uses `label`; TreeSelect forwards `tree-slot-label`. `scrollIntoView({ value })` locates business values; explicit `index` remains a zero-based virtual-list array `index`.


| Focus outline variables | Default |
| --- | --- |
| `--c-tree-focus-outline-width` | `2px` |

## Asynchronous node loading

`loadMore(node)` is an application-provided asynchronous loader. The node has `aria-busy` while pending; on failure, waiting stops and `load-error(error, node)` is emitted. Expand the node again to retry. Stale requests for replaced nodes or loaders, or after unmount, neither update nodes nor emit stale errors. The application loader is responsible for updating its data.

## Reading direction and keyboard interaction

Tree inherits container direction; indentation, connectors and expansion arrows follow it. Keyboard focus is independent of selection. Up/Down moves through available visible nodes and Home/End reaches boundaries. In LTR, Right expands/enters children and Left collapses/returns; RTL swaps the horizontal keys. Enter selects. Space checks a checkable node, otherwise selects it.

Keyboard navigation skips disabled nodes. The root identifies the focused node through `aria-activedescendant` and retains focus during virtualization. If the active node is unmounted, its reference is temporarily removed and restored after remounting. Expanding, filtering or removing nodes corrects the active node. Before/inside/after drop positions remain determined by vertical position and are not reversed in RTL. When embedded in TreeSelect, the combobox manages focus.

Checkboxes visually represent node state and do not create separate Tab stops. Press Space to toggle the active node; pointer clicks also toggle it while retaining tree focus. The node `aria-checked` indicates checked, unchecked, or mixed state.

```css
}
```

Explicit inline styles and props that write the same CSS property take precedence over stylesheet defaults. After Teleport, ordinary CSS variables inherit from the actual mount location. When using ThemeProvider, follow its local-theme and popup configuration rules. Override the component variable directly for local styling; root-level aliases are not recalculated merely because a descendant system variable changes. Internal variables are not public APIs.

<!-- component-css-variables:end -->

# Trigger

SSR limitation: a trigger or `content` slot node using both `v-for` and `v-memo` can make server rendering fail. The trigger slot can fail even while the popup is closed; the `content` slot can fail when the popup is open or `unmount-on-close=false`. Remove `v-memo` from that slot node when rendering on the server; ordinary `v-for` remains supported.

Start with the basic example, then compare related settings before moving to controlled, asynchronous or combined use cases.

## Basic examples

### Basic usage

Preview configuration: `trigger="click"`, `:popup-offset="10"`, `show-arrow`.

Example source: src/trigger/__demos__/basic.vue

```vue
<template>
  <div class="trigger-demo">
    <c-trigger trigger="click" :popup-offset="10" show-arrow>
      <c-button>点击打开</c-button>
      <template #content>
        <div class="trigger-demo__panel">Trigger 只负责浮层行为，面板外观由使用者决定。</div>
      </template>
    </c-trigger>
  </div>
</template>

<style scoped>
.trigger-demo {
  display: flex;
  justify-content: center;
  padding: calc(var(--c-sys-space-8) * 2) var(--c-sys-space-6);
}

.trigger-demo__panel {
  max-width: 260px;
  padding: var(--c-sys-space-5) var(--c-sys-space-6);
  color: var(--c-sys-color-content-primary);
  background: var(--c-sys-color-surface-overlay);
  border: 1px solid var(--c-sys-color-border-default);
  border-radius: var(--c-sys-radius-md);
}
</style>
```

## Triggers and positioning

### Popup placement

placement is the preferred side; auto-fit-position defaults to true and can change the final side. It is not a position coordinate. top-start describes anchor placement and alignment, whereas top-left is a container corner. Top/bottom start and end mirror with reading direction; left/right remain physical, and vertical start/end remain top/bottom.

## Usage notes

### Configuration

These are actual :root defaults. Prefer component variables for business customization; internal positioning variables are not public API.

With Teleport, variables must be in the actual popup scope, for example through `popup-style`. Trigger-button variables do not automatically inherit into popups.

### Reduced motion

`allowClose()` restores the internal closing gate; there is no public counterpart to disable closing, and this method cannot prevent closure.

| --- | --- |

### Trigger Methods

`open()`、`close()`、`resize()`、`allowClose()`、`getReference()`、`setReference(reference?)`、`focusReference()`、`isTopLayer(event?)`。

## Keyboard and accessibility

`trigger="focus"` supports keyboard focus. `esc-to-close` lets only the topmost popup handle Escape. Trigger does not assign `role`, `aria-describedby` or business labels; semantic wrappers such as Tooltip, Popover and Menu must supply them.

With focus triggers, one outside pointer interaction that causes both blur and click requests closing once. If controlled state rejects the request, a later independent click can request closing again; `click-outside` continues to report outside click events.

## Native event modifiers on reference elements

Native `click`, `mouseenter`, `mouseleave`, `focusin`, `focusout`, `contextmenu` listeners and `.once`, `.capture`, `.passive` modifiers bind to the actual reference element, not the popup. `.once` follows the native element's listener lifetime. Replacing a callback does not reactivate a consumed listener; replacing the reference or removing and readding a listener starts a new lifetime. Deactivation/unmount unbind listeners. Listeners only notify; returned Promises do not drive opening/loading, and errors enter Vue's event error chain.

`aria-describedby` from `reference-attrs` is merged and deduplicated with existing reference descriptions; cleanup or reference replacement restores the original attribute.

Fixed positioning uses the actual `fixed` containing block when an ancestor has a transform, filter, perspective, or containing CSS property. Axis-aligned scaling is accounted for; rotated or skewed coordinate systems are not guaranteed. For accessible same-origin iframe references, the reference and popup documents share coordinate conversion and event handling; cross-origin or unrelated browsing contexts are not supported. With `update-at-scroll`, scrolling either document or a scrollable ancestor updates the popup.

When the popup is mounted inside a closed ShadowRoot in the same document, Trigger distinguishes clicks inside the popup from outside clicks. Clicks passing through the closed-root host are classified in a later task; account for this if application behavior depends on dismissal event timing.

When a reference is slotted into a scroll container inside a closed ShadowRoot, the outer Trigger cannot access the slot or container and cannot listen to its scrolling automatically. The closed component can call the Trigger instance's `resize()` on internal scroll or slot changes. For scroll-to-close behavior, call `close()` internally using an application-specific threshold, and remove listeners on unmount.

A popup mounted inside an iframe remains clipped by that iframe's viewport. Content outside the iframe is invisible even when cross-document coordinate conversion is correct.

## CSS Variables

Tooltip/Popover define arrow appearance themselves. Override their component variables rather than Trigger arrow-background.

<!-- component-css-variables:start -->

Use these variables to customize the component. Defaults may vary by the selector condition shown. Each variable applies to the corresponding size, variant and interaction states.

<div class="token-reference-table" style="max-width: 100%; overflow-x: auto;">

| Variable | Default / condition | Affected styles |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--c-trigger-arrow-background` | `var(--c-sys-color-surface-overlay)` | `background-color` |
| `--c-trigger-arrow-radius` | `var(--c-sys-radius-sm)` | `border-radius` |
| `--c-trigger-arrow-size` | `var(--c-sys-space-4)` | `height`, `width` |
| `--c-trigger-transition-duration` | `var(--c-sys-motion-duration-fast)` | `transition` |
| `--c-trigger-transition-easing` | `var(--c-sys-motion-easing-standard)` | `transition` |

</div>

Apply overrides to the rendered component root or the actual popup ancestor. For example, add the following class to that element and replace the value as needed:

```css
.component-theme {
  --c-trigger-arrow-background: var(--c-sys-color-surface-overlay);
}
```

Explicit inline styles and props that write the same CSS property take precedence over stylesheet defaults. After Teleport, ordinary CSS variables inherit from the actual mount location. When using ThemeProvider, follow its local-theme and popup configuration rules. Override the component variable directly for local styling; root-level aliases are not recalculated merely because a descendant system variable changes. Internal variables are not public APIs.

<!-- component-css-variables:end -->

### Reduced motion

Built-in CSS transitions follow `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`. Removing transitions does not change final visibility, selected/expanded state or event semantics. Applications control custom animations inside slots.

## Lifecycle and edge cases

### Scheduler Lifecycle

Example source: src/typography/__demos__/scheduler-lifecycle.vue

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { ref } from "vue";
import { TypographyText } from "../index";

const active = ref(true);
const mounted = ref(true);
const copies = ref(0);
</script>

<template>
  <div>
    <c-button html-type="button" @click="active = !active"
      >切换 KeepAlive</c-button
    >
    <c-button html-type="button" @click="mounted = !mounted"
      >卸载／挂载</c-button
    >
    <p>复制通知：{{ copies }}。连续复制后等待 3 秒，或复制后停用再激活。</p>
    <KeepAlive v-if="mounted">
      <TypographyText
        v-if="active"
        copyable
        :ellipsis="{ rows: 1, expandable: true }"
        @copy="copies++"
      >
        Typography
        测量调度与复制反馈生命周期示例：重复复制只保留最新反馈，停用和卸载取消待处理工作。
      </TypographyText>
    </KeepAlive>
  </div>
</template>
```

## Types

The component exports the following types:

```ts
import type {
  TypographyInstance,
  TypographyParagraphInstance,
  TypographyTitleInstance,
  TypographyTextInstance,
  EllipsisConfig,
} from '@cedar-design/ui-vue'
```
### EllipsisConfig

| Prop | Description | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | :---: |
| rows | Displayed lines; values other than positive safe integers fall back to 1 | `number` | `1` |
| expandable | Whether expand/collapse is supported | `boolean` | `false` |
| ellipsisStr | Ellipsis | `string` | `'...'` |
| suffix | Suffix | `string` | `-` |
| showTooltip | Popup options for truncated content | `boolean \| { type: 'tooltip' \| 'popover'; props: Record<string, any> }` | `false` |
| css | Use CSS truncation; currently does not support expansion, custom ellipsis or suffix | `boolean` | `false` |

While editing, confirming an IME candidate does not end editing. Enter outside composition or blur ends editing.

Success feedback and `copy` are emitted only after the clipboard write succeeds. A browser fallback is attempted if the native write fails; if both fail, no success is reported. Users may retry, and stale results do not overwrite newer state.

CSS ellipsis clips only the content; copy and edit controls remain available outside the clipped region. Expansion, custom ellipsis strings and suffixes are unsupported in CSS mode.

Default copy and ellipsis measurement use the rendered slot text and follow updates within slot components without mounting another copy of them. Rich content follows browser text extraction and does not include HTML or current form-control values; provide `copy-text` when exact content is needed.

Editing preserves the original element, `id`, classes and layout styles. The input uses an explicit `aria-label` / `aria-labelledby`, or a localized edit label. After Enter, focus returns to the edit button when the key is released; blur or an application focus change is respected. Each typography component forwards updates for `v-model:editing` and `v-model:edit-text`.

The root Typography component has a `default` slot. `TypographyEmits` and `TypographyContentSlots` are exported from the package root and component entry; `TypographySlots` describes the root slot. `edit-text` controls the editor value while display content comes from the `default` slot; bind both to the same application value when appropriate. The editor is single-line.

`heading` accepts 1–6 and falls back to h1 for invalid values. `copy-delay` accepts finite values from 0 to 2147483647 ms and falls back to 3000 for invalid values. `info` and `tertiary` use their semantic text colors; `default` or an omitted status uses the normal text color.

<!-- Source: src/upload/README.en-US.md; locale: en-US; page: /en/components/upload/ -->

# Upload

Select files by clicking or dragging, with image lists, previews and controlled uploads. Examples use local files and simulated requests.

## Basic examples

### Basic usage

Choose one or more local files and remove them from the list. Without action / custom-request, files are read locally without requests.

Example source: src/upload/__demos__/en-US/read-only.vue

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { ref } from "vue";
import type { UploadFileItem } from "@cedar-design/ui-vue";

const files = ref<UploadFileItem[]>([]);
</script>

<template>
  <c-upload v-model="files" multiple />
</template>
```

### List types

Switch between text, picture and picture-card using the same file list. Add or remove files, then switch layouts without losing the selection.

Example source: src/upload/__demos__/en-US/list-type.vue

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { ref } from "vue";
import type { UploadFileItem, UploadListType } from "@cedar-design/ui-vue";

const files = ref<UploadFileItem[]>([
  {
    uid: "sample-image",
    name: "landscape.svg",
    type: "image/svg+xml",
    url:
      "data:image/svg+xml," +
      encodeURIComponent(
        '<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="240" height="160" viewBox="0 0 240 160"><rect width="240" height="160" fill="#e0e7ff"/><circle cx="180" cy="42" r="20" fill="#fbbf24"/><path d="M0 160L80 50L150 140L190 90L240 160Z" fill="#6750a4"/></svg>',
      ),
    status: "success",
    percent: 100,
  },
]);
const listType = ref<UploadListType>("picture");
</script>

<template>
  <c-space class="upload-list-type-demo" direction="column">
    <c-form>
      <c-form-item label="List type">
        <c-radio-group v-model="listType" aria-label="List type">
          <c-radio value="text">text</c-radio>
          <c-radio value="picture">picture</c-radio>
          <c-radio value="picture-card">picture-card</c-radio>
        </c-radio-group>
      </c-form-item>
    </c-form>
    <p>
      Switch the layout while keeping the same file list. Add or remove images,
      then switch again; preview remains available.
    </p>
    <c-upload
      v-model="files"
      :list-type="listType"
      accept="image/*"
      multiple
      image-fit="contain"
    />
    <p role="status">Selected images: {{ files.length }}</p>
  </c-space>
</template>
```

### Upload trigger position

Switch the entry between before and after the file list, then compare the three list types. The default places the entry after the list. Switching position keeps the selected files and their order.

Example source: src/upload/__demos__/en-US/trigger-position.vue

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { ref } from "vue";
import type {
  UploadFileItem,
  UploadListType,
  UploadTriggerPosition,
} from "@cedar-design/ui-vue";

const files = ref<UploadFileItem[]>([
  {
    uid: "sample-image",
    name: "landscape.svg",
    type: "image/svg+xml",
    url:
      "data:image/svg+xml," +
      encodeURIComponent(
        '<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="240" height="160" viewBox="0 0 240 160"><rect width="240" height="160" fill="#e0e7ff"/><circle cx="180" cy="42" r="20" fill="#fbbf24"/><path d="M0 160L80 50L150 140L190 90L240 160Z" fill="#6750a4"/></svg>',
      ),
    status: "success",
    percent: 100,
  },
]);
const listType = ref<UploadListType>("picture");
const triggerPosition = ref<UploadTriggerPosition>("after");
</script>

<template>
  <c-space class="upload-trigger-position-demo" direction="column">
    <c-form>
      <c-form-item label="Trigger position">
        <c-radio-group v-model="triggerPosition" aria-label="Trigger position">
          <c-radio value="before">Before the file list</c-radio>
          <c-radio value="after">After the file list</c-radio>
        </c-radio-group>
      </c-form-item>
      <c-form-item label="List type">
        <c-radio-group v-model="listType" aria-label="List type">
          <c-radio value="text">text</c-radio>
          <c-radio value="picture">picture</c-radio>
          <c-radio value="picture-card">picture-card</c-radio>
        </c-radio-group>
      </c-form-item>
    </c-form>
    <c-upload
      v-model="files"
      :trigger-position="triggerPosition"
      :list-type="listType"
      accept="image/*"
      multiple
    />
    <p role="status">Selected files: {{ files.length }}</p>
  </c-space>
</template>
```

## Selection and validation

### Drag and drop

Click the drop zone or drag images into it, then click a thumbnail to preview. Touch devices can use the file picker.

Example source: src/upload/__demos__/en-US/draggable-picture.vue

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { ref } from "vue";
import type { UploadFileItem } from "@cedar-design/ui-vue";

const files = ref<UploadFileItem[]>([
  {
    uid: "sample-image",
    name: "landscape.svg",
    type: "image/svg+xml",
    url:
      "data:image/svg+xml," +
      encodeURIComponent(
        '<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="240" height="160" viewBox="0 0 240 160"><rect width="240" height="160" fill="#e0e7ff"/><circle cx="180" cy="42" r="20" fill="#fbbf24"/><path d="M0 160L80 50L150 140L190 90L240 160Z" fill="#6750a4"/></svg>',
      ),
    status: "success",
    percent: 100,
  },
]);
</script>

<template>
  <c-upload
    v-model="files"
    list-type="picture"
    accept="image/*"
    multiple
    draggable
  >
    <template #trigger="{ dragOver }">
      <div class="upload-dropzone">
        <c-icon-upload class="upload-dropzone__icon" aria-hidden="true" />
        <strong>{{
          dragOver
            ? "Release to add images"
            : "Click or drag images here to add them"
        }}</strong>
        <p>
          Local files only. Click a thumbnail to preview. Do not add sensitive
          files.
        </p>
      </div>
    </template>
  </c-upload>
</template>
<style scoped>
.upload-dropzone {
  display: grid;
  justify-items: center;
  gap: 12px;
  padding: 32px 0;
  text-align: center;
  overflow-wrap: anywhere;
}
.upload-dropzone__icon {
  font-size: 40px;
  color: var(--c-sys-color-content-secondary);
}
```

### File validation

Accept images only, up to 3 files and 2 MiB per image. Rejections show a reason; remove an image to make room for another.

Example source: src/upload/__demos__/en-US/picture-limits.vue

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { ref } from "vue";
import type { UploadFileItem, UploadRejectedFile } from "@cedar-design/ui-vue";

const files = ref<UploadFileItem[]>([]);
const feedback = ref("");
const reasons: Record<string, string> = {
  accept: "Images only",
  "max-files": "Up to 3 images",
  "max-file-size": "Up to 2 MiB per image",
};
function handleRejected(items: UploadRejectedFile[]) {
  feedback.value = items
    .map((item) => `${item.file.name}: ${reasons[item.reason] || item.reason}`)
    .join("; ");
}
</script>

<template>
  <c-space direction="column">
    <p>
      Choose up to 3 images, each no larger than 2 MiB. Remove an image to add
      another.
    </p>
    <c-upload
      v-model="files"
      list-type="picture"
      accept="image/*"
      multiple
      :max-files="3"
      :max-file-size="2 * 1024 * 1024"
      @rejected="handleRejected"
    />
    <p role="status">{{ feedback }}</p>
  </c-space>
</template>
```

## Upload workflow

### Manual upload, progress and retry

Choose files or add a sample, then start uploading. Cancel active uploads and retry a simulated first failure. A local timer simulates requests without sending files.

Example source: src/upload/__demos__/en-US/manual-upload.vue

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { computed, onBeforeUnmount, onDeactivated, ref } from "vue";
import type {
  UploadCustomRequest,
  UploadFileItem,
  UploadInstance,
  UploadProgressEvent,
} from "@cedar-design/ui-vue";

const files = ref<UploadFileItem[]>([]);
const uploader = ref<UploadInstance>();
const failOnce = ref(false);
const timers = new Set<ReturnType<typeof setInterval>>();
const attempts = new Map<string, number>();
const pending = computed(() =>
  files.value.some((file) =>
    ["ready", "error", "canceled"].includes(file.status),
  ),
);
let sequence = 0;
function addSample() {
  const file = new File(
    ["Local upload example."],
    `example-${++sequence}.txt`,
    { type: "text/plain" },
  );
  files.value = [
    ...files.value,
    {
      uid: `sample-${sequence}`,
      name: file.name,
      size: file.size,
      type: file.type,
      file,
      status: "ready",
      percent: 0,
    },
  ];
}
const request: UploadCustomRequest = ({
  file,
  onProgress,
  onSuccess,
  onError,
}) => {
  const attempt = (attempts.get(file.uid) ?? 0) + 1;
  attempts.set(file.uid, attempt);
  const reject = failOnce.value && attempt === 1;
  let percent = 0;
  const stop = () => {
    clearInterval(timer);
    timers.delete(timer);
  };
  const timer = setInterval(() => {
    percent += 10;
    onProgress({ percent } as UploadProgressEvent);
    if (percent >= 100) {
      stop();
      if (reject) {
        onError(new Error("Simulated upload failure; retry to continue"));
      } else {
        onSuccess({ ok: true });
      }
    }
  }, 150);
  timers.add(timer);
  return { abort: stop };
};
function cleanup() {
  uploader.value?.abort();
  timers.forEach((timer) => clearInterval(timer));
  timers.clear();
}
onBeforeUnmount(cleanup);
onDeactivated(cleanup);
</script>

<template>
  <c-space direction="column">
    <c-checkbox v-model="failOnce">Fail the first attempt</c-checkbox>
    <c-upload
      ref="uploader"
      v-model="files"
      multiple
      :auto-upload="false"
      :custom-request="request"
    />
    <c-space wrap>
      <c-button @click="addSample">Add a sample</c-button>
      <c-button :disabled="!pending" @click="uploader?.submit()"
        >Start upload</c-button
      >
    </c-space>
    <p role="status">
      Completed:
      {{ files.filter((file) => file.status === "success").length }} /
      {{ files.length }}
    </p>
  </c-space>
</template>
```

### Confirm before removing

Removing a file opens a confirmation Dialog. Cancel keeps the file; confirm removes it.

Example source: src/upload/__demos__/en-US/remove-confirm.vue

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { onBeforeUnmount, ref } from "vue";
import type { UploadFileItem } from "@cedar-design/ui-vue";

const files = ref<UploadFileItem[]>([
  {
    uid: "sample-image",
    name: "landscape.svg",
    type: "image/svg+xml",
    url:
      "data:image/svg+xml," +
      encodeURIComponent(
        '<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="240" height="160" viewBox="0 0 240 160"><rect width="240" height="160" fill="#e0e7ff"/><circle cx="180" cy="42" r="20" fill="#fbbf24"/><path d="M0 160L80 50L150 140L190 90L240 160Z" fill="#6750a4"/></svg>',
      ),
    status: "success",
    percent: 100,
  },
]);
const open = ref(false);
const name = ref("");
let resolveRemoval: ((allow: boolean) => void) | undefined;
function beforeRemove(file: UploadFileItem) {
  name.value = file.name || "";
  open.value = true;
  return new Promise<boolean>((resolve) => {
    resolveRemoval = resolve;
  });
}
function finish(allow: boolean) {
  const resolve = resolveRemoval;
  resolveRemoval = undefined;
  open.value = false;
  resolve?.(allow);
}
onBeforeUnmount(() => finish(false));
</script>

<template>
  <c-upload
    v-model="files"
    list-type="picture"
    accept="image/*"
    multiple
    :before-remove="beforeRemove"
  />
  <c-dialog
    v-model:open="open"
    title="Confirm removal"
    @confirm="finish(true)"
    @cancel="finish(false)"
    @closed="finish(false)"
  >
    <p>Remove file {{ name }}?</p>
  </c-dialog>
</template>
```

### Externally managed upload state

Manage progress and results through the read event. Add a sample and complete it to see the controlled list update; no built-in request is used.

Example source: src/upload/__demos__/en-US/external-state.vue

```vue
<script setup>
import { computed, ref } from "vue";

const files = ref([]);
const hasUploading = computed(() =>
  files.value.some((file) => file.status === "uploading"),
);
const hasRetryable = computed(() =>
  files.value.some((file) => ["error", "canceled"].includes(file.status)),
);
let sequence = 0;

function read(file) {
  file.status = "uploading";
  file.percent = 40;
}

function addExample() {
  const file = new File(
    ["Local external upload demo."],
    `external-${++sequence}.txt`,
    { type: "text/plain" },
  );
  const item = {
    uid: `external-${sequence}`,
    name: file.name,
    size: file.size,
    type: file.type,
    file,
    status: "ready",
    percent: 0,
  };
  read(item);
  files.value = [...files.value, item];
}

function complete() {
  files.value = files.value.map((file) =>
    file.status === "uploading"
      ? { ...file, status: "success", percent: 100 }
      : file,
  );
}

function retry() {
  files.value = files.value.map((file) =>
    ["error", "canceled"].includes(file.status)
      ? { ...file, status: "uploading", percent: 40 }
      : file,
  );
}
</script>

<template>
  <div>
    <p>
      The application manages progress and results. Add a local sample without
      opening the picker or sending requests.
    </p>
    <c-space wrap>
      <c-button @click="addExample">Add an external upload</c-button>
      <c-button :disabled="!hasUploading" @click="complete"
        >Complete externally</c-button
      >
      <c-button :disabled="!hasRetryable" @click="retry"
        >Retry externally</c-button
      >
    </c-space>
    <c-upload
      v-model="files"
      edit-mode="direct"
      :show-retry-button="false"
      @read="read"
    />
    <p>
      File states:{{
        files
          .map((file) => `${file.name}: ${file.status} (${file.percent}%)`)
          .join("；") || "Empty"
      }}
    </p>
  </div>
</template>
```

### Paste clipboard images

Paste images into the input area and use useUploader.addFiles to reuse reading and validation. Ordinary text keeps its native input behavior.

Example source: src/upload/__demos__/en-US/clipboard.vue

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { ref } from "vue";
import { useUploader, type UploadFileItem } from "@cedar-design/ui-vue";
const files = ref<UploadFileItem[]>([]);
const message = ref("");
const rejectionMessages: Record<string, string> = {
  "max-files": "Up to 3 images",
  "max-file-size": "Each image must be at most 1 MiB",
  accept: "Images only",
};
const uploader = useUploader({
  modelValue: () => files.value,
  onUpdateModelValue: (value) => {
    files.value = value;
  },
  accept: () => "image/*",
  maxFiles: () => 3,
  maxFileSize: () => 1024 * 1024,
  autoUpload: () => false,
  onRejected: (rejected) => {
    message.value = rejected
      .map(
        (item) =>
          rejectionMessages[item.reason] ??
          "Unable to read the file; choose again",
      )
      .join(", ");
  },
});
function paste(event: ClipboardEvent) {
  const incoming = Array.from(event.clipboardData?.files ?? []);
  if (!incoming.length) return;
  event.preventDefault();
  message.value = "";
  uploader.addFiles(incoming);
}
function addExample() {
  message.value = "";
  uploader.addFiles([
    new File(
      ['<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="8" height="8"/>'],
      "local-example.svg",
      { type: "image/svg+xml" },
    ),
  ]);
}
function reset() {
  uploader.reset();
  message.value = "";
}
</script>
<template>
  <c-space direction="column">
    <p>
      Paste clipboard images into the field. Up to 3 images, each at most 1 MiB.
      Files stay local; ordinary text input is unchanged.
    </p>
    <c-textarea placeholder="Paste images or text here" @paste="paste" />
    <c-space wrap>
      <c-button @click="addExample">Add a sample image</c-button>
      <c-button @click="reset">Clear files</c-button>
    </c-space>
    <p role="status">Accepted {{ files.length }} files.{{ message }}</p>
    <ul>
      <li v-for="file in files" :key="file.uid">{{ file.name }}</li>
    </ul>
  </c-space>
</template>
```

## Usage notes

### File selection and device support

For photos, use `accept="image/*"`. Leave `capture` unset or set `:capture="false"` to keep the system file/photo picker. Use `capture` only for direct camera capture; available choices depend on the browser and device.

### Editing and confirmation

This component supports `edit-mode` with field > FormItem > Form precedence. When unset, it defaults to `direct` and preserves `direct` editing. Supported values: `direct / click / dblclick`. Non-direct modes open the editor through the field value trigger and keep one draft; v-model updates only after confirmation. Cancel, reset or enabling readPretty discards the draft.

Cedar uses edit-mode="click" / "dblclick" to open an editor popup near the field. Enter/F2 also opens it; cancel/Escape discards the draft, and confirmation commits it. readPretty is an independent reading setting, separate from readonly and disabled.

`before-commit(value, { previousValue, signal })` can reject an overlay save. FormItem validates the candidate first and keeps the editor open on failure. `open / default-open / update:open` control the editor. Use `#read="{ value, text }"` to customize display. See the full field comparison in Form.

Attachment confirmation commits file-list relationships; it cannot undo completed remote uploads or permanent deletion. To defer network side effects, set `auto-upload="false"` and upload after the final business submission.

`read-pretty` is an independent boolean alongside `readonly` and `disabled`. It inherits from field to FormItem to Form; explicit `false` overrides the parent. The default is `false`. Reading mode renders no editor.

### Configuration

Use `trigger-position="before"` or `trigger-position="after"` to place the built-in entry before or after the file list; the default is after. This also applies to the `trigger` slot and drag-and-drop entry. Values describe DOM order and are not rewritten in RTL. For fully external buttons, set `:show-upload-button="false"` and call the instance method `chooseFile()`.

Public variable suffixes match across platforms; all defaults appear below with c/mp prefixes respectively.

## API

### Empty values and reading placeholders

`empty-values` recognizes empty data; `empty-value` keeps existing clear output. `empty-text` defaults to `'-'` under `read-pretty`, with Field > FormItem > Form precedence and custom read slots first. With explicit `empty-values`, built-in required uses the policy; custom validators receive original data. See the [shared guide](llms/en-US/guide/empty-values.md).

| Prop | Type | Default and scope |
| ------------ | ------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------- |
| empty-values | readonly unknown[] | Field > FormItem > Form > component-family default; replaces the whole list |
| empty-text | string | Field > FormItem > Form > '-'; explicit '' is valid |

These props belong to field presentation; pure panels do not gain reading mode. Form and FormItem provide inherited settings. The existing empty-value type and clear fallback remain component-specific.

### Upload Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| model-value | `UploadFileItem[] \| null` | `undefined` | Controlled file list; use with v-model |
| default-value | `UploadFileItem[]` | `[]` | Initial uncontrolled file list |
| accept | `string` | `undefined` | Accepted file types, e.g. image/* |
| capture | `boolean \| 'user' \| 'environment'` | `false` | False or omitted preserves photo selection; true requests capture, user / environment requests the front / rear camera; device and browser support varies |
| multiple | `boolean` | `false` | Allow multiple files |
| reupload | `boolean` | `false` | Allow replacing a selected file |
| directory | `boolean` | `false` | Select a directory; multiple provides an alternative on unsupported devices |
| draggable | `boolean` | `false` | Enable drag and drop |
| disabled | `boolean` | `undefined` | Disable interaction; inherits Form, explicit false overrides |
| readonly | `boolean` | `undefined` | Read-only; inherits Form, explicit false overrides |
| read-pretty | `boolean` | `undefined` | Pure reading mode: hides the editor and shows the field value. Inherits from FormItem / Form; explicit false overrides inheritance. Resolves to false when unset. |
| action | `string` | `undefined` | Upload request URL |
| method | `string` | `'post'` | Upload request method |
| headers | `UploadHeaders` | `undefined` | Request headers object or async function; preparation remains cancelable |
| data | `UploadData` | `undefined` | Additional request data object or async function; preparation remains cancelable |
| name | `string \| ((file: UploadFileItem) => string)` | `'file'` | Form field name for the uploaded file |
| with-credentials | `boolean` | `false` | Include credentials in cross-origin requests |
| custom-request | `UploadCustomRequest` | `undefined` | Custom transport; may return an object with abort |
| auto-upload | `boolean` | `true` | Upload automatically after selection; requires action or custom-request |
| max-files | `number` | `undefined` | Maximum file count; applies when greater than 0 |
| max-file-size | `number` | `undefined` | Maximum size per file in bytes |
| max-total-size | `number` | `undefined` | Maximum total file size in bytes |
| resolve-type | `'file' \| 'data-url' \| 'object-url'` | `'object-url'` | File reading mode; object-url generates url for files and thumbnailUrl for images |
| create-thumbnail-url | `UploadCreateThumbnailUrl` | `undefined` | Custom thumbnail URL; caller owns the URL and its cleanup |
| before-add | `(files: File[]) => File[] \| Promise<File[]>` | `undefined` | Filter or replace a batch of incoming files |
| before-read | `UploadBeforeRead` | `undefined` | Validate before reading; false / rejection rejects, replacements are revalidated |
| before-upload | `UploadBeforeUpload` | `undefined` | Validate before upload; false keeps ready, throw / rejection reports error, replacements are revalidated |
| before-remove | `UploadBeforeRemove` | `undefined` | Validate before removal; false / rejection prevents removal |
| is-success-response | `UploadIsSuccessResponse` | `undefined` | Custom success predicate; defaults to HTTP 2xx |
| request-choose | `UploadRequestChoose` | `undefined` | Own the selection entry; exceptions do not automatically open a file chooser |
| list-type | `'text' \| 'picture' \| 'picture-card'` | `'text'` | File list appearance; supported on both platforms |
| trigger-position | `'before' \| 'after'` | `'after'` | Place the upload entry before or after the file list; applies to every list-type, custom trigger slots and drag-and-drop entries. Values describe DOM order and are not rewritten in RTL. |
| image-fit | `'fill' \| 'contain' \| 'cover' \| 'none' \| 'scale-down'` | `'cover'` | Thumbnail fit; item.fit overrides |
| preview | `boolean` | `true` | Enable built-in image / video preview |
| show-file-list | `boolean` | `true` | Show the file list |
| show-upload-button | `boolean` | `true` | Show the file selection button |
| show-remove-button | `boolean` | `true` | Show the remove button |
| show-retry-button | `boolean` | `true` | Show the retry button |
| show-cancel-button | `boolean` | `true` | Show the cancel button |
| show-preview-button | `boolean` | `true` | Show the preview button |
| show-download-button | `boolean` | `false` | Show the download button; disabled prevents interaction |
| elevation | `boolean \| number` | `false` | Elevation of the upload trigger |
| ripple | `boolean` | `true` | Enable the upload trigger ripple |

UploadFileItem requires uid, status and percent. name/size/type/file/url/thumbnailUrl/fit/response/error are optional. status is ready/reading/uploading/success/error/canceled/removed.

### Upload Events

- update:model-value(files), change(files, changedFile?): queue proposal order; Form receives one change notification per change, including progress/state updates.
- read(item): reading completed; business code may take over uploading. It does not indicate server success.
- rejected(UploadRejectedFile[]): reason is accept/before-add/before-read/read-error/max-file-size/max-total-size/max-files.
- exceed(nativeFiles, acceptedList): file-count limit exceeded.
- progress(item,event?), success(item), error(item): active-request notifications. Stale/canceled callbacks have no effect.
- remove(item): removal proposal after removal hooks accept it.
- preview(item, UploadPreviewEvent): event.preventDefault() cancels built-in image/video preview. Programmatic previews are cancelable too; originalEvent is optional.

### Upload Slots

- trigger({chooseFile,dragOver,disabled,describedBy}): custom selection entry.

During SSR, interactive elements inside the trigger slot are not detected until hydration. If the slot contains a button, its outer wrapper is initially also a focusable button. To avoid nested interactive semantics in the initial HTML, use decorative slot content and let the wrapper open the file picker. After hydration, the component detects interactive content and adjusts the wrapper role.

Display-only content uses the wrapper button role and Enter/Space entry. Interactive custom content owns its keyboard behavior; the wrapper adds no button role or Tab stop. Bind the slot disabled value to your button. To associate the button itself with form errors and Upload's aria-describedby, bind the slot's describedBy to the button's aria-describedby; it updates as errors appear and clear. Calling chooseFile directly needs no .stop: bubbling does not choose again or also invoke requestChoose. Custom buttons relying on bubbling can still use requestChoose.

```vue
<c-upload aria-describedby="upload-hint">
  <template #trigger="{ chooseFile, disabled, describedBy }">
    <button type="button" :disabled="disabled" :aria-describedby="describedBy" @click="chooseFile">Choose files</button>
  </template>
</c-upload>
<p id="upload-hint">Choose files</p>
```

Use requestChoose for asynchronous decisions, or synchronously call event.preventDefault() before awaiting and invoking chooseFile yourself. Click listener Promises are not collected. Each requestChoose callback selects at most once and expires on unmount or KeepAlive deactivation, even after reopening.
- item({file,index,remove,retry,abort,replace}): customize a whole file item.
- remove-button({file,index,remove,retry,abort,replace}): customize removal actions.
- read({value,text}): field reading content; value is the nullable file model and text is formatted content. This differs from the file-read completion event.

### Upload Methods

Provides chooseFile(), replace(file,replacement?), submit(file?), abort(file?), retry(file), remove(file), reset(), clearSuccess(), clearError(), getFiles(status?), preview(file) and closePreview(). useUploader(options) provides headless upload logic, addFiles(files), and input/drag handlers.

chooseFile, replace, submit, retry and remove return `Promise<void>` for their preparation stages. submit/retry await preparation hooks and request-factory creation, without guaranteeing network completion; success/error events report results. chooseFile completion does not mean the user has selected a file, and remove completion does not mean a controlled parent accepted its proposal. Item/remove-button remove, retry and replace, and trigger chooseFile retain the same Promise types.

All public methods are callable before the editor first mounts. When it is unmounted, closed or deactivated, getFiles(status?) returns shallow snapshots of the accepted model filtered by status; asynchronous mutations settle as no-ops and synchronous mutations are no-ops. To perform an operation, first open and mount the editor through field interaction or controlled open, or use editMode="direct". Stored method references forward to the current instance after closing/reopening; cancelling an editor preserves the accepted model.

### Controlled state and lifecycle

If a controlled parent rejects an addition, only read/list proposals emit; automatic upload waits until that uid is accepted, then runs once. Same-tick proposals merge transactionally; across ticks, the actual parent list is authoritative. Rejected entries do not count toward total size. Parents own consistency of late list replacements. Explicit removal of rejected items, reset or unmount releases generated URLs; external URLs are never revoked. Built-in preview retains its own URL ownership until closing and does not close another component's later preview.

Cancellation covers before-upload, asynchronous headers/data/name and asynchronous custom-request handles. Retrying or replacing a File under the same uid invalidates old callbacks. before-read/before-upload replacements recheck limits. max-total-size counts accepted entries and the current valid prepared batch/request only. Disabled/readonly block selection, removal, submission and other mutations; readonly allows preview/download. KeepAlive deactivation cancels preparation/requests; reactivation allows new operations.

## Types

UploadProps、UploadEmits、UploadSlots、UploadExpose、UploadPublicMethods、UploadFileItem、UploadStatus、UploadListType、UploadTriggerPosition、UploadResolveType、UploadImageFit、UploadCapture、UploadRejectedFile、UploadRejectedReason、UploadRequestOptions、UploadRequest、UploadCustomRequest、UploadProgressEvent、UploadData、UploadHeaders、UploadBeforeRead、UploadBeforeUpload、UploadBeforeRemove、UploadCreateThumbnailUrl、UploadIsSuccessResponse、UploadRequestChoose、UploadPreviewEvent、UseUploaderOptions、UploadInstance。

## Cover attachments and video duration

`reupload` (default false) enables a per-item replacement action, including when maxFiles has been reached. `replace(file, replacement?: File): Promise<void>` opens a single-file chooser or validates the supplied File. It respects readonly/disabled and the chooser hook. Validation and beforeRemove run before an atomic in-place replacement proposal with a new UID; count and total size exclude the old item. Cancellation, rejection, guard veto and stale targets preserve the old item. A controlled parent decides acceptance. The `replace(next, previous)` event is a model proposal, not remote success or removal; remove is not emitted. Once accepted, obsolete transport callbacks are ignored; new upload failures can be retried. The item slot also exposes replace().

`UploadFileItem.duration?: number` uses seconds, displayed as mm:ss / h:mm:ss; unknown/invalid durations are hidden. Metadata reads local File objects only, waits at most 5 seconds and cleans temporary resources. Business code supplies remote durations. Video previews use popupContainer.

Duration-badge variables: `--c-upload-duration-background: var(--c-sys-color-surface-tooltip)`, `--c-upload-duration-color: var(--c-sys-color-content-on-dark)`, `--c-upload-duration-radius: var(--c-sys-radius-sm)`, `--c-upload-duration-padding: var(--c-sys-space-1) var(--c-sys-space-2)`, `--c-upload-duration-font-size: var(--c-sys-font-size-sm)`.

### Async operation feedback

Awaited before-* hooks show loading feedback and aria-busy. Rejection/failure restores interaction, and repeated input does not restart the same operation. Ordinary event return Promises do not participate. Files remain concurrent; feedback aggregates all current guard tasks without treating change/progress notifications as tasks.

`useUploader()` exposes readonly `guardPending`, aggregating currently awaited before hooks. It does not represent upload progress.

Calling `reset()` while disabled or readonly is a no-op and does not clear the pending state of an unfinished hook. A late `beforeAdd` error from work cancelled by reset, deactivation, or unmount does not emit a rejection; an error settling while disabled or readonly also does not emit one. If a `rejected` or `exceed` callback synchronously resets the uploader, prepared files from that batch are not committed. If a list update, change, or read callback resets synchronously, superseded notifications from that operation are stopped.

In field confirmation mode, confirmation waits for file preparation and before hooks; closing the editor still cancels the current edit.

### Preparation vetoes and exceptions

`beforeUpload` returning `false` or resolving to `false` is a business veto: no transport starts, the item stays `ready`, and neither `error` nor `rejected` is emitted. Throwing or rejecting is a preparation failure: no transport starts, the item becomes `error`, and the existing `error(item)` event reports the original cause as `item.error` exactly once. This event covers preparation and transport failures; it does not imply an HTTP request was sent. Both outcomes permit a later submission with a valid hook result. Notification return Promises do not hold the preparation task open. Obsolete or canceled attempts cannot report a new `error`.

## Reading direction

Inherits the nearest `dir="ltr|rtl"`, including runtime changes and local overrides. Verification codes are LTR content: rendering, pasting and focus movement use the original string order, while outer align start/end follows reading direction. RTL does not reverse code characters. Numeric and text codes share this order contract.

## Usage notes

### Editing and confirmation

This component supports `edit-mode` with field > FormItem > Form precedence. When unset, it defaults to `direct` and preserves `direct` editing. Supported values: `direct / click / dblclick`. Non-direct modes open the editor through the field value trigger and keep one draft; v-model updates only after confirmation. Cancel, reset or enabling readPretty discards the draft.

Cedar uses edit-mode="click" / "dblclick" to open an editor popup near the field. Enter/F2 also opens it; cancel/Escape discards the draft, and confirmation commits it. readPretty is an independent reading setting, separate from readonly and disabled.

`before-commit(payload, done, context)` can guard saving the editor. FormItem validates the candidate first; invalid candidates keep the editor open. `open / default-open / update:open` control the editor. `#read="{ value, text }"` customizes read content. See the unified field presentation examples in Form.

`read-pretty` is an independent boolean alongside `readonly` and `disabled`. It inherits from field to FormItem to Form; explicit `false` overrides the parent. The default is `false`. Reading mode renders no editor.
### Configuration

initial means no public override. CSS reads size fallbacks at the component element. Override through component style or theme.

## API

### Empty values and reading placeholders

`empty-values` recognizes empty data; `empty-value` keeps existing clear output. `empty-text` defaults to `'-'` under `read-pretty`, with Field > FormItem > Form precedence and custom read slots first. With explicit `empty-values`, built-in required uses the policy; custom validators receive original data. See the [shared guide](llms/en-US/guide/empty-values.md).

| Prop | Type | Default and scope |
| ------------ | ------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------- |
| empty-values | readonly unknown[] | Field > FormItem > Form > component-family default; replaces the whole list |
| empty-text | string | Field > FormItem > Form > '-'; explicit '' is valid |

These props belong to field presentation; pure panels do not gain reading mode. Form and FormItem provide inherited settings. The existing empty-value type and clear fallback remain component-specific.

Explicit null is a controlled empty code and never falls back to default-value, which applies only when model-value is absent. reset() still proposes an empty string. Presentation clearing can submit null through empty-value=null; finish never receives null. An omitted model-value remains uncontrolled.

In deferred mode input / paste describe editing, while finish describes the finally accepted complete value. Canceling, rejection, readonly, disabled, external replacement or unmount retires unaccepted completion notifications. Ordinary finish listener Promises do not hold confirmation. A synchronous undefined before-commit return waits for done. Invalid type / align values diagnose and fall back to digit / center; gutter=0 and 0px remain valid.

### VerificationCode Props

| Prop | Description | Type | Default |
| --------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------- | ---------------- |
| `model-value` | Controlled complete code | `string \| null` | `undefined` |
| `default-value` | Uncontrolled initial value | `string` | `''` |
| `length` | Positive integer cell count, measured in Unicode code points | `number` | `6` |
| `type` | Character set | `digit / text / alphanumeric` | `digit` |
| `size` | Five wrapper sizes | `xs / sm / md / lg / xl` | Inherited / md |
| `variant` | Input variant | `filled / outline / standard` | Inherited / outline |
| `disabled` | Disabled state; explicit values override inherited Form / Group state | `boolean` | `undefined` |
| `readonly` | Read-only state; explicit values override inherited Form / Group state | `boolean` | `undefined` |
| `error` | Error state; explicit values override inherited Form / Group state | `boolean` | `undefined` |
| `masked` | Visual character masking only, not encryption | `boolean` | `false` |
| `mask-symbol` | Use the first Unicode code point | `string` | `•` |
| `autofocus` | Focus the first empty cell after mounting | `boolean` | `false` |
| `gutter` | Cell gap; numbers are px | `number / string` | Component token |
| `align` | Horizontal alignment | `start / center / end` | `center` |
| `allow-paste` | Allow pasting; false prevents native paste | `boolean` | `true` |
| `paste-transform` | Paste preprocessing, before type/formatter | `(text: string) => string` | `undefined` |
| `formatter` | Per-character formatting: false rejects; true/undefined retains. A returned string contributes its first valid code point | `(character, index, value) => string / boolean` | `undefined` |
| `separator` | Separator after each nonfinal cell | `(index, character) => VNodeChild` | `undefined` |
| `aria-label` | Group name and numbered cell labels | `string` | `undefined` |

| `focus-color` | Custom per-instance focused color; prefer tokens for static themes | `string` | `undefined` |

| `clearable` | Deferred editor clearing; does not change individual input cells | `boolean` | `false` |
| `empty-values` | Empty-value recognition; field takes precedence over FormItem and Form | `readonly unknown[]` | `-` |
| `empty-text` | Read empty text; an explicit empty string is valid | `string` | `'-'` |
| `edit-mode` | Editing mode, inherited from FormItem and Form | `'direct' \| 'click' \| 'dblclick'` | `'direct'` |
| `read-pretty` | Independent read presentation; explicit false overrides the parent | `boolean` | `false` |
| `before-commit` | Guard before saving a deferred edit; return a boolean or Promise, or complete via done | `(payload: { value: unknown; previousValue: unknown }, done: (allow?: boolean) => void, context: { signal: AbortSignal; event?: Event }) => void \| boolean \| Promise<void \| boolean>` | `-` |
| `open` | Controlled editor visibility, separate from native input focus | `boolean` | `-` |
| `default-open` | Initial visibility of an uncontrolled editor | `boolean` | `false` |
| `popup-container` | Editor mount container | `string \| HTMLElement \| false` | `-` |

### VerificationCode Events

| Event | Arguments | Semantics |
| ------------------ | ----------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| input | character, index, event | Starting character and zero-based index of each valid native input proposal |
| update:modelValue | value: string \| null | Complete-code proposal |
| change | value: string \| null | Complete-code proposal for each valid edit, not necessarily accepted by a controlled parent |
| finish | value: string | Direct mode notifies after the parent accepts the complete code in the current render; deferred mode waits for confirmation guards and parent acceptance, never draft completion |
| update:open | open: boolean | Controlled editor visibility update |
| open-change | open: boolean | Actual editor visibility change |
| paste | text, event | Pasted text after paste-transform/type processing |
| focus / blur | FocusEvent | Focus enters/leaves the whole component; moving between cells does not duplicate notifications |
| click | MouseEvent | Non-disabled click |

Valid input order: input → update:modelValue → change. finish waits until the parent accepts the complete value in that render. Rejected controlled values restore native inputs; later asynchronous parent assignments do not add finish. reset() proposes empty and emits update:modelValue/change without simulating native input. Disabled, readonly or composing state prevents reset from changing values.

Paste overwrites from the current cell; root-level paste starts at cell 1. Input beyond the first empty cell moves to that first empty cell. A whole-code native input distributes across subsequent cells. SMS suggestions depend on the platform and browser: Cedar hints one-time-code on the first cell, while Maple retains autocomplete=off for all cells. Typing one character in a filled cell replaces that cell even when the caret follows its old character. Composition prefers the current compositionend text, including multiple code points, and falls back to the native value only when event data is missing. Processing is type filtering, formatter, then length clipping; rejected characters consume no cell. Text counts Unicode code points rather than grapheme clusters. External values affect display without an automatic formatted model update.

### VerificationCode Slots

| Slot | Prop | Description |
| --------- | -------------------- | ----------------------------------------- |
| separator | { index, character } | Overrides separator; not rendered after the last cell |
| read | { value: string \| null, text: string } | Custom read content, taking precedence over empty-text |

### VerificationCode Methods

- focus(index?): zero-based index; defaults to the first empty cell or the last cell when full. Direct readonly fields can receive focus. Deferred mode opens an editable panel first; disabled, readonly, or reading fields do not open.
- blur(): blur the current editor without reopening the panel.
- reset(): in direct mode, propose an empty value while respecting controlled ownership, disabled/readonly state, and composition. In deferred mode, open an empty draft; model and change notifications wait for final confirmation and before-commit approval. Cancellation preserves the original value.

Public methods remain callable from initial component mount. Stored methods resolve the current editor on every call and never use an old input after closure, reopening, or mode changes. Native input references are undefined while no editor is mounted.

### Keyboard and Form

Left/Right move between cells. Backspace removes the current character, or the previous one when empty. Delete removes the current character; following characters shift forward. IME composition does not trim, delete or move focus. Each native input has an SSR-stable id. Cell 1 uses autocomplete=one-time-code, others off. Provide aria-label.

A supplied `aria-invalid` is forwarded to each input. Component or form errors take precedence and mark inputs invalid; when errors clear, the supplied value is restored. The group retains explicit caller attributes and does not add an error state automatically.

InputGroup/Form state is inherited, with explicit disabled/readonly/error/size taking precedence. Internal cell Inputs do not duplicate Form notifications; the complete control notifies input/change once per edit. Both platforms implement three variants/five sizes using local FieldDecorator tokens.

## Types

# Watermark

Start with the basic example, then compare related settings before moving to controlled, asynchronous or combined use cases.

## Basic examples

### Basic usage

Preview configuration: `:content="content"`, `:font="{ color: dark ? 'rgba(255,255,255,0.4)' : 'rgba(0,0,0,0.25)' }"`.

Example source: src/watermark/__demos__/basic.vue

```vue
<script setup>
import { useDemoLocale as useInlineDemoLocale } from "../../__demos__/locale";
const inlineCopy = useInlineDemoLocale("watermarkBasicInline");

import { ref } from "vue";
const dark = ref(false);
const shown = ref(true);
const content = ref("LOCAL DEMO 200");
const clicks = ref(0);
</script>

<template>
  <section class="watermark-contrast-demo">
    <c-checkbox v-model="dark"> {{ inlineCopy.darkSurface }}</c-checkbox>
    <c-checkbox v-model="shown"> {{ inlineCopy.showWatermark }}</c-checkbox>
    <label>{{ inlineCopy.watermarkText }}<c-input v-model="content" /></label>
    <c-watermark
      v-if="shown"
      :content="content"
      :font="{ color: dark ? 'rgba(255,255,255,0.4)' : 'rgba(0,0,0,0.25)' }"
      :style="{
        background: dark ? '#1f2937' : '#ffffff',
        color: dark ? '#ffffff' : '#111827',
      }"
    >
      <div class="watermark-contrast-surface">
        <p>{{ inlineCopy.localSyntheticContent }}</p>
        <c-button html-type="button" @click="clicks++">{{
          inlineCopy.clickThrough
        }}</c-button>
      </div>
    </c-watermark>
    <p role="status">
      Visible: {{ shown }} · Dark: {{ dark }} · Clicks: {{ clicks }}
    </p>
  </section>
</template>
<style scoped>
.watermark-contrast-surface {
  min-height: 240px;
  display: grid;
  place-content: center;
  gap: 12px;
}
</style>
```

### Image

- `width`: Sets the configured width.
- `height`: Constrains the component height.

Example source: src/watermark/__demos__/image.vue

```vue
<script setup>
import { useDemoLocale as useInlineDemoLocale } from "../../__demos__/locale";
const inlineCopy = useInlineDemoLocale("watermarkImageInline");

import { computed, ref } from "vue";
const failed = ref(false);
const errors = ref([]);
const localImage =
  "data:image/svg+xml," +
  encodeURIComponent(
    '<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="160" height="48"><rect width="160" height="48" rx="8" fill="#0284c7"/><circle cx="80" cy="24" r="14" fill="white"/></svg>',
  );
const image = computed(() =>
  failed.value ? "data:image/png;base64,invalid-local-image" : localImage,
);
</script>
<template>
  <section class="watermark-image-failure-demo">
    <c-checkbox v-model="failed"> {{ inlineCopy.failLocalImage }}</c-checkbox>
    <c-button html-type="button" :disabled="!failed" @click="failed = false">{{
      inlineCopy.restoreImage
    }}</c-button>
    <c-watermark
      content="FALLBACK 201"
      :image="image"
      :width="160"
      :height="48"
      :font="{ color: '#be123c' }"
      style="background: white"
      @error="errors.push($event.source)"
    >
      <div style="height: 240px" />
    </c-watermark>
    <p role="status">
      Mode: {{ failed ? "failure" : "image" }} · Errors:
      {{ errors.join(",") || "-" }}
    </p>
  </section>
</template>
```

## Usage notes

### Sizing and redraw

- Supply two finite numbers for `gap` and `offset`; non-negative gaps are recommended. A negative gap is currently clamped to zero only for tile dimensions, while drawing and background offsets use the original value, so do not rely on negative gaps for overlap. Use finite positive values for `width`, `height`, `font.fontSize`, and `font.lineHeight`; rendered width and height are at least 1. `rotate` and `zIndex` should be finite. Invalid inputs are not guaranteed to be corrected; valid `alpha` values are finite and between 0 and 1.
- The default `lineHeight` is `Math.round(fontSize * 1.4)`. Canvas parses the text color: `font.color` takes precedence over the computed color token. Supply a color supported by Canvas; CSS variable expressions are not guaranteed to resolve directly. Asynchronously loaded fonts do not trigger redraw automatically; call `redraw()` after they are ready.
- Image load failures emit `error` and fall back to text when available; Canvas failures also emit `error`. `redraw()` returns a Promise and normally handles rendering failures internally. Older asynchronous results cannot overwrite the current layer or report errors after props change or unmount, but the underlying image request is not cancelled. The `default` slot is not drawn into the watermark image.

## CSS Variables

The watermark reads its color from the computed CSS variable and redraws when a `class` or `style` change on the component or its current ancestors changes that color. Call `redraw()` after changes that cannot be observed, such as CSSOM or media query changes, or after moving it to a new ancestor. `anti-tamper` restores removal and class/style changes to the managed layer; it is not a security boundary.
